entries.name: LocalGaugeData
entries.docstring:
Local gauge data. A gauge group `G₀` with Lie algebra `𝔤`, its group of jets `GJ` with
  Lie algebra of jets `𝔤J`, evaluation at the base point, formal derivatives, the adjoint
  action and the Maurer–Cartan form, subject to the identities used by the transformation
  laws of gauge and matter fields.
entries.snippet:
structure LocalGaugeData (G₀ : Type) [Group G₀] (𝔤 : Type) [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤]
    (GJ : Type) [Group GJ] (𝔤J : Type) [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J] where
  eval : GJ →* G₀
  ofConstant : G₀ →* GJ
  eval_ofConstant : ∀ g, eval (ofConstant g) = g
  evalLie : 𝔤J →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ 𝔤
  ofConstantLie : 𝔤 →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ 𝔤J
  evalLie_ofConstantLie : ∀ a, evalLie (ofConstantLie a) = a
  deriv : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤J →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤J
  deriv_comm : ∀ (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : 𝔤J), deriv μ (deriv ν a) = deriv ν (deriv μ a)
  deriv_bracket : ∀ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : 𝔤J),
    deriv μ ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅deriv μ x, y⁆ + ⁅x, deriv μ y⁆
  deriv_ofConstantLie : ∀ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : 𝔤), deriv μ (ofConstantLie a) = 0
  mulCoord : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤J →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤J
  deriv_mulCoord : ∀ (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : 𝔤J),
    deriv μ (mulCoord ν a) = mulCoord ν (deriv μ a) + if μ = ν then a else 0
  evalLie_mulCoord : ∀ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : 𝔤J), evalLie (mulCoord μ a) = 0
  mulCoord_bracket : ∀ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a b : 𝔤J), ⁅mulCoord μ a, b⁆ = mulCoord μ ⁅a, b⁆
  adjointJ : Representation ℝ GJ 𝔤J
  adjointJ_bracket : ∀ (U : GJ) (x y : 𝔤J), adjointJ U ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅adjointJ U x, adjointJ U y⁆
  adjoint : Representation ℝ G₀ 𝔤
  evalLie_adjointJ : ∀ (U : GJ) (x : 𝔤J), evalLie (adjointJ U x) = adjoint (eval U) (evalLie x)
  maurerCartan : GJ → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤J
  maurerCartan_ofConstant : ∀ (g : G₀) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), maurerCartan (ofConstant g) μ = 0
  maurerCartan_cocycle : ∀ (U V : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
    maurerCartan (U * V) μ = maurerCartan U μ + adjointJ U (maurerCartan V μ)
  maurerCartan_structure : ∀ (U : GJ) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
    deriv μ (maurerCartan U ν) - deriv ν (maurerCartan U μ)
      + ⁅maurerCartan U μ, maurerCartan U ν⁆ = 0
  deriv_adjointJ : ∀ (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : 𝔤J),
    deriv μ (adjointJ U x) = adjointJ U (deriv μ x) - ⁅maurerCartan U μ, adjointJ U x⁆

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.adjoint_bracket
entries.snippet:
lemma adjoint_bracket (g : G₀) (a b : 𝔤) :
    jets.adjoint g ⁅a, b⁆ = ⁅jets.adjoint g a, jets.adjoint g b⁆

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.deriv_adjointJ_ofConstant
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_adjointJ_ofConstant (g : G₀) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : 𝔤J) :
    jets.deriv μ (jets.adjointJ (jets.ofConstant g) x) =
      jets.adjointJ (jets.ofConstant g) (jets.deriv μ x)

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.instRightCommutativeCompDeriv
entries.docstring: Post-composition with `deriv` is right-commutative.
entries.snippet:
instance instRightCommutativeCompDeriv : RightCommutative
    (fun (D : 𝔤J →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤J) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) => D.comp (jets.deriv μ)) where

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv
entries.docstring: The iterated formal derivative on the jet Lie algebra.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def iteratedDeriv (μs : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : 𝔤J →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤J

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_zero
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma iteratedDeriv_zero : jets.iteratedDeriv (0 : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = LinearMap.id

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_cons
entries.snippet:
lemma iteratedDeriv_cons (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μs : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jets.iteratedDeriv (μ ::ₘ μs) = (jets.deriv μ).comp (jets.iteratedDeriv μs)

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_add
entries.docstring: The iterated derivative is additive in the multiset.
entries.snippet:
lemma iteratedDeriv_add (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jets.iteratedDeriv (s + t) = (jets.iteratedDeriv s).comp (jets.iteratedDeriv t)

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_singleton
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma iteratedDeriv_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jets.iteratedDeriv ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = jets.deriv μ

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_cons_eq_comp_deriv
entries.snippet:
lemma iteratedDeriv_cons_eq_comp_deriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jets.iteratedDeriv (μ ::ₘ s) = (jets.iteratedDeriv s).comp (jets.deriv μ)

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_bracket
entries.docstring: The iterated Leibniz rule for the bracket.
entries.snippet:
lemma iteratedDeriv_bracket (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a b : 𝔤J) :
    jets.iteratedDeriv s ⁅a, b⁆ =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        ⁅jets.iteratedDeriv p.1 a, jets.iteratedDeriv p.2 b⁆).sum

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_ofConstantLie_of_ne_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma iteratedDeriv_ofConstantLie_of_ne_zero {p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} (hp : p ≠ 0)
    (a : 𝔤) : jets.iteratedDeriv p (jets.ofConstantLie a) = 0

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_adjointJ_ofConstant
entries.snippet:
lemma iteratedDeriv_adjointJ_ofConstant (g : G₀) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (x : 𝔤J) :
    jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.adjointJ (jets.ofConstant g) x) =
      jets.adjointJ (jets.ofConstant g) (jets.iteratedDeriv s x)

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_mulCoord
entries.snippet:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDeriv_mulCoord (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : 𝔤J) :
    jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.mulCoord μ a)) =
      s.count μ • jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv (s.erase μ) a)

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.Hom
entries.docstring:
A morphism of local gauge data.

  `Hom` is the standard name for a morphism in Lean.
entries.snippet:
structure Hom (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) (jets' : LocalGaugeData G₀' 𝔤' GJ' 𝔤J') where
  group : G₀ →* G₀'
  groupJ : GJ →* GJ'
  eval_groupJ : ∀ U, jets'.eval (groupJ U) = group (jets.eval U)
  groupJ_ofConstant : ∀ g, groupJ (jets.ofConstant g) = jets'.ofConstant (group g)
  lie : 𝔤 →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ 𝔤'
  lieJ : 𝔤J →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ 𝔤J'
  lieJ_ofConstantLie : ∀ c, lieJ (jets.ofConstantLie c) = jets'.ofConstantLie (lie c)
  evalLie_lieJ : ∀ a, jets'.evalLie (lieJ a) = lie (jets.evalLie a)
  lieJ_deriv : ∀ μ a, lieJ (jets.deriv μ a) = jets'.deriv μ (lieJ a)
  lieJ_mulCoord : ∀ μ a, lieJ (jets.mulCoord μ a) = jets'.mulCoord μ (lieJ a)
  lieJ_adjointJ : ∀ U a, lieJ (jets.adjointJ U a) = jets'.adjointJ (groupJ U) (lieJ a)
  lieJ_maurerCartan : ∀ U μ, lieJ (jets.maurerCartan U μ) = jets'.maurerCartan (groupJ U) μ

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.Hom.lie_adjoint
entries.docstring: A morphism intertwines the adjoint actions of the gauge groups.
entries.snippet:
lemma lie_adjoint (g : G₀) (x : 𝔤) :
    f.lie (jets.adjoint g x) = jets'.adjoint (f.group g) (f.lie x)

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.Hom.lieJ_iteratedDeriv
entries.docstring: A morphism commutes with iterated derivatives.
entries.snippet:
lemma lieJ_iteratedDeriv (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : 𝔤J) :
    f.lieJ (jets.iteratedDeriv s a) = jets'.iteratedDeriv s (f.lieJ a)

entries.name: LocalGaugeData.Hom.id
entries.docstring: The identity morphism of local gauge data.
entries.snippet: protected def id (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) : Hom jets jets where

entries.docstring: The composite `g ∘ f` of morphisms of local gauge data.
entries.snippet: def comp (g : Hom jets' jets'') : Hom jets jets'' where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Variation
entries.docstring: A smooth variation of `γ` on `[t₀, t₁]` fixing `γ t₀` and `γ t₁`.
entries.snippet:
@[ext]
structure Variation (γ : Time → M) (t₀ t₁ : Time) where
  toFun : C^∞⟮𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ × Time; I, M⟯
  apply_zero : ∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 (t₁ -ᵥ t₀), toFun (0, s +ᵥ t₀) = γ (s +ᵥ t₀)
  apply_left : ∀ s, toFun (s, t₀) = γ t₀
  apply_right : ∀ s, toFun (s, t₁) = γ t₁

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Variation.nonempty
entries.docstring: A smooth curve admits the constant variation.
entries.snippet:
lemma nonempty {γ : Time → M} {t₀ t₁ : Time} (hγ : ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) I ∞ γ) :
    Nonempty (Variation I γ t₀ t₁)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Variation.contDiff_comp_vadd
entries.docstring: `(s, τ) ↦ h (s, τ +ᵥ t₀)` is smooth.

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Variation.exists_bump
entries.docstring:
For a smooth curve `γ`, smooth `ψ` supported in `(0, t₁ -ᵥ t₀)` and `w : E`, there exists a
variation `h` of `γ` with `h (s, τ +ᵥ t₀) = γ (τ +ᵥ t₀) + s • ψ τ • w`.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_bump {γ : Time → E} {t₀ t₁ : Time} (hγ : ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ γ)
    {ψ : ℝ → ℝ} (hψ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ ψ) (hs : tsupport ψ ⊆ Ioo 0 (t₁ -ᵥ t₀)) (w : E) :
    ∃ h : Variation (M := ⟨E⟩) 𝓘(ℝ, E) γ t₀ t₁,
      ∀ s τ, h.toFun (s, τ +ᵥ t₀) = γ (τ +ᵥ t₀) + s • (ψ τ • w)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.eulerLagrange
entries.docstring:
The Euler-Lagrange covector `∂L/∂q - dₜ(∂L/∂q̇)` of a curve `q`; the covector counterpart of

entries.snippet: noncomputable def eulerLagrange (q : ℝ → E) (τ : ℝ) : E →L[ℝ] ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.contDiff_eulerLagrange
entries.docstring: The Euler-Lagrange covector of a smooth curve is smooth.
entries.snippet:
lemma contDiff_eulerLagrange {q : ℝ → E} (hq : ContDiff ℝ ∞ q) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (eulerLagrange S t₀ q)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.eulerLagrange_congr
entries.docstring: The Euler-Lagrange covector at `τ` depends only on the germ of the curve at `τ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma eulerLagrange_congr {q g : ℝ → E} {τ : ℝ} (h : q =ᶠ[𝓝 τ] g) :
    eulerLagrange S t₀ q τ = eulerLagrange S t₀ g τ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.eulerLagrange_congr_lagrangian
entries.docstring: The Euler-Lagrange covector only depends on the Lagrangian near the curve.
entries.snippet:
lemma eulerLagrange_congr_lagrangian {S' : LagrangianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⟨E⟩} {q : ℝ → E} {τ : ℝ}
    {N : Set E} (hN : IsOpen N) (hq : ∀ᶠ σ in 𝓝 τ, q σ ∈ N)
    (h : ∀ p : ℝ × E × E, p.2.1 ∈ N → S.coord t₀ p = S'.coord t₀ p) :
    eulerLagrange S t₀ q τ = eulerLagrange S' t₀ q τ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket
entries.docstring:
The Poisson bracket of two phase-space functions `f g : X → X → ℝ`, each read as `f p q` for
a momentum `p` and a position `q`, at a point `(p, q)` of phase space.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def poissonBracket (f g : X → X → ℝ) (p q : X) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket_eq_of_hasGradientAt
entries.docstring:
The Poisson bracket of two phase-space functions whose partial gradients at `(p, q)` are
known.
entries.snippet:
lemma poissonBracket_eq_of_hasGradientAt {f g : X → X → ℝ} {p q fp fq gp gq : X}
    (hfp : HasGradientAt (fun p' => f p' q) fp p) (hfq : HasGradientAt (fun q' => f p q') fq q)
    (hgp : HasGradientAt (fun p' => g p' q) gp p) (hgq : HasGradientAt (fun q' => g p q') gq q) :
    poissonBracket f g p q = ⟪fq, gp⟫_ℝ - ⟪fp, gq⟫_ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket_antisymm
entries.docstring: The Poisson bracket is antisymmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma poissonBracket_antisymm (f g : X → X → ℝ) (p q : X) :
    poissonBracket f g p q = -poissonBracket g f p q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket_self
entries.docstring: The Poisson bracket of a phase-space function with itself vanishes.
entries.snippet: lemma poissonBracket_self (f : X → X → ℝ) (p q : X) : poissonBracket f f p q = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket_add_left
entries.docstring:
The Poisson bracket is additive in its first argument, for functions differentiable in both
phase-space directions.
entries.snippet:
lemma poissonBracket_add_left (f₁ f₂ g : X → X → ℝ) (p q : X)
    (hf₁p : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => f₁ p' q) p)
    (hf₂p : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => f₂ p' q) p)
    (hf₁q : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => f₁ p q') q)
    (hf₂q : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => f₂ p q') q) :
    poissonBracket (fun p' q' => f₁ p' q' + f₂ p' q') g p q =
      poissonBracket f₁ g p q + poissonBracket f₂ g p q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket_const_mul_left
entries.docstring:
The Poisson bracket is homogeneous of degree one in its first argument, for a function
differentiable in both phase-space directions.
entries.snippet:
lemma poissonBracket_const_mul_left (c : ℝ) (f g : X → X → ℝ) (p q : X)
    (hfp : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => f p' q) p)
    (hfq : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => f p q') q) :
    poissonBracket (fun p' q' => c * f p' q') g p q = c * poissonBracket f g p q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket_add_right
entries.docstring: The Poisson bracket is additive in its second argument.
entries.snippet:
lemma poissonBracket_add_right (f g₁ g₂ : X → X → ℝ) (p q : X)
    (hg₁p : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => g₁ p' q) p)
    (hg₂p : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => g₂ p' q) p)
    (hg₁q : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => g₁ p q') q)
    (hg₂q : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => g₂ p q') q) :
    poissonBracket f (fun p' q' => g₁ p' q' + g₂ p' q') p q =
      poissonBracket f g₁ p q + poissonBracket f g₂ p q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket_const_mul_right
entries.docstring: The Poisson bracket is homogeneous of degree one in its second argument.
entries.snippet:
lemma poissonBracket_const_mul_right (c : ℝ) (f g : X → X → ℝ) (p q : X)
    (hgp : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => g p' q) p)
    (hgq : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => g p q') q) :
    poissonBracket f (fun p' q' => c * g p' q') p q = c * poissonBracket f g p q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket_mul_left
entries.docstring: The Poisson bracket satisfies the Leibniz rule in its first argument.
entries.snippet:
lemma poissonBracket_mul_left (f₁ f₂ g : X → X → ℝ) (p q : X)
    (hf₁p : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => f₁ p' q) p)
    (hf₂p : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => f₂ p' q) p)
    (hf₁q : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => f₁ p q') q)
    (hf₂q : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => f₂ p q') q) :
    poissonBracket (fun p' q' => f₁ p' q' * f₂ p' q') g p q =
      poissonBracket f₁ g p q * f₂ p q + f₁ p q * poissonBracket f₂ g p q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.poissonBracket_mul_right
entries.docstring: The Poisson bracket satisfies the Leibniz rule in its second argument.
entries.snippet:
lemma poissonBracket_mul_right (f g₁ g₂ : X → X → ℝ) (p q : X)
    (hg₁p : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => g₁ p' q) p)
    (hg₂p : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun p' => g₂ p' q) p)
    (hg₁q : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => g₁ p q') q)
    (hg₂q : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q' => g₂ p q') q) :
    poissonBracket f (fun p' q' => g₁ p' q' * g₂ p' q') p q =
      poissonBracket f g₁ p q * g₂ p q + g₁ p q * poissonBracket f g₂ p q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.deriv_comp_eq_inner_gradient_add
entries.docstring:
The time derivative of a phase-space function `f` composed with trajectories `p q : Time → X`
is the sum of the gradients of `f` paired with the velocities `∂ₜ p` and `∂ₜ q`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_comp_eq_inner_gradient_add (f : X → X → ℝ) (p q : Time → X) (t : Time)
    (hp : DifferentiableAt ℝ p t) (hq : DifferentiableAt ℝ q t)
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ (Function.uncurry f) (p t, q t)) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t => f (p t) (q t)) t =
      ⟪gradient (fun p' => f p' (q t)) (p t), ∂ₜ p t⟫_ℝ +
      ⟪gradient (fun q' => f (p t) q') (q t), ∂ₜ q t⟫_ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.deriv_comp_eq_poissonBracket
entries.docstring:
Along a solution of Hamilton's equations for a Hamiltonian `H`, the time derivative of a
phase-space observable `f` is its Poisson bracket with `H t`.
entries.snippet:
theorem deriv_comp_eq_poissonBracket (H : Time → X → X → ℝ) (p q : Time → X) (f : X → X → ℝ)
    (t : Time) (heq : hamiltonEqOp H p q = 0)
    (hp : DifferentiableAt ℝ p t) (hq : DifferentiableAt ℝ q t)
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ (Function.uncurry f) (p t, q t)) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t => f (p t) (q t)) t = poissonBracket f (H t) (p t) (q t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.trajectory_energy
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_energy (IC : InitialConditions) : S.energy (IC.trajectory S) =
    fun _ => 1/2 * (S.m * ‖IC.v₀‖ ^2 + S.k * ‖IC.x₀‖ ^ 2)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.trajectory_eq_cos
entries.docstring:
Every trajectory of the harmonic oscillator is a single shifted cosine after converting its
  initial conditions to amplitude-phase form.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_eq_cos (IC : InitialConditions) (t : Time) :
    IC.trajectory S t =
      EuclideanSpace.single 0 ((AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A *
        cos (S.ω * t - (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.trajectory_velocity_eq_sin
entries.docstring: The velocity of every trajectory is the corresponding shifted sine in amplitude-phase form.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_velocity_eq_sin (IC : InitialConditions) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (IC.trajectory S) t =
      EuclideanSpace.single 0 (-((AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A * S.ω *
        sin (S.ω * t.val - (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ)))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_sin_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
For nonzero amplitude, the velocity vanishes exactly when the sine factor in
  amplitude-phase form vanishes.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_sin_eq_zero (IC : InitialConditions)
    (hA : (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (IC.trajectory S) t = 0 ↔
      sin (S.ω * t.val - (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ) = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_exists_int
entries.docstring: For nonzero amplitude, the velocity is zero exactly at phase times `φ + nπ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_exists_int (IC : InitialConditions)
    (hA : (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (IC.trajectory S) t = 0 ↔
      ∃ n : ℤ,
        (t : ℝ) =
          ((AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ + n * π) / S.ω

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_norm_eq_amplitude
entries.docstring: The velocity vanishes exactly when the trajectory has norm equal to the amplitude.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_velocity_eq_zero_iff_norm_eq_amplitude (IC : InitialConditions)
    (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (IC.trajectory S) t = 0 ↔
      ‖IC.trajectory S t‖ = (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.trajectory_eq_zero_iff_cos_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
For nonzero amplitude, the trajectory passes through zero exactly when the cosine factor in
  amplitude-phase form vanishes.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_eq_zero_iff_cos_eq_zero (IC : InitialConditions)
    (hA : (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    IC.trajectory S t = 0 ↔
      cos (S.ω * t.val - (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ) = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.trajectory_eq_zero_iff_exists_int
entries.docstring:
For nonzero amplitude, the trajectory passes through zero exactly at phase times
  `φ + (2n + 1)π / 2`.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_eq_zero_iff_exists_int (IC : InitialConditions)
    (hA : (AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).A ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    IC.trajectory S t = 0 ↔
      ∃ n : ℤ,
        (t : ℝ) =
          ((AmplitudePhase.fromInitialConditions S IC).φ + (2 * n + 1) * π / 2) / S.ω

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.«instance@b431e220»
entries.snippet: instance : FunLike (LagrangianSystem I M) (Time × TangentBundle I M) ℝ where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.ofNormedSpace
entries.docstring: The Lagrangian system on a normed space `E` given by a smooth `L(t, q, q̇)`.

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.coord
entries.docstring: `L` in the time coordinate `τ ↦ τ +ᵥ t₀`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def coord (S : LagrangianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⟨E⟩) (t₀ : Time) (p : ℝ × E × E) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.contDiff_coord
entries.docstring: `S.coord t₀` is smooth.
entries.snippet:
lemma contDiff_coord (S : LagrangianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⟨E⟩) (t₀ : Time) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (S.coord t₀)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.action
entries.docstring: The action `∫ L(t, γ, γ̇) dt` over `[t₀, t₁]`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def action (γ : Time → M) (t₀ t₁ : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.action_eq_zero_of_vsub_nonpos
entries.docstring: The action over an empty or one-point interval vanishes.
entries.snippet: lemma action_eq_zero_of_vsub_nonpos (h : t₁ -ᵥ t₀ ≤ 0) : S.action γ t₀ t₁ = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.action_eq_integral_coord
entries.docstring:
The action is the integral over `[0, t₁ -ᵥ t₀]` of `S.coord t₀ (s, q s, q' s)`, where
`q τ = γ (τ +ᵥ t₀)` and `q' = deriv q`.
entries.snippet:
lemma action_eq_integral_coord (S : LagrangianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⟨E⟩) (γ : Time → E) (t₀ t₁ : Time) :
    S.action γ t₀ t₁ = ∫ s in Set.Icc 0 (t₁ -ᵥ t₀),
      S.coord t₀ (s, γ (s +ᵥ t₀), deriv (fun τ : ℝ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ t₀)) s)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.IsCriticalPoint
entries.docstring:
`γ` is smooth and every variation of `γ` fixing the endpoints has zero first variation of the
action, i.e. `d/ds S[γ_s]` vanishes at `s = 0` (Hamilton's principle).
entries.snippet: def IsCriticalPoint (γ : Time → M) (t₀ t₁ : Time) : Prop

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.isCriticalPoint_of_vsub_nonpos
entries.docstring: Every smooth curve is critical over an empty or one-point interval.
entries.snippet:
lemma isCriticalPoint_of_vsub_nonpos (hγ : ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) I ∞ γ) (h : t₁ -ᵥ t₀ ≤ 0) :
    S.IsCriticalPoint γ t₀ t₁

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.isCriticalPoint_of_eulerLagrange_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
If `q σ = γ (σ +ᵥ t₀)` is smooth and `eulerLagrange S t₀ q = 0` on `(0, t₁ -ᵥ t₀)`, then `γ`
is a critical point.
entries.snippet:
lemma isCriticalPoint_of_eulerLagrange_eq_zero
    (hγ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun σ : ℝ ↦ γ (σ +ᵥ t₀))) (hEq : ∀ τ ∈ Ioo 0 (t₁ -ᵥ t₀),
      eulerLagrange S t₀ (fun σ ↦ γ (σ +ᵥ t₀)) τ = 0) : S.IsCriticalPoint γ t₀ t₁

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.eulerLagrange_eq_zero_of_isCriticalPoint
entries.docstring: A critical point `γ` has `eulerLagrange S t₀ q = 0` on `[0, t₁ -ᵥ t₀]`, `q σ = γ (σ +ᵥ t₀)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma eulerLagrange_eq_zero_of_isCriticalPoint (ht : t₁ -ᵥ t₀ ≠ 0)
    (hc : S.IsCriticalPoint γ t₀ t₁) : ∀ τ ∈ Icc 0 (t₁ -ᵥ t₀),
      eulerLagrange S t₀ (fun σ : ℝ ↦ γ (σ +ᵥ t₀)) τ = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.isCriticalPoint_iff_eulerLagrange
entries.docstring:
For `t₁ -ᵥ t₀ ≠ 0`, `γ` is a critical point iff `q σ = γ (σ +ᵥ t₀)` is smooth and
`eulerLagrange S t₀ q = 0` on `[0, t₁ -ᵥ t₀]`.
entries.snippet:
lemma isCriticalPoint_iff_eulerLagrange (ht : t₁ -ᵥ t₀ ≠ 0) :
    S.IsCriticalPoint γ t₀ t₁ ↔ ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun σ : ℝ ↦ γ (σ +ᵥ t₀)) ∧
      ∀ τ ∈ Icc 0 (t₁ -ᵥ t₀), eulerLagrange S t₀ (fun σ : ℝ ↦ γ (σ +ᵥ t₀)) τ = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.fderiv_action_integrand_apply
entries.docstring:
The `s`-derivative of the integrand of the action splits into the Euler-Lagrange term and
a total `τ`-derivative.
entries.snippet:
lemma fderiv_action_integrand_apply (S : LagrangianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⟨E⟩) (t₀ : Time)
    (hH : ContDiff ℝ ∞ H) (τ : ℝ) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ S.coord t₀ (p.2, H p, fderiv ℝ H p (0, 1))) (0, τ) (1, 0) =
      eulerLagrange S t₀ (fun σ ↦ H (0, σ)) τ (fderiv ℝ H (0, τ) (1, 0)) +
        (deriv (canonicalMomentum S t₀ fun σ ↦ H (0, σ)) τ
            (fderiv ℝ H (0, τ) (1, 0)) +
          canonicalMomentum S t₀ (fun σ ↦ H (0, σ)) τ
            (deriv (fun σ ↦ fderiv ℝ H (0, σ) (1, 0)) τ))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.contDiff_action_integrand
entries.docstring: The integrand `L(τ, H, ∂τ H)` of the action is smooth.
entries.snippet:
lemma contDiff_action_integrand (S : LagrangianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⟨E⟩) (t₀ : Time)
    (hH : ContDiff ℝ ∞ H) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ S.coord t₀ (p.2, H p, fderiv ℝ H p (0, 1))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.hasDerivAt_integral_variation
entries.docstring: First variation of `∫ L(τ, H, ∂τ H) dτ` along a variation fixing the endpoints.
entries.snippet:
lemma hasDerivAt_integral_variation (S : LagrangianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⟨E⟩) (t₀ : Time)
    (hH : ContDiff ℝ ∞ H)
    (T : ℝ) (h0 : ∀ s, H (s, 0) = H (0, 0)) (hT : ∀ s, H (s, T) = H (0, T)) :
    HasDerivAt
      (fun s ↦ ∫ τ in (0 : ℝ)..T, S.coord t₀ (τ, H (s, τ), fderiv ℝ H (s, τ) (0, 1)))
      (∫ τ in (0 : ℝ)..T,
        eulerLagrange S t₀ (fun σ ↦ H (0, σ)) τ (fderiv ℝ H (0, τ) (1, 0))) 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.action_variation_eq_integral
entries.docstring:
The action of `t ↦ h (s, t)` is the integral over `[0, t₁ -ᵥ t₀]` of
`S.coord t₀ (τ, q τ, q' τ)`, where `q τ = h (s, τ +ᵥ t₀)` and `q' = deriv q`.
entries.snippet:
lemma action_variation_eq_integral (S : LagrangianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⟨E⟩) {γ : Time → E}
    {t₀ t₁ : Time} (h : Variation (M := ⟨E⟩) 𝓘(ℝ, E) γ t₀ t₁) (ht : 0 ≤ t₁ -ᵥ t₀) (s : ℝ) :
    S.action (fun t ↦ h.toFun (s, t)) t₀ t₁ =
      ∫ τ in (0 : ℝ)..(t₁ -ᵥ t₀), S.coord t₀ (τ, h.toFun (s, τ +ᵥ t₀),
        fderiv ℝ (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ h.toFun (p.1, p.2 +ᵥ t₀)) (s, τ) (0, 1))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangianSystem.hasDerivAt_action_variation
entries.docstring:
The `s`-derivative at `0` of the action of `t ↦ h (s, t)` is the integral over
`[0, t₁ -ᵥ t₀]` of `eulerLagrange S t₀ q τ` applied to the derivative of `s ↦ h (s, τ +ᵥ t₀)` at
`0`, where `q σ = h (0, σ +ᵥ t₀)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma hasDerivAt_action_variation (S : LagrangianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⟨E⟩) {γ : Time → E}
    {t₀ t₁ : Time} (h : Variation (M := ⟨E⟩) 𝓘(ℝ, E) γ t₀ t₁) (ht : 0 ≤ t₁ -ᵥ t₀) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s ↦ S.action (fun t ↦ h.toFun (s, t)) t₀ t₁)
      (∫ τ in (0 : ℝ)..(t₁ -ᵥ t₀),
        eulerLagrange S t₀ (fun σ ↦ h.toFun (0, σ +ᵥ t₀)) τ
          (fderiv ℝ (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ h.toFun (p.1, p.2 +ᵥ t₀)) (0, τ) (1, 0))) 0

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal
entries.docstring:
A crystal with finitely generated abelian translation group `G` and a finite, nonempty unit
cell. The sites are one copy of each unit-cell label in every translated cell.
entries.snippet:
structure Crystal (G : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [AddGroup.FG G] where
  UnitCell : Type*
  [finiteUnitCell : Finite UnitCell]
  [nonemptyUnitCell : Nonempty UnitCell]

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.ofUnitCell
entries.docstring:
Construct a crystal by repeating a unit cell with labels `F`.
The group `G` indexes translated cells; `⟨n, i⟩` is the site with label `i` in cell `n`.
entries.snippet:
abbrev ofUnitCell (G : Type*) (F : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [AddGroup.FG G]
    [Finite F] [Nonempty F] : Crystal G where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.ref
entries.docstring: The site with label `i` in the reference cell, the cell `0`.
entries.snippet: abbrev Site.ref {C : Crystal G} (i : C.UnitCell) : C.Site

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.siteEquiv
entries.docstring: A site is a pair of its unit-cell label and its cell.
entries.snippet: def siteEquiv (C : Crystal G) : C.Site ≃ C.UnitCell × G where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.«instance@133a183a»
entries.docstring: Sites can be compared when cells and unit-cell labels can be compared.
entries.snippet: instance (C : Crystal G) [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq C.UnitCell] : DecidableEq C.Site

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.«instance@8eec9f8f»
entries.docstring: A finite set of cells and a finite unit cell give a finite set of sites.
entries.snippet: instance (C : Crystal G) [Fintype G] [Fintype C.UnitCell] : Fintype C.Site

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.«instance@ac998860»
entries.docstring: A finite translation group, as for periodic boundary conditions, gives a finite crystal.
entries.snippet: instance (C : Crystal G) [Finite G] : Finite C.Site

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.«instance@51b1c054»
entries.docstring: Every crystal has a site in its reference cell.
entries.snippet: instance (C : Crystal G) : Nonempty C.Site

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.«instance@09c5c20a»
entries.docstring: Translate a site to another cell, preserving its unit-cell label.
entries.snippet: instance (C : Crystal G) : AddAction G C.Site where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.vadd_def
entries.docstring: Translation changes a site's cell and preserves its label.
entries.snippet:
lemma Site.vadd_def {C : Crystal G} (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    a +ᵥ x = ⟨a + x.cell, x.label⟩

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.«instance@74514a9e»
entries.docstring:
Translation acts freely: translations are injective on sites, and different translations move
a site to different sites.
entries.snippet: instance (C : Crystal G) : IsCancelVAdd G C.Site where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.mem_orbit_iff_label_eq
entries.docstring: The translates of a site are exactly the sites with the same label.
entries.snippet:
lemma Site.mem_orbit_iff_label_eq {C : Crystal G} (x y : C.Site) :
    y ∈ AddAction.orbit G x ↔ x.label = y.label

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Species
entries.docstring:
A species assignment gives each label of the unit cell a species in `Q`, for example a chemical
element. The same assignment holds in every cell.
entries.snippet: abbrev Species (C : Crystal G) (Q : Type*)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond
entries.docstring: A bond from `source` in one cell to `target` in the cell displaced by `displacement`.
entries.snippet:
structure Bond (C : Crystal G) where
  source : C.UnitCell
  target : C.UnitCell
  displacement : G

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.«instance@a832d07f»
entries.docstring: Bonds can be compared when cells and unit-cell labels can be compared.
entries.snippet: instance {C : Crystal G} [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq C.UnitCell] : DecidableEq (Bond C)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.Links
entries.docstring: Site `x` is the source and site `y` is the target of this bond.
entries.snippet: def Links (b : Bond C) (x y : C.Site) : Prop

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.links_reference
entries.docstring: Every bond links the reference site of its source to the site its displacement points to.
entries.snippet: lemma links_reference (b : Bond C) : b.Links (Site.ref b.source) ⟨b.displacement, b.target⟩

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.eq_of_links
entries.docstring: Two bonds linking the same pair of sites are equal.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_of_links {b b' : Bond C} {x y : C.Site} (h : b.Links x y) (h' : b'.Links x y) :
    b = b'

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.links_vadd
entries.docstring: Translating the endpoints gives another copy of the same bond.
entries.snippet:
lemma links_vadd (b : Bond C) (a : G) (x y : C.Site) :
    b.Links (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) ↔ b.Links x y

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.«instance@69ca0a9e»
entries.docstring: The source and target of a bond can be checked from their site addresses.
entries.snippet: instance [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq C.UnitCell] (b : Bond C) : DecidableRel b.Links

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.bravais
entries.docstring:
The Bravais lattice of dimension `d`: the translation group is `ℤᵈ` and the unit cell has a
single site.
entries.snippet: def bravais (d : ℕ) : Crystal (Fin d → ℤ)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.ofVectors
entries.docstring: The embedding of the Bravais lattice of dimension `d` given by `d` primitive vectors.
entries.snippet: def ofVectors (v : Fin d → E) : Embedding (bravais d) E where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.position_ofVectors
entries.docstring:
The position of a site is the integer combination of the primitive vectors given by its
cell.
entries.snippet:
lemma position_ofVectors (v : Fin d → E) (x : (bravais d).Site) :
    (ofVectors v).position x = ∑ j, x.cell j • v j

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.isSpaceFilling_ofVectors_iff
entries.docstring:
The embedding of a Bravais lattice is space filling exactly when the primitive vectors span
the space.
entries.snippet:
lemma isSpaceFilling_ofVectors_iff (v : Fin d → E) :
    (ofVectors v).IsSpaceFilling ↔ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) = ⊤

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.position_ofVectors_injective
entries.docstring: Linearly independent primitive vectors give distinct positions to distinct sites.
entries.snippet:
lemma position_ofVectors_injective {v : Fin d → E} (hv : LinearIndependent ℝ v) :
    Function.Injective (ofVectors v).position

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.finrank_eq_of_ofVectors
entries.docstring:
A space-filling embedding of a Bravais lattice with linearly independent primitive vectors
lives in a space of dimension `d`.
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_eq_of_ofVectors {v : Fin d → E} (hv : LinearIndependent ℝ v)
    (h : (ofVectors v).IsSpaceFilling) : Module.finrank ℝ E = d

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding
entries.docstring:
An embedding of a crystal in a normed group `E`. It assigns a vector to each translation and a
position to each site of the reference cell.
entries.snippet:
structure Embedding (C : Crystal G) (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] where
  vector : G →+ E
  basis : C.UnitCell → E

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.position
entries.docstring: The site `(n, i)` sits at the vector of `n` plus the position of the label `i`.
entries.snippet: def position (x : C.Site) : E

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.position_vadd
entries.docstring: Translating a site by `a` translates its position by the vector of `a`.
entries.snippet: lemma position_vadd (a : G) (x : C.Site) : R.position (a +ᵥ x) = R.vector a + R.position x

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.action
entries.docstring: The translation group acts on the space by its vectors.
entries.snippet: abbrev action : AddAction G E

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.positionHom
entries.docstring: The positions commute with the translations.
entries.snippet: def positionHom : letI

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.dist_position_vadd
entries.docstring: Translating two sites does not change the distance between their positions.
entries.snippet:
lemma dist_position_vadd (a : G) (x y : C.Site) :
    Dist.dist (R.position (a +ᵥ x)) (R.position (a +ᵥ y)) =
      Dist.dist (R.position x) (R.position y)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.IsSpaceFilling
entries.docstring:
The embedding is space filling if the vectors of the translations span the space, so that the
crystal repeats in every direction.
entries.snippet: def IsSpaceFilling : Prop

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.isSpaceFilling_iff
entries.docstring:
An embedding fills the space exactly when the vectors of a generating set of the translation
group span it.
entries.snippet:
lemma isSpaceFilling_iff {S : Set G} (hS : AddSubgroup.closure S = ⊤) :
    R.IsSpaceFilling ↔ Submodule.span ℝ (R.vector '' S) = ⊤

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.IsSpaceFilling.finiteDimensional
entries.docstring: A space-filling embedding is in a finite-dimensional space.
entries.snippet: lemma IsSpaceFilling.finiteDimensional (h : R.IsSpaceFilling) : FiniteDimensional ℝ E

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.IsSpaceFilling.finrank_eq_rank
entries.docstring:
The dimension equals the rank of the translation group when the vectors of a basis of the
group are linearly independent over `ℝ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsSpaceFilling.finrank_eq_rank (h : R.IsSpaceFilling) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (B : Module.Basis ι ℤ G) (hB : LinearIndependent ℝ (R.vector ∘ B)) :
    Module.finrank ℝ E = Module.finrank ℤ G

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph
entries.docstring:
A periodic pattern of undirected connections between crystal sites, with finitely many
neighbors at each site.
entries.snippet:
structure PeriodicGraph (C : Crystal G) where
  toSimpleGraph : SimpleGraph C.Site
  adj_vadd : ∀ (a : G) (x y : C.Site),
    toSimpleGraph.Adj (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) ↔ toSimpleGraph.Adj x y
  [locallyFinite : toSimpleGraph.LocallyFinite]

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.translateIso
entries.docstring: A translation is an automorphism of the graph.
entries.snippet: def translateIso (g : PeriodicGraph C) (a : G) : g.toSimpleGraph ≃g g.toSimpleGraph where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.degree_vadd
entries.docstring: The degree, the number of neighbors, is the same for all translates of a site.
entries.snippet:
lemma degree_vadd (g : PeriodicGraph C) (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.degree (a +ᵥ x) = g.toSimpleGraph.degree x

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.degree_cell
entries.docstring: The degree of a site depends only on its label.
entries.snippet:
lemma degree_cell (g : PeriodicGraph C) (n : G) (i : C.UnitCell) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.degree ⟨n, i⟩ = g.toSimpleGraph.degree (Site.ref i)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.graphOfBonds
entries.docstring: The undirected graph generated by translating every bond in the set.
entries.snippet: def graphOfBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) : SimpleGraph C.Site

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_graphOfBonds
entries.docstring: Two sites are adjacent when they are different and joined by a bond in either direction.
entries.snippet:
lemma adj_graphOfBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (x y : C.Site) :
    (graphOfBonds bonds).Adj x y ↔ x ≠ y ∧ ∃ b ∈ bonds, b.Links x y ∨ b.Links y x

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_iff
entries.docstring: Adjacency depends only on the labels of the sites and the difference of their cells.
entries.snippet:
lemma adj_iff (g : PeriodicGraph C) (x y : C.Site) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y ↔
      g.toSimpleGraph.Adj (Site.ref x.label) ⟨y.cell - x.cell, y.label⟩

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.«instance@48144578»
entries.docstring: Connections generated by a finite set of bonds can be decided.
entries.snippet: instance (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) : DecidableRel (graphOfBonds bonds).Adj

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.candidates
entries.docstring: The sites reached from `x` by following a bond forwards or backwards.
entries.snippet: def candidates (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (x : C.Site) : Finset C.Site

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.neighborsOfBonds
entries.docstring: The neighbors of a site in the graph generated by finitely many bonds.
entries.snippet: def neighborsOfBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (x : C.Site) : Finset C.Site

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_neighborsOfBonds
entries.docstring: The enumerated neighbors are exactly the adjacent sites.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_neighborsOfBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (x y : C.Site) :
    y ∈ neighborsOfBonds bonds x ↔ (graphOfBonds bonds).Adj x y

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.ofBonds
entries.docstring: The periodic graph obtained by repeating the given bonds in every cell.
entries.snippet: def ofBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) : PeriodicGraph C where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.bonds
entries.docstring: The bonds that join a site of the reference cell to one of its neighbors.
entries.snippet: def bonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) : Finset (Bond C)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_bonds
entries.docstring: A bond of `g.bonds` joins a site of the reference cell to one of its neighbors.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_bonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) (b : Bond C) :
    b ∈ g.bonds ↔ g.toSimpleGraph.Adj (Site.ref b.source) ⟨b.displacement, b.target⟩

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_of_links
entries.docstring: Sites joined by a bond of `g.bonds` are adjacent in `g`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adj_of_links (g : PeriodicGraph C) {b : Bond C} (hb : b ∈ g.bonds) {x y : C.Site}
    (h : b.Links x y) : g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_iff_mem_bonds
entries.docstring: Sites joined by a bond are adjacent exactly when the bond is one of `g.bonds`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adj_iff_mem_bonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) {b : Bond C} {x y : C.Site} (h : b.Links x y) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y ↔ b ∈ g.bonds

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.toSimpleGraph_eq_graphOfBonds
entries.docstring: Every periodic graph is generated by the finitely many bonds leaving the reference cell.
entries.snippet:
lemma toSimpleGraph_eq_graphOfBonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) :
    g.toSimpleGraph = graphOfBonds g.bonds

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.eq_ofBonds
entries.docstring:
Every periodic graph is generated by the finitely many bonds leaving the reference
cell.
entries.snippet: lemma eq_ofBonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) : g = ofBonds g.bonds

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.graphAutomorphisms
entries.docstring: The automorphism group of the underlying graph, without requiring crystal symmetry.
entries.snippet: def graphAutomorphisms (g : PeriodicGraph C) : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm C.Site) where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.PreservesBonds
entries.docstring: A crystal symmetry maps every bond of the reference cell to another such bond.
entries.snippet: def PreservesBonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) (φ : Symmetry C) : Prop

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.preservesBonds_iff_smul_eq
entries.docstring: A symmetry preserves the bonds exactly when it permutes the set of reference-cell bonds.
entries.snippet: lemma preservesBonds_iff_smul_eq : g.PreservesBonds φ ↔ φ • g.bonds = g.bonds

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.PreservesBonds.map_adj
entries.docstring: Preserving the reference-cell bonds implies preserving adjacency in the forward direction.
entries.snippet:
lemma PreservesBonds.map_adj (h : g.PreservesBonds φ) {x y : C.Site}
    (hxy : g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y) : g.toSimpleGraph.Adj (φ x) (φ y)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.PreservesBonds.inv
entries.docstring: The inverse of a symmetry that preserves the bonds preserves them as well.
entries.snippet: lemma PreservesBonds.inv (h : g.PreservesBonds φ) : g.PreservesBonds φ⁻¹

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry
entries.docstring:
A symmetry of a crystal: an automorphism of the action of the translation group on the sites.
It is an automorphism `lattice` of the translation group together with a bijection of the sites
that carries the action along.
entries.snippet:
structure Symmetry (C : Crystal G) where
  lattice : G ≃+ G
  toHom : AddActionHom ⇑lattice C.Site C.Site
  bijective : Function.Bijective toHom

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.ext'
entries.docstring: Symmetries with the same action on the sites are equal, since translations act freely.
entries.snippet: lemma ext' {φ ψ : Symmetry C} (h : ∀ x, φ.toHom x = ψ.toHom x) : φ = ψ

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.«instance@5e568b6a»
entries.docstring: A symmetry acts on the sites.
entries.snippet: instance : FunLike (Symmetry C) C.Site C.Site where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.map_vadd
entries.docstring: Mapping a translated site is translating the mapped site by the image of the vector.
entries.snippet: lemma map_vadd (φ : Symmetry C) (a : G) (x : C.Site) : φ (a +ᵥ x) = φ.lattice a +ᵥ φ x

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.apply_eq
entries.docstring: A symmetry moves the site `⟨n, i⟩` by the lattice automorphism from the image of `⟨0, i⟩`.
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq (φ : Symmetry C) (n : G) (i : C.UnitCell) :
    φ ⟨n, i⟩ = ⟨φ.lattice n + (φ (Site.ref i)).cell, (φ (Site.ref i)).label⟩

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.toEquiv
entries.docstring: A symmetry as a permutation of the sites.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def toEquiv (φ : Symmetry C) : C.Site ≃ C.Site

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.comp_map_vadd
entries.docstring: Composing equivariant maps gives an equivariant map.
entries.snippet:
lemma comp_map_vadd (φ ψ : Symmetry C) (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    (φ ∘ ψ) (a +ᵥ x) = (ψ.lattice.trans φ.lattice) a +ᵥ (φ ∘ ψ) x

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.id_map_vadd
entries.docstring: The identity is equivariant for the identity automorphism.
entries.snippet: lemma id_map_vadd (a : G) (x : C.Site) : id (a +ᵥ x) = AddEquiv.refl G a +ᵥ id x

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.symm_map_vadd
entries.docstring: The inverse of an equivariant bijection is equivariant for the inverse automorphism.
entries.snippet:
lemma symm_map_vadd (φ : Symmetry C) (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    φ.toEquiv.symm (a +ᵥ x) = φ.lattice.symm a +ᵥ φ.toEquiv.symm x

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.«instance@f4063c90»
entries.docstring: Symmetries form a group under composition.
entries.snippet: noncomputable instance (C : Crystal G) : Group (Symmetry C) where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.toPerm
entries.docstring: The permutation of the sites underlying a symmetry.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def toPerm (C : Crystal G) : Symmetry C →* Equiv.Perm C.Site where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.label_apply
entries.docstring: The label of the image of `⟨n, i⟩` does not depend on the cell `n`.
entries.snippet:
lemma label_apply (φ : Symmetry C) (n : G) (i : C.UnitCell) :
    (φ ⟨n, i⟩).label = (φ (Site.ref i)).label

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.«instance@76e399ba»
entries.docstring: A symmetry permutes the labels: it sends `i` to the label of the image of `⟨0, i⟩`.
entries.snippet: instance : MulAction (Symmetry C) C.UnitCell where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.labelHom
entries.docstring: The permutation of the labels by a symmetry, as a homomorphism.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def labelHom (C : Crystal G) : Symmetry C →* Equiv.Perm C.UnitCell

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.labelHom_apply
entries.docstring: The label permutation of a symmetry sends `i` to the label of the image of `⟨0, i⟩`.
entries.snippet:
lemma labelHom_apply (φ : Symmetry C) (i : C.UnitCell) :
    labelHom C φ i = (φ (Site.ref i)).label

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.Offsets
entries.docstring:
One lattice vector for each unit-cell label. Every symmetry has such offsets, and so does every
shift.
entries.snippet: abbrev Offsets (C : Crystal G)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.offset
entries.docstring:
The offsets of a symmetry: at the label `i` the cell in which the image of the reference site of
`i` lies, as a lattice vector in `G`.
entries.snippet: def offset (φ : Symmetry C) : Offsets C

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.apply_eq_components
entries.docstring:
A symmetry sends the site `⟨n, i⟩` to the cell `A n + bᵢ` with label `σ i`, where `A` is its
lattice automorphism, `σ` its label permutation and `bᵢ` its offset at `i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq_components (φ : Symmetry C) (x : C.Site) :
    φ x = ⟨φ.lattice x.cell + φ.offset x.label, labelHom C φ x.label⟩

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.cell_apply
entries.docstring: The cell of the image of `⟨n, i⟩` is `A n + bᵢ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma cell_apply (φ : Symmetry C) (x : C.Site) :
    (φ x).cell = φ.lattice x.cell + φ.offset x.label

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.vadd_map_vadd
entries.docstring: Translations commute, so translating is equivariant for the identity automorphism.
entries.snippet: lemma vadd_map_vadd (c b : G) (x : C.Site) : c +ᵥ (b +ᵥ x) = AddEquiv.refl G b +ᵥ (c +ᵥ x)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.translationHom
entries.docstring:
Translation as a homomorphism, with the lattice written multiplicatively. It is only used to
form the subgroup of translations; use `translation`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def translationHom (C : Crystal G) : Multiplicative G →* Symmetry C where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.translation
entries.docstring: Translation by a lattice vector, as a symmetry.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def translation (C : Crystal G) (a : G) : Symmetry C

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.translation_add
entries.docstring: Translations add.
entries.snippet: lemma translation_add (a b : G) : translation C (a + b) = translation C a * translation C b

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.translation_zero
entries.docstring: Translation by zero is the identity.
entries.snippet: lemma translation_zero : translation C 0 = 1

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.translations
entries.docstring: The translations as a subgroup of the symmetries.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def translations (C : Crystal G) : Subgroup (Symmetry C)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.conj_translation
entries.docstring: Conjugating a translation by a symmetry translates by the image of the vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma conj_translation (φ : Symmetry C) (a : G) :
    φ * translation C a * φ⁻¹ = translation C (φ.lattice a)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.«instance@e4aa0c15»
entries.docstring: The translations are a normal subgroup of the symmetries.
entries.snippet: instance : (translations C).Normal where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.mapBond
entries.docstring: The image of a bond under a crystal symmetry, with displacement `A δ + bⱼ - bᵢ`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def mapBond (b : Bond C) : Bond C where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.mapBond_links
entries.docstring: A symmetry maps sites connected by a bond to sites connected by its image.
entries.snippet:
lemma mapBond_links {b : Bond C} {x y : C.Site} (h : b.Links x y) :
    (φ.mapBond b).Links (φ x) (φ y)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.mapBond_mul
entries.docstring: The image of a bond under a product is the iterated image.
entries.snippet:
lemma mapBond_mul (ψ : Symmetry C) (b : Bond C) :
    (φ * ψ).mapBond b = φ.mapBond (ψ.mapBond b)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.mapBond_one
entries.docstring: The identity symmetry fixes every bond.
entries.snippet: lemma mapBond_one (b : Bond C) : (1 : Symmetry C).mapBond b = b

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.«instance@0ec1c8de»
entries.docstring: The crystal symmetries act on the bonds.
entries.snippet: noncomputable instance : MulAction (Symmetry C) (Bond C) where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.isometries
entries.docstring: The crystal symmetries that preserve distances between all pairs of site positions.
entries.snippet: def isometries : Subgroup (Symmetry C) where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.mem_isometries_iff
entries.docstring: A symmetry is an isometry exactly when it preserves every distance between site positions.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_isometries_iff : φ ∈ R.isometries ↔
    ∀ x y, dist (R.position (φ x)) (R.position (φ y)) = dist (R.position x) (R.position y)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.translations_le_isometries
entries.docstring: Translating both sites by the same lattice vector preserves their distance.
entries.snippet: lemma translations_le_isometries : Symmetry.translations C ≤ R.isometries

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.site_eq_vadd
entries.docstring: A site is the lattice translate of the site with the same label in the reference cell.
entries.snippet: lemma site_eq_vadd (x : C.Site) : x = x.cell +ᵥ (Site.ref x.label)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.mem_isometries_iff_reference
entries.docstring:
A symmetry is an isometry exactly when it preserves the distance from every site `(d, i)` to
every site `(0, j)` of the reference cell.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_isometries_iff_reference : φ ∈ R.isometries ↔ ∀ (i j : C.UnitCell) (d : G),
    dist (R.position (φ ⟨d, i⟩)) (R.position (φ (Site.ref j))) =
      dist (R.position ⟨d, i⟩) (R.position (Site.ref j))

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.componentsEquiv
entries.docstring:
The bijection of the sites `⟨n, i⟩ ↦ ⟨A n + bᵢ, σ i⟩` given by a lattice automorphism `A`, a
label permutation `σ` and offsets `b`.

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.ofComponents
entries.docstring:
The symmetry with lattice automorphism `A`, label permutation `σ` and offsets `b`. It is
equivariant for `A`, since translating `⟨n, i⟩` by `a` translates its image by `A a`.

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.eq_ofComponents
entries.docstring:
Every symmetry is determined by its components: it equals `ofComponents` of its lattice
automorphism, label permutation and offsets.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_ofComponents (φ : Symmetry C) :
    φ = ofComponents C φ.lattice (labelHom C φ) φ.offset

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.ofComponents_mul
entries.docstring:
The product of two symmetries in components: `(A, σ, b) * (A', σ', b') = (A + A', σ * σ', A ∘ b'
+ b ∘ σ')`, where `A + A'` is the composite `A ∘ A'` of lattice automorphisms.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofComponents_mul :
    ofComponents C A σ b * ofComponents C B τ b' =
      ofComponents C (A + B) (σ * τ) (A ∘ b' + b ∘ τ)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.linear
entries.docstring:
The point operation with lattice automorphism `A` and label permutation `σ`: it sends `⟨n, i⟩`
to `⟨A n, σ i⟩` and has no offsets.
entries.snippet: def linear (C : Crystal G) (A : G ≃+ G) (σ : Equiv.Perm C.UnitCell) : Symmetry C

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.linear_add_mul
entries.docstring:
Point operations compose through their components: `linear (A + B) (σ * τ) = linear A σ * linear
B τ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma linear_add_mul :
    linear C (A + B) (σ * τ) = linear C A σ * linear C B τ

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.pointOp
entries.docstring:
The point operation of a symmetry: the point operation with the same lattice automorphism and
label permutation, dropping the shifts. It is a homomorphism. For `ℤᵈ` it is the rotation or
reflection of the lattice.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def pointOp (C : Crystal G) : Symmetry C →* Symmetry C where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.shift
entries.docstring:
The shift by `b`: it moves every site with label `i` by the lattice vector `bᵢ` and fixes the
labels and the lattice.
entries.snippet: def shift (C : Crystal G) (b : Offsets C) : Symmetry C

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.shift_const
entries.docstring: A shift by the same vector `a` on every label is the translation by `a`.
entries.snippet: lemma shift_const (a : G) : shift C (Function.const C.UnitCell a) = translation C a

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.shift_add
entries.docstring: Shifts compose by adding their vectors: `shift (b + b') = shift b * shift b'`.
entries.snippet: lemma shift_add : shift C (b + b') = shift C b * shift C b'

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.shift_mul_linear
entries.docstring:
The point operation `(A, σ)` followed by the shift `b` is the symmetry with components `(A, σ, b
∘ σ)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma shift_mul_linear :
    shift C b * linear C A σ = ofComponents C A σ (b ∘ σ)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.shift_mul_linear_mul
entries.docstring:
The product in the decomposition into shifts and point operations: `(b, A, σ) * (b', B, τ) = (b
+ A ∘ b' ∘ σ⁻¹, A + B, σ * τ)`, where `A + B` is the composite `A ∘ B`.
entries.snippet:
lemma shift_mul_linear_mul :
    (shift C b * linear C A σ) * (shift C b' * linear C B τ) =
      shift C (b + A ∘ b' ∘ σ.symm) * linear C (A + B) (σ * τ)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.eq_shift_mul_linear
entries.docstring: Every symmetry is a point operation followed by a shift, with shift vectors `offset ∘ σ⁻¹`.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_shift_mul_linear (φ : Symmetry C) :
    φ = shift C (φ.offset ∘ (labelHom C φ).symm) * linear C φ.lattice (labelHom C φ)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.exists_eq_shift_mul_pointOp
entries.docstring: Every symmetry is its point operation followed by a shift.
entries.snippet: lemma exists_eq_shift_mul_pointOp (φ : Symmetry C) : ∃ b, φ = shift C b * pointOp C φ

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.pointOp_eq_one_iff
entries.docstring: A symmetry has trivial point operation exactly when it is a shift.
entries.snippet: lemma pointOp_eq_one_iff (φ : Symmetry C) : pointOp C φ = 1 ↔ ∃ b, φ = shift C b

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.pointOp_translation
entries.docstring: A translation has trivial point operation.
entries.snippet: lemma pointOp_translation (a : G) : pointOp C (translation C a) = 1

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.shiftAction
entries.docstring:
The action of the point operations on the shifts: a lattice automorphism `A` and a label
permutation `σ` send `b` to `A ∘ b ∘ σ⁻¹`.

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.semidirectEquiv
entries.docstring:
The symmetry group of a crystal is isomorphic to the semidirect product of the shifts, `UnitCell
→ G`, by the point operations, `Aut G × Perm UnitCell`, acting through `shiftAction`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def semidirectEquiv (C : Crystal G) :
    Multiplicative (Offsets C) ⋊[shiftAction C]
      (Multiplicative (AddAut G) × Equiv.Perm C.UnitCell) ≃* Symmetry C where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.spaceGroup
entries.docstring: The subgroup of crystal symmetries preserving adjacency.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def spaceGroup (g : PeriodicGraph C) : Subgroup (Symmetry C)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_spaceGroup_iff
entries.docstring: A crystal symmetry belongs to the space group exactly when it preserves adjacency.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_spaceGroup_iff :
    φ ∈ g.spaceGroup ↔ ∀ x y, g.toSimpleGraph.Adj (φ x) (φ y) ↔ g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.translation_mem_spaceGroup
entries.docstring: Every lattice translation belongs to the space group.
entries.snippet: lemma translation_mem_spaceGroup (a : G) : Symmetry.translation C a ∈ g.spaceGroup

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.translations_le_spaceGroup
entries.docstring: The translation subgroup is contained in the space group.
entries.snippet: lemma translations_le_spaceGroup : Symmetry.translations C ≤ g.spaceGroup

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.pointGroup
entries.docstring: The image of the space group under the point-operation homomorphism.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def pointGroup (g : PeriodicGraph C) : Subgroup (Symmetry C)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_pointGroup_iff
entries.docstring:
A symmetry is in the point group exactly when it is a point operation of a space-group
element.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_pointGroup_iff :
    ψ ∈ g.pointGroup ↔ ∃ φ ∈ g.spaceGroup, Symmetry.pointOp C φ = ψ

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.PreservesBonds.of_mem_spaceGroup
entries.docstring: Every space-group symmetry preserves the reference-cell bonds.
entries.snippet: lemma PreservesBonds.of_mem_spaceGroup (hφ : φ ∈ g.spaceGroup) : g.PreservesBonds φ

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_spaceGroup_iff_preservesBonds
entries.docstring: A crystal symmetry preserves adjacency exactly when it preserves the reference-cell bonds.
entries.snippet: lemma mem_spaceGroup_iff_preservesBonds : φ ∈ g.spaceGroup ↔ g.PreservesBonds φ

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.spaceGroup_eq_stabilizer
entries.docstring: The space group is the stabilizer of the set of reference-cell bonds.
entries.snippet:
lemma spaceGroup_eq_stabilizer :
    g.spaceGroup = MulAction.stabilizer (Symmetry C) g.bonds

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.speciesGroup
entries.docstring: The crystal symmetries that preserve the species assignment `q`.
entries.snippet: def speciesGroup (q : Species C Q) : Subgroup (Symmetry C) where

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.mem_speciesGroup_iff
entries.docstring: A symmetry preserves `q` exactly when it sends every label to one of the same species.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_speciesGroup_iff {q : Species C Q} {φ : Symmetry C} :
    φ ∈ speciesGroup q ↔ ∀ i, q (φ • i) = q i

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.speciesGroup_const
entries.docstring: Every crystal symmetry preserves a constant species assignment.
entries.snippet: lemma speciesGroup_const (c : Q) : speciesGroup (C := C) (Function.const _ c) = ⊤

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.ker_labelHom_le_speciesGroup
entries.docstring: A symmetry that fixes every unit-cell label preserves any species assignment.
entries.snippet: lemma ker_labelHom_le_speciesGroup (q : Species C Q) : (labelHom C).ker ≤ speciesGroup q

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.speciesGroup_eq_ker_labelHom
entries.docstring: With distinct species on distinct labels, preserving species requires fixing every label.
entries.snippet:
lemma speciesGroup_eq_ker_labelHom {q : Species C Q} (hq : Function.Injective q) :
    speciesGroup q = (labelHom C).ker

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.speciesGroup_le_comp
entries.docstring: Applying `f` to the species values can only enlarge the species group.
entries.snippet:
lemma speciesGroup_le_comp (q : Species C Q) {Q' : Type*} (f : Q → Q') :
    speciesGroup q ≤ speciesGroup (f ∘ q)

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.shift_mem_speciesGroup
entries.docstring: Every shift fixes the unit-cell labels and so preserves species.
entries.snippet:
lemma shift_mem_speciesGroup (q : Species C Q) (b : C.UnitCell → G) :
    shift C b ∈ speciesGroup q

entries.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Symmetry.translations_le_speciesGroup
entries.docstring: Every translation preserves any species assignment.
entries.snippet: lemma translations_le_speciesGroup (q : Species C Q) : translations C ≤ speciesGroup q

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.finrank_hilbertSpace
entries.docstring: The Hilbert space of the chain has dimension `N`.
entries.snippet: lemma finrank_hilbertSpace : Module.finrank ℂ T.HilbertSpace = T.N

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.quantaWaveNumber
entries.docstring: The quantized wavenumber `2 π / (a N) * (n - ⌊N/2⌋)` of the index `n`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def quantaWaveNumber (n : Fin T.N) : T.QuantaWaveNumber

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.quantaWaveNumber_injective
entries.docstring: Distinct indices give distinct quantized wavenumbers.
entries.snippet: lemma quantaWaveNumber_injective : Function.Injective T.quantaWaveNumber

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_ne_zero
entries.docstring: An energy eigenstate is not zero.
entries.snippet: lemma energyEigenstate_ne_zero (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) : T.energyEigenstate k ≠ 0

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_inner_self
entries.docstring: The inner product of an energy eigenstate with itself is `N`.
entries.snippet:
lemma energyEigenstate_inner_self (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) :
    ⟪T.energyEigenstate k, T.energyEigenstate k⟫_ℂ = T.N

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_linearIndependent
entries.docstring: The energy eigenstates are linearly independent.
entries.snippet:
lemma energyEigenstate_linearIndependent :
    LinearIndependent ℂ (fun n : Fin T.N => T.energyEigenstate (T.quantaWaveNumber n))

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_span
entries.docstring: The energy eigenstates span the Hilbert space.
entries.snippet:
lemma energyEigenstate_span :
    ⊤ ≤ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun n : Fin T.N =>
      T.energyEigenstate (T.quantaWaveNumber n))

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_orthonormal
entries.docstring: The normalized energy eigenstates `N ^ (-1/2) • energyEigenstate k` are orthonormal.
entries.snippet:
lemma energyEigenstate_orthonormal :
    Orthonormal ℂ (fun n : Fin T.N =>
      (((Real.sqrt T.N)⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • T.energyEigenstate (T.quantaWaveNumber n))

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenbasis
entries.docstring: The normalized energy eigenstates form an orthonormal basis of the Hilbert space.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def energyEigenbasis : OrthonormalBasis (Fin T.N) ℂ T.HilbertSpace

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenbasis_apply
entries.docstring:
The `n`-th vector of the basis is the normalized energy eigenstate of the `n`-th
wavenumber.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma energyEigenbasis_apply (n : Fin T.N) :
    T.energyEigenbasis n =
      (((Real.sqrt T.N)⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • T.energyEigenstate (T.quantaWaveNumber n)

entries.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.hasEigenvalue_hamiltonian_iff
entries.docstring:
The eigenvalues of the Hamiltonian are exactly the energies `E0 - 2 t cos (k a)` of the
quantized wavenumbers.
entries.snippet:
lemma hasEigenvalue_hamiltonian_iff (E : ℂ) :
    Module.End.HasEigenvalue T.hamiltonian E ↔
      ∃ k : T.QuantaWaveNumber, E = T.energyEigenvalue k

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.age
entries.docstring:
The age of the universe `t₀ = H₀⁻¹ ∫₀¹ dx / (x E(x))` for a reduced Hubble function `E`:
  the time elapsed since `a = 0`, obtained by integrating `dt = da / (a H)` with
  `H = H₀ E(a / a₀)` (interval integral; no convergence is asserted here).
entries.snippet: noncomputable def age (H₀ : ℝ) (E : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.age_eq
entries.docstring: The age is proportional to `1 / H₀`.
entries.snippet: lemma age_eq (H₀ : ℝ) (E : ℝ → ℝ) : age H₀ E = (1 / H₀) * age 1 E

entries.name: Cosmology.SpatialGeometry.curvature
entries.docstring:
The curvature parameter of the spatial geometry, the constant `k` of the first-order
  Friedmann equation `FLRW.FriedmannEquation.FirstOrderFriedmann`:
- `1 / k ^ 2` for `Spherical k`, whose profile `S` is that of a sphere of radius `|k|`,
- `0` for `Flat`,
- `-1 / k ^ 2` for `Saddle k`, whose profile `S` is that of a hyperbolic space of curvature
  radius `|k|`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def curvature : SpatialGeometry → ℝ
  | Spherical k _ => 1 / k ^ 2
  | Flat => 0
  | Saddle k _ => -1 / k ^ 2

entries.name: Cosmology.SpatialGeometry.curvature_flat
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma curvature_flat : Flat.curvature = 0

entries.name: Cosmology.SpatialGeometry.curvature_spherical_pos
entries.docstring: The spherical geometry has a positive curvature parameter.
entries.snippet: lemma curvature_spherical_pos (k : ℝ) (h : k < 0) : 0 < (Spherical k h).curvature

entries.name: Cosmology.SpatialGeometry.curvature_saddle_neg
entries.docstring: The saddle geometry has a negative curvature parameter.
entries.snippet: lemma curvature_saddle_neg (k : ℝ) (h : k > 0) : (Saddle k h).curvature < 0

entries.name: Cosmology.CosmicFluid
entries.docstring:
The cosmic fluid filling an FLRW model, described by its total energy density `ρ` and its
  pressure `p`, both functions of cosmic time, as in the first- and second-order Friedmann
  equations `FLRW.FriedmannEquation.FirstOrderFriedmann` and
  `FLRW.FriedmannEquation.SecondOrderFriedmann`.
entries.snippet:
structure CosmicFluid where
  ρ : Time → ℝ
  p : Time → ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.CosmicFluid.empty
entries.docstring: The empty cosmic fluid, with zero energy density and zero pressure at all times.
entries.snippet: def CosmicFluid.empty : CosmicFluid

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.cosmologicalConstantDensity
entries.docstring: The density `ρ_Λ = Λ c² / (8 π G)` associated with the cosmological constant.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def FLRW.FriedmannEquation.cosmologicalConstantDensity (Λ G c : ℝ) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.cosmologicalConstantPressure
entries.docstring: The pressure `p_Λ = - ρ_Λ c²` associated with the cosmological constant.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def FLRW.FriedmannEquation.cosmologicalConstantPressure (Λ G c : ℝ) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.CosmicFluid.addCosmologicalConstant
entries.docstring: The cosmic fluid `F` with the cosmological constant folded in as a fluid.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def CosmicFluid.addCosmologicalConstant (F : CosmicFluid) (Λ G c : ℝ) :
    CosmicFluid

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.a_ne_zero
entries.snippet: lemma a_ne_zero {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) : U.a t ≠ 0

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.differentiableAt_a
entries.snippet: lemma differentiableAt_a {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) : DifferentiableAt ℝ U.a t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.differentiableAt_deriv_a
entries.snippet: lemma differentiableAt_deriv_a {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) : DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂ₜ U.a) t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.mk_mem_I_of_mem_Icc
entries.docstring: The times between two times of the interval `U.I` of an FLRW model are in `U.I`.
entries.snippet:
lemma mk_mem_I_of_mem_Icc (U : FLRW) {σ τ x : ℝ} (hσ : (⟨σ⟩ : Time) ∈ U.I)
    (hτ : (⟨τ⟩ : Time) ∈ U.I) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc σ τ) : (⟨x⟩ : Time) ∈ U.I

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.continuousOn_deriv_scaleFactor_mk
entries.docstring:
Along the time coordinate, the derivative of the scale factor is continuous on any segment
  of the interval `U.I`.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuousOn_deriv_scaleFactor_mk (U : FLRW) {σ τ : ℝ} (hσ : (⟨σ⟩ : Time) ∈ U.I)
    (hτ : (⟨τ⟩ : Time) ∈ U.I) : ContinuousOn (fun x : ℝ => ∂ₜ U.a ⟨x⟩) (Set.Icc σ τ)

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.scaleFactor_le_tangent
entries.docstring:
If the scale factor decelerates on the interval (`∂ₜ ∂ₜ a ≤ 0` on `U.I`), it lies below its
  tangent line at any time `t₀` of `U.I`: `a t ≤ a t₀ + ∂ₜ a t₀ (t - t₀)` for `t ∈ U.I`. The
  derivative is antitone on the segment between `t` and `t₀`, which lies in `U.I`, and the mean
  value inequality concludes.
entries.snippet:
lemma scaleFactor_le_tangent (U : FLRW) (hdec : ∀ s ∈ U.I, ∂ₜ (∂ₜ U.a) s ≤ 0) {t₀ t : Time}
    (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (ht : t ∈ U.I) : U.a t ≤ U.a t₀ + ∂ₜ U.a t₀ * (t.val - t₀.val)

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.lt_of_mem_I_of_decelerating
entries.docstring:
The Big-Bang bound for an FLRW model: if the scale factor decelerates on `U.I` and the model
  expands at `t₀ ∈ U.I`, every time of `U.I` is later than `t₀ - a t₀ / ∂ₜ a t₀`. Earlier, the
  tangent line, and hence the scale factor, would be non-positive.
entries.snippet:
lemma lt_of_mem_I_of_decelerating (U : FLRW) (hdec : ∀ s ∈ U.I, ∂ₜ (∂ₜ U.a) s ≤ 0)
    {t₀ : Time} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (h0 : 0 < ∂ₜ U.a t₀) {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    t₀.val - U.a t₀ / ∂ₜ U.a t₀ < t.val

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.bddBelow_I_of_decelerating
entries.docstring:
Hence the interval of an FLRW model that decelerates on `U.I` and expands at one of its
  times is bounded below.
entries.snippet:
lemma bddBelow_I_of_decelerating (U : FLRW) (hdec : ∀ s ∈ U.I, ∂ₜ (∂ₜ U.a) s ≤ 0) {t₀ : Time}
    (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (h0 : 0 < ∂ₜ U.a t₀) : BddBelow U.I

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution
entries.docstring:
The proposition that the FLRW model `U` filled with the cosmic fluid `F` solves the
  Friedmann equations: the first- and second-order Friedmann equations, with cosmological
  constant `Λ`, Newton's constant `G` and speed of light `c`, hold at every time of the interval
  `U.I`, the curvature parameter being the one of the spatial geometry. The continuity equation
  of the fluid is not part of it: it follows from the two Friedmann equations
  (`FLRW.FriedmannSolution.continuityEquation` in `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.MatterContent`).
entries.snippet:
structure FriedmannSolution (U : FLRW) (F : CosmicFluid) (Λ G c : ℝ) : Prop where
  firstOrder : ∀ t ∈ U.I, FirstOrderFriedmann U.a F.ρ U.geometry.curvature Λ G c t
  secondOrder : ∀ t ∈ U.I, SecondOrderFriedmann U.a F.ρ F.p Λ G c t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.criticalDensity
entries.docstring:
The critical density `ρ_cr = 3 H² / (8 π G)` of an FLRW model at time `t`, where `H` is the
  Hubble parameter of its scale factor. It is the density of a spatially flat universe without
  cosmological constant expanding at the rate `H`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def criticalDensity (G : ℝ) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.densityParameter
entries.docstring: The density parameter `Ω = ρ / ρ_cr` of a cosmic fluid in an FLRW model.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def densityParameter (F : CosmicFluid) (G : ℝ) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.curvatureDensityParameter
entries.docstring:
The curvature density parameter `Ω_K = - k c² / (H² a²)` of an FLRW model, where `k` is the
  curvature parameter of its spatial geometry. When `H`, `a` and `c` are nonzero, it is positive
  for a saddle geometry, negative for a spherical one and zero for the flat one.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def curvatureDensityParameter (c : ℝ) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.lambdaDensityParameter
entries.docstring:
The density parameter `Ω_Λ = Λ c² / (3 H²)` of the cosmological constant in an FLRW
  model.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def lambdaDensityParameter (Λ c : ℝ) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.lambdaDensityParameter_eq_densityParameter
entries.docstring:
For `G ≠ 0`, `Ω_Λ` is the density parameter of the empty fluid with the cosmological constant
  folded in.
entries.snippet:
lemma lambdaDensityParameter_eq_densityParameter {Λ G c : ℝ} (hG : G ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    U.lambdaDensityParameter Λ c t
      = U.densityParameter (CosmicFluid.empty.addCosmologicalConstant Λ G c) G t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.densityParameter_addCosmologicalConstant
entries.docstring:
For `G ≠ 0`, folding the cosmological constant into a cosmic fluid adds `Ω_Λ` to its
  density parameter.
entries.snippet:
lemma densityParameter_addCosmologicalConstant (F : CosmicFluid) {Λ G c : ℝ} (hG : G ≠ 0)
    (t : Time) :
    U.densityParameter (F.addCosmologicalConstant Λ G c) G t
      = U.densityParameter F G t + U.lambdaDensityParameter Λ c t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.densityParameter_add_lambda_add_curvature
entries.docstring:
The closure relation `Ω + Ω_Λ + Ω_K = 1` for a solution of the Friedmann equations, at the
  times of the interval of the model at which `H ≠ 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma densityParameter_add_lambda_add_curvature (h : U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c) {t : Time}
    (ht : t ∈ U.I) (hH : hubbleConstant U.a t ≠ 0) :
    U.densityParameter F G t + U.lambdaDensityParameter Λ c t
      + U.curvatureDensityParameter c t = 1

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.densityParameter_add_curvature
entries.docstring:
The closure relation `Ω + Ω_K = 1` for a solution of the Friedmann equations without
  cosmological constant, at the times of the interval of the model at which `H ≠ 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma densityParameter_add_curvature (h : U.FriedmannSolution F 0 G c) {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I)
    (hH : hubbleConstant U.a t ≠ 0) :
    U.densityParameter F G t + U.curvatureDensityParameter c t = 1

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deSitter
entries.docstring:
The de Sitter model, defined at all times: the FLRW model with the scale factor
  `deSitterScaleFactor a₀ σ Λ c`, `a₀ > 0`, and the flat spatial geometry.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def _root_.Cosmology.FLRW.deSitter (a₀ σ Λ c : ℝ) (ha₀ : 0 < a₀) : FLRW where

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.friedmannSolution_deSitter
entries.docstring:
The de Sitter model filled with the empty cosmic fluid solves the Friedmann equations with
  cosmological constant `Λ > 0`, for `σ = ±1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.Cosmology.FLRW.friedmannSolution_deSitter {a₀ σ Λ : ℝ} (G c : ℝ) (hΛ : 0 < Λ)
    (ha₀ : 0 < a₀) (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) :
    (FLRW.deSitter a₀ σ Λ c ha₀).FriedmannSolution CosmicFluid.empty Λ G c

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.not_bddBelow_deSitter_I
entries.docstring:
The de Sitter model, which solves the Friedmann equations with `0 < Λ`
  (`FLRW.friedmannSolution_deSitter`), is defined at all times: its interval is not bounded
  below.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.Cosmology.FLRW.not_bddBelow_deSitter_I (a₀ σ Λ c : ℝ) (ha₀ : 0 < a₀) :
    ¬ BddBelow (FLRW.deSitter a₀ σ Λ c ha₀).I

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.comovingDistance
entries.docstring:
The line-of-sight comoving distance `χ = c ∫_t^{t₀} dτ / a(τ)` of a source emitting at `t`
  and observed at `t₀`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def comovingDistance (c : ℝ) (t t₀ : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_comovingDistance
entries.docstring: For `t` and `t₀` in the interval of the model, `∂ₜ χ = - c / a`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_comovingDistance {c : ℝ} {t₀ t : Time} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => U.comovingDistance c s t₀) t = -c / U.a t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.redshift
entries.docstring:
The redshift `z` of a source emitting at `t` and observed at `t₀`, with
  `1 + z = a(t₀) / a(t)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def redshift (t₀ t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.one_add_redshift
entries.snippet: lemma one_add_redshift (t₀ t : Time) : 1 + U.redshift t₀ t = U.a t₀ / U.a t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_redshift
entries.docstring: For `t` in the interval of the model, `∂ₜ z = -(1 + z) H`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_redshift {t₀ t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    ∂ₜ (U.redshift t₀) t = -(1 + U.redshift t₀ t) * hubbleConstant U.a t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_scaleFactor_eq_mul_hubbleConstant
entries.docstring: For `t` in the interval of the model, `∂ₜ a = a H`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_scaleFactor_eq_mul_hubbleConstant {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    ∂ₜ U.a t = U.a t * hubbleConstant U.a t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_comovingDistance_eq_mul_deriv_redshift
entries.docstring:
For `t` and `t₀` in the interval of the model with `H(t) ≠ 0`,
  `∂ₜ χ = (c / (a(t₀) H)) ∂ₜ z`. For `a(t₀) = 1`, this is the change of variables
  `dχ = c dz / H`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_comovingDistance_eq_mul_deriv_redshift {c : ℝ} {t₀ t : Time} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I)
    (ht : t ∈ U.I) (hH : hubbleConstant U.a t ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => U.comovingDistance c s t₀) t
      = c / (U.a t₀ * hubbleConstant U.a t) * ∂ₜ (U.redshift t₀) t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.properDistance
entries.docstring: The proper distance `D = a χ` at fixed comoving distance `χ`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def properDistance (χ : ℝ) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_properDistance
entries.docstring: The Hubble-Lemaître law `∂ₜ D = H D`, for `t` in the interval of the model.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_properDistance {χ : ℝ} {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    ∂ₜ (U.properDistance χ) t = hubbleConstant U.a t * U.properDistance χ t

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.hubbleRadius
entries.docstring: The Hubble radius `R_H = c / H`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def hubbleRadius (c : ℝ) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_properDistance_eq_iff
entries.docstring:
For `t` in the interval of the model with `H(t) ≠ 0`, the recession velocity `∂ₜ D` equals
