entries.name: HasGradientAt.add
entries.docstring: The gradient of a sum is the sum of the gradients.
entries.snippet:
lemma HasGradientAt.add (hf : HasGradientAt f f' x) (hg : HasGradientAt g g' x) :
    HasGradientAt (fun y => f y + g y) (f' + g') x

entries.name: HasGradientAt.sub
entries.docstring: The gradient of a difference is the difference of the gradients.
entries.snippet:
lemma HasGradientAt.sub (hf : HasGradientAt f f' x) (hg : HasGradientAt g g' x) :
    HasGradientAt (fun y => f y - g y) (f' - g') x

entries.name: HasGradientAt.mul
entries.docstring: The gradient of a product is given by the Leibniz rule.
entries.snippet:
lemma HasGradientAt.mul (hf : HasGradientAt f f' x) (hg : HasGradientAt g g' x) :
    HasGradientAt (fun y => f y * g y) (f x • g' + g x • f') x

entries.name: HasGradientAt.const_mul
entries.docstring: The gradient of a constant multiple is the constant multiple of the gradient.
entries.snippet:
lemma HasGradientAt.const_mul (c : ℝ) (hf : HasGradientAt f f' x) :
    HasGradientAt (fun y => c * f y) (c • f') x

entries.name: gradient_add
entries.docstring: The gradient of a sum of differentiable functions is the sum of their gradients.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_add {f g : F → ℝ} {x : F} (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x)
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g x) :
    gradient (fun y => f y + g y) x = gradient f x + gradient g x

entries.name: HasDerivAt.comp_hasGradientAt
entries.docstring:
The gradient of `y ↦ φ (f y)` is `φ'` times the gradient of `f`, for `φ'` the derivative of
`φ` at `f x`.
entries.snippet:
lemma HasDerivAt.comp_hasGradientAt {φ : ℝ → ℝ} {φ' : ℝ} (hf : HasGradientAt f f' x)
    (hφ : HasDerivAt φ φ' (f x)) : HasGradientAt (fun y => φ (f y)) (φ' • f') x

entries.name: hasGradientAt_inner_left
entries.docstring: The gradient of `y ↦ ⟪a, y⟫` is `a`.
entries.snippet: lemma hasGradientAt_inner_left (a x : F) : HasGradientAt (fun y : F => ⟪a, y⟫_ℝ) a x

entries.name: hasGradientAt_inner_right
entries.docstring: The gradient of `y ↦ ⟪y, a⟫` is `a`.
entries.snippet: lemma hasGradientAt_inner_right (a x : F) : HasGradientAt (fun y : F => ⟪y, a⟫_ℝ) a x

entries.name: hasGradientAt_inner_self
entries.docstring: The gradient of `y ↦ ⟪y, y⟫` is `2 • y`.
entries.snippet: lemma hasGradientAt_inner_self (x : F) : HasGradientAt (fun y : F => ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ) ((2 : ℝ) • x) x

entries.name: hasGradientAt_norm
entries.docstring: Away from the origin, the gradient of the norm is the unit vector `‖x‖⁻¹ • x`.
entries.snippet: lemma hasGradientAt_norm (hx : x ≠ 0) : HasGradientAt (fun y : F => ‖y‖) (‖x‖⁻¹ • x) x

entries.name: hasGradientAt_coord
entries.docstring:
The gradient of the `i`-th coordinate functional on Euclidean space is the `i`-th basis
vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma hasGradientAt_coord {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (i : ι)
    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) :
    HasGradientAt (fun y : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι => y i) (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) x

entries.name: fderiv_apply_parametric_intervalIntegral
entries.snippet:
lemma fderiv_apply_parametric_intervalIntegral
    {F : M → ℝ → N} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 ↿F) (x₀ : M) (v : M) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun (x : M) => ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..1, F x t ∂(volume)) x₀ v =
      ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..1, fderiv ℝ (F · t) x₀ v ∂(volume)

entries.name: fderiv_parametric_intervalIntegral
entries.snippet:
lemma fderiv_parametric_intervalIntegral
    {F : M → ℝ → N} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 ↿F) (x₀ : M) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun (x : M) => ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..1, F x t ∂(volume)) =
      fun x => ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..1, fderiv ℝ (F · t) x ∂(volume)

entries.name: hasDerivAt_intervalIntegral_of_contDiff
entries.docstring: Differentiation under the integral sign for a `C¹` integrand.
entries.snippet:
lemma hasDerivAt_intervalIntegral_of_contDiff {F : ℝ × ℝ → N}
    (hF : ContDiff ℝ 1 F) (a b x₀ : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun x ↦ ∫ t in a..b, F (x, t))
      (∫ t in a..b, fderiv ℝ F (x₀, t) (1, 0)) x₀

entries.name: fderiv_partial_snd
entries.docstring: The derivative in the middle argument of `f` as a restriction of the total derivative.
entries.snippet:
lemma fderiv_partial_snd {f : X × Y × Z → F} {a : X} {y : Y} {z : Z}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f (a, y, z)) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun y' ↦ f (a, y', z)) y = (fderiv ℝ f (a, y, z)).comp
      ((0 : Y →L[ℝ] X).prod ((ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ Y).prod (0 : Y →L[ℝ] Z)))

entries.name: fderiv_partial_thd
entries.docstring: The derivative in the last argument of `f` as a restriction of the total derivative.
entries.snippet:
lemma fderiv_partial_thd {f : X × Y × Z → F} {a : X} {y : Y} {z : Z}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f (a, y, z)) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun z' ↦ f (a, y, z')) z = (fderiv ℝ f (a, y, z)).comp
      ((0 : Z →L[ℝ] X).prod ((0 : Z →L[ℝ] Y).prod (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ Z)))

entries.name: fderiv_apply_zero_prod
entries.docstring: The total derivative of `f` on `(0, u, w)` splits into its middle and last partials.
entries.snippet:
lemma fderiv_apply_zero_prod {f : X × Y × Z → F} {a : X} {y : Y} {z : Z}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f (a, y, z)) (u : Y) (w : Z) :
    fderiv ℝ f (a, y, z) (0, u, w) =
      fderiv ℝ (fun y' ↦ f (a, y', z)) y u + fderiv ℝ (fun z' ↦ f (a, y, z')) z w

entries.name: deriv_fderiv_apply_comm
entries.docstring: Mixed partial derivatives of a two-parameter family, `C²` at the point, commute.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_fderiv_apply_comm {s τ : ℝ} (hH : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 H (s, τ)) :
    deriv (fun σ ↦ fderiv ℝ H (s, σ) (1, 0)) τ =
      fderiv ℝ (fun p ↦ fderiv ℝ H p (0, 1)) (s, τ) (1, 0)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.clinear_of_dWirtingerAntiDir_eq_zero
entries.docstring: The converse of `dWirtingerAntiDir_eq_zero_of_clinear`. It needs no differentiability.
entries.snippet:
lemma clinear_of_dWirtingerAntiDir_eq_zero {v : V} (h : dWirtingerAntiDir f v u = 0) :
    fderiv ℝ f u (Complex.I • v) = Complex.I • fderiv ℝ f u v

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.differentiableAt_complex_iff_dWirtingerAntiDir_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
**Cauchy–Riemann.** `f` is `ℂ`-differentiable at `u` iff it is real-differentiable there and
every anti-holomorphic Wirtinger derivative vanishes. Real differentiability is needed: `fderiv`
is `0` where `f` is not differentiable.
entries.snippet:
theorem differentiableAt_complex_iff_dWirtingerAntiDir_eq_zero (f : V → ℂ) (u : V) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ f u ↔
      DifferentiableAt ℝ f u ∧ ∀ v, dWirtingerAntiDir f v u = 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.differentiableAt_complex_iff_dWirtingerAntiCoord_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
**Cauchy–Riemann in coordinates**, the form `∂̄_Ī W = 0` used in physics. Coordinate
directions suffice by `LinearMap.commutesI_of_basis`.
entries.snippet:
theorem differentiableAt_complex_iff_dWirtingerAntiCoord_eq_zero
    (f : (ι → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : ι → ℂ) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ f u ↔
      DifferentiableAt ℝ f u ∧ ∀ I, dWirtingerAntiCoord f I u = 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_zero
entries.docstring:
If the inner continuous ℝ-linear map `P` kills the coordinate column `c`, the holomorphic
coordinate Wirtinger derivative of `h ∘ P` along `c` vanishes.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_zero {C_s : Type} [Fintype C_s]
    (P : (D → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (C_s → ℂ)) (h : (C_s → ℂ) → ℂ) (c : D) (u : D → ℂ)
    (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h (P u))
    (h1 : P (Pi.single c 1) = 0) (hI : P (Pi.single c Complex.I) = 0) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v => h (P v)) c u = 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_col
entries.docstring:
If the inner continuous ℝ-linear map `P` reads the coordinate column `c` as the sector
coordinate `a₀`, the holomorphic coordinate Wirtinger derivative of `h ∘ P` along `c` is that
of `h` along `a₀`, evaluated at `P u`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_col {C_s : Type} [Fintype C_s] [DecidableEq C_s]
    (P : (D → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (C_s → ℂ)) (h : (C_s → ℂ) → ℂ) (c : D) (a₀ : C_s)
    (u : D → ℂ) (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h (P u))
    (h1 : P (Pi.single c 1) = Pi.single a₀ 1)
    (hI : P (Pi.single c Complex.I) = Pi.single a₀ Complex.I) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v => h (P v)) c u = dWirtingerCoord h a₀ (P u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_clm_zero
entries.docstring: Anti-holomorphic mirror of `dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_zero`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_clm_zero {C_s : Type} [Fintype C_s]
    (P : (D → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (C_s → ℂ)) (h : (C_s → ℂ) → ℂ) (c : D) (u : D → ℂ)
    (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h (P u))
    (h1 : P (Pi.single c 1) = 0) (hI : P (Pi.single c Complex.I) = 0) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => h (P v)) c u = 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_clm_col
entries.docstring: Anti-holomorphic mirror of `dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_col`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_clm_col {C_s : Type} [Fintype C_s] [DecidableEq C_s]
    (P : (D → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (C_s → ℂ)) (h : (C_s → ℂ) → ℂ) (c : D) (a₀ : C_s)
    (u : D → ℂ) (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h (P u))
    (h1 : P (Pi.single c 1) = Pi.single a₀ 1)
    (hI : P (Pi.single c Complex.I) = Pi.single a₀ Complex.I) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => h (P v)) c u = dWirtingerAntiCoord h a₀ (P u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf
entries.docstring: The mixed Wirtinger Hessian of `f` at `u`: the matrix with `(I, J)` entry `∂_I ∂̄_J f`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def hessianMatrixOf (f : (ι → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : ι → ℂ) : Matrix ι ι ℂ

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOfR
entries.docstring:
The mixed Wirtinger Hessian of a real-valued `K`, through `Complex.ofReal`. An `abbrev`, so
lemmas about `hessianMatrixOf` apply to it.
entries.snippet: noncomputable abbrev hessianMatrixOfR (K : (ι → ℂ) → ℝ) (u : ι → ℂ) : Matrix ι ι ℂ

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOfR_isHermitian
entries.docstring:
The mixed Wirtinger Hessian of a real function `C²` at `u` is Hermitian,
`(g_{JĪ})^* = g_{IJ̄}`.
entries.snippet:
lemma hessianMatrixOfR_isHermitian {K : (ι → ℂ) → ℝ} {u : ι → ℂ} (hK : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 K u) :
    Matrix.IsHermitian (hessianMatrixOfR K u)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrict
entries.docstring: The restriction `q ↦ q ∘ Sigma.mk k` to sector `k`, as a continuous ℝ-linear map.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def restrict (k : K) : ((Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (ι k → ℂ)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrict_single_same
entries.docstring: `restrict k` sends the basis vector of field `⟨k, a'⟩` to the basis vector of field `a'`.
entries.snippet:
lemma restrict_single_same (k : K) (a' : ι k) (z : ℂ) :
    restrict k (Pi.single (⟨k, a'⟩ : Σ k, ι k) z) = Pi.single a' z

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrict_single_ne
entries.docstring: `restrict k` sends the basis vector of a field of another sector to zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma restrict_single_ne {k k' : K} (h : k ≠ k') (a' : ι k') (z : ℂ) :
    restrict k (Pi.single (⟨k', a'⟩ : Σ k, ι k) z) = 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_block_own
entries.docstring: `∂_⟨k, a⟩` of a function of sector `k` alone is its `∂_a`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_block_own {k : K} (g : (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (a : ι k)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun q => g (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) (⟨k, a⟩ : Σ k, ι k) u
      = dWirtingerCoord g a (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_block_ne
entries.docstring: `∂_⟨k, a⟩` of a function of another sector vanishes.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_block_ne {k k' : K} (h : k ≠ k') (g : (ι k' → ℂ) → ℂ) (a : ι k)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (u ∘ Sigma.mk k')) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun q => g (q ∘ Sigma.mk k')) (⟨k, a⟩ : Σ k, ι k) u = 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_own
entries.docstring: Anti-holomorphic mirror of `dWirtingerCoord_block_own`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_own {k : K} (g : (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (a : ι k)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun q => g (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) (⟨k, a⟩ : Σ k, ι k) u
      = dWirtingerAntiCoord g a (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_ne
entries.docstring: Anti-holomorphic mirror of `dWirtingerCoord_block_ne`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_ne {k k' : K} (h : k ≠ k') (g : (ι k' → ℂ) → ℂ) (a : ι k)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (u ∘ Sigma.mk k')) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun q => g (q ∘ Sigma.mk k')) (⟨k, a⟩ : Σ k, ι k) u = 0

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_block_sum
entries.docstring: `∂_⟨k₀, a⟩` of a sum of sector functions is the `∂_a` of the sector-`k₀` function.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_block_sum (f : ∀ k, (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (k₀ : K) (a : ι k₀)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hf : ∀ k, DifferentiableAt ℝ (f k) (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun q => ∑ k, f k (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) ⟨k₀, a⟩ u
      = dWirtingerCoord (f k₀) a (u ∘ Sigma.mk k₀)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_sum
entries.docstring: `∂̄_⟨k₀, a⟩` of a sum of sector functions is the `∂̄_a` of the sector-`k₀` function.
entries.snippet:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_sum (f : ∀ k, (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (k₀ : K) (a : ι k₀)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hf : ∀ k, DifferentiableAt ℝ (f k) (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun q => ∑ k, f k (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) ⟨k₀, a⟩ u
      = dWirtingerAntiCoord (f k₀) a (u ∘ Sigma.mk k₀)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf_sum_eq_blockDiagonal'
entries.docstring:
The Hessian of a sum of sector functions is the block-diagonal matrix of the sector
Hessians.
entries.snippet:
lemma hessianMatrixOf_sum_eq_blockDiagonal' (f : ∀ k, (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ)
    (hf : ∀ k, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (f k) (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    hessianMatrixOf (fun q => ∑ k, f k (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) u
      = blockDiagonal' (fun k => hessianMatrixOf (f k) (u ∘ Sigma.mk k))

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.precompEquiv
entries.docstring: The relabelling `q ↦ q ∘ ε.symm` along `ε`, as a continuous ℝ-linear map.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def precompEquiv (ε : ι ≃ ι') : (ι → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (ι' → ℂ)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.precompEquiv_single
entries.docstring: `precompEquiv ε` sends the basis vector of field `c` to the basis vector of field `ε c`.
entries.snippet:
lemma precompEquiv_single (ε : ι ≃ ι') (c : ι) (z : ℂ) :
    precompEquiv ε (Pi.single c z) = Pi.single (ε c) z

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf_comp_equiv
entries.docstring: Relabelling the coordinates by `ε` reindexes the Hessian by `ε`.
entries.snippet:
lemma hessianMatrixOf_comp_equiv (ε : ι ≃ ι') (H : (ι' → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : ι → ℂ)
    (hH : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 H (u ∘ ε.symm)) :
    hessianMatrixOf (fun q => H (q ∘ ε.symm)) u
      = (hessianMatrixOf H (u ∘ ε.symm)).submatrix ε ε

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrictInl
entries.docstring: The restriction `q ↦ q ∘ Sum.inl` to the first sector, as a continuous ℝ-linear map.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def restrictInl : (ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (ι₁ → ℂ)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrictInr
entries.docstring: The restriction `q ↦ q ∘ Sum.inr` to the second sector, as a continuous ℝ-linear map.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def restrictInr : (ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (ι₂ → ℂ)

entries.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf_add_eq_fromBlocks
entries.docstring:
The Hessian of `f₁ (q ∘ Sum.inl) + f₂ (q ∘ Sum.inr)` is `fromBlocks` of the two sector
Hessians.
entries.snippet:
lemma hessianMatrixOf_add_eq_fromBlocks
    (f₁ : (ι₁ → ℂ) → ℂ) (f₂ : (ι₂ → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → ℂ)
    (hf₁ : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f₁ (u ∘ Sum.inl)) (hf₂ : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f₂ (u ∘ Sum.inr)) :
    hessianMatrixOf (fun q => f₁ (q ∘ Sum.inl) + f₂ (q ∘ Sum.inr)) u
      = Matrix.fromBlocks (hessianMatrixOf f₁ (u ∘ Sum.inl)) 0 0
          (hessianMatrixOf f₂ (u ∘ Sum.inr))

entries.name: Physlib.Distribution.integrable_eval_of_bound
entries.docstring: Evaluations of a distribution family with an integrable seminorm bound are integrable.
entries.snippet: lemma integrable_eval_of_bound (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) : Integrable (fun a => u a η) μ

entries.name: Physlib.Distribution.integralOfBound
entries.docstring:
The weak integral of a family of distributions with an integrable Schwartz seminorm bound.
It acts on a test function by integrating the evaluations of the family.
entries.snippet: def integralOfBound : E →d[𝕜] F

entries.name: Physlib.Distribution.integralOfBound_apply
entries.docstring: Evaluation of the weak integral is the integral of the evaluations.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma integralOfBound_apply (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) :
    integralOfBound u s b hb hmeas hbound hb_nonneg η = ∫ a, u a η ∂μ

entries.name: Physlib.Distribution.integrable_fderivD_eval_of_bound
entries.docstring: Differentiated evaluations of a family with an integrable seminorm bound are integrable.
entries.snippet:
lemma integrable_fderivD_eval_of_bound (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) (v : E) :
    Integrable (fun a => fderivD 𝕜 (u a) η v) μ

entries.name: Physlib.Distribution.fderivD_integralOfBound_apply
entries.docstring:
Distributional differentiation commutes with the weak integral after evaluation at a test
function and a direction.
entries.snippet:
lemma fderivD_integralOfBound_apply (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) (v : E) :
    fderivD 𝕜 (integralOfBound u s b hb hmeas hbound hb_nonneg) η v =
      ∫ a, fderivD 𝕜 (u a) η v ∂μ

entries.name: LinearMap.map_smul_of_commutesI
entries.docstring: An `ℝ`-linear map commuting with `i` along `v` commutes with every complex scalar along `v`.

entries.name: LinearMap.commutesI_of_basis
entries.docstring: An `ℝ`-linear map commuting with `i` on a `ℂ`-basis commutes with `i` everywhere.
entries.snippet:
lemma commutesI_of_basis {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (L : V →ₗ[ℝ] E) (b : Module.Basis ι ℂ V)
    (h : ∀ i, L (Complex.I • b i) = Complex.I • L (b i)) (v : V) :
    L (Complex.I • v) = Complex.I • L v

entries.name: ContinuousLinearMap.complexOfCommutesI
entries.docstring: A continuous `ℝ`-linear map commuting with `i`, as a continuous `ℂ`-linear map.
entries.snippet:
def complexOfCommutesI (L : V →L[ℝ] E)
    (h : ∀ v, L (Complex.I • v) = Complex.I • L v) : V →L[ℂ] E where

entries.name: ContinuousLinearMap.complexOfCommutesI_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma complexOfCommutesI_apply (L : V →L[ℝ] E)
    (h : ∀ v, L (Complex.I • v) = Complex.I • L v) (v : V) :
    complexOfCommutesI L h v = L v

entries.name: Integration.integral_withDensity_ofReal_eq_integral_smul
entries.docstring:
Integrating `g` against the measure with real-valued density `f` (taken through
`ENNReal.ofReal`) is integrating `f x • g x` against the original measure, for measurable
`f` that is everywhere nonnegative. This is the `ℝ`-valued form of
`integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul`, which takes an `NNReal`-valued density.
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_withDensity_ofReal_eq_integral_smul {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
    {μ : Measure α} {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) (hf0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (g : α → E) :
    ∫ x, g x ∂(μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (f x)) = ∫ x, f x • g x ∂μ

entries.name: LinearMap.IsPosDef
entries.docstring:
A sesquilinear form `B` is **positive-definite** if it is symmetric and `0 < B x x` for every
nonzero `x`.
entries.snippet:
structure IsPosDef [LT R] (B : M →ₛₗ[I₁] M →ₗ[R] R) : Prop extends isSymm : B.IsSymm where
  pos : ∀ x, x ≠ 0 → 0 < B x x

entries.name: LinearMap.isPosDef_def
entries.snippet:
lemma isPosDef_def [LT R] {B : M →ₛₗ[I₁] M →ₗ[R] R} :
    B.IsPosDef ↔ B.IsSymm ∧ ∀ x, x ≠ 0 → 0 < B x x

entries.name: LinearMap.IsPosDef.isPosSemidef
entries.docstring: A positive-definite form is positive-semidefinite.
entries.snippet: lemma IsPosDef.isPosSemidef (hB : B.IsPosDef) : B.IsPosSemidef where

entries.name: LinearMap.IsPosDef.nondegenerate
entries.docstring: A positive-definite form is nondegenerate: a nonzero `x` is not orthogonal to itself.
entries.snippet: lemma IsPosDef.nondegenerate (hB : B.IsPosDef) : B.Nondegenerate

entries.name: LinearMap.isPosDef_iff_posDef_toMatrix
entries.docstring: A sesquilinear form is positive-definite exactly when its matrix in a basis is.
entries.snippet: lemma isPosDef_iff_posDef_toMatrix (b : Basis n R M) : B.IsPosDef ↔ (toMatrix₂ b b B).PosDef

entries.name: hasDerivAt_tanh
entries.docstring: The derivative of tanh at `x` is `1 - tanh(x)^2`
entries.snippet: lemma hasDerivAt_tanh (x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt Real.tanh (1 - Real.tanh x ^ 2) x

entries.name: tendsto_tanh_atTop
entries.docstring: tanh(x) tends to `1` as `x → ∞`
entries.snippet: lemma tendsto_tanh_atTop : Filter.Tendsto Real.tanh Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

entries.name: tendsto_tanh_atBot
entries.docstring: tanh(x) tends to `-1` as `x → -∞`
entries.snippet: lemma tendsto_tanh_atBot : Filter.Tendsto Real.tanh Filter.atBot (nhds (-1))

entries.name: GroupTheory.SO3.eq_of_apply_two
entries.docstring: A rotation fixing the third axis is a rotation in the first two coordinates.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_of_apply_two (A : SO(3)) (hA : ∀ i, A.1 i 2 = if i = 2 then 1 else 0) :
    A.1 = !![A.1 0 0, A.1 0 1, 0; -A.1 0 1, A.1 0 0, 0; 0, 0, 1]

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint
entries.docstring: The adjoint representation `x ↦ g x g†` of `SU(n)` on its real Lie algebra `su(n)`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def adjoint {n : ℕ} :
    Representation ℝ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (SULieAlgebra n ℂ)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_val
entries.docstring: The underlying matrix of `adjoint g x` is `g x g†`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma adjoint_val {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    (adjoint g x).1 = g.1 * x.1 * star g.1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_lie
entries.docstring:
The adjoint representation preserves the bracket, so `SU(n)` acts on `su(n)` by Lie algebra
  automorphisms.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjoint_lie {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjoint g ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅adjoint g x, adjoint g y⁆

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_eq_one_iff
entries.docstring:
The kernel of the adjoint representation is the centre of `SU(n)`: `g` acts trivially exactly
  when it is a scalar matrix `c 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjoint_eq_one_iff {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjoint g = 1 ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, g.1 = c • 1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_eq_iff
entries.docstring:
Two elements of `SU(n)` have the same adjoint action exactly when they differ by a scalar:
  the adjoint representation is faithful on `SU(n)` modulo its centre.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjoint_eq_iff {n : ℕ} (g h : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjoint g = adjoint h ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, g.1 = c • h.1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ
entries.docstring:
The adjoint representation of `SU(n)` on the complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)`: the
  complexification of the adjoint representation `adjoint` on `su(n)`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def adjointℂ {n : ℕ} :
    Representation ℂ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (Complexification n)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_tmul
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma adjointℂ_tmul {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (z : ℂ) (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointℂ g (z ⊗ₜ x) = z ⊗ₜ adjoint g x

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_lie
entries.docstring:
The complex adjoint representation preserves the bracket of the complexification, so `SU(n)`
  acts on `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)` by Lie algebra automorphisms.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂ_lie {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂ g ⁅A, B⁆ = ⁅adjointℂ g A, adjointℂ g B⁆

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_eq_one_iff
entries.docstring:
The kernel of the complex adjoint representation is the centre of `SU(n)`, as for the real
  adjoint representation.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂ_eq_one_iff {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjointℂ g = 1 ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, g.1 = c • 1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_eq_iff
entries.docstring:
Two elements of `SU(n)` have the same complex adjoint action exactly when they differ by a
  scalar, as for the real adjoint representation.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂ_eq_iff {n : ℕ} (g h : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjointℂ g = adjointℂ h ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, g.1 = c • h.1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ
entries.docstring: The adjoint representation conjugates the matrix, `M ↦ g M g†`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ {n} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (A : Complexification n) :
    toMatrixℂ (adjointℂ g A) = g.1 * toMatrixℂ A * star g.1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_eq_unitary
entries.docstring:
Conjugation by any unitary matrix is the adjoint action of an element of `SU(n)`: a
  unitary matrix agrees with an element of `SU(n)` up to a phase, which conjugation does not
  see.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_eq_unitary {n : ℕ} (U : unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ, ∀ A : Complexification n,
      toMatrixℂ (adjointℂ g A) = U.1 * toMatrixℂ A * star U.1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_apply_perm
entries.docstring:
The adjoint action realises any permutation `σ` of the coordinates: some element of `SU(n)`
  moves the entry `(x, y)` of every matrix to `(σ x, σ y)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_apply_perm {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ, ∀ A x y,
      toMatrixℂ (adjointℂ g A) (σ x) (σ y) = toMatrixℂ A x y

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_apply_of_diagonal
entries.docstring:
The adjoint action of a diagonal element of `SU(n)` scales the entry at `(x, y)` of the
  matrix by `d x * star (d y)`.

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_trace
entries.snippet:
lemma toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_trace {n} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (A : Complexification n) :
    (toMatrixℂ (adjointℂ g A)).trace = (toMatrixℂ A).trace

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_adjointℂ_singleℂ_eq_singleℂ
entries.docstring: All the off-diagonal matrix units `singleℂ` lie in one adjoint orbit
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_adjointℂ_singleℂ_eq_singleℂ {n : ℕ} {i j p q : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ, adjointℂ g (singleℂ i j hij) = singleℂ p q hpq

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.singleℂ_mem_span_range_adjointℂ
entries.docstring:
If the matrix of `A` has a non-zero entry at the off-diagonal position `(p, q)`, then
  `singleℂ p q h` lies in the span of the adjoint orbit of `A`.
entries.snippet:
lemma singleℂ_mem_span_range_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} {p q : Fin n} (h : p ≠ q)
    {A : Complexification n} (hA : toMatrixℂ A p q ≠ 0) :
    singleℂ p q h ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun g => adjointℂ g A)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_adjointℂ_eq_of_toMatrixℂ_eq_diagonal
entries.docstring:
The adjoint action of some element of `SU(n)` — the rotation by `π / 4` in the `(p, q)`-plane —
  changes an element whose matrix is the diagonal matrix `d` only in the `(p, q)`-block, by
  `(d p - d q) / 2` times `singleℂ p q h + singleℂ q p h.symm - diagDiffℂ p q`.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_adjointℂ_eq_of_toMatrixℂ_eq_diagonal {n : ℕ} {p q : Fin n} (h : p ≠ q)
    {A : Complexification n} {d : Fin n → ℂ} (hA : toMatrixℂ A = diagonal d) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ, adjointℂ g A =
      A + ((d p - d q) / 2) • (singleℂ p q h + singleℂ q p h.symm - diagDiffℂ p q)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_diagDiffℂ_eq_adjointℂ_singleℂ_add_singleℂ
entries.docstring:
The difference of two diagonal entries lies in the adjoint orbit of the sum of the two
  elements supported at the corresponding off-diagonal entries.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_diagDiffℂ_eq_adjointℂ_singleℂ_add_singleℂ {n : ℕ} {p q : Fin n} (h : p ≠ q) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ,
      diagDiffℂ p q = adjointℂ g (singleℂ p q h + singleℂ q p h.symm)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_singleℂ_mem_span_range_adjointℂ
entries.docstring:
The span of the adjoint orbit of a non-zero element contains an element supported at a single
  off-diagonal entry.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_singleℂ_mem_span_range_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} {A : Complexification n} (hA : A ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (p q : Fin n) (h : p ≠ q),
      singleℂ p q h ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun g => adjointℂ g A)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.isIrreducible_adjointℂ
entries.docstring: The complex adjoint representation of `SU(n)` is irreducible for `2 ≤ n`.
entries.snippet: lemma isIrreducible_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (adjointℂ (n := n)).IsIrreducible

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.end_eq_smul_id_of_commute_adjointℂ
entries.docstring: An endomorphism of the complexification commuting with the adjoint action is a scalar.
entries.snippet:
lemma end_eq_smul_id_of_commute_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} {T : Module.End ℂ (Complexification n)}
    (hT : ∀ g, T ∘ₗ adjointℂ g = adjointℂ g ∘ₗ T) : ∃ μ : ℂ, T = μ • LinearMap.id

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.submodule
entries.docstring: The traceless hermitian `n × n` matrices with entries in `R`, as a real subspace.
entries.snippet:
abbrev SULieAlgebra.submodule (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [StarRing R] [Algebra ℝ R]
    [StarModule ℝ R] : Submodule ℝ (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra
entries.docstring:
Traceless hermitian `n × n` matrices with entries in `R`, as a real Lie algebra;
  `SULieAlgebra n ℂ` is `su(n)`.
entries.snippet:
abbrev SULieAlgebra (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [StarRing R] [Algebra ℝ R]
    [StarModule ℝ R] : Type _

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.ofMatrix
entries.docstring: The element given by a traceless hermitian matrix.
entries.snippet:
def ofMatrix (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) (hA : star A = A) (hT : A.trace = 0) :
    SULieAlgebra n R

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.val_ofMatrix
entries.docstring: The underlying matrix of `ofMatrix A hA hT` is `A`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma val_ofMatrix (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) (hA : star A = A) (hT : A.trace = 0) :
    (ofMatrix A hA hT).1 = A

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.star_val_eq
entries.docstring: The underlying matrix of an element is hermitian.
entries.snippet: lemma star_val_eq (x : SULieAlgebra n R) : star x.1 = x.1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.trace_val_eq_zero
entries.docstring: The underlying matrix of an element is traceless.
entries.snippet: lemma trace_val_eq_zero (x : SULieAlgebra n R) : x.1.trace = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.conj
entries.docstring: The conjugation representation of the unitary group on `SULieAlgebra n R`: `x ↦ U x U†`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def conj : Representation ℝ (unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (SULieAlgebra n R) where

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.val_conj_apply
entries.docstring: The underlying matrix of `conj U x` is `U x U†`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma val_conj_apply (U : unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (x : SULieAlgebra n R) :
    (conj U x).1 = U.1 * x.1 * star U.1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.«instance@e0607ee2»
entries.docstring: The bracket `⁅x, y⁆ = i (x y - y x)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable instance : Bracket (SULieAlgebra n R) (SULieAlgebra n R) where

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.val_bracket
entries.docstring: The underlying matrix of `⁅x, y⁆` is `i (x y - y x)`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma val_bracket (x y : SULieAlgebra n R) :
    ⁅x, y⁆.1 = Complex.I • (x.1 * y.1 - y.1 * x.1)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.«instance@e1f2330c»
entries.docstring: `⁅x, y⁆ = i (x y - y x)` makes `SULieAlgebra n R` a Lie ring.
entries.snippet: noncomputable instance : LieRing (SULieAlgebra n R) where

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.«instance@1df0b349»
entries.docstring: The bracket is `ℝ`-bilinear, so `SULieAlgebra n R` is a real Lie algebra.
entries.snippet: noncomputable instance : LieAlgebra ℝ (SULieAlgebra n R) where

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.conj_lie
entries.docstring:
Conjugation by a unitary matrix preserves the bracket, so `conj` acts by Lie algebra
  automorphisms.
entries.snippet:
lemma conj_lie (U : unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (x y : SULieAlgebra n R) :
    conj U ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅conj U x, conj U y⁆

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.Complexification
entries.docstring: The complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)` of `su(n)`, a complex Lie algebra.
entries.snippet: abbrev Complexification (n : ℕ) : Type

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ
entries.docstring: The underlying matrix of an element of the complexification, `z ⊗ x ↦ z x`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def toMatrixℂ : Complexification n →ₗ[ℂ] Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_tmul
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toMatrixℂ_tmul (z : ℂ) (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) : toMatrixℂ (z ⊗ₜ x) = z • x.1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.trace_toMatrixℂ
entries.docstring: The underlying matrix of an element of the complexification is traceless.
entries.snippet: lemma trace_toMatrixℂ (A : Complexification n) : (toMatrixℂ A).trace = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_lie
entries.docstring:
The matrix of a bracket is `i` times the commutator of the matrices, `[A, B] ↦ i (A B - B A)`,
  as in `su(n)` itself.
entries.snippet:
lemma toMatrixℂ_lie (A B : Complexification n) :
    toMatrixℂ ⁅A, B⁆ = Complex.I • (toMatrixℂ A * toMatrixℂ B - toMatrixℂ B * toMatrixℂ A)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.ofTracelessℂ
entries.docstring: The element `1 ⊗ ℜ M + i ⊗ ℑ M` of the complexification with the traceless matrix `M`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def ofTracelessℂ (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hM : M.trace = 0) :
    Complexification n

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_ofTracelessℂ
entries.docstring: The matrix of `ofTracelessℂ M` is `M = ℜ M + i ℑ M`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toMatrixℂ_ofTracelessℂ (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hM : M.trace = 0) :
    toMatrixℂ (ofTracelessℂ M hM) = M

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.ofTracelessℂ_add
entries.docstring: `ofTracelessℂ` is additive.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofTracelessℂ_add (M N : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hM : M.trace = 0) (hN : N.trace = 0)
    (hMN : (M + N).trace = 0) :
    ofTracelessℂ (M + N) hMN = ofTracelessℂ M hM + ofTracelessℂ N hN

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.ofTracelessℂ_toMatrixℂ
entries.docstring: An element of the complexification is recovered from its matrix.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofTracelessℂ_toMatrixℂ (A : Complexification n) :
    ofTracelessℂ (toMatrixℂ A) (trace_toMatrixℂ A) = A

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_injective
entries.docstring: An element of the complexification is determined by its matrix.
entries.snippet: lemma toMatrixℂ_injective : Function.Injective (toMatrixℂ (n := n))

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.range_toMatrixℂ
entries.docstring: The matrices of elements of the complexification are exactly the traceless matrices.
entries.snippet:
lemma range_toMatrixℂ :
    LinearMap.range (toMatrixℂ (n := n)) = LinearMap.ker (Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin n) ℂ ℂ)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.commute_of_forall_commute_val
entries.docstring:
A matrix commuting with every element of `su(n)` commutes with every matrix: it commutes with
  the traceless matrices, which `su(n)` spans over `ℂ`, and with the identity.
entries.snippet:
lemma commute_of_forall_commute_val {M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ}
    (h : ∀ x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ, Commute M x.1) (N : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) : Commute M N

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.equivTraceKer
entries.docstring:
The linear equivalence between the complexification of `su(n)` and the traceless complex
  matrices, sending an element to its matrix.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def equivTraceKer :
    Complexification n ≃ₗ[ℂ] LinearMap.ker (Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin n) ℂ ℂ) where

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.val_equivTraceKer
entries.docstring: The matrix of `equivTraceKer A` is the matrix of `A`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma val_equivTraceKer (A : Complexification n) : (equivTraceKer A).1 = toMatrixℂ A

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_equivTraceKer_symm
entries.docstring: The matrix of `equivTraceKer.symm M` is `M`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toMatrixℂ_equivTraceKer_symm (M : LinearMap.ker (traceLinearMap (Fin n) ℂ ℂ)) :
    toMatrixℂ (equivTraceKer.symm M) = M.1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.singleℂ
entries.docstring: The element of the complexification supported at the single off-diagonal entry `(p, q)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def singleℂ (p q : Fin n) (h : p ≠ q) : Complexification n

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.diagDiffℂ
entries.docstring:
The element of the complexification corresponding to the difference of diagonal
  entries `(p, p) - (q, q)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def diagDiffℂ (p q : Fin n) : Complexification n

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.submodule_eq_top_of_singleℂ_mem_of_diagDiffℂ_mem
entries.docstring:
A submodule of the complexification containing every element supported at a single
  off-diagonal entry, and every difference of two diagonal entries, is everything.

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.singleℂ_diagDiffℂ_span_eq_top
entries.docstring:
The elements supported at a single off-diagonal entry, together with the differences of two
  diagonal entries, span the complexification.
entries.snippet:
lemma singleℂ_diagDiffℂ_span_eq_top {n : ℕ} :
    Submodule.span ℂ ({A : Complexification n | ∃ (p q : Fin n) (h : p ≠ q), A = singleℂ p q h} ∪
      {A : Complexification n | ∃ p q : Fin n, A = diagDiffℂ p q}) = ⊤

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.finrank_complexification
entries.docstring:
The complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)` has complex dimension `n² - 1`: it is the traceless
  matrices, and the trace is onto for `0 < n`.
entries.snippet: lemma finrank_complexification : Module.finrank ℂ (Complexification n) = n ^ 2 - 1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.finrank_eq
entries.docstring: `su(n)` has real dimension `n² - 1`, the dimension of its complexification.
entries.snippet: lemma finrank_eq : Module.finrank ℝ (SULieAlgebra n ℂ) = n ^ 2 - 1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr
entries.docstring:
The contraction of two real adjoint indices: the trace form `x ⊗ y ↦ tr (x y)` on `su(n)`,
  which is real since `x` and `y` are hermitian.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def adjointContr {n : ℕ} : ((adjoint (n := n)).tprod adjoint).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℝ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ℝ) where

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_tmul
entries.docstring: The real contraction is the real part of the trace, `x ⊗ y ↦ re tr (x y)`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma adjointContr_tmul {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = (x.1 * y.1).trace.re

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_adjoint
entries.docstring:
The adjoint representation preserves the real contraction, so `SU(n)` acts on `su(n)` by
  isometries.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_adjoint {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (adjoint g x ⊗ₜ adjoint g y) = adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.ofReal_adjointContr_tmul
entries.docstring: The trace `tr (x y)` of two elements of `su(n)` is real, equal to their contraction.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofReal_adjointContr_tmul {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    (adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) : ℂ) = (x.1 * y.1).trace

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_symm
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_symm {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = adjointContr (y ⊗ₜ x)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_lie
entries.docstring:
The real contraction is invariant under the bracket, `tr (⁅x, y⁆ z) = tr (x ⁅y, z⁆)`; in terms
  of generators, the structure constants `tr (T^a ⁅T^b, T^c⁆)` are totally antisymmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_lie {n : ℕ} (x y z : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (⁅x, y⁆ ⊗ₜ z) = adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ ⁅y, z⁆)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_self_nonneg
entries.docstring: The real contraction is positive semidefinite: `tr (x x) = tr (x x†) ≥ 0`.
entries.snippet: lemma adjointContr_self_nonneg {n : ℕ} (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) : 0 ≤ adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ x)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_self_eq_zero_iff
entries.docstring: The real contraction of `x` with itself vanishes only for `x = 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_self_eq_zero_iff {n : ℕ} (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ x) = 0 ↔ x = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_self_pos
entries.docstring: The real contraction is positive definite, making it an inner product on `su(n)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_self_pos {n : ℕ} {x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    0 < adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ x)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_separating_left
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_separating_left {n : ℕ} (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ)
    (hx : ∀ y, adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = 0) : x = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_separating_right
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_separating_right {n : ℕ} (y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ)
    (hy : ∀ x, adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = 0) : y = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_flip_injective
entries.docstring: The real contraction separates `su(n)`: `y ↦ (x ↦ re tr (x y))` is injective.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_flip_injective {n : ℕ} :
    Function.Injective (TensorProduct.curry (adjointContr (n := n)).toLinearMap).flip

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_isSymm
entries.docstring: The real contraction, as a bilinear form, is symmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_isSymm {n : ℕ} :
    LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm (TensorProduct.curry (adjointContr (n := n)).toLinearMap)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_nondegenerate
entries.docstring: The real contraction, as a bilinear form, is nondegenerate.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_nondegenerate {n : ℕ} :
    (TensorProduct.curry (adjointContr (n := n)).toLinearMap).Nondegenerate

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr
entries.docstring:
The contraction of two complex adjoint indices: the complexification of the real contraction
  `adjointContr`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def adjointℂContr {n : ℕ} : ((adjointℂ (n := n)).tprod adjointℂ).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℂ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ℂ) where

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_adjointℂ
entries.docstring: The adjoint representation preserves the complex contraction.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ)
    (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (adjointℂ g A ⊗ₜ adjointℂ g B) = adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_tmul
entries.docstring: The contraction is the trace form, `A ⊗ B ↦ tr (A B)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_tmul (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = (toMatrixℂ A * toMatrixℂ B).trace

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_one_tmul
entries.docstring:
On the real elements `1 ⊗ x` of the complexification the complex contraction is the real
  contraction, so the two agree on real gauge fields.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_one_tmul {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointℂContr ((1 ⊗ₜ x) ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ y)) = adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_symm
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_symm {n} (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = adjointℂContr (B ⊗ₜ A)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_lie
entries.docstring: The complex contraction is invariant under the bracket, `tr (⁅A, B⁆ C) = tr (A ⁅B, C⁆)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_lie {n} (A B C : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (⁅A, B⁆ ⊗ₜ C) = adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ ⁅B, C⁆)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_separating_left
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_separating_left {n} (A : Complexification n)
    (hA : ∀ B, adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = 0) : A = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_separating_right
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_separating_right {n} (B : Complexification n)
    (hB : ∀ A, adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = 0) : B = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_flip_injective
entries.docstring: The contraction separates the complexification: `B ↦ (A ↦ tr (A B))` is injective.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_flip_injective :
    Function.Injective (TensorProduct.curry (adjointℂContr (n := n)).toLinearMap).flip

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_isSymm
entries.docstring: The complex contraction, as a bilinear form, is symmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_isSymm {n : ℕ} :
    LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm (TensorProduct.curry (adjointℂContr (n := n)).toLinearMap)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_nondegenerate
entries.docstring: The complex contraction, as a bilinear form, is nondegenerate.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_nondegenerate {n : ℕ} :
    (TensorProduct.curry (adjointℂContr (n := n)).toLinearMap).Nondegenerate

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_eq_adjointℂContr_tmul
entries.docstring:
Every bilinear form on the complexification is the contraction against an endomorphism,
  the contraction being nondegenerate.

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_comp_eq_of_adjointℂContr_tmul
entries.docstring:
The endomorphism representing an invariant bilinear form commutes with the adjoint
  action.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂ_comp_eq_of_adjointℂContr_tmul {n : ℕ}
    (B : ((adjointℂ (n := n)).tprod adjointℂ).IntertwiningMap
      (Representation.trivial ℂ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ℂ))
    {T : Module.End ℂ (Complexification n)} (hT : ∀ A C, B (A ⊗ₜ C) = adjointℂContr (T A ⊗ₜ C))
    (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    T ∘ₗ adjointℂ g = adjointℂ g ∘ₗ T

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.intertwiningMap_eq_smul_adjointℂContr
entries.docstring:
Every intertwiner `adj ⊗ adj → ℂ` is a multiple of the contraction: up to scale, the
  contraction is the unique `SU(n)`-invariant bilinear form on the complexification.
entries.snippet:
lemma intertwiningMap_eq_smul_adjointℂContr {n : ℕ}
    (B : ((adjointℂ (n := n)).tprod adjointℂ).IntertwiningMap
      (Representation.trivial ℂ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ℂ)) :
    ∃ z : ℂ, B = z • adjointℂContr

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis
entries.docstring:
The matrix of the adjoint action of `g` in the Gell-Mann basis, a real matrix, as a monoid
  homomorphism from `SU(n)`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def adjointGellMannBasis {n : ℕ} :
    specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ →* Matrix (GellMannIndex n) (GellMannIndex n) ℝ

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis_apply
entries.docstring: The entries of the matrix of the adjoint action, `re tr (λ_i g λ_j g†) / 2`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointGellMannBasis_apply {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ)
    (i j : GellMannIndex n) : adjointGellMannBasis g i j =
      ((gellMannMatrices i).1 * (g.1 * (gellMannMatrices j).1 * star g.1)).trace.re / 2

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis_inv
entries.docstring:
The matrix of the adjoint action of `g⁻¹` is the transpose of that of `g`, the adjoint action
  preserving the contraction.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointGellMannBasis_inv {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjointGellMannBasis g⁻¹ = (adjointGellMannBasis g)ᵀ

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis_transpose_mul_self
entries.docstring: The matrix of the adjoint action is orthogonal.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointGellMannBasis_transpose_mul_self {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    (adjointGellMannBasis g)ᵀ * adjointGellMannBasis g = 1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrix_adjointℂ_gellMannBasisℂ
entries.docstring:
The matrix of the complex adjoint action in the complex Gell-Mann basis is the real matrix of
  the adjoint action.
entries.snippet:
lemma toMatrix_adjointℂ_gellMannBasisℂ {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix gellMannBasisℂ gellMannBasisℂ (adjointℂ g) =
      (adjointGellMannBasis g).map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_gellMannMatrices
entries.docstring:
The adjoint action on a Gell-Mann matrix is a combination of Gell-Mann matrices with
  coefficients the entries of the matrix of the adjoint action,
  `g λ_j g† = ∑ i, R_ij(g) λ_i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjoint_gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (j : GellMannIndex n) :
    adjoint g (gellMannMatrices j) = ∑ i, adjointGellMannBasis g i j • gellMannMatrices i

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasis_repr_adjoint
entries.docstring:
The adjoint action on the coordinates in the Gell-Mann basis is multiplication by the matrix of
  the adjoint action, `A^i ↦ R_ij(g) A^j`.
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannBasis_repr_adjoint {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ)
    (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    gellMannBasis.repr (adjoint g x) = adjointGellMannBasis g *ᵥ gellMannBasis.repr x

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.GellMannIndex
entries.docstring: The indexing type of the Gell-Mann matrices.
entries.snippet:
inductive GellMannIndex (n : ℕ)
  | symm (p : Fin n) (q : Fin n) (h : p < q) : GellMannIndex n
  | antisymm (p : Fin n) (q : Fin n) (h : p < q) : GellMannIndex n
  | diag (l : Fin (n - 1)) : GellMannIndex n

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannIndex_card
entries.docstring:
There are `n² - 1` generalized Gell-Mann matrices: `n (n - 1) / 2` symmetric ones, as many
  antisymmetric ones, and `n - 1` diagonal ones.
entries.snippet: lemma gellMannIndex_card {n : ℕ} : Fintype.card (GellMannIndex n) = n ^ 2 - 1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices
entries.docstring:
The generalized Gell-Mann matrices, as elements of `su(n)`:

- for `p < q`, the symmetric matrix `E_pq + E_qp`,
- for `p < q`, the antisymmetric matrix `-i E_pq + i E_qp`,
- for `l : Fin (n - 1)`, with `m = l + 1`, the diagonal matrix
  `√(2 / (m (m + 1))) (E_00 + ⋯ + E_(m-1)(m-1) - m E_mm)`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} : GellMannIndex n → SULieAlgebra n ℂ
  | .symm p q h => ofMatrix (single p q 1 + single q p 1)
      (by simp [star_eq_conjTranspose, conjTranspose_single, add_comm])
      (by rw [trace_add, trace_single_eq_of_ne _ _ _ h.ne, trace_single_eq_of_ne _ _ _ h.ne',
        add_zero])
  | .antisymm p q h => ofMatrix (single p q (-Complex.I) + single q p Complex.I)
      (by simp [star_eq_conjTranspose, conjTranspose_single, add_comm])
      (by rw [trace_add, trace_single_eq_of_ne _ _ _ h.ne, trace_single_eq_of_ne _ _ _ h.ne',
        add_zero])
  | .diag l => ofMatrix (diagonal fun x => (√(2 / ((l.1 + 1) * (l.1 + 2))) : ℝ) *
      if x.1 ≤ l.1 then 1 else if x.1 = l.1 + 1 then -(l.1 + 1 : ℂ) else 0)
      (by
        ext x y
        simp only [star_apply, diagonal_apply]
        split_ifs <;> simp_all [Complex.conj_ofReal]
        omega)
      (by
        have hl := l.2
        rw [trace_diagonal, ← Finset.mul_sum, Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun x =>
          if x ≤ l.1 then (1 : ℂ) else if x = l.1 + 1 then -(l.1 + 1 : ℂ) else 0),
          ← Finset.sum_range_add_sum_Ico _ (show l.1 + 2 ≤ n by omega), Finset.sum_range_succ,
          Finset.sum_congr (s₁ := Finset.range (l.1 + 1)) rfl fun x hx =>
            ite_eq_left (Nat.lt_succ_iff.1 (Finset.mem_range.1 hx)),
          Finset.sum_eq_zero (s := Finset.Ico (l.1 + 2) n) fun x hx => by
            have := (Finset.mem_Ico.1 hx).1
            rw [ite_eq_right (by omega), ite_eq_right (by omega)]]
        simp)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_symm_isSymm
entries.docstring: The symmetric generalized Gell-Mann matrices are symmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannMatrices_symm_isSymm {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q) :
    Matrix.IsSymm (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h)).1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_antisymm_transpose
entries.docstring: The antisymmetric generalized Gell-Mann matrices are antisymmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannMatrices_antisymm_transpose {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q) :
    (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h)).1ᵀ = -(gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h)).1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_diag_isDiag
entries.docstring: The diagonal generalized Gell-Mann matrices are diagonal.
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannMatrices_diag_isDiag {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    Matrix.IsDiag (gellMannMatrices (.diag l)).1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_symm_val_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannMatrices_symm_val_eq {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q) :
    (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h)).1 = single p q 1 + single q p 1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_antisymm_val_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannMatrices_antisymm_val_eq {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q) :
    (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h)).1 = single p q (-Complex.I) + single q p Complex.I

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_diag_val_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannMatrices_diag_val_eq {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    (gellMannMatrices (.diag l)).1 = diagonal fun x => (√(2 / ((l.1 + 1) * (l.1 + 2))) : ℝ) *
      if x.1 ≤ l.1 then 1 else if x.1 = l.1 + 1 then -(l.1 + 1 : ℂ) else 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_antisymm_eq_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_antisymm_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (p' q' : Fin n) (h' : p' < q') :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p' q' h')) = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_diag_eq_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_diag_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.diag l)) = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_symm_eq_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_symm_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (p' q' : Fin n) (h' : p' < q') :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.symm p' q' h')) = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_diag_eq_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_diag_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.diag l)) = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_symm_eq_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_symm_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) (p q : Fin n)
    (h : p < q) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.diag l) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h)) = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_antisymm_eq_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_antisymm_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) (p q : Fin n)
    (h : p < q) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.diag l) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h)) = 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_orthogonal
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_orthogonal {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (p' q' : Fin n) (h' : p' < q') :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.symm p' q' h')) =
      if p = p' ∧ q = q' then 2 else 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_orthogonal
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_orthogonal {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (p' q' : Fin n) (h' : p' < q') :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p' q' h')) =
      if p = p' ∧ q = q' then 2 else 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_self
entries.docstring: The diagonal Gell-Mann matrices are normalized, `tr (λ_l λ_l) = 2`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_self {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.diag l) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.diag l)) = 2

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_orthogonal
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_orthogonal {n : ℕ} (l l' : Fin (n - 1)) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.diag l) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.diag l')) =
      if l = l' then 2 else 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices
entries.docstring:
The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are orthogonal under the trace pairing,
  with normalization `tr (λ_i λ_j) = 2 δ_ij`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} (i j : GellMannIndex n) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices i ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices j) = if i = j then 2 else 0

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.linearIndependent_gellMannMatrices
entries.docstring:
The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are linearly independent over `ℝ`, being orthogonal under
  the contraction.
entries.snippet:
lemma linearIndependent_gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} :
    LinearIndependent ℝ (gellMannMatrices (n := n))

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasis
entries.docstring: The generalized Gell-Mann basis of `su(n)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def gellMannBasis {n : ℕ} : Module.Basis (GellMannIndex n) ℝ (SULieAlgebra n ℂ)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasis_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma gellMannBasis_apply {n : ℕ} (i : GellMannIndex n) : gellMannBasis i = gellMannMatrices i

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasis_repr_apply
entries.docstring:
The coordinates in the Gell-Mann basis are the contractions with the Gell-Mann matrices,
  `x = ∑ (adjointContr (λ_i ⊗ x) / 2) λ_i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannBasis_repr_apply {n : ℕ} (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) (i : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannBasis.repr x i = adjointContr (gellMannMatrices i ⊗ₜ x) / 2

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasisℂ
entries.docstring: The generalized Gell-Mann basis `1 ⊗ λ_i` of the complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def gellMannBasisℂ {n : ℕ} : Module.Basis (GellMannIndex n) ℂ (Complexification n)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasisℂ_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannBasisℂ_apply {n : ℕ} (i : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannBasisℂ i = 1 ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices i

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_gellMannBasisℂ
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toMatrixℂ_gellMannBasisℂ {n : ℕ} (i : GellMannIndex n) :
    toMatrixℂ (gellMannBasisℂ i) = (gellMannMatrices i).1

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasisℂ_repr_apply
entries.docstring:
The coordinates in the complex Gell-Mann basis are the contractions with the Gell-Mann
  matrices, `A = ∑ (adjointℂContr (λ_i ⊗ A) / 2) λ_i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannBasisℂ_repr_apply {n : ℕ} (A : Complexification n) (i : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannBasisℂ.repr A i = adjointℂContr (gellMannBasisℂ i ⊗ₜ A) / 2

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannStructureConst
entries.docstring:
The structure constants of `su(n)` in the Gell-Mann basis, with the physics normalisation
  `[λ_a, λ_b] = 2 i ∑ c, f_abc λ_c`, read off by the contraction:
  `f_abc = tr ([λ_a, λ_b] λ_c) / (4 i) = -(1 / 4) adjointContr (⁅λ_a, λ_b⁆ ⊗ λ_c)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def gellMannStructureConst {n : ℕ} (a b c : GellMannIndex n) : ℝ

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.lie_gellMannMatrices
entries.docstring:
The bracket of two Gell-Mann matrices in terms of the structure constants,
  `⁅λ_a, λ_b⁆ = -2 ∑ c, f_abc λ_c`, the bracket `⁅x, y⁆ = i (x y - y x)` carrying a factor `i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma lie_gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} (a b : GellMannIndex n) :
    ⁅gellMannMatrices a, gellMannMatrices b⁆ =
      ∑ c, (-2 * gellMannStructureConst a b c) • gellMannMatrices c

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannStructureConst_swap
entries.docstring: The structure constants are antisymmetric in their first two indices.
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannStructureConst_swap {n : ℕ} (a b c : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannStructureConst b a c = -gellMannStructureConst a b c

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannStructureConst_cycle
entries.docstring:
The structure constants are invariant under cyclic permutations of their indices, the
  contraction being invariant under the bracket. With `gellMannStructureConst_swap`, they are
  totally antisymmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannStructureConst_cycle {n : ℕ} (a b c : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannStructureConst b c a = gellMannStructureConst a b c

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.GellMannIndex.equivTwo
entries.docstring:
For `n = 2`, the labelling of the generalized Gell-Mann matrices as the Pauli matrices
  `σ₁, σ₂, σ₃` (as `0, 1, 2`): the symmetric, antisymmetric and diagonal matrices.
entries.snippet: def GellMannIndex.equivTwo : GellMannIndex 2 ≃ Fin 3 where

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_two
entries.docstring:
For `n = 2` the generalized Gell-Mann matrices are the Pauli matrices `σ₁, σ₂, σ₃`, labelled
  by `GellMannIndex.equivTwo`.
entries.snippet:
lemma gellMannMatrices_two (i : Fin 3) :
    (gellMannMatrices (GellMannIndex.equivTwo.symm i)).1 = PauliMatrix.pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i)

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.GellMannIndex.equivThree
entries.docstring:
For `n = 3`, the labelling of the Gell-Mann matrices in the standard order `λ₁, …, λ₈`
  (as `0, …, 7`): `λ₁, λ₂, λ₃` are the symmetric, antisymmetric and diagonal matrices of the first
  two coordinates, `λ₄, λ₅` the symmetric and antisymmetric ones of the coordinates `0, 2`,
  `λ₆, λ₇` those of the coordinates `1, 2`, and `λ₈` the second diagonal matrix.
entries.snippet: def GellMannIndex.equivThree : GellMannIndex 3 ≃ Fin 8 where

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_three
entries.docstring:
For `n = 3` the generalized Gell-Mann matrices are the Gell-Mann matrices `λ₁, …, λ₈`, labelled
  in the standard order by `GellMannIndex.equivThree`.

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.killingForm_eq_trace
entries.docstring:
The Killing form of the complexification is the trace form of the matrices,
  `K(A, B) = -2n tr (A B)`. The sign comes from the factor `i` in the bracket, which makes
  `ad A ∘ ad B` the map `M ↦ -[A, [B, M]]`.
entries.snippet:
lemma killingForm_eq_trace {n : ℕ} (A B : Complexification n) :
    killingForm ℂ (Complexification n) A B = - (2 * n) * (toMatrixℂ A * toMatrixℂ B).trace

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_eq_killingForm
entries.docstring:
The contraction is the Killing form on the complexified Lie
  algebra, up to a factor of `-1/(2n)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointℂContr_eq_killingForm {n : ℕ} (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = -(1 / (2 * (n : ℂ))) * killingForm ℂ (Complexification n) A B

entries.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_eq_killingForm
entries.docstring: The contraction is the Killing form on the Lie algebra, up to a factor of `-1/(2n)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjointContr_eq_killingForm {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = -(1 / (2 * (n : ℝ))) * killingForm ℝ (SULieAlgebra n ℂ) x y

entries.name: InnerProductSpace.exp_mul_gaussian
entries.docstring: Multiplication by a real linear exponential shifts and rescales a general Gaussian.
entries.snippet:
lemma exp_mul_gaussian (v : E) :
    (ofReal (rexp (inner ℝ v x)) : 𝕜) * gaussian 𝕜 B x₀ x =
      (ofReal (rexp (inner ℝ v x₀ + 2⁻¹ * ‖B.toContinuousLinearMap.adjoint v‖ ^ 2)) : 𝕜) *
        gaussian 𝕜 B (x₀ + B (B.toContinuousLinearMap.adjoint v)) x

entries.name: InnerProductSpace.gaussianExpMul
entries.docstring:
The product of `gaussian 𝕜 B x₀` with the real exponential `exp ⟪v, x⟫`, as a Schwartz map.
It has center `x₀ + B (Bᵀ v)` and the same covariance, with scale factor
`exp (⟪v, x₀⟫ + 2⁻¹ * ‖Bᵀ v‖ ^ 2)`.
entries.snippet: def gaussianExpMul (v : E) : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)

entries.name: InnerProductSpace.gaussianExpMul_apply
entries.docstring: Evaluation of the bundled product agrees with pointwise multiplication by the exponential.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma gaussianExpMul_apply (v : E) :
    gaussianExpMul 𝕜 B x₀ v x = (ofReal (rexp (inner ℝ v x)) : 𝕜) * gaussian 𝕜 B x₀ x

entries.name: sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_self_card
entries.docstring:
**Full contraction over an arbitrary finite type.** Summing `δ^{h}_{h}` over all `k`-tuples
`h` of indices gives the falling product `card α · (card α - 1) ⋯ (card α - k + 1)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_self_card (k : ℕ) :
    ∑ h : Fin k → α, generalizedKroneckerDelta h h
      = ∏ j ∈ Finset.range k, ((Fintype.card α : ℤ) - j)

entries.name: sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_cons_card
entries.docstring:
**Single contraction over an arbitrary finite type.** Contracting the last `k` of `k+1`
index pairs leaves one free pair `σ, τ`, with the falling product
`(card α - 1) (card α - 2) ⋯`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_cons_card (σ τ : α) (k : ℕ) :
    ∑ h : Fin k → α,
        generalizedKroneckerDelta (Fin.cons σ h) (Fin.cons τ h)
      = (∏ j ∈ Finset.range k, ((Fintype.card α : ℤ) - 1 - j))
        * ((kroneckerDelta σ τ : ℕ) : ℤ)

entries.name: sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_cons₂_card
entries.docstring:
**Double contraction over an arbitrary finite type.** Contracting the last `k` of `k+2`
index pairs leaves two free pairs, with value a `2×2` generalized Kronecker delta times the
falling product `(card α - 2) (card α - 3) ⋯`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_cons₂_card (ρ σ τ ω : α) (k : ℕ) :
    ∑ h : Fin k → α,
        generalizedKroneckerDelta (Fin.cons ρ (Fin.cons σ h)) (Fin.cons τ (Fin.cons ω h))
      = (∏ j ∈ Finset.range k, ((Fintype.card α : ℤ) - 2 - j))
        * generalizedKroneckerDelta ![ρ, σ] ![τ, ω]

entries.name: sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_self_eq_factorial
entries.docstring: When the index type has exactly `k` elements, the full contraction is `k!`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_self_eq_factorial {k : ℕ} (hk : Fintype.card α = k) :
    ∑ h : Fin k → α, generalizedKroneckerDelta h h = (k.factorial : ℤ)

entries.name: eqOn_Icc_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
If `f : ℝ → V →L[ℝ] ℝ` is continuous on `[a, b]` and `∫ x in a..b, f x (ψ x • v) = 0` for
every smooth `ψ` supported in `(a, b)` and every `v : V`, then `f = 0` on `[a, b]`.
entries.snippet:
lemma eqOn_Icc_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero {f : ℝ → V →L[ℝ] ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hab : a < b)
    (hint : ∀ ψ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ ψ → tsupport ψ ⊆ Ioo a b →
      ∀ v : V, ∫ x in a..b, f x (ψ x • v) = 0) :
    ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, f x = 0

entries.name: Frequency
entries.docstring:
The type `Frequency` represents the measure of of how often sinusodial components
 of a wave repeat per unit time, i.e. a nonnegative real number carrying the dimension
 of inverse time, in a given (but arbitrary) set of units.
entries.snippet: abbrev Frequency : Type

entries.name: Wavelength
entries.docstring:
The type `Wavelength` represents the distance between consecutive
corresponding points of the same phase on the wave, such as two adjacent
crests, troughs, or zero crossings, i.e. a nonnegative real number
carrying the dimension of length.
entries.snippet: abbrev Wavelength : Type

entries.name: Wavelength.ofFrequency
entries.docstring:
The wavelength of a wave of frequency `ν` propagating at a speed `c`,
given by `λ = c / ν`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def ofFrequency (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (ν : Frequency) (_ν_pos : 0 < ν.val) :
    Wavelength

entries.name: Wavelength.ofFrequency_val
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofFrequency_val (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (ν : Frequency) (hν : 0 < ν.val) :
    (ofFrequency c ν hν).val = c.val / ν.val

entries.name: Wavelength.ofFrequency_pos
entries.docstring:
Positivity of the wavelength associated with a positive frequency and a positive
speed.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofFrequency_pos (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (hc : 0 < c.val) (ν : Frequency)
    (hν : 0 < ν.val) : 0 < (ofFrequency c ν hν).val

entries.name: Wavelength.ofFrequency_mul
entries.docstring: The wavelength associated with a frequency satisfies `λ * ν = c`.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofFrequency_mul (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (ν : Frequency) (hν : 0 < ν.val) :
    (ofFrequency c ν hν).val * ν.val = c.val

entries.name: Wavelength.ofFrequency_scaleUnit
entries.docstring:
The wavelength associated with a frequency scales with units as a wavelength should:
changing the units from `u1` to `u2` rescales the resulting wavelength by the scale factor
of the dimension of length.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofFrequency_scaleUnit (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (ν : Frequency) (hν : 0 < ν.val)
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    ofFrequency (scaleUnit u1 u2 c) (scaleUnit u1 u2 ν) (WithDim.scaleUnit_val_pos ν hν u1 u2) =
      scaleUnit u1 u2 (ofFrequency c ν hν)

entries.name: Frequency.ofWavelength
entries.docstring:
The frequency of a wave of wavelength `w` propagating at a speed `c`,
given by `ν = c / w`. We can't use `λ` due to Lean anon function.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def ofWavelength (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (w : Wavelength) (_w_pos : 0 < w.val) :
    Frequency

entries.name: Frequency.ofWavelength_val
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofWavelength_val (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (w : Wavelength) (w_pos : 0 < w.val) :
    (ofWavelength c w w_pos).val = c.val / w.val

entries.name: Frequency.ofWavelength_pos
entries.docstring:
Positivity of the frequency associated with a positive wavelength and a positive
speed.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofWavelength_pos (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (c_pos : 0 < c.val) (w : Wavelength)
    (hw : 0 < w.val) : 0 < (ofWavelength c w hw).val

entries.name: Frequency.ofWavelength_mul
entries.docstring: The frequency associated with a wavelength satisfies `ν * λ = c`.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofWavelength_mul (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (w : Wavelength) (w_pos : 0 < w.val) :
    (ofWavelength c w w_pos).val * w.val = c.val

entries.name: Frequency.ofWavelength_scaleUnit
entries.docstring:
The frequency associated with a wavelength scales with units as a frequency should:
changing the units from `u1` to `u2` rescales the resulting frequency by the scale factor
of the dimension of inverse time.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofWavelength_scaleUnit (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (w : Wavelength) (w_pos : 0 < w.val)
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    ofWavelength (scaleUnit u1 u2 c) (scaleUnit u1 u2 w)
      (WithDim.scaleUnit_val_pos w w_pos u1 u2) =
      scaleUnit u1 u2 (ofWavelength c w w_pos)

entries.name: Frequency.ofWavelength_ofFrequency
entries.docstring: Converting a wavelength to a frequency and back recovers the wavelength.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofWavelength_ofFrequency (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (hc : 0 < c.val)
    (ν : Frequency) (hν : 0 < ν.val) :
    ofWavelength c (Wavelength.ofFrequency c ν hν)
      (Wavelength.ofFrequency_pos c hc ν hν) = ν

entries.name: Wavelength.ofFrequency_ofWavelength
entries.docstring: Converting a frequency to a wavelength and back recovers the frequency.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofFrequency_ofWavelength (c : WithDim (L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ≥0) (hc : 0 < c.val)
    (w : Wavelength) (hw : 0 < w.val) :
    ofFrequency c (Frequency.ofWavelength c w hw)
      (Frequency.ofWavelength_pos c hc w hw) = w

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsIntertwining
entries.docstring: A channel intertwines two group actions if it commutes with their transformations.
entries.snippet: def IsIntertwining (Φ : E →ₚ₁[ℝ] F) : Prop

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isIntertwining_id
