The all-orders gauge transformation of the derived bracket `⁅A_ρ, F⁆` against an
  adjoint gauge tensor `F`: since `F` transforms homogeneously, only one `ad`
  cross-term convolution survives — the analogue of `repGauge_commutatorFam`
  with a gauge tensor in the second slot.
entries.snippet:
lemma TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_bracketFamConv
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B}
    (hF : TransformsInAdjoint jets repGauge F)
    (U : GJ) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    repGauge U (bracketFamConv h.A ρ F s φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        bracketFamConv h.A ρ F p.2 (jets.adjointDualCoeff U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum
      + (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          (p.2.antidiagonal.map fun r =>
            F r.2 (jets.adjointDualCoeff U⁻¹ r.1
              (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ 𝔤 (jets.evalLie
                (jets.iteratedDeriv p.1
                  (jets.maurerCartan U⁻¹ ρ)))))).sum).sum

entries.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.TransformsInAdjoint.covDerivAdjoint
entries.docstring:
**Adjoint gauge tensors are closed under the covariant derivative**: if `F`
  transforms in the adjoint, so does `∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + ⁅A_ρ, F⁆`. The single
  inhomogeneous convolution of `[∂_{ρ ::ₘ s} F]`
  (`TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_cons`) cancels the single `ad` cross-term
  convolution of `⁅A_ρ, F⁆` (`TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_bracketFamConv`)
  through the coassociativity of the antidiagonal; no structural equation is needed.
  Together with `transformsInAdjoint_fieldStrength` this makes every iterated
  covariant derivative of the field strength an adjoint gauge tensor, by recursion.
entries.snippet:
lemma TransformsInAdjoint.covDerivAdjoint
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B}
    (hF : TransformsInAdjoint jets repGauge F) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    TransformsInAdjoint jets repGauge (GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivAdjoint h.A F ρ)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData
entries.docstring:
The field data of a gauge theory. Over a gauge context, given by a jet gauge group `GJ`
  with global group `G₀`, a finite-dimensional real gauge algebra `𝔤` with jet algebra
  `𝔤J` and a local-gauge-data package `jets` over them, it records a finite family of fermionic
  species and a finite family of bosonic species, each given by an existing
  `MatterField jets`. The species types are `Fintype` rather than merely `Finite`, so
  that a theory may be summed over its species: this is what lets the several fermionic
  multiplets be assembled into the single fermionic matter field of
  `GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField`.

  Nothing is repeated from `MatterField`, whose fields already carry the value space, the
  Lorentz representation, the local-gauge-data action, the mass weight and the declared
  statistic of a species. The fermionic family supplies the generators of the exterior-algebra
  factor of the local field algebra `GaugeFieldData.LocalFieldAlgebra`, and the bosonic family
  those of its symmetric-algebra factor; the fields `fermion_statistic` and `boson_statistic`
  require every entry of each family to be declared with the corresponding statistics.
  Nothing is repeated from the gauge context either, and the gauge bosons are not a species,
  since their generator space is determined by `𝔤` alone.

  This is data before a Lagrangian. Collecting representations of the several species does
  not assert that they are jointly consistent. Gauge-Lorentz compatibility, factorization
  of the jet action through its global value, and richness of the jet group are separate
  conditions, none of them imposed here.
entries.snippet:
structure GaugeFieldData {G₀ : Type} [Group G₀] {𝔤 : Type} [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤]
    [Module.Finite ℝ 𝔤] {GJ : Type} [Group GJ] {𝔤J : Type} [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J]
    (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) where
  FermionSpecies : Type
  [decidableEqFermionSpecies : DecidableEq FermionSpecies]
  [fintypeFermionSpecies : Fintype FermionSpecies]
  fermion : FermionSpecies → MatterField jets
  fermion_statistic : ∀ i, (fermion i).statistic = .fermionic
  BosonSpecies : Type
  [decidableEqBosonSpecies : DecidableEq BosonSpecies]
  [fintypeBosonSpecies : Fintype BosonSpecies]
  boson : BosonSpecies → MatterField jets
  boson_statistic : ∀ j, (boson j).statistic = .bosonic

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.FermionValue
entries.docstring: The value space of a fermionic species.
entries.snippet: abbrev FermionValue (i : T.FermionSpecies) : Type

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.BosonValue
entries.docstring: The value space of a bosonic species.
entries.snippet: abbrev BosonValue (j : T.BosonSpecies) : Type

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.PureJetsActTrivially
entries.docstring: Pure gauge jets act trivially at the base point on every species of the datum.
entries.snippet: def PureJetsActTrivially : Prop

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCompatible
entries.docstring:
The infinitesimal gauge action of every species of the datum commutes with its Lorentz
  representation.
entries.snippet: def GaugeLorentzCompatible : Prop

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.BosonGenerators
entries.docstring:
The bosonic generator space of the datum, holding the component functions `∂_s φ_α`
  and their conjugates of every bosonic species at once, as a direct sum over the species.
  A component function of the theory is a finitely supported family of component functions
  of the species.

  The direct sum, rather than a single component space on the product of the value spaces,
  is what lets the species carry different mass weights: the scaling of one component space
  is natural in the value space — `JetComponentSpace.comap_comp_massWeightScale` — and so
  cannot tell the species apart. When the weights do agree the two descriptions coincide,
  which is section C below.

  This `def` and its explicit instances reduce instance-term expansion in the symmetric
  algebra and tensor products built on it. Use the inclusion, assembly and extensionality
  API in downstream proofs; unfold the direct-sum representation explicitly when necessary.
entries.snippet: def BosonGenerators : Type

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.«instance@e996c1df»
entries.snippet: instance : AddCommGroup T.BosonGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.«instance@cab8f88d»
entries.snippet: instance : Module ℂ T.BosonGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.inclBoson
entries.docstring:
The inclusion of the component space of one bosonic species into the bosonic generator
  space.
entries.snippet:
def inclBoson (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    JetComponentSpace (T.boson i) →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.assembleBoson
entries.docstring:
The assembly of a species-wise family of linear maps out of the bosonic generator space
  into a common target.
entries.snippet:
def assembleBoson (f : ∀ i, JetComponentSpace (T.boson i) →ₗ[ℂ] N) :
    T.BosonGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] N

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.assembleBoson_inclBoson
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma assembleBoson_inclBoson (f : ∀ i, JetComponentSpace (T.boson i) →ₗ[ℂ] N)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) (x : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.assembleBoson f (T.inclBoson i x) = f i x

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGenerators_hom_ext
entries.docstring:
Two linear maps out of the bosonic generator space agreeing on every species are
  equal.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonGenerators_hom_ext {F F' : T.BosonGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] N}
    (h : ∀ i x, F (T.inclBoson i x) = F' (T.inclBoson i x)) : F = F'

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBoson
entries.docstring:
The Lorentz action on the bosonic generator space, acting on each species through the
  Lorentz representation of its matter field.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def repLorentzBoson : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.BosonGenerators where

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBoson_inclBoson
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma repLorentzBoson_inclBoson (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.repLorentzBoson Λ (T.inclBoson i x)
      = T.inclBoson i (JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.boson i) Λ x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetBoson
entries.docstring:
The action of the jet gauge group on the bosonic generator space, acting on each
  species through the fibrewise jet action of its matter field. Both the fibrewise
  hypothesis and the finite dimensionality of the value space that
  `JetComponentSpace.repJet` needs are already fields of `MatterField`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def repJetBoson : Representation ℂ GJ T.BosonGenerators where

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetBoson_inclBoson
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma repJetBoson_inclBoson (U : GJ) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.repJetBoson U (T.inclBoson i x)
      = T.inclBoson i
        (JetComponentSpace.repJet (T.boson i) U x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleBoson
entries.docstring:
The mass-weight scaling on the bosonic generator space, with the weight of each species
  taken from its matter field. Species of different weight scale differently, which is the
  property the direct-sum generator space was chosen to have.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def massWeightScaleBoson (c : ℂ) :
    T.BosonGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson
entries.docstring:
On the summand of a species the scaling is that species' own mass-weight scaling, with
  the weight recorded in its matter field.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson (c : ℂ) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.massWeightScaleBoson c (T.inclBoson i x)
      = T.inclBoson i
        (JetComponentSpace.massWeightScale (T.boson i).massWeight c x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson_basis_tmul
entries.docstring:
A component function `∂_s φ_α` of a species scales by `c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`, where `w` is
  the mass weight of that species. There is one factor of `c` per unit of mass dimension of
  the field and two per derivative.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson_basis_tmul (c : ℂ) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue i)) :
    T.massWeightScaleBoson c (T.inclBoson i
        ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0) : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i)))
      = c ^ ((T.boson i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s) • T.inclBoson i
          ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0) : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i))

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson_basis_tmul_conj
entries.docstring:
The conjugate component functions of a species scale with the same weight as its
  unconjugated ones.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson_basis_tmul_conj (c : ℂ) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue i))) :
    T.massWeightScaleBoson c (T.inclBoson i
        ((0, SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ) : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i)))
      = c ^ ((T.boson i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s) • T.inclBoson i
          ((0, SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ) : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i))

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivBoson
entries.docstring:
The ordinary derivative shift on the bosonic generator space, acting on each species'
  component functions by appending `∂_μ` to the derivative label.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def jetDerivBoson (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    T.BosonGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivBoson_inclBoson
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma jetDerivBoson_inclBoson (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.jetDerivBoson μ (T.inclBoson i x)
      = T.inclBoson i (JetComponentSpace.jetDeriv μ x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivBoson_comm
entries.docstring:
Mixed partials agree on the bosonic generator space, because they do on each
  species.
entries.snippet:
lemma jetDerivBoson_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (T.jetDerivBoson μ).comp (T.jetDerivBoson ν)
      = (T.jetDerivBoson ν).comp (T.jetDerivBoson μ)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBoson_jetDerivBoson
entries.docstring:
The derivative shift is a Lorentz vector on the bosonic generator space: it is one
  on each species, and both operations are species-diagonal.
entries.snippet:
lemma repLorentzBoson_jetDerivBoson (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (x : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.repLorentzBoson Λ (T.jetDerivBoson μ x)
      = ∑ a, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          T.jetDerivBoson a (T.repLorentzBoson Λ x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleBoson_jetDerivBoson
entries.docstring:
The derivative carries mass weight two on the bosonic generator space, whatever the
  weights of the species: the shift adds two units of mass dimension to every component
  function alike.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightScaleBoson_jetDerivBoson (c : ℂ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (T.massWeightScaleBoson c).comp (T.jetDerivBoson μ)
      = c ^ 2 • (T.jetDerivBoson μ).comp (T.massWeightScaleBoson c)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv
entries.docstring:
**The bosonic generator space is the component space of the bosonic matter field.** The
  direct sum over the species of their component spaces is, the species type being finite,
  the same thing as the space of component functions of the single field
  `T.bosonMatterField w h` — the presentation of the boson content used in writing a theory
  down. The shared weight `w` enters only because a component space is now taken of a
  matter field, and the only matter field on `T.BosonModule` is that one; the underlying
  identification does not use it.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def bosonGeneratorsEquiv (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    T.BosonGenerators ≃ₗ[ℂ] JetComponentSpace (T.bosonMatterField w h)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_inclBoson
entries.docstring:
**A species sits inside the bosonic generators as the pullback along the projection
  onto it.** A component function of the multiplet `i` becomes the component function of
  the whole field whose target covector is supported on that multiplet.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_inclBoson (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) (x : JetComponentSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.inclBoson i x)
      = JetComponentSpace.comap
        (T.projBosonField w h i) x

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonFieldComponents_hom_ext
entries.docstring:
Two linear maps out of the component space of the bosonic matter field agree as soon as
  they agree on every species, the species pullbacks spanning it. This is the counterpart,
  on the single-field side of the identification, of `bosonGenerators_hom_ext`.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonFieldComponents_hom_ext {N : Type} [AddCommGroup N] [Module ℂ N]
    (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    {F F' : JetComponentSpace (T.bosonMatterField w h) →ₗ[ℂ] N}
    (hs : ∀ i x, F (JetComponentSpace.comap
        (T.projBosonField w h i) x)
      = F' (JetComponentSpace.comap
        (T.projBosonField w h i) x)) : F = F'

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzBoson
entries.docstring:
**The identification is Lorentz-equivariant.** The species-diagonal Lorentz action on
  the generator space is the Lorentz action on the component functions of the single field:
  each species is a subrepresentation of the bosonic matter field, so pulling back along the
  projection onto it commutes with the two actions.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzBoson (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (y : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.repLorentzBoson Λ y)
      = JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.bosonMatterField w h) Λ
        (T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repJetBoson
entries.docstring:
The identification is equivariant for the jet gauge action. The species-diagonal
  action of the jets of gauge transformations on the generator space is the action on the
  component functions of the single boson field, for the same reason as in the fermionic
  case: each species is a subrepresentation of the bosonic module. The common mass weight
  enters only through the packaging of the bosonic module as a matter field; both halves
  of the component space, with every derivative label, are covered.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repJetBoson (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (U : GJ) (y : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.repJetBoson U y)
      = JetComponentSpace.repJet (T.bosonMatterField w h) U
        (T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleBoson
entries.docstring:
**The identification carries the species-wise mass-weight scaling to a single
  scaling.** With one weight `w` shared by every species, the scaling that acts on each
  species through its own weight is the scaling of weight `w` on the component functions of
  the one field: `comap` is natural in the value space, so it does not see which species a
  generator came from.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleBoson (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (c : ℂ) (y : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.massWeightScaleBoson c y)
      = JetComponentSpace.massWeightScale w c (T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivBoson
entries.docstring:
The identification carries the derivative shift across. The species-diagonal shift
  of the derivative label on the generator space is the shift on the component functions of
  the single boson field: `comap` is natural in the value space, and the shift touches only
  the derivative label, so neither operation sees which species a generator came from. The
  common mass weight enters only through the packaging of the bosonic module as a matter
  field.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivBoson (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (y : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.jetDerivBoson μ y)
      = JetComponentSpace.jetDeriv μ (T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField
entries.docstring:
**The bosonic matter field of a gauge theory**: the direct sum of the bosonic
  species, valued in `T.BosonModule`, with the Lorentz group, the jets of gauge
  transformations and the gauge algebra all acting species by species. It exists only for
  a family degenerate in mass dimension: `w` is the common mass weight of the species and
  `h` the proof that they all have it, which for the Standard Model, whose only scalar is
  the Higgs doublet, is weight two.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def bosonMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    MatterField jets

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_V
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonMatterField_V (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).V = T.BosonModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_massWeight
entries.docstring: The bosonic matter field carries the common mass weight of the species.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma bosonMatterField_massWeight (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).massWeight = w

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_statistic
entries.docstring: The bosonic matter field is bosonic, as every bosonic species is declared to be.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma bosonMatterField_statistic (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).statistic = .bosonic

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBosonModule
entries.docstring:
**The Lorentz action on the bosonic module**, acting species by species. This is the
  Lorentz representation of the bosonic matter field, typed on `T.BosonModule` itself so
  that it can be spoken of without fixing a common mass weight.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def repLorentzBosonModule : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.BosonModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBosonModule_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma repLorentzBosonModule_apply (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : T.BosonModule) (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    T.repLorentzBosonModule Λ v i = (T.boson i).repLorentz Λ (v i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetBosonModule
entries.docstring:
The action of the jets of gauge transformations on the jets of the bosonic
  module, acting species by species, and typed on `T.BosonModule` itself so that it can
  be spoken of without fixing a common mass weight.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def repJetBosonModule :
    Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] T.BosonModule)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetBosonModule_smul
entries.docstring: The jet gauge action on the bosonic module is fibrewise, as each species is.
entries.snippet:
lemma repJetBosonModule_smul (U : GJ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] T.BosonModule) :
    T.repJetBosonModule U (χ • z) = χ • T.repJetBosonModule U z

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.lTensor_projBosonValue_repJetBosonModule
entries.docstring:
A bosonic species is a subrepresentation of the jet gauge action on the bosonic
  module: the projection onto its value space intertwines the two actions on the jets.
entries.snippet:
lemma lTensor_projBosonValue_repJetBosonModule (j : T.BosonSpecies) (U : GJ) :
    (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (T.projBosonValue j)).comp (T.repJetBosonModule U)
      = ((T.boson j).repJet U).comp
        (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (T.projBosonValue j))

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repJet
entries.docstring: The jet gauge action of the bosonic matter field is that of the bosonic module.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonMatterField_repJet (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repJet = T.repJetBosonModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repLorentz
entries.docstring: The Lorentz action of the bosonic matter field is that of the bosonic module.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonMatterField_repLorentz (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repLorentz = T.repLorentzBosonModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repLorentz_apply
entries.docstring: The Lorentz group acts on a bosonic configuration species by species.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma bosonMatterField_repLorentz_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : T.BosonModule)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repLorentz Λ v i = (T.boson i).repLorentz Λ (v i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repAlgebra_apply
entries.docstring: The gauge algebra acts on a bosonic configuration species by species.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma bosonMatterField_repAlgebra_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (c : 𝔤) (v : T.BosonModule)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repAlgebra c v i = (T.boson i).repAlgebra c (v i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repJet_apply
entries.docstring:
The jets of gauge transformations act on the jets of the bosonic field species by
  species, through the identification `jetPiEquiv` of the jets of the bosonic module
  with the family of the jets of the species.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonMatterField_repJet_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (U : GJ)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] T.BosonModule) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repJet U z =
      (jetPiEquiv T.BosonValue).symm
        (fun i => (T.boson i).repJet U (jetPiEquiv T.BosonValue z i))

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repCoeff_bosonMatterField
entries.docstring:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the bosonic jet action are those of the
  species, index by index.
entries.snippet:
lemma repCoeff_bosonMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (U : GJ)
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff (T.bosonMatterField w h).repJet U x =
      LinearMap.piMap fun i =>
        GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff (T.boson i).repJet U x

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repLorentz_inclBosonValue
entries.docstring:
**A bosonic species is a Lorentz subrepresentation of the bosonic matter field**:
  including a value of one species and then transforming is transforming and then
  including. Assembling the species into one field therefore loses no Lorentz
  information.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonMatterField_repLorentz_inclBosonValue (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : T.BosonValue i) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repLorentz Λ (T.inclBosonValue i x)
      = T.inclBosonValue i ((T.boson i).repLorentz Λ x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repAlgebra_inclBosonValue
entries.docstring:
**A bosonic species is a subrepresentation of the gauge algebra action** on the
  bosonic matter field, for the same reason: the gauge algebra does not mix the
  species.
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonMatterField_repAlgebra_inclBosonValue (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (c : 𝔤) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : T.BosonValue i) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repAlgebra c (T.inclBosonValue i x)
      = T.inclBosonValue i ((T.boson i).repAlgebra c x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.finrank_bosonMatterField
entries.docstring:
The dimension of the bosonic matter field is the sum of the dimensions of the
  species.
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_bosonMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    Module.finrank ℂ (T.bosonMatterField w h).V
      = ∑ i, Module.finrank ℂ (T.BosonValue i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projBosonField
entries.docstring:
The projection of the bosonic matter field onto one species, typed as a map out of
  `(T.bosonMatterField w h).V` rather than out of `T.BosonModule`. The two are the same
  type by definition, but naming the first keeps unification from having to unfold the
  direct sum every time the projection meets the matter field.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable abbrev projBosonField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) : (T.bosonMatterField w h).V →ₗ[ℂ] (T.boson i).V

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.BosonModule
entries.docstring:
**The bosonic module of a gauge theory**: the product, over the bosonic species,
  of their value spaces. One element of it is a value of the entire bosonic content of
  the theory — the column of all the boson fields — as opposed to
  `GaugeFieldData.BosonGenerators`, which is a space of component *functions* and is
  infinite-dimensional. Since the species type is finite the product is also their direct
  sum.
entries.snippet: abbrev BosonModule : Type

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projBosonValue
entries.docstring: The component of a bosonic configuration in one species.
entries.snippet:
abbrev projBosonValue (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    T.BosonModule →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonValue i

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.inclBosonValue
entries.docstring:
The inclusion of one bosonic species into the bosonic module, extending a value
  of that species by zero in every other.
entries.snippet:
abbrev inclBosonValue (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    T.BosonValue i →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projBosonValue_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma projBosonValue_apply (i : T.BosonSpecies) (v : T.BosonModule) :
    T.projBosonValue i v = v i

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projBosonValue_inclBosonValue_self
entries.snippet:
lemma projBosonValue_inclBosonValue_self (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (v : T.BosonValue i) : T.projBosonValue i (T.inclBosonValue i v) = v

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projBosonValue_inclBosonValue_of_ne
entries.docstring:
A value of one species has no component in any other species: the inclusions of
  distinct species have disjoint supports.
entries.snippet:
lemma projBosonValue_inclBosonValue_of_ne {i j : T.BosonSpecies} (h : i ≠ j)
    (v : T.BosonValue j) : T.projBosonValue i (T.inclBosonValue j v) = 0

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.sum_inclBosonValue_proj
entries.docstring:
**A bosonic configuration is the sum of its species components**. The product over
  the species is their direct sum, the species type being finite, so nothing is lost in
  describing the bosonic content of the theory by one module.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_inclBosonValue_proj (v : T.BosonModule) :
    ∑ i, T.inclBosonValue i (v i) = v

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonModule_hom_ext
entries.docstring: Two linear maps out of the bosonic module agreeing on every species are equal.

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.finrank_bosonModule
entries.docstring:
**The dimension of the bosonic module is the sum of the dimensions of the
  species**, each species contributing the number of complex components of its
  multiplet.
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_bosonModule :
    Module.finrank ℂ T.BosonModule = ∑ i, Module.finrank ℂ (T.BosonValue i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators
entries.docstring:
The fermionic generator space of the datum, holding the component functions `∂_s ψ_α`
  and their conjugates of every fermionic species at once, as a direct sum over the species.
  A component function of the theory is a finitely supported family of component functions
  of the species.

  The direct sum, rather than a single component space on the product of the value spaces,
  is what lets the species carry different mass weights: the scaling of one component space
  is natural in the value space — `JetComponentSpace.comap_comp_massWeightScale` — and so
  cannot tell the species apart. When the weights do agree the two descriptions coincide,
  which is section C below.

  This `def` and its explicit instances reduce instance-term expansion in the exterior
  algebra and tensor products built on it. Use the inclusion, assembly and extensionality
  API in downstream proofs; unfold the direct-sum representation explicitly when necessary.
entries.snippet: def FermionGenerators : Type

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.«instance@f5afae50»
entries.snippet: instance : AddCommGroup T.FermionGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.«instance@43e52997»
entries.snippet: instance : Module ℂ T.FermionGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.inclFermion
entries.docstring:
The inclusion of the component space of one fermionic species into the fermionic generator
  space.
entries.snippet:
def inclFermion (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i) →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.assembleFermion
entries.docstring:
The assembly of a species-wise family of linear maps out of the fermionic generator space
  into a common target.
entries.snippet:
def assembleFermion (f : ∀ i, JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i) →ₗ[ℂ] N) :
    T.FermionGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] N

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.assembleFermion_inclFermion
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma assembleFermion_inclFermion (f : ∀ i, JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i) →ₗ[ℂ] N)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.assembleFermion f (T.inclFermion i x) = f i x

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGenerators_hom_ext
entries.docstring:
Two linear maps out of the fermionic generator space agreeing on every species are
  equal.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionGenerators_hom_ext {F F' : T.FermionGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] N}
    (h : ∀ i x, F (T.inclFermion i x) = F' (T.inclFermion i x)) : F = F'

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermion
entries.docstring:
The Lorentz action on the fermionic generator space, acting on each species through the
  Lorentz representation of its matter field.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def repLorentzFermion : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.FermionGenerators where

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermion_inclFermion
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma repLorentzFermion_inclFermion (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.repLorentzFermion Λ (T.inclFermion i x)
      = T.inclFermion i (JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.fermion i) Λ x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetFermion
entries.docstring:
The action of the jet gauge group on the fermionic generator space, acting on each
  species through the fibrewise jet action of its matter field. Both the fibrewise
  hypothesis and the finite dimensionality of the value space that
  `JetComponentSpace.repJet` needs are already fields of `MatterField`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def repJetFermion : Representation ℂ GJ T.FermionGenerators where

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetFermion_inclFermion
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma repJetFermion_inclFermion (U : GJ) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.repJetFermion U (T.inclFermion i x)
      = T.inclFermion i
        (JetComponentSpace.repJet (T.fermion i) U x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleFermion
entries.docstring:
The mass-weight scaling on the fermionic generator space, with the weight of each species
  taken from its matter field. Species of different weight scale differently, which is the
  property the direct-sum generator space was chosen to have.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def massWeightScaleFermion (c : ℂ) :
    T.FermionGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion
entries.docstring:
On the summand of a species the scaling is that species' own mass-weight scaling, with
  the weight recorded in its matter field.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion (c : ℂ) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.massWeightScaleFermion c (T.inclFermion i x)
      = T.inclFermion i
        (JetComponentSpace.massWeightScale (T.fermion i).massWeight c x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion_basis_tmul
entries.docstring:
A component function `∂_s ψ_α` of a species scales by `c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`, where `w` is
  the mass weight of that species. There is one factor of `c` per unit of mass dimension of
  the field and two per derivative.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion_basis_tmul (c : ℂ) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    T.massWeightScaleFermion c (T.inclFermion i
        ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0) : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)))
      = c ^ ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s) • T.inclFermion i
          ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0) : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i))

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion_basis_tmul_conj
entries.docstring:
The conjugate component functions of a species scale with the same weight as its
  unconjugated ones.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion_basis_tmul_conj (c : ℂ) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) :
    T.massWeightScaleFermion c (T.inclFermion i
        ((0, SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ) : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)))
      = c ^ ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s) • T.inclFermion i
          ((0, SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ) : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i))

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivFermion
entries.docstring:
The ordinary derivative shift on the fermionic generator space, acting on each species'
  component functions by appending `∂_μ` to the derivative label.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def jetDerivFermion (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    T.FermionGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionGenerators

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivFermion_inclFermion
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma jetDerivFermion_inclFermion (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.jetDerivFermion μ (T.inclFermion i x)
      = T.inclFermion i (JetComponentSpace.jetDeriv μ x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivFermion_comm
entries.docstring:
Mixed partials agree on the fermionic generator space, because they do on each
  species.
entries.snippet:
lemma jetDerivFermion_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (T.jetDerivFermion μ).comp (T.jetDerivFermion ν)
      = (T.jetDerivFermion ν).comp (T.jetDerivFermion μ)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermion_jetDerivFermion
entries.docstring:
The derivative shift is a Lorentz vector on the fermionic generator space: it is
  one on each species, and both operations are species-diagonal.
entries.snippet:
lemma repLorentzFermion_jetDerivFermion (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (x : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.repLorentzFermion Λ (T.jetDerivFermion μ x)
      = ∑ a, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          T.jetDerivFermion a (T.repLorentzFermion Λ x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleFermion_jetDerivFermion
entries.docstring:
The derivative carries mass weight two on the fermionic generator space, whatever
  the weights of the species: the shift adds two units of mass dimension to every
  component function alike.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightScaleFermion_jetDerivFermion (c : ℂ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (T.massWeightScaleFermion c).comp (T.jetDerivFermion μ)
      = c ^ 2 • (T.jetDerivFermion μ).comp (T.massWeightScaleFermion c)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv
entries.docstring:
**The fermionic generator space is the component space of the fermionic matter field.** The
  direct sum over the species of their component spaces is, the species type being finite,
  the same thing as the space of component functions of the single field
  `T.fermionMatterField w h` — the presentation of the fermion content used in writing a theory
  down. The shared weight `w` enters only because a component space is now taken of a
  matter field, and the only matter field on `T.FermionModule` is that one; the underlying
  identification does not use it.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def fermionGeneratorsEquiv (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    T.FermionGenerators ≃ₗ[ℂ] JetComponentSpace (T.fermionMatterField w h)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_inclFermion
entries.docstring:
**A species sits inside the fermionic generators as the pullback along the projection
  onto it.** A component function of the multiplet `i` becomes the component function of
  the whole field whose target covector is supported on that multiplet.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_inclFermion (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.inclFermion i x)
      = JetComponentSpace.comap
        (T.projFermionField w h i) x

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionFieldComponents_hom_ext
entries.docstring:
Two linear maps out of the component space of the fermionic matter field agree as soon as
  they agree on every species, the species pullbacks spanning it. This is the counterpart,
  on the single-field side of the identification, of `fermionGenerators_hom_ext`.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionFieldComponents_hom_ext {N : Type} [AddCommGroup N] [Module ℂ N]
    (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    {F F' : JetComponentSpace (T.fermionMatterField w h) →ₗ[ℂ] N}
    (hs : ∀ i x, F (JetComponentSpace.comap
        (T.projFermionField w h i) x)
      = F' (JetComponentSpace.comap
        (T.projFermionField w h i) x)) : F = F'

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzFermion
entries.docstring:
**The identification is Lorentz-equivariant.** The species-diagonal Lorentz action on
  the generator space is the Lorentz action on the component functions of the single field:
  each species is a subrepresentation of the fermionic matter field, so pulling back along the
  projection onto it commutes with the two actions.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzFermion (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (y : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.repLorentzFermion Λ y)
      = JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.fermionMatterField w h) Λ
        (T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repJetFermion
entries.docstring:
The identification is equivariant for the jet gauge action. The species-diagonal
  action of the jets of gauge transformations on the generator space is the action on the
  component functions of the single fermion field: each species is a subrepresentation of
  the fermionic module, so pulling back along the projection onto it commutes with the two
  actions.

  The common mass weight enters only through the packaging of the fermionic module as the
  matter field `T.fermionMatterField w h`; the gauge action itself is `repJetFermionModule`,
  which exists whatever the weights are. Both halves of the component space are covered,
  the conjugate one included, and every derivative label with them: this is
  `JetComponentSpace.comap_comp_repJet` at the species projection.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repJetFermion (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (U : GJ) (y : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.repJetFermion U y)
      = JetComponentSpace.repJet (T.fermionMatterField w h) U
        (T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleFermion
entries.docstring:
**The identification carries the species-wise mass-weight scaling to a single
  scaling.** With one weight `w` shared by every species, the scaling that acts on each
  species through its own weight is the scaling of weight `w` on the component functions of
  the one field: `comap` is natural in the value space, so it does not see which species a
  generator came from.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleFermion (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (c : ℂ) (y : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.massWeightScaleFermion c y)
      = JetComponentSpace.massWeightScale w c (T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivFermion
entries.docstring:
The identification carries the derivative shift across. The species-diagonal shift
  of the derivative label on the generator space is the shift on the component functions of
  the single fermion field: `comap` is natural in the value space, and the shift touches
  only the derivative label, so neither operation sees which species a generator came from.
  The common mass weight enters only through the packaging of the fermionic module as a
  matter field.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivFermion (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (y : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.jetDerivFermion μ y)
      = JetComponentSpace.jetDeriv μ (T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField
entries.docstring:
**The fermionic matter field of a gauge theory**: the direct sum of the fermionic
  species, valued in `T.FermionModule`, with the Lorentz group, the jets of gauge
  transformations and the gauge algebra all acting species by species. It exists only for
  a family degenerate in mass dimension: `w` is the common mass weight of the species and
  `h` the proof that they all have it, which for the Standard Model, and for any theory
  whose fermions are Weyl spinors, is weight three.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def fermionMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    MatterField jets

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_V
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionMatterField_V (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).V = T.FermionModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_massWeight
entries.docstring: The fermionic matter field carries the common mass weight of the species.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma fermionMatterField_massWeight (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).massWeight = w

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_statistic
entries.docstring: The fermionic matter field is fermionic, as every fermionic species is declared to be.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma fermionMatterField_statistic (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).statistic = .fermionic

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermionModule
entries.docstring:
**The Lorentz action on the fermionic module**, acting species by species. This is the
  Lorentz representation of the fermionic matter field, typed on `T.FermionModule` itself so
  that it can be spoken of without fixing a common mass weight.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def repLorentzFermionModule : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.FermionModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermionModule_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma repLorentzFermionModule_apply (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : T.FermionModule) (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    T.repLorentzFermionModule Λ v i = (T.fermion i).repLorentz Λ (v i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetFermionModule
entries.docstring:
The action of the jets of gauge transformations on the jets of the fermionic
  module, acting species by species. Like `repLorentzFermionModule` it is typed on
  `T.FermionModule` itself, so that it can be spoken of without fixing a common mass
  weight; the gauge action of a theory whose fermions carry different mass dimensions is
  perfectly well defined, only its packaging as one `MatterField` is not.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def repJetFermionModule :
    Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] T.FermionModule)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetFermionModule_smul
entries.docstring: The jet gauge action on the fermionic module is fibrewise, as each species is.
entries.snippet:
lemma repJetFermionModule_smul (U : GJ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] T.FermionModule) :
    T.repJetFermionModule U (χ • z) = χ • T.repJetFermionModule U z

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.lTensor_projFermionValue_repJetFermionModule
entries.docstring:
A fermionic species is a subrepresentation of the jet gauge action on the fermionic
  module: the projection onto its value space intertwines the two actions on the jets.
entries.snippet:
lemma lTensor_projFermionValue_repJetFermionModule (i : T.FermionSpecies) (U : GJ) :
    (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (T.projFermionValue i)).comp (T.repJetFermionModule U)
      = ((T.fermion i).repJet U).comp
        (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (T.projFermionValue i))

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repJet
entries.docstring: The jet gauge action of the fermionic matter field is that of the fermionic module.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionMatterField_repJet (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repJet = T.repJetFermionModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repLorentz
entries.docstring: The Lorentz action of the fermionic matter field is that of the fermionic module.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionMatterField_repLorentz (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repLorentz = T.repLorentzFermionModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repLorentz_apply
entries.docstring: The Lorentz group acts on a fermionic configuration species by species.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma fermionMatterField_repLorentz_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : T.FermionModule)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repLorentz Λ v i = (T.fermion i).repLorentz Λ (v i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repAlgebra_apply
entries.docstring: The gauge algebra acts on a fermionic configuration species by species.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma fermionMatterField_repAlgebra_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (c : 𝔤) (v : T.FermionModule)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repAlgebra c v i = (T.fermion i).repAlgebra c (v i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repJet_apply
entries.docstring:
The jets of gauge transformations act on the jets of the fermionic field species by
  species, through the identification `jetPiEquiv` of the jets of the fermionic module
  with the family of the jets of the species.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionMatterField_repJet_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (U : GJ)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] T.FermionModule) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repJet U z =
      (jetPiEquiv T.FermionValue).symm
        (fun i => (T.fermion i).repJet U (jetPiEquiv T.FermionValue z i))

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.repCoeff_fermionMatterField
entries.docstring:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the fermionic jet action are those of the
  species, index by index.
entries.snippet:
lemma repCoeff_fermionMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (U : GJ)
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff (T.fermionMatterField w h).repJet U x =
      LinearMap.piMap fun i =>
        GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff (T.fermion i).repJet U x

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repLorentz_inclFermionValue
entries.docstring:
**A fermionic species is a Lorentz subrepresentation of the fermionic matter field**:
  including a value of one species and then transforming is transforming and then
  including. Assembling the species into one field therefore loses no Lorentz
  information.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionMatterField_repLorentz_inclFermionValue (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : T.FermionValue i) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repLorentz Λ (T.inclFermionValue i x)
      = T.inclFermionValue i ((T.fermion i).repLorentz Λ x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repAlgebra_inclFermionValue
entries.docstring:
**A fermionic species is a subrepresentation of the gauge algebra action** on the
  fermionic matter field, for the same reason: the gauge algebra does not mix the
  species.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionMatterField_repAlgebra_inclFermionValue (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (c : 𝔤) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : T.FermionValue i) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repAlgebra c (T.inclFermionValue i x)
      = T.inclFermionValue i ((T.fermion i).repAlgebra c x)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.finrank_fermionMatterField
entries.docstring:
The dimension of the fermionic matter field is the sum of the dimensions of the
  species.
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_fermionMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    Module.finrank ℂ (T.fermionMatterField w h).V
      = ∑ i, Module.finrank ℂ (T.FermionValue i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projFermionField
entries.docstring:
The projection of the fermionic matter field onto one species, typed as a map out of
  `(T.fermionMatterField w h).V` rather than out of `T.FermionModule`. The two are the same
  type by definition, but naming the first keeps unification from having to unfold the
  direct sum every time the projection meets the matter field.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable abbrev projFermionField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) : (T.fermionMatterField w h).V →ₗ[ℂ] (T.fermion i).V

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.FermionModule
entries.docstring:
**The fermionic module of a gauge theory**: the product, over the fermionic species,
  of their value spaces. One element of it is a value of the entire fermionic content of
  the theory — the column of all the fermion fields — as opposed to
  `GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators`, which is a space of component *functions* and is
  infinite-dimensional. Since the species type is finite the product is also their direct
  sum.
entries.snippet: abbrev FermionModule : Type

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projFermionValue
entries.docstring: The component of a fermionic configuration in one species.
entries.snippet:
abbrev projFermionValue (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    T.FermionModule →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionValue i

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.inclFermionValue
entries.docstring:
The inclusion of one fermionic species into the fermionic module, extending a value
  of that species by zero in every other.
entries.snippet:
abbrev inclFermionValue (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    T.FermionValue i →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionModule

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projFermionValue_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma projFermionValue_apply (i : T.FermionSpecies) (v : T.FermionModule) :
    T.projFermionValue i v = v i

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projFermionValue_inclFermionValue_self
entries.snippet:
lemma projFermionValue_inclFermionValue_self (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (v : T.FermionValue i) : T.projFermionValue i (T.inclFermionValue i v) = v

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.projFermionValue_inclFermionValue_of_ne
entries.docstring:
A value of one species has no component in any other species: the inclusions of
  distinct species have disjoint supports.
entries.snippet:
lemma projFermionValue_inclFermionValue_of_ne {i j : T.FermionSpecies} (h : i ≠ j)
    (v : T.FermionValue j) : T.projFermionValue i (T.inclFermionValue j v) = 0

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.sum_inclFermionValue_proj
entries.docstring:
**A fermionic configuration is the sum of its species components**. The product over
  the species is their direct sum, the species type being finite, so nothing is lost in
  describing the fermionic content of the theory by one module.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_inclFermionValue_proj (v : T.FermionModule) :
    ∑ i, T.inclFermionValue i (v i) = v

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionModule_hom_ext
entries.docstring: Two linear maps out of the fermionic module agreeing on every species are equal.

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.finrank_fermionModule
entries.docstring:
**The dimension of the fermionic module is the sum of the dimensions of the
  species**, each species contributing the number of complex components of its
  multiplet.
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_fermionModule :
    Module.finrank ℂ T.FermionModule = ∑ i, Module.finrank ℂ (T.FermionValue i)

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.covGenerators
entries.docstring:
The covariant generators of the local field algebra: the included field-strength tower
  and the covariant matter towers of every species, unconjugated and conjugate, along all
  ordered tuples of directions.
entries.snippet: def covGenerators : Set T.LocalFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra
entries.docstring:
The covariant field algebra of a field datum: the complex unital subalgebra of its local
  field algebra generated by the covariant matter towers of every species, their conjugates,
  and the included field-strength tower.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def LocalCovFieldAlgebra : Subalgebra ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covDerivFieldStrength_mem
entries.snippet:
lemma covDerivFieldStrength_mem (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) : T.covDerivFieldStrength l μ ν φ ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covDerivFermion_mem
entries.snippet:
lemma covDerivFermion_mem (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) : T.covDerivFermion i l φ ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covDerivConjFermion_mem
entries.snippet:
lemma covDerivConjFermion_mem (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) :
    T.covDerivConjFermion i l φ ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covDerivBoson_mem
entries.snippet:
lemma covDerivBoson_mem (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) : T.covDerivBoson j l φ ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covDerivConjBoson_mem
entries.snippet:
lemma covDerivConjBoson_mem (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))) :
    T.covDerivConjBoson j l φ ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.fermionSymbol_zero_mem
entries.docstring:
The undifferentiated matter symbols lie in the covariant field algebra, as the case of
  zero covariant derivatives.
entries.snippet:
lemma fermionSymbol_zero_mem (i : T.FermionSpecies) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    T.fermionSymbol i 0 φ ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.conjFermionSymbol_zero_mem
entries.snippet:
lemma conjFermionSymbol_zero_mem (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) :
    T.conjFermionSymbol i 0 φ ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.bosonSymbol_zero_mem
entries.snippet:
lemma bosonSymbol_zero_mem (j : T.BosonSpecies) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) :
    T.bosonSymbol j 0 φ ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.conjBosonSymbol_zero_mem
entries.snippet:
lemma conjBosonSymbol_zero_mem (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))) :
    T.conjBosonSymbol j 0 φ ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covGenerators_cases
entries.docstring: Case analysis on the covariant generators.
entries.snippet:
lemma covGenerators_cases {P : T.LocalFieldAlgebra → Prop} {b : T.LocalFieldAlgebra}
    (hb : b ∈ T.covGenerators)
    (hF : ∀ (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤),
      P (T.covDerivFieldStrength l μ ν φ))
    (hψ : ∀ (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)), P (T.covDerivFermion i l φ))
    (hψc : ∀ (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))), P (T.covDerivConjFermion i l φ))
    (hφ : ∀ (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)), P (T.covDerivBoson j l φ))
    (hφc : ∀ (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))), P (T.covDerivConjBoson j l φ)) :
    P b

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.induction
entries.docstring:
The generation principle: a property holding on the covariant generators and on the
  scalars, and closed under sums and products, holds on the whole covariant field
  algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma induction {P : T.LocalFieldAlgebra → Prop} {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hF : ∀ (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤),
      P (T.covDerivFieldStrength l μ ν φ))
    (hψ : ∀ (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)), P (T.covDerivFermion i l φ))
    (hψc : ∀ (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))), P (T.covDerivConjFermion i l φ))
    (hφ : ∀ (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)), P (T.covDerivBoson j l φ))
    (hφc : ∀ (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))), P (T.covDerivConjBoson j l φ))
    (halg : ∀ z : ℂ, P (z • (1 : T.LocalFieldAlgebra)))
    (hadd : ∀ x y, P x → P y → P (x + y))
    (hmul : ∀ x y, P x → P y → P (x * y)) : P x

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mapsTo
entries.docstring:
An algebra endomorphism carrying the covariant generators into the covariant field
  algebra carries the whole covariant field algebra into itself.
entries.snippet:
lemma mapsTo (f : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra)
    (hgen : ∀ b ∈ T.covGenerators, f b ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    f x ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.algHom_ext
entries.docstring:
Two algebra maps out of the covariant field algebra agreeing on the covariant
  generators are equal. This is uniqueness only: the covariant field algebra is not free on
  its generators, so an assignment of their images does not by itself define a map.
entries.snippet:
lemma algHom_ext {B : Type} [Semiring B] [Algebra ℂ B]
    {f g : ↥T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] B}
    (h : ∀ b (hb : b ∈ T.covGenerators), f ⟨b, Algebra.subset_adjoin hb⟩
      = g ⟨b, Algebra.subset_adjoin hb⟩) : f = g

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covFieldStrength
entries.docstring:
The included field-strength tower `∇_l F_μν^φ`, as elements of the covariant field
  algebra.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def covFieldStrength (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

The covariant tower `∇_l ψ^φ` of a fermionic species, as elements of the covariant field

entries.snippet:
noncomputable def covFermion (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i) →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra where

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covConjFermion
entries.docstring:
The conjugate covariant tower of a fermionic species, as elements of the covariant field
  algebra.

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covBoson
entries.docstring: The covariant tower of a bosonic species, as elements of the covariant field algebra.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def covBoson (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j) →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra where

entries.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covConjBoson

The conjugate covariant tower of a bosonic species, as elements of the covariant field

entries.snippet:
noncomputable def covConjBoson (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
