entries.name: Representation.exteriorAlgebra_algebraMap
entries.snippet:
lemma exteriorAlgebra_algebraMap (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (r : R) :
    ρ.exteriorAlgebra g (algebraMap R (ExteriorAlgebra R M) r)
      = algebraMap R (ExteriorAlgebra R M) r

entries.name: ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorAlgebra_derivationOfLinear
entries.docstring:
Covariance of the derivation under the representation. If the representation
  carries each endomorphism of a family into a combination of the others on the generators,
  then it carries the derivation extending one into the same combination of the derivations
  extending the others on the whole exterior algebra. This is the shape the statement that
  the total derivative is a Lorentz vector takes; it is proved by induction rather than by
  algebra-map extensionality, a derivation not being an algebra map.
entries.snippet:
lemma exteriorAlgebra_derivationOfLinear {G κ : Type*} [Monoid G] [Fintype κ]
    (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (d : κ → M →ₗ[R] M) (μ : κ) (c : κ → R)
    (h : ∀ x, ρ g (d μ x) = ∑ a, c a • d a (ρ g x)) (y : ExteriorAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.exteriorAlgebra g (derivationOfLinear (d μ) y)
      = ∑ a, c a • derivationOfLinear (d a) (ρ.exteriorAlgebra g y)

entries.name: ExteriorAlgebra.algHom_exteriorAlgebra
entries.docstring:
An algebra map carries one representation to the other when the linear map it is
  determined by on the generators intertwines the two representations on them. Unlike the
  derivation statement this is pure extensionality of algebra maps, each group element
  acting by one; the hypotheses are stated pointwise so that the lemma can be applied
  without rewriting inside a large algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma algHom_exteriorAlgebra {N G : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Monoid G]
    (F : ExteriorAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R N) {f : M →ₗ[R] N}
    (hF : ∀ x, F (ι R x) = ι R (f x))
    {ρ : Representation R G M} {σ : Representation R G N} (g : G)
    (h : ∀ x, f (ρ g x) = σ g (f x)) (y : ExteriorAlgebra R M) :
    F (ρ.exteriorAlgebra g y) = σ.exteriorAlgebra g (F y)

entries.name: ExteriorAlgebra.mapEquiv
entries.docstring:
Transport of an exterior algebra along a linear equivalence, built from
  `ExteriorAlgebra.map` so that no `CliffordAlgebra` isometry has to be unfolded.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def mapEquiv {R M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) :
    ExteriorAlgebra R M ≃ₐ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R N

entries.name: ExteriorAlgebra.mapEquiv_apply_ι
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma mapEquiv_apply_ι {R M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) (x : M) :
    mapEquiv e (ExteriorAlgebra.ι R x) = ExteriorAlgebra.ι R (e x)

entries.name: Matrix.star_scalar
entries.docstring: The conjugate transpose of a scalar matrix is the scalar matrix of the star.
entries.snippet: lemma star_scalar [StarRing R] (x : R) : star (scalar n x) = scalar n (star x)

entries.name: Matrix.map_scalar
entries.docstring: An entrywise map fixing zero sends a scalar matrix to a scalar matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma map_scalar {S : Type*} [CommRing S] (f : R → S) (hf : f 0 = 0) (x : R) :
    (scalar n x).map f = scalar n (f x)

entries.name: Matrix.scalar_smul
entries.docstring: A scalar action passes into a scalar matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma scalar_smul {M : Type*} [Monoid M] [DistribMulAction M R] (c : M) (x : R) :
    scalar n (c • x) = c • scalar n x

entries.name: Matrix.scalar_eq_conj
entries.docstring: Conjugation by a unitary scalar fixes a scalar matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma scalar_eq_conj [StarRing R] {u : R} (hu : u * star u = 1) (x : R) :
    scalar n x = scalar n u * scalar n x * star (scalar n u)

entries.name: Matrix.scalarSelfAdjoint
entries.docstring: A self-adjoint element as a scalar matrix, real-linearly.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def scalarSelfAdjoint [StarRing R] [Algebra ℝ R] [StarModule ℝ R] :
    ↥(selfAdjoint R) →ₗ[ℝ] Matrix n n R where

entries.name: Matrix.scalarSelfAdjoint_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma scalarSelfAdjoint_apply [StarRing R] [Algebra ℝ R] [StarModule ℝ R]
    (a : ↥(selfAdjoint R)) : (scalarSelfAdjoint (n := n)) a = scalar n a.1

entries.name: Matrix.eq_scalar_fin_one
entries.docstring: A `1 × 1` matrix is the scalar matrix of its entry.
entries.snippet: lemma eq_scalar_fin_one (A : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) R) : A = scalar (Fin 1) (A 0 0)

entries.name: Physlib.Fin.sum_pi_succ_prod_smul
entries.docstring:
A sum over tuples of indices, weighted by one scalar factor per slot, split into the
  first slot and the remaining ones.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_pi_succ_prod_smul {R M ι : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    [Fintype ι] {n : ℕ} (c : Fin (n + 1) → ι → R) (X : (Fin (n + 1) → ι) → M) :
    ∑ q : Fin (n + 1) → ι, (∏ i, c i (q i)) • X q =
      ∑ b : ι, ∑ p : Fin n → ι, (c 0 b * ∏ i, c i.succ (p i)) • X (Fin.cons b p)

entries.name: Physlib.Fin.sum_filter_weight_succ
entries.docstring:
Peeling the first slot off a sum over the tuples of a prescribed total weight: the first
  slot takes its own weight `w b` and the remaining slots make up the rest. Each slot draws its
  letter from the same alphabet `ι`, `w` gives a letter its weight and the weights of the slots
  add; `f s` is the factor contributed by slot `s`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_filter_weight_succ {R ι : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [Fintype ι] {n : ℕ} (w : ι → ℤ)
    (f : Fin (n + 1) → ι → R) (m : ℤ) :
    ∑ q ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun q : Fin (n + 1) → ι => (∑ s, w (q s)) = m), ∏ s, f s (q s)
      = ∑ b : ι, f 0 b
          * ∑ q ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun q : Fin n → ι => (∑ s, w (q s)) = m - w b),
              ∏ s, f s.succ (q s)

entries.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule
entries.docstring: The degree-`w` part of `A` for `f`: the elements `x ∈ A` with `f x = monomial w x`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def homogeneousSubmodule (A : Subalgebra R B) (f : B →ₐ[R] Polynomial B)
    (w : ℕ) : Submodule R B

entries.name: Subalgebra.mem_homogeneousSubmodule_iff
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_homogeneousSubmodule_iff {w : ℕ} {x : B} :
    x ∈ A.homogeneousSubmodule f w ↔ x ∈ A ∧ f x = Polynomial.monomial w x

entries.name: Subalgebra.one_le_homogeneousSubmodule_zero
entries.docstring: The scalars have degree zero.
entries.snippet: lemma one_le_homogeneousSubmodule_zero : (1 : Submodule R B) ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f 0

entries.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_mul_le
entries.docstring: Degrees add under multiplication.
entries.snippet:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_mul_le (m n : ℕ) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f m * A.homogeneousSubmodule f n
      ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f (m + n)

entries.name: Submodule.productsOfDegree
entries.docstring:
The span of the products `D n₁ * ⋯ * D nₖ` whose degrees `deg n₁ + ⋯ + deg nₖ` add up
  to `w`. Every order of the factors occurs separately, and the empty product is `1`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def productsOfDegree (D : ℕ → Submodule R B) (deg : ℕ → ℕ) (w : ℕ) :
    Submodule R B

entries.name: Submodule.list_prod_le_productsOfDegree
entries.snippet:
lemma list_prod_le_productsOfDegree (l : List ℕ) :
    (l.map D).prod ≤ productsOfDegree D deg (l.map deg).sum

entries.name: Submodule.productsOfDegree_mul_le
entries.docstring: Concatenating products adds their degrees.
entries.snippet:
lemma productsOfDegree_mul_le (a b : ℕ) :
    productsOfDegree D deg a * productsOfDegree D deg b ≤ productsOfDegree D deg (a + b)

entries.name: Subalgebra.le_homogeneousSubmodule
entries.docstring: A generator in `D n` has degree `deg n`.
entries.snippet: lemma le_homogeneousSubmodule (n : ℕ) : D n ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f (deg n)

entries.name: Subalgebra.list_prod_le_homogeneousSubmodule
entries.docstring: A product of generators has the sum of their degrees.
entries.snippet:
lemma list_prod_le_homogeneousSubmodule (l : List ℕ) :
    (l.map D).prod ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f (l.map deg).sum

entries.name: Subalgebra.productsOfDegree_le_homogeneousSubmodule
entries.docstring: The products of generators of total degree `w` lie in the degree-`w` part of `A`.
entries.snippet:
lemma productsOfDegree_le_homogeneousSubmodule (w : ℕ) :
    productsOfDegree D deg w ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f w

entries.name: Subalgebra.coeff_mem_productsOfDegree
entries.docstring:
Every coefficient of `f x`, for `x ∈ A`, is a sum of products of generators: the one
  induction over the generation of `A`.
entries.snippet:
lemma coeff_mem_productsOfDegree {x : B} (hx : x ∈ A) (m : ℕ) :
    (f x).coeff m ∈ productsOfDegree D deg m

entries.name: Subalgebra.coeff_mem_homogeneousSubmodule
entries.docstring: The coefficient of `X ^ m` in `f x`, for `x ∈ A`, lies in the degree-`m` part of `A`.
entries.snippet:
lemma coeff_mem_homogeneousSubmodule {x : B} (hx : x ∈ A) (m : ℕ) :
    (f x).coeff m ∈ A.homogeneousSubmodule f m

entries.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree
entries.docstring:
The degree-`w` part of `A` is spanned by the products of generators, in every order,
  whose degrees add up to `w`.
entries.snippet:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree (w : ℕ) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f w = productsOfDegree D deg w

entries.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul
entries.docstring:
For positive `w`, the degree-`w` part of `A` is spanned by the products of a generator
  `D k` of degree at most `w` with the part of the remaining degree. The bound `n ≤ deg n`
  only makes the range of `k` finite.
entries.snippet:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul (hle : ∀ n, n ≤ deg n) {w : ℕ} (hw : 0 < w) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f w
      = ⨆ k ∈ (Finset.range (w + 1)).filter (fun k => deg k ≤ w),
          D k * A.homogeneousSubmodule f (w - deg k)

entries.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one
entries.docstring: If every generator has positive degree, degree zero is the scalar submodule.
entries.snippet:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < deg n) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f 0 = 1

entries.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul
entries.docstring:
If `n < deg n` for every `n`, the degree-`i` part of `A`, for positive `i`, is spanned
  by the generators of degree `i` and the products of two parts of positive degrees adding
  up to `i`. It follows from removing the leftmost generator: a generator of degree `i`
  leaves degree zero, which is the scalars.
entries.snippet:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul (hlt : ∀ n, n < deg n) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f i
      = (⨆ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun k : Fin i => deg k = i), D k)
        ⊔ (⨆ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin i × Fin i => (p.1 : ℕ) + (p.2 : ℕ) = i),
            A.homogeneousSubmodule f p.1 * A.homogeneousSubmodule f p.2)

entries.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot
entries.docstring:
If a set of degrees contains `0` and every `deg n` and is closed under addition, a
  degree outside it has zero part. This proves vanishing only: a degree in the set may
  still have zero part.
entries.snippet:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot (P : ℕ → Prop) (h0 : P 0) (hP : ∀ n, P (deg n))
    (hadd : ∀ a b, P a → P b → P (a + b)) {w : ℕ} (hw : ¬ P w) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f w = ⊥

entries.name: IsStableUnder
entries.docstring: A submodule carried into itself by every map of the family `σ`.
entries.snippet: def IsStableUnder (σ : G → B →ₗ[R] B) (V : Submodule R B) : Prop

entries.name: IsFixedBy
entries.docstring: A submodule fixed pointwise by every map of the family `σ`.
entries.snippet: def IsFixedBy (σ : G → B →ₗ[R] B) (V : Submodule R B) : Prop

entries.name: isStableUnder_iff_map
entries.docstring: Stability as an inclusion of images.
entries.snippet:
lemma isStableUnder_iff_map {V : Submodule R B} :
    IsStableUnder σ V ↔ ∀ g, Submodule.map (σ g) V ≤ V

entries.name: IsFixedBy.isStableUnder
entries.docstring: A pointwise-fixed submodule is stable.
entries.snippet: lemma IsFixedBy.isStableUnder {V : Submodule R B} (hV : IsFixedBy σ V) : IsStableUnder σ V

entries.name: IsFixedBy.sup
entries.docstring: A join of two pointwise-fixed submodules is pointwise fixed.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsFixedBy.sup {V V' : Submodule R B} (hV : IsFixedBy σ V) (hV' : IsFixedBy σ V') :
    IsFixedBy σ (V ⊔ V')

entries.name: isStableUnder_bot
entries.docstring: The zero submodule is stable.
entries.snippet: lemma isStableUnder_bot : IsStableUnder σ (⊥ : Submodule R B)

entries.name: IsStableUnder.sup
entries.docstring: A join of two stable submodules is stable.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsStableUnder.sup {V V' : Submodule R B} (hV : IsStableUnder σ V)
    (hV' : IsStableUnder σ V') : IsStableUnder σ (V ⊔ V')

entries.name: isStableUnder_iSup
entries.docstring:
An indexed join of stable submodules is stable. The index is a `Sort`, so this covers
  the bounded join `⨆ i ∈ s, V i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma isStableUnder_iSup {ι : Sort*} {V : ι → Submodule R B}
    (hV : ∀ i, IsStableUnder σ (V i)) : IsStableUnder σ (⨆ i, V i)

entries.name: isFixedBy_span_singleton
entries.docstring: The span of a fixed vector is pointwise fixed.
entries.snippet: lemma isFixedBy_span_singleton {b : B} (hb : ∀ g, σ g b = b) : IsFixedBy σ (R ∙ b)

entries.name: isFixedBy_iSup
entries.docstring: An indexed join of pointwise-fixed submodules is pointwise fixed.
entries.snippet:
lemma isFixedBy_iSup {ι : Sort*} {V : ι → Submodule R B} (hV : ∀ i, IsFixedBy σ (V i)) :
    IsFixedBy σ (⨆ i, V i)

entries.name: isFixedBy_span_range
entries.docstring: The span of a family of fixed vectors is pointwise fixed.
entries.snippet:
lemma isFixedBy_span_range {ι : Sort*} {T : ι → B} (hT : ∀ i g, σ g (T i) = T i) :
    IsFixedBy σ (Submodule.span R (Set.range T))

entries.name: isStableUnder_span_range
entries.docstring: The span of a family is stable when each map sends each member into the span.

entries.name: isStableUnder_span_range_of_sum
entries.docstring:
The span of a finite family is stable when each map sends each member to a combination
  of the family.

entries.name: IsStableUnder.mul
entries.docstring:
A product of two stable submodules of an algebra is stable under maps respecting
  multiplication.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsStableUnder.mul {R A : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A]
    {σ : G → A →ₗ[R] A} (hσ : ∀ g (a b : A), σ g (a * b) = σ g a * σ g b)
    {V V' : Submodule R A} (hV : IsStableUnder σ V) (hV' : IsStableUnder σ V') :
    IsStableUnder σ (V * V')

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo
entries.docstring: Every invariant of `V ⊔ S`, for `S` a `σ`-stable submodule, lies in `W ⊔ S`.
entries.snippet: def ReducesInvariantsTo (σ : G → B →ₗ[R] B) (V W : Submodule R B) : Prop

entries.name: reducesInvariantsTo_of_le
entries.docstring: A submodule reduces to any submodule containing it.
entries.snippet:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_of_le {V W : Submodule R B} (hVW : V ≤ W) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.mono_left
entries.docstring: A reduction restricts to a smaller source.
entries.snippet:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.mono_left {V V' W : Submodule R B} (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V' W)
    (hV : V ≤ V') : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.mono_right
entries.docstring: A reduction extends to a larger target.
entries.snippet:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.mono_right {V W W' : Submodule R B}
    (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W') (hW : W' ≤ W) : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.trans
entries.docstring: Successive reductions compose.
entries.snippet:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.trans {V W W' : Submodule R B} (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W)
    (hQ : ReducesInvariantsTo σ W W') : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W'

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.sup
entries.docstring:
Reductions of `V` and of a stable `V'` to a common stable target combine to a reduction of
  `V ⊔ V'`.
entries.snippet:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.sup {V V' W : Submodule R B} (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W)
    (hQ : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V' W) (hV' : IsStableUnder σ V') (hW : IsStableUnder σ W) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (V ⊔ V') W

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup
entries.docstring: Reductions of stable submodules to a common stable target combine over a finite set.
entries.snippet:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {V : ι → Submodule R B}
    {W : Submodule R B} (hP : ∀ i, ReducesInvariantsTo σ (V i) W)
    (hV : ∀ i, IsStableUnder σ (V i)) (hW : IsStableUnder σ W) (s : Finset ι) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (⨆ i ∈ s, V i) W

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup_of_biSup
entries.docstring:
A reduction of every join over a finite set of indices is a reduction of the join over the
  whole index type, which may be infinite: an element of the join lies in the join over finitely
  many of the summands. No stability is assumed of the summands or of the target; the remainder
  is stable, as in every reduction.

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup
entries.docstring:
Reductions of stable submodules to a common stable target combine over any index type,
  finite or not: `biSup` combines them over every finite set of indices, and
  `iSup_of_biSup` passes to the whole join.

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.comp
entries.docstring:
A reduction for the subfamily `σ ∘ ι` is a reduction for `σ`: an invariant of `σ` is an
  invariant of the subfamily, and a `σ`-stable submodule is stable under the subfamily.
entries.snippet:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.comp {G' : Type*} (ι : G' → G) {V W : Submodule R B}
    (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g' => σ (ι g')) V W) : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

entries.name: reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul
entries.docstring:
A submodule on which one map of the family acts by a scalar `μ ≠ 1` reduces to `⊥`. An
  invariant `v + s` of `V ⊔ S` has `(μ - 1) • v = s - σ g s`, which lies in `S`, and so does
  `v`. Of the stability of `S` only stability under `σ g` is used.
entries.snippet:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul (g : G) {μ : K} (hμ : μ ≠ 1)
    {V : Submodule K B} (hV : ∀ v ∈ V, σ g v = μ • v) : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V ⊥

entries.name: IsStableUnder.mem_sup_of_quotient
entries.docstring:
An invariant of `V ⊔ S` lies in `W ⊔ S` when every invariant of the image of `V` in
  `B ⧸ S` lies in the image of `W`.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsStableUnder.mem_sup_of_quotient (hS : IsStableUnder σ S)
    (hclass : ∀ x ∈ V.map S.mkQ, (∀ g, S.mapQ S (σ g) (hS g) x = x) → x ∈ W.map S.mkQ)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ g, σ g x = x) : x ∈ W ⊔ S

entries.name: reducesInvariantsTo_of_quotient
entries.docstring:
`V` reduces to `W` when, for every stable `S`, every invariant of the image of `V` in
  `B ⧸ S` lies in the image of `W`.
entries.snippet:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_of_quotient
    (hclass : ∀ S : Submodule R B, ∀ hS : IsStableUnder σ S, ∀ x ∈ V.map S.mkQ,
      (∀ g, S.mapQ S (σ g) (hS g) x = x) → x ∈ W.map S.mkQ) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

entries.name: IsFixedBy.exists_add_of_mem_sup
entries.docstring:
An invariant of `W ⊔ S`, for `W` pointwise fixed, is an element of `W` plus an invariant
  element of `S`.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsFixedBy.exists_add_of_mem_sup (hW : IsFixedBy σ W) {x : B} (hx : x ∈ W ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g, σ g x = x) : ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ y ∈ S, x = w + y ∧ ∀ g, σ g y = y

entries.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_forall_eq_self_iff
entries.docstring:
A reduction of `V` to a pointwise-fixed `W ≤ V` describes the invariants of `V ⊔ S`, for
  `S` stable, exactly: they are the elements of `W` plus an invariant element of `S`. This is
  the form in which a classification is stated.
entries.snippet:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_forall_eq_self_iff (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W)
    (hWV : W ≤ V) (hW : IsFixedBy σ W) (hS : IsStableUnder σ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ V ⊔ S ∧ ∀ g, σ g x = x) ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g, σ g y = y) ∧ x - y ∈ W

entries.name: IsStableUnder.exists_add_of_quotient
entries.docstring:
Quotient to remainder: when every invariant of the image of `V` in `B ⧸ S` lies in the
  image of a pointwise-fixed `W`, an invariant of `V ⊔ S` is an element of `W` plus an
  invariant element of `S`.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsStableUnder.exists_add_of_quotient (hS : IsStableUnder σ S) (hW : IsFixedBy σ W)
    (hclass : ∀ x ∈ V.map S.mkQ, (∀ g, S.mapQ S (σ g) (hS g) x = x) → x ∈ W.map S.mkQ)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ g, σ g x = x) :
    ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ y ∈ S, x = w + y ∧ ∀ g, σ g y = y

entries.name: IsStableUnder.exists_smul_add_of_quotient
entries.docstring:
Quotient to remainder for a single fixed vector `v`: when every invariant of the image of
  `V` in `B ⧸ S` is a multiple of the class of `v`, an invariant of `V ⊔ S` is a multiple of
  `v` plus an invariant element of `S`.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsStableUnder.exists_smul_add_of_quotient (hS : IsStableUnder σ S) {v : B}
    (hv : ∀ g, σ g v = v)
    (hclass : ∀ x ∈ V.map S.mkQ, (∀ g, S.mapQ S (σ g) (hS g) x = x) → ∃ c : R, x = c • S.mkQ v)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ g, σ g x = x) :
    ∃ c : R, ∃ y ∈ S, x = c • v + y ∧ ∀ g, σ g y = y

entries.name: InvariantReductionToSpan
entries.docstring:
A stable submodule `V` together with a fixed vector such that, for every stable `S`, every
  invariant of `V ⊔ S` is a multiple of that vector plus an element of `S`. The vector need not
  be nonzero or lie in `V`.
entries.snippet:
structure InvariantReductionToSpan (σ : G → B →ₗ[R] B) (V : Submodule R B) where
  spanningVector : B
  stable : IsStableUnder σ V
  spanningVector_fixed : ∀ g, σ g spanningVector = spanningVector
  reduce : ∀ S : Submodule R B, IsStableUnder σ S → ∀ x ∈ V ⊔ S, (∀ g, σ g x = x) →
    ∃ c : R, ∃ y ∈ S, x = c • spanningVector + y

entries.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.reducesInvariantsTo
entries.docstring: The submodule reduces to the span of the spanning vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo (r : InvariantReductionToSpan σ V) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ V (R ∙ r.spanningVector)

entries.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.reducesInvariantsTo_iSup
entries.docstring:
A family of reductions to spans, over any index type, reduces the join of the submodules to
  the span of the spanning vectors.
entries.snippet:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_iSup {κ : Type*} {V : κ → Submodule R B}
    (r : ∀ k, InvariantReductionToSpan σ (V k)) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (⨆ k, V k)
      (Submodule.span R (Set.range fun k => (r k).spanningVector))

entries.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.ofReducesInvariantsTo
entries.docstring: The reduction of a stable submodule to the span of a fixed vector.
entries.snippet:
def ofReducesInvariantsTo (hV : IsStableUnder σ V) (v : B) (hv : ∀ g, σ g v = v)
    (h : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V (R ∙ v)) : InvariantReductionToSpan σ V where

entries.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.ofFixed
entries.docstring: The span of a fixed vector reduces to itself.
entries.snippet:
def ofFixed (b : B) (hb : ∀ g, σ g b = b) :
    InvariantReductionToSpan σ (R ∙ b) where

entries.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.ofFixedFamily
entries.docstring:
The span of a nonempty family whose members all equal one fixed vector reduces to the
  span of that vector.

entries.name: Submodule.mapQ_mkQ_eq_sum_smul
entries.docstring:
A map moving each member of a family by a matrix moves their classes modulo a submodule
  that it preserves by the same matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma Submodule.mapQ_mkQ_eq_sum_smul {R B ι : Type*} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup B] [Module R B]
    [Fintype ι] (S : Submodule R B) {f : B →ₗ[R] B} (hS : ∀ y ∈ S, f y ∈ S) {T : ι → B}
    {M : Matrix ι ι R} {l : ι} (hf : f (T l) = ∑ a, M a l • T a) :
    S.mapQ S f hS (S.mkQ (T l)) = ∑ a, M a l • S.mkQ (T a)

entries.name: reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq
entries.docstring:
A family moved by matrices whose conjugate transposes are among them reduces to the
  combinations of any submodule `E` of coefficient vectors containing every vector fixed by
  all the matrices.
entries.snippet:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq (T : ι → B) (M : G → Matrix ι ι ℂ)
    (hT : ∀ g l, σ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a) (hM : ∀ g, ∃ g', M g' = (M g)ᴴ)
    (E : Submodule ℂ (ι → ℂ)) (hE : ∀ c, (∀ g, M g *ᵥ c = c) → c ∈ E) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T))
      (E.map (Fintype.linearCombination ℂ T))

entries.name: reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_mulVec_eq
entries.docstring:
The form of `reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq` when no nonzero coefficient vector is
  fixed: the span reduces to `⊥`.
entries.snippet:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_mulVec_eq (T : ι → B) (M : G → Matrix ι ι ℂ)
    (hT : ∀ g l, σ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a) (hM : ∀ g, ∃ g', M g' = (M g)ᴴ)
    (hE : ∀ c, (∀ g, M g *ᵥ c = c) → c = 0) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)) ⊥

entries.name: reducesInvariantsTo_span_singleton_of_mulVec_eq
entries.docstring:
The form of `reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq` when every fixed coefficient vector is a
  multiple of `e`: the span reduces to the span of the combination with coefficients `e`.
entries.snippet:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_span_singleton_of_mulVec_eq (T : ι → B) (M : G → Matrix ι ι ℂ)
    (hT : ∀ g l, σ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a) (hM : ∀ g, ∃ g', M g' = (M g)ᴴ)
    (e : ι → ℂ) (hE : ∀ c, (∀ g, M g *ᵥ c = c) → ∃ z : ℂ, c = z • e) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)) (ℂ ∙ ∑ i, e i • T i)

entries.name: cast_leviCivitaSymbol
entries.docstring:
The symbol as a determinant over any commutative ring, the integer determinant carried
along the ring map from `ℤ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma cast_leviCivitaSymbol (g : ι → ι) :
    ((leviCivitaSymbol g : ℤ) : R)
      = (Matrix.of fun i j : ι => if g i = j then (1 : R) else 0).det

entries.name: det_eq_sum_perm_prod
entries.docstring: The Leibniz formula with the permutation moving the column index.
entries.snippet:
private lemma det_eq_sum_perm_prod (X : Matrix ι ι R) :
    X.det = ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm ι, ((Equiv.Perm.sign σ : ℤ) : R) * ∏ i, X i (σ i)

entries.name: sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod
entries.docstring:
Contracted against the rows of `M` selected by `a`, the symbol gives `det M` times the
symbol of `a`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod (M : Matrix ι ι R) (a : ι → ι) :
    ∑ g : ι → ι, ((leviCivitaSymbol g : ℤ) : R) * ∏ i, M (a i) (g i)
      = M.det * ((leviCivitaSymbol a : ℤ) : R)

entries.name: Submodule.map_span_range
entries.docstring: The image of the span of a family is the span of the images.
entries.snippet:
lemma Submodule.map_span_range {R B B' : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid B] [Module R B]
    [AddCommMonoid B'] [Module R B'] {ι : Sort*} (f : B →ₗ[R] B') (T : ι → B) :
    (Submodule.span R (Set.range T)).map f = Submodule.span R (Set.range fun i => f (T i))

entries.name: Fintype.sum_sum_mul_smul
entries.docstring:
Contracting the components against coefficients moved by a matrix is the original
  combination of the matrix-moved components.
entries.snippet:
lemma Fintype.sum_sum_mul_smul (M : ι → κ → R) (c : κ → R) (T : ι → B) :
    ∑ a, (∑ d, c d * M a d) • T a = ∑ d, c d • ∑ a, M a d • T a

entries.name: LinearMap.map_sum_smul_of_forall_eq
entries.docstring:
A linear map that moves each component of a family by a matrix moves a combination of the
  components by that matrix acting on the coefficients, with the free index first.
entries.snippet:
lemma LinearMap.map_sum_smul_of_forall_eq (φ : B →ₗ[R] B') (T : ι → B) (T' : κ → B')
    (M : κ → ι → R) (hT : ∀ l, φ (T l) = ∑ a, M a l • T' a) (c : ι → R) :
    φ (∑ l, c l • T l) = ∑ a, (∑ l, c l * M a l) • T' a

entries.name: LinearMap.map_sum_smul_eq_sum_mulVec_smul
entries.docstring:
The matrix form of `LinearMap.map_sum_smul_of_forall_eq`: a linear map moving `T l` to
  `∑ a, M a l • T' a` moves the combination with coefficients `c` to the combination with
  coefficients `M *ᵥ c`.
entries.snippet:
lemma LinearMap.map_sum_smul_eq_sum_mulVec_smul (φ : B →ₗ[R] B') (T : ι → B) (T' : κ → B')
    (M : Matrix κ ι R) (hT : ∀ l, φ (T l) = ∑ a, M a l • T' a) (c : ι → R) :
    φ (∑ l, c l • T l) = ∑ a, (M *ᵥ c) a • T' a

entries.name: Fintype.exists_invariant_coeff_of_adjoint_mem
entries.docstring:
A vector of the span of `T` fixed by every `φ g` is the combination of coefficients fixed
  by every `A g`, where `φ g` moves combinations by moving their coefficients with `A g`. The
  one condition on `A` is that for every `g` some `g'` acts as the adjoint of `g` for the
  standard inner product on coefficients; neither the `φ g` nor the `A g` need form a
  representation, and `B` carries no inner product. The components may be dependent, so the
  coefficients need not be unique: the proof takes the part of any coefficients orthogonal to
  those contracting to `0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma Fintype.exists_invariant_coeff_of_adjoint_mem {ι G B : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [AddCommGroup B] [Module ℂ B] (T : ι → B) (φ : G → B →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (A : G → (ι → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] (ι → ℂ))
    (hφ : ∀ (g : G) (c : ι → ℂ), φ g (∑ i, c i • T i) = ∑ i, A g c i • T i)
    (hA : ∀ g : G, ∃ g' : G, ∀ u v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι,
      ⟪u, WithLp.toLp 2 (A g v.ofLp)⟫_ℂ = ⟪WithLp.toLp 2 (A g' u.ofLp), v⟫_ℂ)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)) (hinv : ∀ g, φ g x = x) :
    ∃ c : ι → ℂ, x = ∑ i, c i • T i ∧ ∀ g, A g c = c

entries.name: Fintype.exists_mulVec_eq_of_conjTranspose_mem
entries.docstring:
The matrix form of `Fintype.exists_invariant_coeff_of_adjoint_mem`: when each `φ g` moves
  the family by a matrix `M g`, and the conjugate transpose of each `M g` is some `M g'`, a
  vector of the span fixed by every `φ g` is the combination of a coefficient vector fixed by
  every `M g`.
entries.snippet:
lemma Fintype.exists_mulVec_eq_of_conjTranspose_mem {ι G B : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [AddCommGroup B] [Module ℂ B] (T : ι → B) (φ : G → B →ₗ[ℂ] B) (M : G → Matrix ι ι ℂ)
    (hT : ∀ g l, φ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a) (hM : ∀ g, ∃ g', M g' = (M g)ᴴ)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)) (hinv : ∀ g, φ g x = x) :
    ∃ c : ι → ℂ, x = ∑ i, c i • T i ∧ ∀ g, M g *ᵥ c = c

entries.name: LinearMap.range_eq_span_range_basis
entries.docstring: The range of a linear map is the span of the images of a basis.
entries.snippet:
lemma LinearMap.range_eq_span_range_basis {ι R M N : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
    [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    LinearMap.range f = Submodule.span R (Set.range fun i => f (b i))

entries.name: Submodule.mul_le_of_le_span_range
entries.docstring:
A product of two submodules, each inside the span of a family, lies in any submodule
  containing the products of the members of the two families.
entries.snippet:
lemma Submodule.mul_le_of_le_span_range {ι κ R A : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A]
    [Algebra R A] {V V' X : Submodule R A} {a : ι → A} {b : κ → A}
    (hV : V ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range a)) (hV' : V' ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range b))
    (hX : ∀ i j, a i * b j ∈ X) : V * V' ≤ X

entries.name: Submodule.mul_mul_le_of_le_span_range
entries.docstring: The three-factor form of `Submodule.mul_le_of_le_span_range`.
entries.snippet:
lemma Submodule.mul_mul_le_of_le_span_range {ι κ ν R A : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A]
    [Algebra R A] {V V' V'' X : Submodule R A} {a : ι → A} {b : κ → A} {c : ν → A}
    (hV : V ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range a)) (hV' : V' ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range b))
    (hV'' : V'' ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range c)) (hX : ∀ i j k, a i * (b j * c k) ∈ X) :
    V * (V' * V'') ≤ X

entries.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.pi_mono
entries.docstring:
The finite product measure `Measure.pi μ` is monotone in the family of measures `μ`:
if `μ i ≤ ν i` for every `i`, then `Measure.pi μ ≤ Measure.pi ν`.
entries.snippet:
lemma pi_mono {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {α : ι → Type*} [∀ i, MeasurableSpace (α i)]
    {μ ν : (i : ι) → Measure (α i)} (h : ∀ i, μ i ≤ ν i) : Measure.pi μ ≤ Measure.pi ν

entries.name: ConjModule.«instance@e302da93»
entries.snippet: instance : Ring (ConjModule A)

entries.name: ConjModule.instAlgebra
entries.docstring:
The conjugate module of a `k`-algebra is a `k`-algebra: the same ring, with scalars
acting through `star`.
entries.snippet: instance instAlgebra [Algebra k A] : Algebra k (ConjModule A)

entries.name: conjDualEquiv
entries.docstring:
The canonical conjugate-linear equivalence between the dual of a module `M` and
  the dual of its conjugate.
entries.snippet: def conjDualEquiv : Module.Dual k M ≃ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] Module.Dual k (ConjModule M) where

entries.name: Representation.conj
entries.docstring:
The conjugate of a representation `ρ` of `G` on `M`: the same maps `ρ g`, acting on
`ConjModule M` through `conjEquiv`.
entries.snippet:
def _root_.Representation.conj {G} [Group G] (ρ : Representation k G M) :
    Representation k G (ConjModule M) where

entries.name: Representation.conj_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.Representation.conj_apply {G} [Group G] (ρ : Representation k G M) (g : G)
    (m : ConjModule M) :
    ρ.conj g m = conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M) (ρ g ((conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M)).symm m))

entries.name: Representation.conj_trivial_dual_apply
entries.docstring: The dual of the conjugate of the trivial representation acts trivially.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.Representation.conj_trivial_dual_apply {G : Type*} [Group G] (g : G)
    (φ : Module.Dual k (ConjModule M)) :
    ((Representation.trivial k G M).conj).dual g φ = φ

entries.name: ConjModule.map
entries.docstring:
Functoriality of conjugation: a `k`-linear map induces a `k`-linear map of the
conjugate modules, given by the same underlying function.
entries.snippet: def map (f : M →ₗ[k] N) : ConjModule M →ₗ[k] ConjModule N where

entries.name: ConjModule.map_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma map_apply (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (x : ConjModule M) : map f x = f x

entries.name: ConjModule.prodEquiv
entries.docstring:
**Conjugation commutes with finite products.** The conjugate of a product is the product
of the conjugates, by the identity underlying function: the twisted scalar action is applied
componentwise.
entries.snippet: def prodEquiv : ConjModule (M × N) ≃ₗ[k] ConjModule M × ConjModule N where

entries.name: ConjModule.prodEquiv_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma prodEquiv_apply (x : ConjModule (M × N)) :
    prodEquiv (k := k) x = (map (LinearMap.fst k M N) x, map (LinearMap.snd k M N) x)

entries.name: ConjModule.piEquiv
entries.docstring:
**Conjugation commutes with arbitrary products.** The conjugate of a product of a
family of modules is the product of their conjugates, by the identity underlying
function: the twisted scalar action is applied componentwise, so no finiteness of the
index type is needed.
entries.snippet: def piEquiv : ConjModule (∀ i, P i) ≃ₗ[k] ∀ i, ConjModule (P i) where

entries.name: ConjModule.piEquiv_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma piEquiv_apply (x : ConjModule (∀ i, P i)) (i : ι) :
    (piEquiv P : ConjModule (∀ i, P i) ≃ₗ[k] ∀ i, ConjModule (P i)) x i
      = map (k := k) (LinearMap.proj i) x

entries.name: ConjModule.piEquiv_symm_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma piEquiv_symm_apply (x : ∀ i, ConjModule (P i)) (i : ι) :
    map (k := k) (LinearMap.proj i)
        ((piEquiv P : ConjModule (∀ i, P i) ≃ₗ[k] ∀ i, ConjModule (P i)).symm x) = x i

entries.name: ConjModule.instFinite
entries.docstring:
The conjugate module of a finite free module is finite: the conjugated basis
`Basis.conj` is indexed by the same type.
entries.snippet:
instance instFinite [Module.Free k M] [Module.Finite k M] :
    Module.Finite k (ConjModule M)

entries.name: ConjModule.tensorHom
entries.docstring:
The canonical `k`-linear map `ConjModule M ⊗ ConjModule N → ConjModule (M ⊗ N)`,
the identity on pure tensors.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def tensorHom : ConjModule M ⊗[k] ConjModule N →ₗ[k] ConjModule (M ⊗[k] N)

entries.name: ConjModule.tensorHom_tmul
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma tensorHom_tmul (m : ConjModule M) (n : ConjModule N) :
    tensorHom (k := k) (m ⊗ₜ[k] n)
      = conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M ⊗[k] N)
        ((conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M)).symm m ⊗ₜ[k] (conjEquiv (k := k) (M := N)).symm n)

entries.name: ConjModule.tensorInv
entries.docstring:
The inverse map `ConjModule (M ⊗ N) → ConjModule M ⊗ ConjModule N`, again the identity
on pure tensors. A `k`-linear map out of `ConjModule X` is the same data as a `k`-linear
map into `ConjModule` of the target, which is what `map` and `involution` package here.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def tensorInv : ConjModule (M ⊗[k] N) →ₗ[k] ConjModule M ⊗[k] ConjModule N

entries.name: ConjModule.tensorEquiv
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def tensorEquiv :
    ConjModule M ⊗[k] ConjModule N ≃ₗ[k] ConjModule (M ⊗[k] N)

entries.name: ConjModule.tensorEquiv_tmul
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma tensorEquiv_tmul (m : ConjModule M) (n : ConjModule N) :
    tensorEquiv (k := k) (m ⊗ₜ[k] n)
      = conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M ⊗[k] N)
        ((conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M)).symm m ⊗ₜ[k] (conjEquiv (k := k) (M := N)).symm n)

entries.name: ConjModule.tensorEquiv_symm_conjEquiv_tmul
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma tensorEquiv_symm_conjEquiv_tmul (m : M) (n : N) :
    (tensorEquiv (k := k) (M := M) (N := N)).symm
        (conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M ⊗[k] N) (m ⊗ₜ[k] n))
      = conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M) m ⊗ₜ[k] conjEquiv (k := k) (M := N) n

entries.name: ConjModule.endConj
entries.docstring:
A linear endomorphism read on the conjugate module: the same underlying map,
  through the identity `conjEquiv`. Conjugating twists nothing at the level of the
  additive group, so all structural identities (`comp`, `add`, `neg`, sums) hold
  definitionally.

entries.name: ConjModule.endConj_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma endConj_apply {k : Type*} [CommRing k] [StarRing k] {M : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M] (f : M →ₗ[k] M) (v : ConjModule M) :
    ConjModule.endConj f v =
      conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M) (f ((conjEquiv (k := k) (M := M)).symm v))

entries.name: ConjModule.endConj_id
ConjModule.endConj_comp
ConjModule.endConj_add
ConjModule.endConj_neg
ConjModule.endConj_multiset_sum
entries.snippet:
lemma endConj_multiset_sum {k : Type*} [CommRing k] [StarRing k]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M] (S : Multiset (M →ₗ[k] M)) :
    ConjModule.endConj S.sum = (S.map ConjModule.endConj).sum

entries.name: ConjModule.endConj_real_smul
entries.docstring:
Conjugation of endomorphisms commutes with real scalars: the star on the
  conjugated complex scalar is invisible on the reals.
entries.snippet:
lemma endConj_real_smul {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℂ M]
    (r : ℝ) (f : M →ₗ[ℂ] M) :
    ConjModule.endConj (r • f) = r • ConjModule.endConj f

entries.name: Multiset.sum_antidiagonal_assoc
entries.docstring:
Coassociativity of antidiagonal sums: summing over `s = u + v` and then `u = x + y`
  is summing over `s = x + t` and then `t = y + v`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_antidiagonal_assoc {ι M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (s : Multiset ι) (h : Multiset ι → Multiset ι → Multiset ι → M) :
    (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
      (p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q => h q.1 q.2 p.2).sum).sum =
    (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
      (p.2.antidiagonal.map fun q => h p.1 q.1 q.2).sum).sum

entries.name: Multiset.sum_antidiagonal_exchange
entries.docstring:
The exchange law of doubly-split antidiagonal sums: splitting `s = u + v` and then
  `u = x + y`, `v = z + w` is, with the middle parts exchanged, splitting `s = u' + v'`
  and then `u' = x + z`, `v' = y + w`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_antidiagonal_exchange {ι M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (s : Multiset ι) (h : Multiset ι → Multiset ι → Multiset ι → Multiset ι → M) :
    (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
      (p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q =>
        (p.2.antidiagonal.map fun r => h q.1 q.2 r.1 r.2).sum).sum).sum =
    (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
      (p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q =>
        (p.2.antidiagonal.map fun r => h q.1 r.1 q.2 r.2).sum).sum).sum

entries.name: Multiset.sum_linearMap_apply
entries.docstring: A multiset sum of linear maps, applied: the sum of the applications.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_linearMap_apply {R M N : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R M] [Module R N] (S : Multiset (M →ₗ[R] N)) (x : M) :
    S.sum x = (S.map fun f => f x).sum

entries.name: Multiset.tmul_sum
entries.docstring: A pure tensor against a multiset sum distributes over the sum.
entries.snippet:
lemma tmul_sum {R M N : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R M] [Module R N] (m : M) (S : Multiset N) :
    m ⊗ₜ[R] S.sum = (S.map fun n => m ⊗ₜ[R] n).sum

entries.name: Multiset.sum_antidiagonal_swap
entries.docstring: Antidiagonal sums are symmetric under swapping the two parts.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_antidiagonal_swap {ι M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (s : Multiset ι) (h : Multiset ι → Multiset ι → M) :
    (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => h p.1 p.2).sum =
    (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => h p.2 p.1).sum

entries.name: Multiset.sum_map_neg''
entries.docstring: A multiset sum of negations is the negation of the sum.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_map_neg'' {ι M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M]
    (s : Multiset ι) (f : ι → M) :
    (s.map fun i => -f i).sum = -(s.map f).sum

entries.name: Multiset.sum_map_finsetSum
entries.docstring: The exchange of a finite sum with a multiset sum.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_map_finsetSum {α β M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (m : Multiset α) (t : Finset β) (f : β → α → M) :
    (m.map fun a => ∑ b ∈ t, f b a).sum = ∑ b ∈ t, (m.map (f b)).sum

entries.name: Multiset.fst_le_of_mem_antidiagonal
entries.docstring: The first part of a splitting of `s` is a sub-multiset of `s`.
entries.snippet:
lemma fst_le_of_mem_antidiagonal {ι : Type*} {s : Multiset ι} {p : Multiset ι × Multiset ι}
    (hp : p ∈ s.antidiagonal) : p.1 ≤ s

entries.name: Multiset.snd_le_of_mem_antidiagonal
entries.docstring: The second part of a splitting of `s` is a sub-multiset of `s`.
entries.snippet:
lemma snd_le_of_mem_antidiagonal {ι : Type*} {s : Multiset ι} {p : Multiset ι × Multiset ι}
    (hp : p ∈ s.antidiagonal) : p.2 ≤ s

entries.name: Multiset.sum_antidiagonal_eq_of_fst_ne_zero
entries.docstring:
A sum over the antidiagonal of a family vanishing off `p.1 = 0` collapses to the
  single term at `(0, s)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_antidiagonal_eq_of_fst_ne_zero {ι M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (s : Multiset ι) (F : Multiset ι × Multiset ι → M)
    (hF : ∀ p ∈ s.antidiagonal, p.1 ≠ 0 → F p = 0) :
    (s.antidiagonal.map F).sum = F (0, s)

entries.name: Multiset.sum_antidiagonal_eq_of_snd_ne_zero
entries.docstring:
A sum over the antidiagonal of a family vanishing off `p.2 = 0` collapses to the
  single term at `(s, 0)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_antidiagonal_eq_of_snd_ne_zero {ι M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (s : Multiset ι) (F : Multiset ι × Multiset ι → M)
    (hF : ∀ p ∈ s.antidiagonal, p.2 ≠ 0 → F p = 0) :
    (s.antidiagonal.map F).sum = F (s, 0)

entries.name: Multiset.sum_antidiagonal_middle_exchange
entries.docstring: The exchange of the second and third slot in a nested antidiagonal sum.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_antidiagonal_middle_exchange {ι M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (s : Multiset ι) (h : Multiset ι → Multiset ι → Multiset ι → M) :
    (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        (p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q => h q.1 q.2 p.2).sum).sum
      = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        (p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q => h q.1 p.2 q.2).sum).sum

entries.name: MvPolynomial.eval_aeval
entries.docstring:
Evaluation of a substitution of a multivariate polynomial: substitution followed
  by evaluation is evaluation at the evaluated substituents.
entries.snippet:
lemma eval_aeval (x : I → R) (g : I → MvPolynomial I R) (p : MvPolynomial I R) :
    eval x (aeval g p) = eval (fun i => eval x (g i)) p

entries.name: MvPolynomial.aeval_update_zero_eq_of_forall_aeval_add_eq
entries.docstring:
A polynomial invariant under all translations of a fixed variable is unchanged
  by setting that variable to zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma aeval_update_zero_eq_of_forall_aeval_add_eq (Q : MvPolynomial I R) (j : I)
    (hQ : ∀ r : R, aeval (fun i => X i + C (if i = j then r else 0)) Q = Q) :
    aeval (fun i => if i = j then 0 else X i) Q = Q

entries.name: MvPolynomial.notMem_vars_of_forall_aeval_add_eq
entries.docstring:
A polynomial invariant under all translations of a fixed variable does not
  involve that variable.
entries.snippet:
lemma notMem_vars_of_forall_aeval_add_eq (Q : MvPolynomial I R) (j : I)
    (hQ : ∀ r : R, aeval (fun i => X i + C (if i = j then r else 0)) Q = Q) :
    j ∉ Q.vars

entries.name: MvPolynomial.mem_adjoin_range_X_sub_X_of_forall_aeval_add_eq
entries.docstring:
A multivariate polynomial over an infinite integral domain that is invariant
  under simultaneously translating, for every fiber of an idempotent map `π` on the
  variables, all the variables in that fiber by a common constant, is a polynomial
  in the differences `X i - X (π i)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_adjoin_range_X_sub_X_of_forall_aeval_add_eq (π : I → I)
    (hπ : ∀ i, π (π i) = π i) (P : MvPolynomial I R)
    (hP : ∀ (i₀ : I) (r : R),
      aeval (fun i => X i + C (if π i = π i₀ then r else 0)) P = P) :
    P ∈ Algebra.adjoin R (Set.range fun i => (X i - X (π i) : MvPolynomial I R))

entries.name: Polynomial.eq_zero_of_forall_eval_algebraMap_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
A polynomial with coefficients in an algebra over an infinite field vanishes as soon as
  it vanishes at the image of every scalar. Linear functionals separate the coefficients,
  and over an infinite field a polynomial is determined by its values.

entries.name: Polynomial.ext_of_forall_eval_algebraMap
entries.docstring:
Two polynomials with coefficients in an algebra over an infinite field are equal as soon
  as they agree at the image of every scalar.

entries.name: Polynomial.mapCoeffs
entries.docstring:
The polynomial obtained by applying a function to every coefficient. Unlike
  `Polynomial.map` this needs no multiplicativity, so it applies to derivations.

  The argument is a bare function rather than a linear map: on an algebra built as a tensor
  product the module structure coming from the algebra and the one coming from the tensor
  product are equal but not syntactically so, and bundling would force the caller to
  reconcile them. The properties needed are taken as hypotheses instead.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def mapCoeffs {A : Type*} [Semiring A] (f : A → A) (p : Polynomial A) :
    Polynomial A

entries.name: Polynomial.coeff_mapCoeffs
entries.snippet:
lemma coeff_mapCoeffs {A : Type*} [Semiring A] {f : A → A} (hf0 : f 0 = 0)
    (p : Polynomial A) (n : ℕ) : (mapCoeffs f p).coeff n = f (p.coeff n)

entries.name: Polynomial.mapCoeffs_zero
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma mapCoeffs_zero {A : Type*} [Semiring A] (f : A → A) : mapCoeffs f 0 = 0

entries.name: Polynomial.mapCoeffs_monomial
entries.snippet:
lemma mapCoeffs_monomial {A : Type*} [Semiring A] {f : A → A} (hf0 : f 0 = 0)
    (n : ℕ) (a : A) :
    mapCoeffs f (Polynomial.monomial n a) = Polynomial.monomial n (f a)

entries.name: Polynomial.mapCoeffs_add
entries.snippet:
lemma mapCoeffs_add {A : Type*} [Semiring A] {f : A → A} (hf0 : f 0 = 0)
    (hadd : ∀ a b : A, f (a + b) = f a + f b) (p q : Polynomial A) :
    mapCoeffs f (p + q) = mapCoeffs f p + mapCoeffs f q

entries.name: Polynomial.eval_algebraMap_mapAlgHom
entries.docstring:
Evaluation at a scalar commutes with pushing a polynomial along an algebra map: an
  algebra map fixes the scalars.
entries.snippet:
lemma eval_algebraMap_mapAlgHom {k A B : Type*} [CommSemiring k] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B] (f : A →ₐ[k] B) (p : Polynomial A) (c : k) :
    (Polynomial.mapAlgHom f p).eval (algebraMap k B c) = f (p.eval (algebraMap k A c))

entries.name: Polynomial.eval_algebraMap_mapCoeffs
entries.docstring:
Evaluation at a scalar commutes with applying a linear map to the coefficients: the
  powers of the scalar are central, so they pass through the linear map.
entries.snippet:
lemma eval_algebraMap_mapCoeffs {k A : Type*} [Field k] [Ring A] [Algebra k A]
    (f : A →ₗ[k] A) (p : Polynomial A) (c : k) :
    (mapCoeffs f p).eval (algebraMap k A c) = f (p.eval (algebraMap k A c))

entries.name: Polynomial.eval_one_mapAlgHom
entries.docstring: Evaluation at one commutes with pushing a polynomial along an algebra map.
entries.snippet:
lemma eval_one_mapAlgHom {k A B : Type*} [CommSemiring k] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B] (f : A →ₐ[k] B) (p : Polynomial A) :
    (Polynomial.mapAlgHom f p).eval 1 = f (p.eval 1)

entries.name: Polynomial.mapCoeffs_mul_of_leibniz
entries.docstring:
A map satisfying the Leibniz rule satisfies it coefficientwise on polynomials. Applied to
  a total derivative this is the Leibniz rule for the mass-weight polynomial.
entries.snippet:
lemma mapCoeffs_mul_of_leibniz {A : Type*} [Ring A] {D : A → A} (hD0 : D 0 = 0)
    (hDadd : ∀ a b : A, D (a + b) = D a + D b)
    (hD : ∀ a b : A, D (a * b) = D a * b + a * D b) (p q : Polynomial A) :
    mapCoeffs D (p * q) = mapCoeffs D p * q + p * mapCoeffs D q

entries.name: Representation.dual_apply_dualBasis
entries.docstring:
The components of a dual representation on a dual basis: if `ρ g⁻¹` has
  matrix `M` in the basis `b` (columns indexing the argument), then `ρ.dual g`
  acts on the dual basis by the rows of `M`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dual_apply_dualBasis {k G V ι : Type*} [CommRing k]
    [Group G] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ρ : Representation k G V) (b : Module.Basis ι k V) (g : G) (i : ι)
    (M : Matrix ι ι k) (hM : ∀ j, ρ g⁻¹ (b j) = ∑ l, M l j • b l) :
    ρ.dual g (b.dualBasis i) = ∑ j, M i j • b.dualBasis j

entries.name: Representation.prodMap_apply

@[simp]
lemma Representation.prodMap_apply {k G₁ G₂ V₁ V₂ : Type*} [CommSemiring k]

    Function.Injective (fun p : Fin (n1 + 1) × Fin (n2 + 1) =>

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsBivariateGrid
entries.docstring:
A family `g` indexed by the grid `Fin (n1 + 1) × Fin (n2 + 1)` realises the standard
`V(n1) ⊗ V(n2)` action of two commuting `sl₂`-triples: `g (a, b)` has weights
`(n1 - 2a, n2 - 2b)`, the lowering operators shift one index, and the raising operators
shift it back with the standard coefficients.
entries.snippet:
structure IsBivariateGrid (h1 e1 f1 h2 e2 f2 : Module.End K V) (n1 n2 : ℕ)
    (g : Fin (n1 + 1) × Fin (n2 + 1) → V) : Prop where
  h1_apply (a : Fin (n1 + 1)) (b : Fin (n2 + 1)) :
    h1 (g (a, b)) = ((n1 : K) - 2 * (a : ℕ)) • g (a, b)
  h2_apply (a : Fin (n1 + 1)) (b : Fin (n2 + 1)) :
    h2 (g (a, b)) = ((n2 : K) - 2 * (b : ℕ)) • g (a, b)
  e1_zero (b : Fin (n2 + 1)) : e1 (g (0, b)) = 0
  e1_pos (a : Fin (n1 + 1)) (_ : 0 < (a : ℕ)) (b : Fin (n2 + 1)) : e1 (g (a, b)) =
    (((a : ℕ) : K) * ((n1 : K) - ((a : ℕ) : K) + 1)) • g (⟨(a : ℕ) - 1, by omega⟩, b)
  f1_lt (a : Fin (n1 + 1)) (_ : (a : ℕ) < n1) (b : Fin (n2 + 1)) :
    f1 (g (a, b)) = g (⟨(a : ℕ) + 1, by omega⟩, b)
  f1_last (b : Fin (n2 + 1)) : f1 (g (Fin.last n1, b)) = 0
  e2_zero (a : Fin (n1 + 1)) : e2 (g (a, 0)) = 0
  e2_pos (a : Fin (n1 + 1)) (b : Fin (n2 + 1)) (_ : 0 < (b : ℕ)) : e2 (g (a, b)) =
    (((b : ℕ) : K) * ((n2 : K) - ((b : ℕ) : K) + 1)) • g (a, ⟨(b : ℕ) - 1, by omega⟩)
  f2_lt (a : Fin (n1 + 1)) (b : Fin (n2 + 1)) (_ : (b : ℕ) < n2) :
    f2 (g (a, b)) = g (a, ⟨(b : ℕ) + 1, by omega⟩)
  f2_last (a : Fin (n1 + 1)) : f2 (g (a, Fin.last n2)) = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.grid_h1
entries.docstring: The first Cartan weight of a grid vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma grid_h1 {b : ℕ} (a : ℕ) (hb : b ≤ n2) :
    h1 (gridVec f1 f2 m0 a b) = ((n1 : K) - 2 * a) • gridVec f1 f2 m0 a b

entries.snippet: lemma grid_e1_zero {b : ℕ} (hb : b ≤ n2) : e1 (gridVec f1 f2 m0 0 b) = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.grid_e1_succ
entries.docstring: The first raising operator on a grid vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma grid_e1_succ {b : ℕ} (a : ℕ) (hb : b ≤ n2) :
    e1 (gridVec f1 f2 m0 (a + 1) b) =
      (((a : K) + 1) * ((n1 : K) - a)) • gridVec f1 f2 m0 a b

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.grid_f1
entries.docstring: The first lowering operator shifts the first index.
entries.snippet: lemma grid_f1 (a b : ℕ) : f1 (gridVec f1 f2 m0 a b) = gridVec f1 f2 m0 (a + 1) b

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.grid_e2_zero

entries.snippet: lemma grid_e2_zero (a : ℕ) : e2 (gridVec f1 f2 m0 a 0) = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.grid_e2_succ
entries.docstring: The second raising operator on a grid vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma grid_e2_succ (a b : ℕ) :
    e2 (gridVec f1 f2 m0 a (b + 1)) =
      (((b : K) + 1) * ((n2 : K) - b)) • gridVec f1 f2 m0 a b

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.grid_f2
entries.docstring: The second lowering operator shifts the second index.
entries.snippet: lemma grid_f2 (a b : ℕ) : f2 (gridVec f1 f2 m0 a b) = gridVec f1 f2 m0 a (b + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.grid_f2_last

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.gridSpan_stable_f2

entries.snippet: lemma gridSpan_stable_f2 : ∀ v ∈ gridSpan f1 f2 m0 n1 n2, f2 v ∈ gridSpan f1 f2 m0 n1 n2

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.mem_primSpace
entries.docstring: Membership in `primSpace`, in plain-operator form.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_primSpace {h e : Module.End K V} {n : K} {v : V} :
    v ∈ primSpace h e n ↔ e v = 0 ∧ h v = n • v

entries.docstring: The primitive space of the first triple is stable under every operator of the second.

lemma primSpace_stable {n : K} {y : Module.End K V} {v : V}
    (hc : ∀ x ∈ ({h1, e1, f1} : Set (Module.End K V)),

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.exists_joint_primitive
entries.docstring:
Two commuting triples have a common primitive vector. The primitive-weight space for
the first triple is invariant under the second, so a primitive vector for the second can be
chosen inside it.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_joint_primitive : ∃ (n1 n2 : ℕ) (m0 : V), m0 ≠ 0 ∧
    t1.HasPrimitiveVectorWith m0 (n1 : K) ∧ t2.HasPrimitiveVectorWith m0 (n2 : K)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.exists_bivariate_basis
entries.docstring:
For a jointly irreducible pair of commuting triples, the vectors `f1 ^ a (f2 ^ b m0)`
form a basis. The basis realises the standard bivariate action, including the endpoints of
each string.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_bivariate_basis :
    ∃ (n1 n2 : ℕ) (B : Module.Basis (Fin (n1 + 1) × Fin (n2 + 1)) K V),

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.classification
entries.docstring:
A finite-dimensional irreducible module for the generated `sl₂` subalgebra is
equivalent to a standard highest-weight module.
entries.snippet:
lemma classification [IsAlgClosed K] [CharZero K] [FiniteDimensional K M] (t : IsSl2Triple h e f)
    [LieModule.IsIrreducible K ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K)) M] :
    ∃ n : ℕ, letI

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.classification_n_eq_finrank_sub_one
entries.docstring:
Uniqueness of the highest weight: the `n` produced by
`classification` is determined by `M` alone, namely `n = finrank K M - 1`.

Unlike `classification`, irreducibility is not actually needed here: only the bare existence of
some `K`-linear equivalence `M ≃ₗ[K] V(n)` (forgetting the Lie-module structure `hn` provides) is
used, via a dimension count.
entries.snippet:
lemma classification_n_eq_finrank_sub_one [CharZero K]
    {t : IsSl2Triple h e f} {n : ℕ}
    (hn : letI := standardSl2ModuleLieRingModule (K := K) (n := n) t
      Nonempty (M ≃ₗ⁅K, ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K))⁆ StandardSl2Module K n)) :
    n = Module.finrank K M - 1

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sum_arithmetic_progression
entries.docstring: The arithmetic progression underlying the Clebsch–Gordan dimension count.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_arithmetic_progression (m d : ℕ) :
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), (d + 2 * k + 1) = (m + 1) * (d + m + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.clebsch_gordan_finrank_aux
entries.docstring: Reindex the dimension sum when `m ≤ n`.
entries.snippet:
lemma clebsch_gordan_finrank_aux (m n : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n) :
    (m + 1) * (n + 1) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), (m + n - 2 * k + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.clebsch_gordan_finrank
entries.docstring:
Clebsch–Gordan decomposition, dimension form:
the numerical shadow `(m+1)(n+1) = ∑_{k=0}^{min(m,n)} (m+n-2k+1)` of the module
isomorphism `V(m) ⊗ V(n) ≅ ⊕_k V(m+n-2k)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma clebsch_gordan_finrank (m n : ℕ) :
    (m + 1) * (n + 1) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (min m n + 1), (m + n - 2 * k + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.clebsch_gordan
entries.docstring:
Clebsch–Gordan decomposition, vector-space form:
`V(m) ⊗ V(n)` is linearly isomorphic to `⊕_{k=0}^{min(m,n)} V(m+n-2k)`.

The equivalence follows only from equal dimensions. It does not identify the diagonal
`sl₂` action with the action on the direct sum or provide Clebsch–Gordan coefficients.
entries.snippet:
lemma clebsch_gordan (m n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n ≃ₗ[K]
      ⨁ _k : Fin (min m n + 1), StandardSl2Module K (m + n - 2 * (_k : ℕ)))

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.finrank_standardSl2Module
entries.docstring: The standard module `V(k)` has dimension `k + 1`.
entries.snippet: lemma finrank_standardSl2Module (k : ℕ) : Module.finrank K (StandardSl2Module K k) = k + 1

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.commuting_classification_finrank
entries.docstring: Dimension consequence of `commuting_classification`: `finrank K V = (m+1)(n+1)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma commuting_classification_finrank :
    ∃ m n : ℕ, Module.finrank K V = (m + 1) * (n + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.commuting_classification
entries.docstring:
Classification of jointly irreducible commuting `sl₂`-actions.
Two `sl₂`-triples of operators on a
finite-dimensional space `V`, commuting with each other and with no proper
subspace invariant under both, force `V` to be linearly isomorphic to a tensor
product `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` of standard modules.

The equivalence is obtained from a dimension count. An equivalence intertwining the two
actions remains to be constructed.
entries.snippet:
lemma commuting_classification :
    ∃ m n : ℕ, Nonempty (V ≃ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

`e` acting on `StandardSl2Module K n`: `ρE (v k) = (k(n-k+1)) • v (k-1)`, `ρE (v 0) = 0`.
As a per-component formula (component `k` of the output reads from input component `k+1`,
scaled by the coefficient attached to *that* input index): zero at `k = n` (nothing shifts
down into the top component), else `((k+1)(n-k)) • w (k+1)`.

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.rel_ef_last_zero
entries.docstring:
The `sl₂` relations hold for `(ρH,ρE,ρF)` on `StandardSl2Module K n`: `[ρE,ρF]=ρH`,
`[ρH,ρE]=2ρE`, `[ρH,ρF]=-2ρF`. Checked componentwise on an arbitrary vector `w`: each
composite operator, evaluated at output index `j`, only ever reads `w j` itself (the
`E`/`F` shifts cancel), so the identity reduces to the coefficient computation already
recorded in the `ρ_v` lemmas' docstrings.
entries.snippet:
lemma rel_ef_last_zero (w : StandardSl2Module K n) (j : Fin (n + 1))
    (hjn : (j : ℕ) = n) (hj0 : (j : ℕ) = 0) :
    (((ρE * ρF - ρF * ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) w) j) =
      (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) w j

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.rel_ef_last_pos
entries.snippet:
lemma rel_ef_last_pos (w : StandardSl2Module K n) (j : Fin (n + 1))
    (hjn : (j : ℕ) = n) (hj0 : (j : ℕ) ≠ 0) :
    (((ρE * ρF - ρF * ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) w) j) =
      (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) w j

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.rel_ef_first
entries.snippet:
lemma rel_ef_first (w : StandardSl2Module K n) (j : Fin (n + 1))
    (hjn : (j : ℕ) ≠ n) (hj0 : (j : ℕ) = 0) :
    (((ρE * ρF - ρF * ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) w) j) =
      (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) w j

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.rel_ef_middle
entries.snippet:
lemma rel_ef_middle (w : StandardSl2Module K n) (j : Fin (n + 1))
    (hjn : (j : ℕ) ≠ n) (hj0 : (j : ℕ) ≠ 0) :
    (((ρE * ρF - ρF * ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) w) j) =
      (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) w j

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.rel_ef
entries.docstring: The standard raising and lowering operators have commutator `ρH`.
entries.snippet:
lemma rel_ef :
    ⁅(ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)), (ρF : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n))⁆
      = ρH

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.rel_he
entries.snippet:
lemma rel_he :
    ⁅(ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)), (ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n))⁆
      = (2 : K) • ρE

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.rel_hf
entries.snippet:
lemma rel_hf :
    ⁅(ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)), (ρF : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n))⁆
      = (-2 : K) • ρF

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.endLieSkew
entries.docstring:
Antisymmetry of the bracket on `Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)`, proved directly via
the associative-ring commutator rather than via the generic `lie_skew` (which does not
syntactically match brackets here, since Mathlib derives a `LieRing`/`Bracket` structure on an
endomorphism ring through more than one route).
entries.snippet: lemma endLieSkew (a b : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) : ⁅a, b⁆ = -⁅b, a⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.endAddLie
entries.docstring:
Bilinearity of the bracket on `Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)`, proved directly via
the associative-ring commutator for the same reason as `endLieSkew`.
entries.snippet:
lemma endAddLie (a b c : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) :
    ⁅a + b, c⁆ = ⁅a, c⁆ + ⁅b, c⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.endLieAdd
entries.snippet:
lemma endLieAdd (a b c : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) :
    ⁅a, b + c⁆ = ⁅a, b⁆ + ⁅a, c⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.endSmulLie
entries.snippet:
lemma endSmulLie (r : K) (a b : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) :
    ⁅r • a, b⁆ = r • ⁅a, b⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.endLieSmul
entries.snippet:
lemma endLieSmul (r : K) (a b : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) :
    ⁅a, r • b⁆ = r • ⁅a, b⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Φ
entries.docstring:
The Lie-algebra homomorphism from the `sl₂`-subalgebra generated by `t` into
`Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)`, sending `e ↦ ρE`, `f ↦ ρF`, `h ↦ ρH`. Built by
transporting `![ρE,ρF,ρH]` along the basis `subalgebraBasis t`; the fact that it respects
brackets (`Φ_lie`, below) is checked on the generators via `rel_ef`/`rel_he`/`rel_hf` and
then extended to the whole subalgebra by bilinearity.
entries.snippet:
def Φ (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) :
    ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K)) →ₗ[K] Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Φ_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma Φ_apply (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) (i : Fin 3) :
    Φ t (subalgebraBasis t i) = ![(ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)), ρF, ρH] i

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.lie_subalgebraBasis
entries.docstring:
Transports a bracket identity among the generators `(e,f,h)` down to the corresponding
identity among the basis elements `subalgebraBasis t 0,1,2` of the subalgebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma lie_subalgebraBasis (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) (i j k : Fin 3) (c : K)
    (hc : ⁅![e, f, h] i, ![e, f, h] j⁆ = c • ![e, f, h] k) :
    ⁅subalgebraBasis (K := K) t i, subalgebraBasis (K := K) t j⁆
      = c • subalgebraBasis (K := K) t k

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Φ_bracket_refl
entries.snippet:
lemma Φ_bracket_refl (t : IsSl2Triple h e f)
    (x : ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K))) :
    Φ (K := K) (n := n) t ⁅x, x⁆ = ⁅Φ (K := K) (n := n) t x, Φ (K := K) (n := n) t x⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Φ_bracket_swap
entries.snippet:
lemma Φ_bracket_swap (t : IsSl2Triple h e f)
    (x y : ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K)))
    (hxy : Φ (K := K) (n := n) t ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅Φ (K := K) (n := n) t x, Φ (K := K) (n := n) t y⁆) :
    Φ (K := K) (n := n) t ⁅y, x⁆ = ⁅Φ (K := K) (n := n) t y, Φ (K := K) (n := n) t x⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Φ_bracket_ef
entries.snippet:
lemma Φ_bracket_ef (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) :
    Φ (K := K) (n := n) t
      ⁅subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 0, subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 1⁆ =
        ⁅Φ (K := K) (n := n) t (subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 0),
          Φ (K := K) (n := n) t (subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 1)⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Φ_bracket_he
entries.snippet:
lemma Φ_bracket_he (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) :
    Φ (K := K) (n := n) t
      ⁅subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 2, subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 0⁆ =
        ⁅Φ (K := K) (n := n) t (subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 2),
          Φ (K := K) (n := n) t (subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 0)⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Φ_bracket_hf
entries.snippet:
lemma Φ_bracket_hf (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) :
    Φ (K := K) (n := n) t
      ⁅subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 2, subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 1⁆ =
        ⁅Φ (K := K) (n := n) t (subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 2),
          Φ (K := K) (n := n) t (subalgebraBasis (K := K) t 1)⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Φ_bracket_basis
entries.docstring: The action map preserves brackets on pairs of the three generators.
entries.snippet:
lemma Φ_bracket_basis (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) (i j : Fin 3) :
    Φ (K := K) (n := n) t
      ⁅subalgebraBasis (K := K) t i, subalgebraBasis (K := K) t j⁆ =
        ⁅Φ (K := K) (n := n) t (subalgebraBasis (K := K) t i),
          Φ (K := K) (n := n) t (subalgebraBasis (K := K) t j)⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Φ_lie
entries.docstring: The action map preserves brackets because it does so on pairs of basis elements.
entries.snippet:
lemma Φ_lie (t : IsSl2Triple h e f)
    (x y : ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K))) :
    Φ (K := K) (n := n) t ⁅x, y⁆
      =
      ⁅(Φ (K := K) (n := n) t x : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)),
        (Φ (K := K) (n := n) t y : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n))⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner
entries.docstring:
A linear map between standard modules is an intertwiner if it commutes with the raising,
lowering and weight operators.
entries.snippet:
structure IsIntertwiner (φ : StandardSl2Module K a →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K b) : Prop where
  comm_ρE : φ ∘ₗ ρE = ρE ∘ₗ φ
  comm_ρF : φ ∘ₗ ρF = ρF ∘ₗ φ
  comm_ρH : φ ∘ₗ ρH = ρH ∘ₗ φ

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.apply_ρE
entries.snippet: lemma apply_ρE (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) (x : StandardSl2Module K a) : φ (ρE x) = ρE (φ x)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.apply_ρF
entries.snippet: lemma apply_ρF (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) (x : StandardSl2Module K a) : φ (ρF x) = ρF (φ x)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.apply_ρH
entries.snippet: lemma apply_ρH (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) (x : StandardSl2Module K a) : φ (ρH x) = ρH (φ x)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.apply_ρF_pow
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_ρF_pow (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) (l : ℕ) (x : StandardSl2Module K a) :
    φ ((ρF ^ l) x) = (ρF ^ l) (φ x)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.id
entries.docstring: The identity is an intertwiner.
entries.snippet: lemma id : IsIntertwiner (LinearMap.id : StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.smul
entries.docstring: Scalar multiples of intertwiners are intertwiners.
entries.snippet: lemma smul (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) (c : K) : IsIntertwiner (c • φ) where

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.add
entries.docstring: Sums of intertwiners are intertwiners.
entries.snippet: lemma add (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) (hψ : IsIntertwiner ψ) : IsIntertwiner (φ + ψ) where

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρF_pow_vNat_zero
entries.docstring: The lowering string of `v_0` runs through the coordinate vectors: `f^l v_0 = v_l`.
entries.snippet:
lemma ρF_pow_vNat_zero (l : ℕ) :
    ((ρF : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) ^ l) (vNat n 0) = vNat n l

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StandardSl2Module.linearMap_ext_vNat
entries.docstring: Two linear maps out of a standard module agree if they agree on all `v_l`.
entries.snippet:
lemma StandardSl2Module.linearMap_ext_vNat {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module K M] {α β : StandardSl2Module K a →ₗ[K] M} (h : ∀ l, α (vNat a l) = β (vNat a l)) :
    α = β

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.eq_smul_vNat_zero_of_ρE_eq_zero
entries.docstring: A vector of `V(n)` killed by the raising operator is a multiple of `v_0`.

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.apply_vNat_zero
entries.docstring: The image of `v_0` under an intertwiner is a multiple of `v_0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_vNat_zero (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) :
    φ (vNat a 0) = φ (vNat a 0) ⟨0, Nat.succ_pos b⟩ • vNat b 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.apply_vNat
entries.docstring:
An intertwiner sends every coordinate vector `v_l` to the same multiple `c • v_l`, where `c`
is the `v_0`-coordinate of the image of `v_0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_vNat (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) (l : ℕ) :
    φ (vNat a l) = φ (vNat a 0) ⟨0, Nat.succ_pos b⟩ • vNat b l

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.coeff_eq_zero_of_ne
entries.docstring: The scalar of an intertwiner vanishes unless the two highest weights agree.
entries.snippet:
lemma coeff_eq_zero_of_ne (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    φ (vNat a 0) ⟨0, Nat.succ_pos b⟩ = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.eq_zero_of_ne
entries.docstring: **Schur's lemma**, first half: an intertwiner `V(a) → V(b)` with `a ≠ b` is zero.
entries.snippet: lemma eq_zero_of_ne (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) (hab : a ≠ b) : φ = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsIntertwiner.eq_smul_id
entries.docstring:
**Schur's lemma**, second half: an intertwiner `V(n) → V(n)` is a scalar multiple of the
identity.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_smul_id {φ : StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K n} (hφ : IsIntertwiner φ) :
    φ = φ (vNat n 0) ⟨0, Nat.succ_pos n⟩ • LinearMap.id

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.stringVec
entries.docstring: The `l`-th vector `f^l w_k` of the lowering string of `hwVec m n k`.
entries.snippet: def stringVec (m n k l : ℕ) : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorF_stringVec
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorF_stringVec (k l : ℕ) :
    tensorF (K := K) m n (stringVec m n k l) = stringVec m n k (l + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorH_stringVec
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorH_stringVec (l : ℕ) :
    tensorH (K := K) m n (stringVec m n k l) =
      (((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : K) - 2 * l) • stringVec m n k l

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorE_stringVec_succ
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorE_stringVec_succ (l : ℕ) :
    tensorE (K := K) m n (stringVec m n k (l + 1)) =
      (((l : K) + 1) * (((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : K) - l)) • stringVec m n k l

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.stringVec_ne_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma stringVec_ne_zero {l : ℕ} (hl : l ≤ m + n - 2 * k) :
    stringVec (K := K) m n k l ≠ 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.stringVec_eq_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma stringVec_eq_zero {l : ℕ} (hl : m + n - 2 * k < l) :
    stringVec (K := K) m n k l = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorE_stringVec_zero
entries.snippet: lemma tensorE_stringVec_zero : tensorE (K := K) m n (stringVec m n k 0) = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.separator
entries.docstring:
The operator `M (2EF + 2FE + H²) + H` with `M = 2(m + n) + 1`. The bracket is a multiple of
the Casimir element, which distinguishes the strings; the weight `H` distinguishes the vectors
within a string.
entries.snippet: def separator (m n : ℕ) : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sepVal
entries.docstring: The eigenvalue of `separator` on `stringVec m n k l`.
entries.snippet: def sepVal (m n k l : ℕ) : K

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.separator_stringVec
entries.snippet:
lemma separator_stringVec {k : ℕ} (hmn : 0 < m + n) (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (l : ℕ) :
    separator (K := K) m n (stringVec m n k l) =
      sepVal (K := K) m n k l • stringVec m n k l

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StringIndex
entries.docstring: Index set of the lowering strings: `k ≤ min m n` and `l ≤ m + n - 2k`.
entries.snippet: abbrev StringIndex (m n : ℕ) : Type

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.«instance@c778abb2»
entries.snippet: instance : Nonempty (StringIndex m n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StringIndex.le_left
entries.snippet: lemma StringIndex.le_left (i : StringIndex m n) : (i.1 : ℕ) ≤ m

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StringIndex.le_right
entries.snippet: lemma StringIndex.le_right (i : StringIndex m n) : (i.1 : ℕ) ≤ n

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sepVal_int_injective
entries.docstring:
Integer core of `sepVal_injective`: with `M = 2s + 1`, the value `M N (N + 2) + N - 2l`
determines `N` and `l`, provided `N ≤ s` and `l ≤ N`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sepVal_int_injective {s N N' l l' : ℕ} (hN : N ≤ s) (hN' : N' ≤ s) (hl : l ≤ N)
    (hl' : l' ≤ N')
    (h : (2 * s + 1 : ℤ) * (N * (N + 2)) + N - 2 * l =
      (2 * s + 1 : ℤ) * (N' * (N' + 2)) + N' - 2 * l') : N = N' ∧ l = l'

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sepVal_injective
entries.docstring: The eigenvalues of `separator` on the lowering strings are pairwise distinct.
entries.snippet:
lemma sepVal_injective :
    Function.Injective (fun i : StringIndex m n => sepVal (K := K) m n i.1 i.2)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.stringVec_linearIndependent
entries.docstring: The lowering strings of the highest-weight vectors are linearly independent.
entries.snippet:
lemma stringVec_linearIndependent (hmn : 0 < m + n) :
    LinearIndependent K (fun i : StringIndex m n => stringVec (K := K) m n i.1 i.2)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.card_stringIndex
entries.snippet: lemma card_stringIndex : Fintype.card (StringIndex m n) = (m + 1) * (n + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.finrank_standardSl2Module_tensor
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_standardSl2Module_tensor :
    Module.finrank K (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n) = (m + 1) * (n + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorStringBasis
entries.docstring: The basis of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` formed by the lowering strings of the highest-weight vectors.
entries.snippet:
def tensorStringBasis (hmn : 0 < m + n) :
    Module.Basis (StringIndex m n) K (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorStringBasis_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorStringBasis_apply (hmn : 0 < m + n) (i : StringIndex m n) :
    tensorStringBasis (K := K) hmn i = stringVec m n i.1 i.2

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.CGSummand
entries.docstring: The summand `V(m + n - 2k)` of the Clebsch–Gordan decomposition.
entries.snippet: abbrev CGSummand (K : Type*) (m n : ℕ) (k : Fin (min m n + 1)) : Type _

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.CGSum
entries.docstring: The direct sum `⨁_k V(m + n - 2k)` of the Clebsch–Gordan decomposition.
entries.snippet: abbrev CGSum (K : Type*) [Field K] (m n : ℕ) : Type _

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sumVec
entries.docstring: The coordinate vector `v_l` of the `k`-th summand of `CGSum`.
entries.snippet: def sumVec (m n : ℕ) (k : Fin (min m n + 1)) (l : ℕ) : CGSum K m n

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sumEnd
entries.docstring: The endomorphism of `CGSum` acting by `A k` on the `k`-th summand.
entries.snippet: def sumEnd (A : ∀ k, Module.End K (CGSummand K m n k)) : Module.End K (CGSum K m n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sumEnd_lof
entries.snippet:
lemma sumEnd_lof (A : ∀ k, Module.End K (CGSummand K m n k)) (k : Fin (min m n + 1))
    (x : CGSummand K m n k) :
    sumEnd A (DirectSum.lof K _ (CGSummand K m n) k x) =
      DirectSum.lof K _ (CGSummand K m n) k (A k x)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sumVec_linearIndependent
entries.snippet:
lemma sumVec_linearIndependent :
    LinearIndependent K (fun i : StringIndex m n => sumVec (K := K) m n i.1 i.2)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sumBasis
entries.docstring: The basis of `CGSum` formed by the coordinate vectors of the summands.
entries.snippet: def sumBasis (m n : ℕ) : Module.Basis (StringIndex m n) K (CGSum K m n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sumBasis_apply
entries.snippet: lemma sumBasis_apply (i : StringIndex m n) : sumBasis (K := K) m n i = sumVec m n i.1 i.2

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv
entries.docstring:
The Clebsch–Gordan equivalence `V(m) ⊗ V(n) ≃ ⨁_k V(m + n - 2k)`, sending the `l`-th
vector of the `k`-th lowering string to the coordinate vector `v_l` of the `k`-th summand.
entries.snippet:
def cgEquiv (hmn : 0 < m + n) :
    (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n) ≃ₗ[K] CGSum K m n

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_stringVec
entries.docstring: `cgEquiv` on the lowering strings, for every `l : ℕ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma cgEquiv_stringVec (hmn : 0 < m + n) (k : Fin (min m n + 1)) (l : ℕ) :
    cgEquiv (K := K) hmn (stringVec m n k l) = sumVec m n k l

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_tensorF
entries.docstring: `cgEquiv` intertwines the diagonal lowering operator with `ρF` on each summand.
entries.snippet:
lemma cgEquiv_tensorF (hmn : 0 < m + n) (x : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n) :
    cgEquiv hmn (tensorF m n x) = sumEnd (fun _ => ρF) (cgEquiv hmn x)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_tensorH
entries.docstring: `cgEquiv` intertwines the diagonal weight operator with `ρH` on each summand.
entries.snippet:
lemma cgEquiv_tensorH (hmn : 0 < m + n) (x : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n) :
    cgEquiv hmn (tensorH m n x) = sumEnd (fun _ => ρH) (cgEquiv hmn x)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_tensorE
entries.docstring: `cgEquiv` intertwines the diagonal raising operator with `ρE` on each summand.
entries.snippet:
lemma cgEquiv_tensorE (hmn : 0 < m + n) (x : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n) :
    cgEquiv hmn (tensorE m n x) = sumEnd (fun _ => ρE) (cgEquiv hmn x)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd
entries.docstring: The diagonal action `A ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ B` of two endomorphisms on `M ⊗ N`.
entries.snippet: def diagEnd (A : Module.End K M) (B : Module.End K N) : Module.End K (M ⊗[K] N)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd_tmul
entries.snippet:
lemma diagEnd_tmul (A : Module.End K M) (B : Module.End K N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    diagEnd A B (x ⊗ₜ y) = A x ⊗ₜ y + x ⊗ₜ B y

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.lie_diagEnd
entries.docstring: The diagonal action respects commutators.
entries.snippet:
lemma lie_diagEnd (A A' : Module.End K M) (B B' : Module.End K N) :
    ⁅diagEnd A B, diagEnd A' B'⁆ = diagEnd ⁅A, A'⁆ ⁅B, B'⁆

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd_smul
entries.snippet:
lemma diagEnd_smul (c : K) (A : Module.End K M) (B : Module.End K N) :
    diagEnd (c • A) (c • B) = c • diagEnd A B

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd_add
entries.docstring: The diagonal action is additive in both endomorphisms.
entries.snippet:
lemma diagEnd_add (A A' : Module.End K M) (B B' : Module.End K N) :
    diagEnd (A + A') (B + B') = diagEnd A B + diagEnd A' B'

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd_sub
entries.docstring: The diagonal action respects differences.
entries.snippet:
lemma diagEnd_sub (A A' : Module.End K M) (B B' : Module.End K N) :
    diagEnd (A - A') (B - B') = diagEnd A B - diagEnd A' B'

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StandardSl2Module.vNat
entries.docstring:
The coordinate vector `v_i` of `StandardSl2Module K n`, indexed by a natural number;
it is zero for `i > n`.
entries.snippet: def StandardSl2Module.vNat (n i : ℕ) : StandardSl2Module K n

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StandardSl2Module.vNat_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma vNat_apply (i : ℕ) (k : Fin (n + 1)) :
    vNat (K := K) n i k = if (k : ℕ) = i then 1 else 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StandardSl2Module.vNat_eq_v
entries.snippet: lemma vNat_eq_v {i : ℕ} (hi : i ≤ n) : vNat (K := K) n i = v ⟨i, by omega⟩

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StandardSl2Module.vNat_of_lt
entries.snippet: lemma vNat_of_lt {i : ℕ} (hi : n < i) : vNat (K := K) n i = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρH_vNat
entries.snippet:
lemma ρH_vNat (i : ℕ) :
    (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) (vNat n i) = ((n : K) - 2 * i) • vNat n i

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρF_vNat
entries.snippet:
lemma ρF_vNat (i : ℕ) :
    (ρF : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) (vNat n i) = vNat n (i + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_vNat_zero
entries.snippet:
