lemma ρE_vNat_zero :
    (ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) (vNat n 0) = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_vNat_succ
entries.snippet:
lemma ρE_vNat_succ [CharZero K] (i : ℕ) :
    (ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) (vNat n (i + 1)) =
      (((i : K) + 1) * ((n : K) - i)) • vNat n i

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorE
entries.docstring: The diagonal raising operator on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
entries.snippet: def tensorE (m n : ℕ) : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorF
entries.docstring: The diagonal lowering operator on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
entries.snippet: def tensorF (m n : ℕ) : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorH
entries.docstring: The diagonal weight operator on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
entries.snippet: def tensorH (m n : ℕ) : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorCoord
entries.docstring: The coefficient of `v_i ⊗ v_j` in an element of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
entries.snippet:
def tensorCoord (m n : ℕ) (i : Fin (m + 1)) (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
    StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] K

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorCoord_tmul
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorCoord_tmul (i : Fin (m + 1)) (j : Fin (n + 1)) (x : StandardSl2Module K m)
    (y : StandardSl2Module K n) : tensorCoord m n i j (x ⊗ₜ y) = x i * y j

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorH_tmul_vNat
entries.docstring: The diagonal weight operator on a product of coordinate vectors.
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorH_tmul_vNat (a b : ℕ) :
    tensorH (K := K) m n (vNat m a ⊗ₜ vNat n b) =
      ((m : K) + n - 2 * (a + b)) • (vNat m a ⊗ₜ vNat n b)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.isSl2Triple_tensor
entries.docstring: The diagonal operators on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` form an `sl₂` triple when `m + n > 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma isSl2Triple_tensor [CharZero K] (hmn : 0 < m + n) :
    IsSl2Triple (tensorH (K := K) m n) (tensorE m n) (tensorF m n) where

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoeff
entries.docstring:
The coefficient of `v_a ⊗ v_{k-a}` in the highest-weight vector of weight `m + n - 2k`
of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`: `(-1)^a (k choose a) (n-k+a)! (m-a)!`.
entries.snippet: def cgCoeff (m n k a : ℕ) : K

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoeff_rec
entries.docstring: The two-term recursion of the coefficients that makes the raising operator vanish.
entries.snippet:
lemma cgCoeff_rec {j a : ℕ} (hjm : j + 1 ≤ m) (hjn : j + 1 ≤ n) (ha : a ≤ j) :
    cgCoeff (K := K) m n (j + 1) (a + 1) * (((a : K) + 1) * ((m : K) - a)) +
      cgCoeff m n (j + 1) a * ((((j - a : ℕ) : K) + 1) * ((n : K) - ((j - a : ℕ) : K))) = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwVec
entries.docstring: The highest-weight vector of weight `m + n - 2k` in `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
entries.snippet: def hwVec (m n k : ℕ) : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorH_hwVec
entries.docstring: `hwVec m n k` has weight `m + n - 2k`.
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorH_hwVec (k : ℕ) :
    tensorH (K := K) m n (hwVec m n k) = ((m : K) + n - 2 * k) • hwVec m n k

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorE_hwVec
entries.docstring: `hwVec m n k` is killed by the diagonal raising operator when `k ≤ min m n`.
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorE_hwVec [CharZero K] {k : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    tensorE (K := K) m n (hwVec m n k) = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwVec_ne_zero
entries.docstring: `hwVec m n k` is nonzero for `k ≤ n`: its `v_0 ⊗ v_k` coefficient is `(n-k)! m!`.
entries.snippet:
lemma hwVec_ne_zero [CharZero K] {k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    hwVec (K := K) m n k ≠ 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwVec_hasPrimitiveVectorWith
entries.docstring: `hwVec m n k` is a primitive vector of weight `m + n - 2k` for the diagonal action.
entries.snippet:
lemma hwVec_hasPrimitiveVectorWith [CharZero K] {k : ℕ} (hmn : 0 < m + n) (hkm : k ≤ m)
    (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    (isSl2Triple_tensor (K := K) hmn).HasPrimitiveVectorWith (hwVec (K := K) m n k)
      ((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : K) where

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorF_pow_hwVec_ne_zero
entries.docstring: The first `m + n - 2k + 1` members of the lowering string of `hwVec m n k` are nonzero.
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorF_pow_hwVec_ne_zero [CharZero K] {k l : ℕ} (hmn : 0 < m + n) (hkm : k ≤ m)
    (hkn : k ≤ n) (hl : l ≤ m + n - 2 * k) :
    (tensorF (K := K) m n ^ l) (hwVec m n k) ≠ 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorF_pow_hwVec_eq_zero
entries.docstring: The lowering string of `hwVec m n k` ends after `m + n - 2k + 1` steps.
entries.snippet:
lemma tensorF_pow_hwVec_eq_zero [CharZero K] {k : ℕ} (hmn : 0 < m + n) (hkm : k ≤ m)
    (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    (tensorF (K := K) m n ^ (m + n - 2 * k + 1)) (hwVec m n k) = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner
entries.docstring:
A linear map `V(m) ⊗ V(n) → V(p)` is a tensor intertwiner if it carries the diagonal raising,
lowering and weight operators on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` to those on `V(p)`.
entries.snippet:
structure IsTensorIntertwiner
    (φ : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K p) : Prop where
  comm_E : φ ∘ₗ tensorE m n = ρE ∘ₗ φ
  comm_F : φ ∘ₗ tensorF m n = ρF ∘ₗ φ
  comm_H : φ ∘ₗ tensorH m n = ρH ∘ₗ φ

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.smul
entries.docstring: Scalar multiples of tensor intertwiners are tensor intertwiners.
entries.snippet: lemma smul (hφ : IsTensorIntertwiner φ) (c : K) : IsTensorIntertwiner (c • φ) where

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.add
entries.docstring: Sums of tensor intertwiners are tensor intertwiners.
entries.snippet:
lemma add (hφ : IsTensorIntertwiner φ) (hψ : IsTensorIntertwiner ψ) :
    IsTensorIntertwiner (φ + ψ) where

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.component_sumEnd
entries.docstring: The component of a direct sum commutes with a summand-wise endomorphism.
entries.snippet:
lemma component_sumEnd (A : ∀ j, Module.End K (CGSummand K m n j)) (j : Fin (min m n + 1))
    (y : CGSum K m n) :
    DirectSum.component K _ (CGSummand K m n) j (sumEnd A y) =
      A j (DirectSum.component K _ (CGSummand K m n) j y)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj
entries.docstring:
The projection of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` onto the summand `V(m + n - 2j)` of the Clebsch–Gordan
decomposition.

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma cgProj_apply (hmn : 0 < m + n) (j : Fin (min m n + 1))
    (x : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n) :
    cgProj hmn j x = DirectSum.component K _ (CGSummand K m n) j (cgEquiv hmn x)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj_isTensorIntertwiner
entries.docstring: The projections are tensor intertwiners.
entries.snippet:
lemma cgProj_isTensorIntertwiner (hmn : 0 < m + n) (j : Fin (min m n + 1)) :
    IsTensorIntertwiner (cgProj (K := K) hmn j) where

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj_cgEquiv_symm_lof
entries.docstring:
The projection sends the preimage of the highest-weight vector of the `j`-th summand to that
vector; in particular it is not zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma cgProj_cgEquiv_symm_lof (hmn : 0 < m + n) (j : Fin (min m n + 1))
    (z : CGSummand K m n j) :
    cgProj hmn j ((cgEquiv hmn).symm (DirectSum.lof K _ (CGSummand K m n) j z)) = z

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj_ne_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma cgProj_ne_zero (hmn : 0 < m + n) (j : Fin (min m n + 1)) :
    cgProj (K := K) hmn j ≠ 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_E
entries.snippet:
lemma cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_E (y : CGSum K m n) :
    (cgEquiv hmn).symm (sumEnd (fun _ => ρE) y) = tensorE m n ((cgEquiv hmn).symm y)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_F
entries.snippet:
lemma cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_F (y : CGSum K m n) :
    (cgEquiv hmn).symm (sumEnd (fun _ => ρF) y) = tensorF m n ((cgEquiv hmn).symm y)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_H
entries.snippet:
lemma cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_H (y : CGSum K m n) :
    (cgEquiv hmn).symm (sumEnd (fun _ => ρH) y) = tensorH m n ((cgEquiv hmn).symm y)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgRestrict
entries.docstring:
The restriction of a linear map on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` to the `j`-th summand of the
Clebsch–Gordan decomposition.
entries.snippet:
def cgRestrict
    (φ : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K p)
    (j : Fin (min m n + 1)) : CGSummand K m n j →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K p

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.cgRestrict_isIntertwiner
entries.docstring: The restriction of a tensor intertwiner to a summand is an intertwiner.
entries.snippet:
lemma cgRestrict_isIntertwiner (hφ : IsTensorIntertwiner φ) (j : Fin (min m n + 1)) :
    IsIntertwiner (cgRestrict hmn φ j) where

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.eq_of_cgRestrict_eq
entries.docstring: A linear map on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` is determined by its restrictions to the summands.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_of_cgRestrict_eq (hmn : 0 < m + n) {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module K M]
    {α β : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] M}
    (h : ∀ j, α ∘ₗ (cgEquiv hmn).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ DirectSum.lof K _ (CGSummand K m n) j =
      β ∘ₗ (cgEquiv hmn).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ DirectSum.lof K _ (CGSummand K m n) j) :
    α = β

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.eq_zero_of_forall_ne
entries.docstring:
**Selection rule.** If `p` is not of the form `m + n - 2j` with `j ≤ min m n`, every tensor
intertwiner `V(m) ⊗ V(n) → V(p)` is zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_zero_of_forall_ne (hmn : 0 < m + n)
    {φ : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K p}
    (hφ : IsTensorIntertwiner φ) (hp : ∀ j : Fin (min m n + 1), m + n - 2 * (j : ℕ) ≠ p) :
    φ = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.exists_eq_smul_cgProj
entries.docstring:
Every tensor intertwiner onto the summand `V(m + n - 2j)` is a scalar multiple of the
projection `cgProj`.

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace
entries.docstring: The eigenspace of the Cartan operator `h` with eigenvalue `n`.
entries.snippet: def weightSpace (_t : IsSl2Triple h e f) (n : K) : Submodule K M

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.e_mapsTo_weightSpace
entries.docstring: The raising operator maps weight `n` into weight `n + 2`.
entries.snippet:
lemma e_mapsTo_weightSpace (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) (n : K) :
    ∀ v ∈ weightSpace (M := M) t n, LieModule.toEnd K L M e v ∈ weightSpace t (n + 2)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.f_mapsTo_weightSpace
entries.docstring: `f` lowers the weight by `2`. Dual to `e_mapsTo_weightSpace`.
entries.snippet:
lemma f_mapsTo_weightSpace (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) (n : K) :
    ∀ v ∈ weightSpace (M := M) t n, LieModule.toEnd K L M f v ∈ weightSpace t (n - 2)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.repr_apply_diag
entries.docstring: If a basis diagonalises `T`, then `T` multiplies the `i`-th coordinate by `μ i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma repr_apply_diag {ι : Type*} (b : Module.Basis ι K M) (T : Module.End K M)
    (μ : ι → K) (hT : ∀ j, T (b j) = μ j • b j) (i : ι) (w : M) :
    b.repr (T w) i = μ i * b.repr w i

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.string_coord_eq_zero
entries.docstring: A weight vector has vanishing string coordinates at every other weight.
entries.snippet:
lemma string_coord_eq_zero {n : K} {w : M} (hw : w ∈ weightSpace (M := M) t n)
    (i : Fin (N + 1)) (hi : (N : K) - 2 * (i : ℕ) ≠ n) : (stringBasis P).repr w i = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace_eq_bot_of_ne
entries.docstring: The weight space is trivial at a value that is not a weight of the string.
entries.snippet:
lemma weightSpace_eq_bot_of_ne {n : K} (hn : ∀ i : Fin (N + 1), (N : K) - 2 * (i : ℕ) ≠ n) :
    weightSpace (M := M) t n = ⊥

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace_finrank_le_one_of_eq
entries.docstring: The weight space of a weight of the string has dimension at most one.
entries.snippet:
lemma weightSpace_finrank_le_one_of_eq {n : K} (i₀ : Fin (N + 1))
    (hi₀ : (N : K) - 2 * (i₀ : ℕ) = n) : Module.finrank K (weightSpace (M := M) t n) ≤ 1

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace_finrank_le_one
entries.docstring:
Every Cartan weight space of a finite-dimensional irreducible `sl₂` module has
dimension at most one. The lowering-string basis has pairwise distinct weights.
entries.snippet:
lemma weightSpace_finrank_le_one [IsAlgClosed K] [CharZero K] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) [LieModule.IsIrreducible K ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K)) M]
    (n : K) : Module.finrank K (weightSpace (M := M) t n) ≤ 1

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.lie_e_eq_zero_of_top_weight
entries.docstring: A vector at a weight with empty weight space two steps above is killed by `e`.
entries.snippet:
lemma lie_e_eq_zero_of_top_weight {n : K} {v : M} (t : IsSl2Triple h e f)
    (hv : v ∈ weightSpace (M := M) t n) (hn : weightSpace (M := M) t (n + 2) = ⊥) :
    ⁅e, v⁆ = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.finrank_of_top_weight
entries.docstring: A top weight `p` of a finite-dimensional irreducible module fixes the dimension.
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_of_top_weight [CharZero K] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) [LieModule.IsIrreducible K ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K)) M]
    {p : ℕ} (hp : weightSpace (M := M) t (p : K) ≠ ⊥)
    (hp' : weightSpace (M := M) t ((p : K) + 2) = ⊥) : Module.finrank K M = p + 1

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace_highest_unique
entries.docstring:
A nonzero weight space with no weight space two steps above it determines the
highest weight of a finite-dimensional irreducible module.
entries.snippet:
lemma weightSpace_highest_unique [CharZero K] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) [LieModule.IsIrreducible K ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K)) M]
    {m n : ℕ} (hm : weightSpace (M := M) t (m : K) ≠ ⊥)
    (hm' : weightSpace (M := M) t ((m : K) + 2) = ⊥)
    (hn : weightSpace (M := M) t (n : K) ≠ ⊥)
    (hn' : weightSpace (M := M) t ((n : K) + 2) = ⊥) : m = n

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.laguerreCoeff
entries.docstring: The coefficient `(-1)^i C(N + α, N - i) / i!` of `x^i` in `L_N^(α)`.
entries.snippet: def laguerreCoeff (N α i : ℕ) : ℝ

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.laguerre
entries.docstring: The generalised Laguerre polynomial `L_N^(α)(x) = Σ_i (-1)^i C(N + α, N - i) x^i / i!`.
entries.snippet: def laguerre (N α : ℕ) : ℝ[X]

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.eval_laguerre
entries.snippet:
lemma eval_laguerre (x : ℝ) :
    (laguerre N α).eval x = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α i * x ^ i

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.eval_laguerre_zero
entries.snippet: lemma eval_laguerre_zero : (laguerre N α).eval 0 = ((N + α).choose N : ℝ)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.eval_derivative_laguerre
entries.snippet:
lemma eval_derivative_laguerre (x : ℝ) :
    (derivative (laguerre N α)).eval x =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α i * ((i : ℝ) * x ^ (i - 1))

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.eval_derivative_derivative_laguerre
entries.snippet:
lemma eval_derivative_derivative_laguerre (x : ℝ) :
    (derivative (derivative (laguerre N α))).eval x =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1),
        laguerreCoeff N α i * ((i : ℝ) * ((i - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * x ^ (i - 1 - 1))

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.laguerreCoeff_succ_mul
entries.docstring: The two-term recursion of the coefficients.
entries.snippet:
lemma laguerreCoeff_succ_mul {i : ℕ} (hi : i < N) :
    laguerreCoeff N α (i + 1) * (((i : ℝ) + 1) * ((i : ℝ) + 1 + α)) =
      -((N : ℝ) - i) * laguerreCoeff N α i

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.laguerre_ode
entries.docstring: **Laguerre's differential equation** `x L'' + (α + 1 - x) L' + N L = 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma laguerre_ode (x : ℝ) :
    x * (derivative (derivative (laguerre N α))).eval x +
      ((α : ℝ) + 1 - x) * (derivative (laguerre N α)).eval x +
        (N : ℝ) * (laguerre N α).eval x = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.sum_choose_mul_choose_neg
entries.docstring:
`Σ_i (-1)^i C(N + α, N - i) C(q + i, i) = C(N + α - q - 1, N)`, the Chu–Vandermonde identity
with a negative upper index.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_choose_mul_choose_neg (q : ℕ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), (-1 : ℤ) ^ i * ((N + α).choose (N - i) : ℤ) * ((q + i).choose i) =
      Ring.choose ((N + α : ℤ) - q - 1) N

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.sum_laguerreCoeff_mul_factorial
entries.docstring:
**Moments.** `Σ_i c_i (q + i)! = q! C(N + α - q - 1, N)`, the integral of `x^q e^(-x) L_N^(α)`
with the integer binomial coefficient `Ring.choose`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_laguerreCoeff_mul_factorial (q : ℕ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α i * ((q + i).factorial : ℝ) =
      (q.factorial : ℝ) * ((Ring.choose ((N + α : ℤ) - q - 1) N : ℤ) : ℝ)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.ringChoose_natCast_of_lt
entries.snippet: lemma ringChoose_natCast_of_lt {t : ℕ} (h : t < N) : Ring.choose (t : ℤ) N = 0

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.ringChoose_neg_one
entries.snippet: lemma ringChoose_neg_one : Ring.choose (-1 : ℤ) N = (-1) ^ N

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.ringChoose_neg_two
entries.snippet: lemma ringChoose_neg_two : Ring.choose (-2 : ℤ) N = (-1) ^ N * (N + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.integrableOn_pow_mul_exp_neg
entries.snippet:
lemma integrableOn_pow_mul_exp_neg (q : ℕ) :
    IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ => x ^ q * Real.exp (-x)) (Ioi 0)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_pow_mul_exp_neg
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_pow_mul_exp_neg (q : ℕ) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ q * Real.exp (-x) = q.factorial

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_laguerre_sq
entries.docstring: `∫₀^∞ x^e e^(-x) L(x)² dx = Σ_j c_j Σ_i c_i (e + j + i)!`.
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_laguerre_sq (e : ℕ) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ e * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α j *
        ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α i * ((e + j + i).factorial : ℝ)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_laguerre_sq_eq
entries.docstring: The integrals through the moments.
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_laguerre_sq_eq (e : ℕ) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ e * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α j * (((e + j).factorial : ℝ) *
        ((Ring.choose ((N + α : ℤ) - (e + j : ℕ) - 1) N : ℤ) : ℝ))

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.neg_one_pow_mul_self
entries.snippet: lemma neg_one_pow_mul_self (n : ℕ) : (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * (-1) ^ n = 1

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_laguerre_sq_alpha
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_laguerre_sq_alpha :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ α * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ((N + α).factorial : ℝ) / N.factorial

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_add_one
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_add_one :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ (α + 1) * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ((N + α).factorial : ℝ) / N.factorial * (2 * N + α + 1)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_one
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_one (hα : 1 ≤ α) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ (α - 1) * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ((N + α).factorial : ℝ) / (N.factorial * α)

entries.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_two
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_two (hα : 2 ≤ α) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ (α - 2) * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ((N + α).factorial : ℝ) * (2 * N + α + 1) /
        (N.factorial * (((α : ℝ) - 1) * α * (α + 1)))

entries.name: walshSign
entries.docstring: The sign `(-1) ^ (j * k)` for `j k : Fin 2`, as a complex number.
entries.snippet: def walshSign (j k : Fin 2) : ℂ

entries.name: walshSign_zero_left
entries.docstring: The sign `walshSign 0 k` is `1`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma walshSign_zero_left (k : Fin 2) : walshSign 0 k = 1

entries.name: walshSign_zero_right
entries.docstring: The sign `walshSign j 0` is `1`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma walshSign_zero_right (j : Fin 2) : walshSign j 0 = 1

entries.name: walshSign_one_one
entries.docstring: The sign `walshSign 1 1` is `-1`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma walshSign_one_one : walshSign 1 1 = -1

entries.name: walshSign_comm
entries.docstring: The sign `(-1) ^ (j * k)` is symmetric in `j` and `k`.
entries.snippet: lemma walshSign_comm (j k : Fin 2) : walshSign j k = walshSign k j

entries.name: walshSign_mul_self
entries.docstring: A sign squares to one.
entries.snippet: lemma walshSign_mul_self (j k : Fin 2) : walshSign j k * walshSign j k = 1

entries.name: conj_walshSign
entries.docstring: A sign equals its complex conjugate.
entries.snippet: lemma conj_walshSign (j k : Fin 2) : starRingEnd ℂ (walshSign j k) = walshSign j k

entries.name: norm_walshSign
entries.docstring: A sign has unit norm.
entries.snippet: lemma norm_walshSign (j k : Fin 2) : ‖walshSign j k‖ = 1

entries.name: sum_walshSign_mul_walshSign
entries.docstring: Orthogonality of the signs on `Fin 2`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_walshSign_mul_walshSign (a b : Fin 2) :
    ∑ k, walshSign a k * walshSign b k = if a = b then 2 else 0

entries.name: walsh
entries.docstring: The Walsh character `∏ i, (-1) ^ (x i * z i)` on `Fin n → Fin 2`.
entries.snippet: def walsh (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : ℂ

entries.name: walsh_eq
entries.docstring: The Walsh character is the product of the signs of the components.
entries.snippet: lemma walsh_eq (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : walsh x z = ∏ i, walshSign (x i) (z i)

entries.name: walsh_comm
entries.docstring: The Walsh character `walsh x z` is symmetric in `x` and `z`.
entries.snippet: lemma walsh_comm (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : walsh x z = walsh z x

entries.name: walsh_mul_self
entries.docstring: A Walsh character squares to one.
entries.snippet: lemma walsh_mul_self (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : walsh x z * walsh x z = 1

entries.name: conj_walsh
entries.docstring: A Walsh character equals its complex conjugate.
entries.snippet: lemma conj_walsh (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : starRingEnd ℂ (walsh x z) = walsh x z

entries.name: norm_walsh
entries.docstring: A Walsh character has unit norm.
entries.snippet: lemma norm_walsh (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : ‖walsh x z‖ = 1

entries.name: sum_walsh_mul_walsh
entries.docstring: Orthogonality of the Walsh characters.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_walsh_mul_walsh (x y : Fin n → Fin 2) :
    ∑ z, walsh x z * walsh y z = if x = y then 2 ^ n else 0

entries.name: walshVec
entries.docstring:
The rescaled Walsh vector `z ↦ (√(2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z` in
`EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n → Fin 2)`.
entries.snippet: def walshVec (x : Fin n → Fin 2) : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n → Fin 2)

entries.name: walshVec_apply
entries.docstring: The component `z` of `walshVec x` is `(√(2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma walshVec_apply (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) :
    walshVec x z = (Real.sqrt (2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z

entries.name: orthonormal_walshVec
entries.docstring: The rescaled Walsh vectors are orthonormal.
entries.snippet: lemma orthonormal_walshVec : Orthonormal ℂ (walshVec (n := n))

entries.name: walshBasis
entries.docstring:
The orthonormal basis of `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n → Fin 2)` formed by the rescaled Walsh
vectors `walshVec x`.
entries.snippet:
def walshBasis (n : ℕ) :
    OrthonormalBasis (Fin n → Fin 2) ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n → Fin 2))

entries.name: coe_walshBasis
entries.docstring: The vectors of `walshBasis n` are the rescaled Walsh vectors.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma coe_walshBasis (n : ℕ) : ⇑(walshBasis n) = walshVec

entries.name: sum_norm_sq_sum_mul_inv_sqrt_mul_walsh
entries.docstring:
Parseval's identity for the rescaled Walsh vectors. The vector
`x ↦ ∑ z, β z * (√(2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z` has the same squared norm as `β`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_norm_sq_sum_mul_inv_sqrt_mul_walsh (n : ℕ) (β : (Fin n → Fin 2) → ℂ) :
    ∑ x : Fin n → Fin 2, ‖∑ z, β z * ((Real.sqrt (2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z)‖ ^ 2 =
      ∑ z, ‖β z‖ ^ 2

entries.name: Subalgebra.polyRange
entries.docstring:
The polynomials with coefficients in a subalgebra, as a subalgebra of the polynomials
  with coefficients in the ambient algebra.
entries.snippet: noncomputable abbrev polyRange (S : Subalgebra R A) : Subalgebra R (Polynomial A)

entries.name: Subalgebra.monomial_mem_polyRange
entries.docstring: A monomial with a coefficient in `S` has coefficients in `S`.
entries.snippet:
lemma monomial_mem_polyRange {S : Subalgebra R A} {n : ℕ} {y : A} (hy : y ∈ S) :
    Polynomial.monomial n y ∈ S.polyRange

entries.name: Subalgebra.mem_range_mapAlgHom_of_adjoin
entries.docstring:
If an algebra map into the polynomials sends every generator of an adjoined subalgebra
  into the polynomials over `S`, it sends the whole subalgebra there: the condition cuts out
  a subalgebra, and the generators lie in it.

entries.name: Subalgebra.mapAlgHom_val_injective
entries.docstring: Polynomials over a subalgebra inject into polynomials over the ambient algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma mapAlgHom_val_injective (S : Subalgebra R A) :
    Function.Injective (Polynomial.mapAlgHom S.val)

entries.name: Subalgebra.polyRestrict
entries.docstring:
An algebra map into the polynomials, restricted to a subalgebra it carries into the
  polynomials over that subalgebra.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def polyRestrict (S : Subalgebra R A) (f : A →ₐ[R] Polynomial A)
    (hf : ∀ x : S, f (x : A) ∈ S.polyRange) : S →ₐ[R] Polynomial S

entries.name: Subalgebra.mapAlgHom_polyRestrict
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma mapAlgHom_polyRestrict {S : Subalgebra R A} {f : A →ₐ[R] Polynomial A}
    (hf : ∀ x : S, f (x : A) ∈ S.polyRange) (x : S) :
    Polynomial.mapAlgHom S.val (S.polyRestrict f hf x) = f (x : A)

entries.name: Subalgebra.polyRestrict_eq_monomial_iff
entries.docstring: An eigenvalue equation for the restricted map is the ambient eigenvalue equation.
entries.snippet:
lemma polyRestrict_eq_monomial_iff {S : Subalgebra R A} {f : A →ₐ[R] Polynomial A}
    (hf : ∀ x : S, f (x : A) ∈ S.polyRange) {n : ℕ} (x : S) :
    S.polyRestrict f hf x = Polynomial.monomial n x
      ↔ f (x : A) = Polynomial.monomial n (x : A)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.map
entries.docstring:
The algebra homomorphism between symmetric algebras induced by a linear map of the
  underlying modules.
entries.snippet: def map (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : SymmetricAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.map_apply_ι
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma map_apply_ι (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (x : M) : map f (ι R M x) = ι R N (f x)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.map_id
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma map_id : map (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[R] M) = AlgHom.id R (SymmetricAlgebra R M)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.map_comp_map
entries.snippet:
lemma map_comp_map (f : N →ₗ[R] P) (g : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    (map f).comp (map g) = map (f ∘ₗ g)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.congr
entries.docstring:
The algebra equivalence between symmetric algebras induced by a linear equivalence of
  the underlying modules.
entries.snippet: def congr (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) : SymmetricAlgebra R M ≃ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.congr_apply_ι
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma congr_apply_ι (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) (x : M) : congr e (ι R M x) = ι R N (e x)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.adjoin_range_ι
entries.docstring:
The symmetric algebra is generated, as an `R`-algebra, by the degree-one elements.
  Only a commutative semiring of scalars and a module are needed, so that the statement
  applies to a module whose additive structure is not presented as a group, such as a
  direct sum.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma adjoin_range_ι :
    Algebra.adjoin R (Set.range (ι R M)) = (⊤ : Subalgebra R (SymmetricAlgebra R M))

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.prodToTensor
entries.docstring:
The forward half of `prodEquiv`: a generator `(m, n)` is sent to
  `ι m ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ ι n`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def prodToTensor :
    SymmetricAlgebra R (M × N) →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R M ⊗[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.prodToTensor_ι
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma prodToTensor_ι (x : M × N) :
    prodToTensor (ι R (M × N) x)
      = ι R M x.1 ⊗ₜ[R] 1 + (1 : SymmetricAlgebra R M) ⊗ₜ[R] ι R N x.2

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.tensorToProd
entries.docstring:
The backward half of `prodEquiv`: the two inclusions of the factors, multiplied
  together.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def tensorToProd :
    SymmetricAlgebra R M ⊗[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R (M × N)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.tensorToProd_tmul
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma tensorToProd_tmul (a : SymmetricAlgebra R M) (b : SymmetricAlgebra R N) :
    tensorToProd (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) = map (LinearMap.inl R M N) a * map (LinearMap.inr R M N) b

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.prodEquiv
entries.docstring:
**The symmetric algebra of a direct sum is the tensor product of the symmetric
  algebras.** Two bosonic fields taken together are one field valued in the direct sum of
  their target spaces; their generators commute, so the ordinary tensor product suffices —
  no grading is needed, in contrast to the exterior-algebra analogue.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def prodEquiv :
    SymmetricAlgebra R (M × N) ≃ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R M ⊗[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.prodEquiv_ι
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma prodEquiv_ι (x : M × N) :
    prodEquiv (ι R (M × N) x)
      = ι R M x.1 ⊗ₜ[R] 1 + (1 : SymmetricAlgebra R M) ⊗ₜ[R] ι R N x.2

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationHom
entries.docstring:
The lift of the derivation extending `d` to the trivial square-zero extension of the
  symmetric algebra: the algebra homomorphism `x ↦ (x, derivationOfLinear d x)`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def derivationHom :
    SymmetricAlgebra R M →ₐ[R]
      TrivSqZeroExt (SymmetricAlgebra R M) (SymmetricAlgebra R M)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationHom_ι
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma derivationHom_ι (x : M) :
    derivationHom d (ι R M x) = (ι R M x, ι R M (d x))

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationHom_fst
entries.docstring: The first component of the square-zero lift is the identity.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma derivationHom_fst (x : SymmetricAlgebra R M) : (derivationHom d x).fst = x

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear
entries.docstring:
**The derivation of the symmetric algebra extending a linear endomorphism** `d` of `M`:
  the map obeying the Leibniz rule whose value on a generator `ι x` is `ι (d x)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def derivationOfLinear : SymmetricAlgebra R M →ₗ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R M where

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_ι
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma derivationOfLinear_ι (x : M) :
    derivationOfLinear d (ι R M x) = ι R M (d x)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_one
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma derivationOfLinear_one : derivationOfLinear d (1 : SymmetricAlgebra R M) = 0

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_algebraMap
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma derivationOfLinear_algebraMap (r : R) :
    derivationOfLinear d (algebraMap R (SymmetricAlgebra R M) r) = 0

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_mul
entries.docstring: The Leibniz rule for the derivation extending `d`.
entries.snippet:
lemma derivationOfLinear_mul (x y : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    derivationOfLinear d (x * y)
      = derivationOfLinear d x * y + x * derivationOfLinear d y

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_comm_apply
entries.docstring: Derivations extending commuting endomorphisms commute.
entries.snippet:
lemma derivationOfLinear_comm_apply {d₁ d₂ : M →ₗ[R] M} (h : d₁ ∘ₗ d₂ = d₂ ∘ₗ d₁)
    (x : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    derivationOfLinear d₁ (derivationOfLinear d₂ x)
      = derivationOfLinear d₂ (derivationOfLinear d₁ x)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.algHom_derivationOfLinear
entries.docstring:
An algebra map carries one derivation to the other when the linear map it is
  determined by on the generators intertwines the two endomorphisms. The hypotheses are
  stated pointwise so that the lemma can be applied without rewriting inside a large
  algebra.

entries.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra
entries.docstring:
The representation on the symmetric algebra extending a representation on the
  generators: the substitution homomorphism determined by the action on the generators.
  It is built from `SymmetricAlgebra.lift` rather than from `SymmetricAlgebra.map`, so that
  it is available over a commutative semiring and an additive commutative monoid — the
  generality the generator spaces of a multi-species field theory, which are direct sums,
  are elaborated at.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def symmetricAlgebra (ρ : Representation R G M) :
    Representation R G (SymmetricAlgebra R M) where

entries.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebraAlgHom
entries.docstring: The action of a group element, as an algebra homomorphism.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def symmetricAlgebraAlgHom (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) :
    SymmetricAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R M

entries.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_apply (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G)
    (x : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g x = ρ.symmetricAlgebraAlgHom g x

entries.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_ι
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma symmetricAlgebra_ι (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (x : M) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (SymmetricAlgebra.ι R M x)
      = SymmetricAlgebra.ι R M (ρ g x)

entries.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_apply_one
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma symmetricAlgebra_apply_one (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (1 : SymmetricAlgebra R M) = 1

entries.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_apply_mul
entries.snippet:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_apply_mul (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G)
    (x y : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (x * y)
      = ρ.symmetricAlgebra g x * ρ.symmetricAlgebra g y

entries.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_algebraMap
entries.snippet:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_algebraMap (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (r : R) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (algebraMap R (SymmetricAlgebra R M) r)
      = algebraMap R (SymmetricAlgebra R M) r

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.symmetricAlgebra_derivationOfLinear
entries.docstring:
Covariance of the derivation under the representation. If the representation
  carries each endomorphism of a family into a combination of the others on the generators,
  then it carries the derivation extending one into the same combination of the derivations
  extending the others on the whole exterior algebra. This is the shape the statement that
  the total derivative is a Lorentz vector takes; it is proved by induction rather than by
  algebra-map extensionality, a derivation not being an algebra map.
entries.snippet:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_derivationOfLinear {G κ : Type*} [Monoid G] [Fintype κ]
    (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (d : κ → M →ₗ[R] M) (μ : κ) (c : κ → R)
    (h : ∀ x, ρ g (d μ x) = ∑ a, c a • d a (ρ g x)) (y : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (derivationOfLinear (d μ) y)
      = ∑ a, c a • derivationOfLinear (d a) (ρ.symmetricAlgebra g y)

entries.name: SymmetricAlgebra.algHom_symmetricAlgebra
entries.docstring:
An algebra map carries one representation to the other when the linear map it is
  determined by on the generators intertwines the two representations on them. Unlike the
  derivation statement this is pure extensionality of algebra maps, each group element
  acting by one; the hypotheses are stated pointwise so that the lemma can be applied
  without rewriting inside a large algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma algHom_symmetricAlgebra {N G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Monoid G]
    (F : SymmetricAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N) {f : M →ₗ[R] N}
    (hF : ∀ x, F (ι R M x) = ι R N (f x))
    {ρ : Representation R G M} {σ : Representation R G N} (g : G)
    (h : ∀ x, f (ρ g x) = σ g (f x)) (y : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    F (ρ.symmetricAlgebra g y) = σ.symmetricAlgebra g (F y)

entries.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
entries.docstring:
**Bochner's theorem on a discrete abelian group.** A function on a discrete abelian group is
positive definite if and only if it is the Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite inner regular
measure on the Pontryagin dual.
entries.snippet:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq (φ : G → ℂ) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ ↔
      ∃ μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
        μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_continuousAt
entries.docstring:
**Bochner's theorem on a locally compact abelian group**, existence half.
A positive-definite function that is continuous at `0` is the Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a
finite inner regular measure on the Pontryagin dual.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsPositiveDefiniteSub.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_continuousAt {φ : G → ℂ}
    (hφ : IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ) (hφ₀ : ContinuousAt φ 0) :
    ∃ μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
      μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

entries.name: TauCeti.«lemma@69465c7e»
entries.docstring:
**Unique inner regular form of Bochner's theorem.** A positive-definite function continuous at
`0` has a unique finite inner regular representing measure on the Pontryagin dual. No countability
or metrizability assumption is needed.
entries.snippet:
lemma
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub.existsUnique_innerRegular_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_continuousAt
    {φ : G → ℂ} (hφ : IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ) (hφ₀ : ContinuousAt φ 0) :
    ∃! μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
      μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

entries.name: TauCeti.«lemma@c96371b0»
entries.docstring:
**Bochner's characterization without countability assumptions.** A function on a locally
compact abelian group is continuous and positive definite if and only if it is the
Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a unique finite inner regular measure on the Pontryagin dual.
entries.snippet:
lemma
    continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_existsUnique_innerRegular_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
    (φ : G → ℂ) :
    (Continuous φ ∧ IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ) ↔
      ∃! μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
        μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

entries.name: TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_existsUnique_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
entries.docstring:
**Bochner's characterization on a locally compact abelian group with Polish dual.** A
function is continuous and positive definite if and only if it is the Fourier–Stieltjes
transform of a unique finite positive Borel measure on the dual group. The dual is Polish when
the group is second countable.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_existsUnique_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
    [PolishSpace (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))] (φ : G → ℂ) :
    (Continuous φ ∧ IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ) ↔
      ∃! μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
        μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

entries.name: TauCeti.CharacterSpaceMeasure.nonneg_apply_symm_realToRCLike
entries.docstring:
Pulled back along the Gelfand transform, a functional nonnegative on `star a * a` is
nonnegative on nonnegative real functions: such a function is `star h * h` for `h = √g`.

entries.name: TauCeti.CharacterSpaceMeasure.apply_symm_realToRCLike_eq_re
entries.docstring:
Pulled back along the Gelfand transform, a functional nonnegative on `star a * a` is real on
real functions.
entries.snippet:
private lemma apply_symm_realToRCLike_eq_re (hf : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f (star a * a))
    (g : C(characterSpace ℂ A, ℝ)) :
    f ((gelfandStarTransform A).symm (g.realToRCLike ℂ)) =
      (f ((gelfandStarTransform A).symm (g.realToRCLike ℂ))).re

entries.name: TauCeti.CharacterSpaceMeasure.realFunctional
entries.docstring:
The positive linear functional on `C_c(Δ, ℝ) = C(Δ, ℝ)` induced by `f` through the Gelfand
transform.
entries.snippet:
private def realFunctional (hf : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f (star a * a)) :
    C_c(characterSpace ℂ A, ℝ) →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ where

entries.name: TauCeti.CharacterSpaceMeasure.realFunctional_apply
entries.snippet:
private lemma realFunctional_apply (hf : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f (star a * a))
    (g : C_c(characterSpace ℂ A, ℝ)) :
    realFunctional f hf g =
      (f ((gelfandStarTransform A).symm (g.toContinuousMap.realToRCLike ℂ))).re

entries.name: LinearMap.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq
entries.docstring:
**Positive functionals on a commutative C⋆-algebra are measures on its character space.**
A linear functional on a unital commutative C⋆-algebra that is nonnegative on every
`star a * a` is integration against a finite inner regular positive measure `μ` on the
character space: `f a = ∫ ω, ω a ∂μ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma LinearMap.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq (f : A →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ)
    (hf : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f (star a * a)) :
    ∃ μ : Measure (characterSpace ℂ A), IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ μ.InnerRegular ∧
      ∀ a, f a = ∫ ω, ω a ∂μ

entries.name: WeakDual.CharacterSpace.integral_apply_star_mul_self
entries.docstring:
For a measure `μ` on the character space of a unital C⋆-algebra, integrating
`ω ↦ ω (star a * a) = |ω a|²` gives the squared `L²` norm of `ω ↦ ω a`. Hence if `μ` represents a
functional `f`, as in `LinearMap.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq`, then
`f (star a * a) = ∫ |ω a|² dμ(ω)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma WeakDual.CharacterSpace.integral_apply_star_mul_self {E : Type*} [CStarAlgebra E]
    [MeasurableSpace (characterSpace ℂ E)] (μ : Measure (characterSpace ℂ E)) (a : E) :
    ∫ ω, ω (star a * a) ∂μ = ((∫ ω, ‖ω a‖ ^ 2 ∂μ : ℝ) : ℂ)

entries.name: inner_star_mul_self_apply
entries.docstring:
For a star algebra `B` of operators, the positive vector functional of `ξ` takes the value
`‖a ξ‖²` at `star a * a`.
entries.snippet:
private lemma inner_star_mul_self_apply (ξ : H) (a : B) :
    ⟪ξ, ((star a * a : B) : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ⟫_ℂ = ((‖(a : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)

entries.name: StarSubalgebra.integral_norm_sq_eq_norm_apply_sq
entries.docstring:
For a closed star algebra `B` of operators, if a measure `μ` on the character space
represents the positive vector functional of `ξ`, then `∫ |ω a|² dμ(ω) = ‖a ξ‖²` for every
`a ∈ B`.

entries.name: StarSubalgebra.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq_inner
entries.docstring:
**Positive vector functionals are measures on the character space.** For a closed
commutative star algebra `B` of operators on a complex Hilbert space and a vector `ξ`, the
positive vector functional `a ↦ ⟪ξ, a ξ⟫` is integration against a finite inner regular positive
measure on the character space of `B`.
entries.snippet:
lemma StarSubalgebra.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq_inner (ξ : H) :
    ∃ μ : Measure (characterSpace ℂ B), IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ μ.InnerRegular ∧
      ∀ a : B, ⟪ξ, (a : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ⟫_ℂ = ∫ ω, ω a ∂μ

entries.name: MonoidHom.existsUnique_pontryaginDual_of_unitary_translate
entries.docstring:
A character nonzero on a commuting operator with norm-continuous unitary translates
induces a unique continuous circle-valued character. It describes every translate in the subalgebra,
not just the translates of the witnessing operator.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.MonoidHom.existsUnique_pontryaginDual_of_unitary_translate
    (ρ : G →* B) (hρ : ∀ g, ρ g ∈ unitary B)
    (A : StarSubalgebra ℂ B) [CompleteSpace A]
    (a : A) (hcomm : ∀ g, Commute (ρ g) (a : B))
    (hmem : ∀ g, ρ g * (a : B) ∈ A)
    (hcont : Continuous fun g => ρ g * (a : B))
    (ω : characterSpace ℂ A) (ha : ω a ≠ 0) :
    ∃! χ : PontryaginDual G,
      ∀ (g : G) (b : A) (hb : ρ g * (b : B) ∈ A),
        ω ⟨ρ g * (b : B), hb⟩ = (χ g : ℂ) * ω b

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.continuous_pontryaginMeasureTransform
entries.docstring:
The transform of a tight finite measure on the Pontryagin dual is continuous. Tightness is
automatic for finite Radon measures and is the regularity needed when the dual is not metrizable.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.continuous_pontryaginMeasureTransform
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)))
    (hμ : IsTightMeasureSet {μ.toMeasure}) :
    Continuous μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform

entries.name: TauCeti.PontryaginDual.continuous_coe_eval_const
entries.docstring: Complex-valued evaluation of a Pontryagin character at a fixed monoid element is continuous.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma continuous_coe_eval_const (g : G) :
    Continuous (fun χ : _root_.PontryaginDual G => (χ g : ℂ))

entries.name: TauCeti.PontryaginDual.integrable_coe_eval
entries.docstring: Complex-valued evaluation of a Pontryagin character is integrable against a finite measure.
entries.snippet:
lemma integrable_coe_eval
    {μ : Measure (_root_.PontryaginDual G)} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (g : G) :
    Integrable (fun χ : _root_.PontryaginDual G => (χ g : ℂ)) μ

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform
entries.docstring:
The Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite measure on the Pontryagin dual of an
additive group.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) (g : G) : ℂ

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_apply
entries.docstring: The transform evaluated at a group element is the integral of character evaluations.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_apply
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) (g : G) :
    μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform g =
      ∫ χ, (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ) ∂μ.toMeasure

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_zero
entries.docstring: At the identity, the transform records the total mass of the measure.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_zero
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) :
    μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform 0 = (μ.toMeasure.real Set.univ : ℂ)

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_zero_measure
entries.docstring: The transform of the zero measure vanishes.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_zero_measure :
    (0 : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))).pontryaginMeasureTransform = 0

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_smul
entries.docstring: The transform commutes with nonnegative scalar multiplication of finite measures.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_smul
    (c : NNReal) (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) :
    (c • μ).pontryaginMeasureTransform = c • μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_add
entries.docstring: The transform commutes with addition of finite measures.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_add
    (μ ν : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) :
    (μ + ν).pontryaginMeasureTransform =
      μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform + ν.pontryaginMeasureTransform

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_dirac
entries.docstring: The transform of a point mass is its character.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_dirac
    (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) (g : G) :
    FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform
      (⟨Measure.dirac χ, inferInstance⟩ : FiniteMeasure
        (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) g =
      (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ)

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.algebra
entries.docstring: The closed star algebra generated by the integrated operators, for a Haar measure.
entries.snippet: private abbrev algebra : StarSubalgebra ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.«instance@710d4642»
entries.snippet: private instance : IsMulCommutative (algebra π hcont hπ)

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.«instance@9485f75a»
entries.snippet: private noncomputable instance : CommCStarAlgebra (algebra π hcont hπ) where

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.op
entries.docstring: An integrated operator, as an element of the integrated algebra.
entries.snippet: private abbrev op (f : G →₁[Measure.addHaar] ℂ) : algebra π hcont hπ

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.translate
entries.docstring: A translated integrated operator `π(g) π(f)`, as an element of the integrated algebra.
entries.snippet: private abbrev translate (f : G →₁[Measure.addHaar] ℂ) (g : G) : algebra π hcont hπ

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.translate_eq
entries.snippet:
private lemma translate_eq (f : G →₁[Measure.addHaar] ℂ) (g : G) :
    translate π hcont hπ f g =
      op π hcont hπ (Lp.compMeasurePreserving (fun x ↦ -g + x)
        (measurePreserving_add_left Measure.addHaar (-g)) f)

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.mem_algebra
entries.snippet:
private lemma mem_algebra (f : G →₁[Measure.addHaar] ℂ) :
    π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hπ.exists_norm_le Measure.addHaar f ∈ algebra π hcont hπ

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.op_eq
entries.snippet:
private lemma op_eq (f : G →₁[Measure.addHaar] ℂ) :
    op π hcont hπ f = ⟨_, mem_algebra π hcont hπ f⟩

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.support
entries.docstring:
The characters of the integrated algebra that do not annihilate every integrated
operator.
entries.snippet: private abbrev support : Set (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.dual
entries.docstring:
The continuous group character attached to a character of the integrated algebra, and `1`
for a character annihilating every integrated operator.
entries.snippet:
private def dual (ω : characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ)) :
    PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.apply_translate
entries.docstring:
**The translation equation.** Every character of the integrated algebra multiplies a
translated integrated operator by its group character.

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.continuousOn_dual
entries.docstring:
The group character of a character of the integrated algebra depends continuously on it, on
the open set of characters that do not annihilate every integrated operator.
entries.snippet: private lemma continuousOn_dual : ContinuousOn (dual π hcont hπ) (support π hcont hπ)

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.ae_mem_support
entries.docstring: A vector-state measure gives zero mass to characters annihilating all integrated operators.
entries.snippet:
private lemma ae_mem_support [MeasurableSpace (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))]
    [BorelSpace (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))]
    {ν : Measure (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))} [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {ξ : H}
    (hrep : ∀ a : algebra π hcont hπ, ⟪ξ, (a : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ⟫_ℂ = ∫ ω, ω a ∂ν) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂ν, ω ∈ support π hcont hπ

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.norm_integral_mul_apply_le
entries.docstring:
If `ν` represents the positive vector functional of `ξ`, then integrating `ω ↦ ω a` against
a weight bounded by `1` costs at most `δ ν(Δ) + ‖a ξ‖² / δ`, for every `δ > 0`. This is the
bound of an `L¹` norm by an `L²` norm, through `‖z‖ ≤ δ + ‖z‖² / δ`.
entries.snippet:
private lemma norm_integral_mul_apply_le [MeasurableSpace (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))]
    [BorelSpace (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))]
    {ν : Measure (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))} [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {ξ : H}
    (hrep : ∀ a : algebra π hcont hπ, ⟪ξ, (a : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ⟫_ℂ = ∫ ω, ω a ∂ν)
    {w : characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ) → ℂ}
    (hw₁ : ∀ ω, ‖w ω‖ ≤ 1) (a : algebra π hcont hπ) {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ‖∫ ω, w ω * ω a ∂ν‖ ≤ δ * ν.real Set.univ + ‖(a : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ‖ ^ 2 / δ

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.measurable_dual
entries.docstring: The group character of a character of the integrated algebra depends measurably on it.
entries.snippet:
private lemma measurable_dual [MeasurableSpace (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))]
    [BorelSpace (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))] : Measurable (dual π hcont hπ)

entries.name: TauCeti.StronglyContinuousSpectral.inner_eq_integral_dual
entries.docstring:
**The matrix coefficient is the integral of the group characters.** If `ν` represents the
positive vector functional of `ξ` on the integrated algebra, then
`⟪ξ, π(g) ξ⟫ = ∫ χ_ω(g) dν(ω)`.
entries.snippet:
private lemma inner_eq_integral_dual [MeasurableSpace (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))]
    [BorelSpace (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))]
    {ν : Measure (characterSpace ℂ (algebra π hcont hπ))} [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {ξ : H}
    (hrep : ∀ a : algebra π hcont hπ, ⟪ξ, (a : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ⟫_ℂ = ∫ ω, ω a ∂ν) (g : G) :
    ⟪ξ, π (.ofAdd g) ξ⟫_ℂ = ∫ ω, (dual π hcont hπ ω (.ofAdd g) : ℂ) ∂ν

entries.name: ContRepresentation.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_inner
entries.docstring:
**Spectral theorem for strongly continuous unitary representations**, cyclic form. For a
strongly continuous unitary representation `π` of a locally compact abelian group `G` on a
Hilbert space `H` and a vector `ξ`, the matrix coefficient `g ↦ ⟪ξ, π(g) ξ⟫` is the
Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite inner regular measure on the Pontryagin dual of `G`.
entries.snippet:
lemma ContRepresentation.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_inner
    (π : ContRepresentation ℂ (Multiplicative G) H)
    (hcont : ∀ v, Continuous fun g : G ↦ π (.ofAdd g) v)
    (hπ : ContRepresentation.IsUnitary π) (ξ : H) :
    ∃ μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
      μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ ∀ g, μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform g = ⟪ξ, π (.ofAdd g) ξ⟫_ℂ

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous
entries.docstring:
Evaluation at `g`, as a bounded continuous complex-valued function on the Pontryagin dual.
Its values lie on the unit circle, so its norm is bounded by one.
entries.snippet:
def evalBoundedContinuous (g : G) :
    _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_apply
entries.docstring: Evaluation of `evalBoundedContinuous` at a character.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_apply (g : G)
    (χ : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    evalBoundedContinuous g χ = (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ)

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_zero
entries.docstring: Evaluation at zero is the constant function one.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_zero :
    evalBoundedContinuous (0 : G) = 1

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_add
entries.docstring: Evaluation turns addition in the original group into pointwise multiplication.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_add (g h : G) :
    evalBoundedContinuous (g + h) =
      evalBoundedContinuous g * evalBoundedContinuous h

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_neg
entries.docstring: Evaluation at the negative of a group element is the pointwise star of evaluation there.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_neg (g : G) :
    evalBoundedContinuous (-g) = star (evalBoundedContinuous g)

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalMonoidHom
entries.docstring: Evaluation as a monoid homomorphism from the multiplicative copy of the original group.
entries.snippet:
def evalMonoidHom : Multiplicative G →*
    (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ) where

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalMonoidHom_apply
entries.docstring: Evaluation of `evalMonoidHom` at a character.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma evalMonoidHom_apply (g : Multiplicative G)
    (χ : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    evalMonoidHom g χ = (χ g : ℂ)

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalAlgHom
entries.docstring:
The algebra homomorphism sending a formal finite linear combination of group elements to the
corresponding finite linear combination of evaluation characters.
entries.snippet:
def evalAlgHom : AddMonoidAlgebra ℂ G →ₐ[ℂ]
    (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ)

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalAlgHom_apply
entries.docstring: Evaluation of `evalAlgHom` is the corresponding finite linear combination of characters.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma evalAlgHom_apply (a : AddMonoidAlgebra ℂ G)
    (χ : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    evalAlgHom a χ = a.coeff.sum fun g c => c * (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ)

entries.name: PontryaginDual.star_mem_range_evalAlgHom
entries.docstring: The range of `evalAlgHom` is closed under pointwise complex conjugation.

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalPoly
entries.docstring: The star subalgebra of bounded continuous functions generated by evaluation characters.
entries.snippet:
def evalPoly : StarSubalgebra ℂ
    (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ) where

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalPoly_toSubalgebra
entries.docstring: The underlying subalgebra of `evalPoly` is the range of `evalAlgHom`.
entries.snippet:
lemma evalPoly_toSubalgebra :
    (evalPoly (G := G)).toSubalgebra = evalAlgHom.range

entries.name: PontryaginDual.mem_evalPoly
entries.docstring:
Membership in `evalPoly` means being a finite linear combination of evaluation
characters.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_evalPoly (f : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ) :
    f ∈ evalPoly ↔
      ∃ a : AddMonoidAlgebra ℂ G,
        f = a.coeff.sum fun g c => c • evalBoundedContinuous g

entries.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_mem_evalPoly
entries.docstring: Every evaluation character belongs to `evalPoly`.
entries.snippet:
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_mem_evalPoly (g : G) :
    evalBoundedContinuous g ∈ evalPoly

entries.name: PontryaginDual.separatesPoints_evalPoly
entries.docstring: The evaluation-character algebra separates points of the Pontryagin dual.
entries.snippet:
lemma separatesPoints_evalPoly :
    ((evalPoly : StarSubalgebra ℂ
      (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ)).map
        (BoundedContinuousFunction.toContinuousMapStarₐ ℂ)).SeparatesPoints

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.integral_eq_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
entries.docstring:
Two finite measures on the dual with the same Fourier--Stieltjes transform integrate every
finite linear combination of evaluation characters equally.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.integral_eq_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
    {P Q : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    (h : ∀ g, P.pontryaginMeasureTransform g = Q.pontryaginMeasureTransform g)
    {f : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ} (hf : f ∈ _root_.PontryaginDual.evalPoly) :
    ∫ χ, f χ ∂P = ∫ χ, f χ ∂Q

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
entries.docstring:
**Uniqueness of Fourier--Stieltjes measures on a Polish Pontryagin dual.** Two finite measures
on the dual are equal when their transforms agree on every element of the original group.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
    {P Q : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    (h : ∀ g, P.pontryaginMeasureTransform g = Q.pontryaginMeasureTransform g) :
    P = Q

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_injective
entries.docstring:
The Fourier--Stieltjes transform is injective on finite measures on a Polish Pontryagin
dual.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_injective :
    Function.Injective
      (fun P : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) =>
        P.pontryaginMeasureTransform)

entries.name: TauCeti.«lemma@add06f0d»
entries.docstring:
**Uniqueness of inner regular Fourier--Stieltjes measures.** On the Pontryagin dual of a
locally compact abelian group, two finite inner regular measures are equal when their transforms
agree on every element of the group. No countability or metrizability is assumed.
entries.snippet:
lemma
    _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_innerRegular
    {P Q : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    [P.toMeasure.InnerRegular] [Q.toMeasure.InnerRegular]
    (h : ∀ g, P.pontryaginMeasureTransform g = Q.pontryaginMeasureTransform g) :
    P = Q

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_injOn_innerRegular
entries.docstring:
The Fourier--Stieltjes transform is injective on finite inner regular measures on the
Pontryagin dual of a locally compact abelian group.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_injOn_innerRegular :
    Set.InjOn
      (fun P : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) =>
        P.pontryaginMeasureTransform)
      {P | P.toMeasure.InnerRegular}

entries.name: OrthonormalBasis.spanIndices
entries.docstring:
The subspace spanned by the orthonormal basis vectors `b i` for indices
`i ∈ s`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def spanIndices (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Set ι) :
    Submodule 𝕜 E

entries.name: OrthonormalBasis.spanIndices_eq_span
entries.docstring:
The selected subspace is the span of its basis vectors.
Use this identity to apply `Submodule.span`'s induction or universal property.
entries.snippet:
lemma spanIndices_eq_span (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Set ι) :
    b.spanIndices s = Submodule.span 𝕜 (b '' s)

entries.name: OrthonormalBasis.spanIndices_mono
entries.docstring: Selecting more indices spans more.
entries.snippet:
lemma spanIndices_mono (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) {s t : Set ι} (h : s ⊆ t) :
    b.spanIndices s ≤ b.spanIndices t

entries.name: OrthonormalBasis.mem_spanIndices_of_mem
entries.docstring: A selected basis vector lies in the span of its index set.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_spanIndices_of_mem (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) {s : Set ι} {i : ι}
    (hi : i ∈ s) : b i ∈ b.spanIndices s

entries.name: OrthonormalBasis.repr_eq_zero_of_mem_spanIndices
entries.docstring:
A vector in the span of a selected subfamily has zero coordinate at any
index outside the selection.
entries.snippet:
lemma repr_eq_zero_of_mem_spanIndices (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E)
    {s : Set ι} {x : E} (hx : x ∈ b.spanIndices s) {i : ι} (hi : i ∉ s) :
    b.repr x i = 0

entries.name: OrthonormalBasis.mem_spanIndices_iff
entries.docstring:
Membership in the span of a selected subfamily is exactly the vanishing of
the coordinates outside the selection.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma mem_spanIndices_iff (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E)
    {s : Set ι} {x : E} :
    x ∈ b.spanIndices s ↔ ∀ i ∉ s, b.repr x i = 0

entries.name: OrthonormalBasis.finrank_spanIndices
entries.docstring:
The span of a selected subfamily has dimension the number of selected
indices.
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_spanIndices (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Finset ι) :
    finrank 𝕜 (b.spanIndices ↑s) = s.card

entries.name: OrthonormalBasis.finrank_spanIndices_set
entries.docstring:
The span of a selected set of basis vectors has dimension equal to the
number of selected indices.
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_spanIndices_set (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Set ι) :
    finrank 𝕜 (b.spanIndices s) = s.ncard

entries.name: OrthonormalBasis.orthogonal_spanIndices
entries.docstring:
The orthogonal complement of the span of a selected subfamily is the span
of the complementary subfamily.
entries.snippet:
lemma orthogonal_spanIndices (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Set ι) :
    (b.spanIndices s)ᗮ = b.spanIndices sᶜ

entries.name: sum_sq_norm_repr_eq_sq_norm
entries.docstring:
Parseval: in an orthonormal basis the squared norms of the coordinates sum
to the squared norm.  Thin wrapper around
`OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_norm_inner_right`.
entries.snippet:
private lemma sum_sq_norm_repr_eq_sq_norm (b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) 𝕜 E) (x : E) :
    ∑ i : Fin n, ‖b.repr x i‖ ^ 2 = ‖x‖ ^ 2

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_of_eigenbasis
entries.docstring:
Diagonalization of the quadratic form in any orthonormal eigenbasis: if
`S (w i) = μ i • w i` for all `i`, then
`re ⟪S x, x⟫ = ∑ i, μ i * ‖w.repr x i‖ ^ 2`.
entries.snippet:
lemma re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_of_eigenbasis
    (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (w : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) 𝕜 E) {μ : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hw : ∀ i, S (w i) = (μ i : 𝕜) • w i) (x : E) :
    RCLike.re ⟪S x, x⟫_𝕜 = ∑ i : Fin n, μ i * ‖w.repr x i‖ ^ 2

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.le_re_inner_of_eigenbasis
entries.docstring:
On the span of the eigenvectors selected by `s`, the quadratic form is
bounded below by any lower bound on the selected values (general-eigenbasis
version of `le_re_inner_apply_self_of_mem_spanIndices`).

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_le_of_eigenbasis
entries.docstring: Dual of `le_re_inner_of_eigenbasis`.

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_eigenvalues_mul_sq
entries.docstring:
The quadratic form `re ⟪T x, x⟫` of a symmetric operator `T` expressed in
its eigenbasis: it is the eigenvalue-weighted sum of the squared norms of the
coordinates of `x`.  This is the diagonalization of the quadratic form.  (For
symmetric `T` the inner product `⟪T x, x⟫` is real, so no information is lost
by taking the real part.)
entries.snippet:
lemma re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_eigenvalues_mul_sq
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (x : E) :
    RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜
      = ∑ i : Fin n, hT.eigenvalues hn i * ‖(hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).repr x i‖ ^ 2

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_apply_self_le_of_mem_spanIndices
entries.docstring:
On the span of a selected subfamily of the eigenbasis, the quadratic form
is bounded by any bound on the selected eigenvalues: if
`x ∈ b.spanIndices s` (so its coordinates vanish off `s`) and every selected
eigenvalue satisfies `λᵢ ≤ c`, then `re ⟪T x, x⟫ ≤ c ‖x‖²`.
entries.snippet:
lemma re_inner_apply_self_le_of_mem_spanIndices
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) {s : Set (Fin n)} {c : ℝ}
    (hc : ∀ i ∈ s, hT.eigenvalues hn i ≤ c)
    {x : E} (hx : x ∈ (hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).spanIndices s) :
    RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ c * ‖x‖ ^ 2

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.le_re_inner_apply_self_of_mem_spanIndices
entries.docstring:
Dual of `re_inner_apply_self_le_of_mem_spanIndices`: if
`x ∈ b.spanIndices s` and every selected eigenvalue satisfies `c ≤ λᵢ`, then
`c ‖x‖² ≤ re ⟪T x, x⟫`.
entries.snippet:
lemma le_re_inner_apply_self_of_mem_spanIndices
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) {s : Set (Fin n)} {c : ℝ}
    (hc : ∀ i ∈ s, c ≤ hT.eigenvalues hn i)
    {x : E} (hx : x ∈ (hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).spanIndices s) :
    c * ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.exists_unit_vector_re_inner_le_eigenvalue
entries.docstring:
**Courant–Fischer, upper direction.** On any subspace `V` of dimension
`k + 1` there is a unit vector `x` with `re ⟪T x, x⟫ ≤ λₖ(T)`, where `λ` is the
decreasing enumeration `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` of the eigenvalues
of the symmetric operator `T`.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_unit_vector_re_inner_le_eigenvalue
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n)
    (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) (hV : finrank 𝕜 V = (k : ℕ) + 1) :
    ∃ x ∈ V, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧ RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ hT.eigenvalues hn k

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.exists_submodule_forall_unit_eigenvalue_le_re_inner
entries.docstring:
**Courant–Fischer, lower direction.** There is a subspace `V` of dimension
`k + 1` on which every unit vector `x` satisfies `λₖ(T) ≤ re ⟪T x, x⟫`, where
`λ` is the decreasing enumeration `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` of the
eigenvalues of the symmetric operator `T`.

Witness: `V = span {bᵢ : i ≤ k}`; on it the quadratic form is bounded below by
`λₖ` since all involved eigenvalues are `≥ λₖ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_submodule_forall_unit_eigenvalue_le_re_inner
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n) :
    ∃ V : Submodule 𝕜 E, finrank 𝕜 V = (k : ℕ) + 1 ∧
      ∀ x ∈ V, ‖x‖ = 1 → hT.eigenvalues hn k ≤ RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_eq_iSup_iInf_re_inner
entries.docstring:
**Courant–Fischer min-max equality.** The `k`-th (decreasingly sorted)
eigenvalue of a symmetric operator on a finite-dimensional inner product space
over `𝕜 = ℝ, ℂ` is the supremum, over the subspaces `V` of dimension `k + 1`,
of the infimum of the Rayleigh quotient `re ⟪T x, x⟫` over the unit vectors of
`V`.

Horn & Johnson, *Matrix Analysis* 2nd ed., Theorem 4.2.6.
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenvalues_eq_iSup_iInf_re_inner
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn k =
      ⨆ V : {V : Submodule 𝕜 E // finrank 𝕜 V = (k : ℕ) + 1},
        ⨅ x : {x : E // x ∈ (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) ∧ ‖x‖ = 1},
          RCLike.re ⟪T (x : E), (x : E)⟫_𝕜

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_eq_of_eigenbasis
entries.docstring:
**Sorted-eigenvalue uniqueness.**  If an orthonormal basis `w`
diagonalizes the symmetric operator `S` with an *antitone* value list `μ`,
then `μ` is the sorted eigenvalue list: `hS.eigenvalues hn = μ`.
(Courant–Fischer: both lists satisfy the same minimax characterization.)
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenvalues_eq_of_eigenbasis
    (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (w : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) 𝕜 E)
    {μ : Fin n → ℝ} (hμ : Antitone μ) (hw : ∀ i, S (w i) = (μ i : 𝕜) • w i) :
    hS.eigenvalues hn = μ

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_mono
entries.docstring:
**Loewner monotonicity of the sorted eigenvalues.**  If the quadratic form
of `T` is dominated by that of `S`, then so is every sorted eigenvalue.
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenvalue_mono
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (h : ∀ x, RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ RCLike.re ⟪S x, x⟫_𝕜) (k : Fin n) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn k ≤ hS.eigenvalues hn k

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.map_mem_spanIndices
entries.docstring:
The span of a selected subfamily of the eigenbasis of a symmetric operator
is invariant under the operator.
entries.snippet:
lemma map_mem_spanIndices (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (s : Set (Fin n)) {x : E}
    (hx : x ∈ (hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).spanIndices s) :
    T x ∈ (hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).spanIndices s

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_sub_le
entries.docstring:
One-sided Weyl bound: `λₖ(S) − λₖ(T) ≤ ‖S − T‖op`.  This is the core
estimate; Weyl's inequality follows by symmetry.

We take a witness subspace `V` of dimension `k + 1` on which
`λₖ(S) ≤ re ⟪S x, x⟫` (lower direction for `S`), then a unit vector `x ∈ V`
with `re ⟪T x, x⟫ ≤ λₖ(T)` (upper direction for `T`).  The difference is
controlled by Cauchy–Schwarz.
entries.snippet:
private lemma eigenvalues_sub_le
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : ∀ x : E, ‖(S - T) x‖ ≤ ε * ‖x‖) (k : Fin n) :
    hS.eigenvalues hn k - hT.eigenvalues hn k ≤ ε

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le
entries.docstring:
**Weyl's inequality** for symmetric operators on a finite-dimensional inner
product space over `𝕜 = ℝ, ℂ`: the `k`-th (decreasingly sorted) eigenvalues of
`T` and `S` differ by at most the operator norm of `T − S`.

At `LinearMap` level there is no operator norm, so the bound is supplied as the
pointwise hypothesis `∀ x, ‖(T − S) x‖ ≤ ε * ‖x‖`; see
`LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le_norm` for the continuous-linear-map
operator-norm form.

Horn & Johnson, *Matrix Analysis* 2nd ed., Theorem 4.3.1; Bhatia,
*Matrix Analysis*, Corollary III.2.6.
entries.snippet:
lemma abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : ∀ x : E, ‖(T - S) x‖ ≤ ε * ‖x‖) (k : Fin n) :
    |hT.eigenvalues hn k - hS.eigenvalues hn k| ≤ ε

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le_norm
entries.docstring:
**Weyl's inequality**, operator-norm form, for symmetric (equivalently,
self-adjoint) continuous linear maps on a finite-dimensional inner product
space: the `k`-th sorted eigenvalues of `T` and `S` differ by at most
`‖T − S‖`.  The symmetry hypotheses are stated on the underlying linear maps
so that the signature does not require the adjoint star structure (whose
instance needs `CompleteSpace E`, which `FiniteDimensional` deliberately does
not register as an instance).

The bound is expressed directly in the norm of a continuous linear map.
entries.snippet:
lemma abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le_norm
    {T S : E →L[𝕜] E}
    (hT : LinearMap.IsSymmetric (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E))
    (hS : LinearMap.IsSymmetric (S : E →ₗ[𝕜] E))
    (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n) :
    |hT.eigenvalues hn k - hS.eigenvalues hn k| ≤ ‖T - S‖

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalues_sub_le_opNorm
entries.docstring:
Weyl's inequality for linear maps, using the operator norm of the
corresponding continuous linear map.  Unlike the preceding theorem, the symmetry
hypotheses and eigenvalue enumeration are directly attached to `LinearMap`s.
entries.snippet:
lemma abs_eigenvalues_sub_le_opNorm
    {T S : E →ₗ[𝕜] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric)
    (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n) :
    |hT.eigenvalues hn k - hS.eigenvalues hn k|
      ≤ ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (T - S)‖

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_congr
entries.docstring:
Sorted eigenvalues are congruent along an operator equality (the eigenvalue
enumeration depends only on the operator, not on the symmetry proof).
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenvalues_congr {S₁ S₂ : E →ₗ[𝕜] E} (h : S₁ = S₂)
    (hS₁ : S₁.IsSymmetric) (hS₂ : S₂.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) :
    hS₁.eigenvalues hn = hS₂.eigenvalues hn

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_cast
entries.docstring:
The eigenvalue enumeration does not depend on which witness of the dimension indexes
it: two witnesses `finrank 𝕜 E = m` and `finrank 𝕜 E = n` enumerate the same eigenvalues,
read across the induced `Fin m ≃ Fin n`.

Both spellings occur in practice.  A matrix over `Fin n` has
`Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues₀` indexed by `Fin (Fintype.card (Fin n))`, while the
operator theory it is transported to indexes by `Fin n`; `Fintype.card (Fin n) = n` is a
theorem and not definitional, so the two index types are genuinely different.

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.exists_unit_vector_re_inner_le_eigenvalue_of_le
entries.docstring:
**Courant–Fischer, upper direction, for large subspaces.** On any subspace `W` of dimension
at least `k + 1` there is a unit vector `x` with `re ⟪T x, x⟫ ≤ λₖ(T)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_unit_vector_re_inner_le_eigenvalue_of_le
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n)
    (W : Submodule 𝕜 E) (hW : (k : ℕ) + 1 ≤ finrank 𝕜 W) :
    ∃ x ∈ W, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧ RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ hT.eigenvalues hn k

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_compression_le
entries.docstring:
**Upper Cauchy interlacing.** If the quadratic form of the symmetric operator `A` on `V`
agrees with that of `T`, then `μₖ(A) ≤ λₖ(T)` for every `k < m`.
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenvalue_compression_le
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (hm : finrank 𝕜 V = m)
    (hcomp : ∀ y : V, RCLike.re ⟪A y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜)
    (k : Fin m) (hk : (k : ℕ) < n) :
    hA.eigenvalues hm k ≤ hT.eigenvalues hn ⟨k, hk⟩

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_le_eigenvalue_compression
entries.docstring:
**Lower Cauchy interlacing.** If the quadratic form of the symmetric operator `A` on `V`
agrees with that of `T`, then `λ_{k + (n - m)}(T) ≤ μₖ(A)` for every `k < m`.
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenvalue_le_eigenvalue_compression
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (hm : finrank 𝕜 V = m)
    (hcomp : ∀ y : V, RCLike.re ⟪A y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜)
    (k : Fin m) (hmn : m ≤ n) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn ⟨k + (n - m), by omega⟩ ≤ hA.eigenvalues hm k

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_ascending_le_ritz
entries.docstring:
**Hylleraas–Undheim–MacDonald.** In ascending order, the `k`-th lowest Ritz value is an upper
bound for the `k`-th lowest exact eigenvalue: `λ↑ₖ(T) ≤ μ↑ₖ(S)` for every `k < m`.
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenvalue_ascending_le_ritz
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (hm : finrank 𝕜 V = m)
    (hcomp : ∀ y : V, RCLike.re ⟪A y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜)
    (hmn : m ≤ n) (k : ℕ) (hk : k < m) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn ⟨n - 1 - k, by omega⟩ ≤ hA.eigenvalues hm ⟨m - 1 - k, by omega⟩

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_min_le_ritz_min
entries.docstring:
**Variational ground-state bound.** The lowest Ritz value bounds the lowest exact eigenvalue
from above.
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenvalue_min_le_ritz_min
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (hm : finrank 𝕜 V = m)
    (hcomp : ∀ y : V, RCLike.re ⟪A y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜)
    (hmn : m ≤ n) (hm0 : 0 < m) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ ≤ hA.eigenvalues hm ⟨m - 1, by omega⟩

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.compression
entries.docstring: The compression `P_V ∘ T ∘ ι_V` of `T` to the subspace `V` (the Ritz operator).
entries.snippet: noncomputable def compression (_hT : T.IsSymmetric) (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) : V →ₗ[𝕜] V

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.inner_compression_left
entries.docstring: The compression has the inner products of `T` against vectors of `V`.
entries.snippet:
lemma inner_compression_left (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) (y z : V) :
    ⟪hT.compression V y, z⟫_𝕜 = ⟪T y, z⟫_𝕜

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.compression_isSymmetric
entries.docstring: The compression of a symmetric operator is symmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma compression_isSymmetric (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) :
    (hT.compression V).IsSymmetric

entries.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_compression
entries.docstring:
The compression has the quadratic form of `T` on `V`, as required by the interlacing
lemmas.
entries.snippet:
lemma re_inner_compression (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) (y : V) :
    RCLike.re ⟪hT.compression V y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜

entries.name: Finsupp.norm_linearCombination_eq_of_inner_eq
entries.docstring:
Families with equal pairwise inner products give linear combinations of equal norm
for the same finitely supported coefficients.

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.finTwo_posSemidef
entries.docstring: The `2 × 2` principal submatrix at two indices is positive semidefinite.

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.normSq_le
entries.docstring: Scalar Cauchy--Schwarz for an `RCLike`-valued positive-semidefinite matrix.

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_left
entries.docstring: A zero diagonal entry forces the corresponding row entry to vanish.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_left {K : α → α → 𝕜}
    (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) {a b : α} (ha : K a a = 0) : K a b = 0

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_right
entries.docstring: A zero diagonal entry forces the corresponding column entry to vanish.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_right {K : α → α → 𝕜}
    (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) {a b : α} (hb : K b b = 0) : K a b = 0

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_le_one_of_apply_self_eq_one
entries.docstring:
If two diagonal entries are `1`, then the corresponding off-diagonal entry has norm at most
