`1`.

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_le_of_norm_apply_self_le
entries.docstring:
**The diagonal of a positive-semidefinite matrix bounds all of its entries.** Cauchy--Schwarz
turns a uniform bound on the (nonnegative real) diagonal entries into the same bound everywhere.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_le_of_norm_apply_self_le {K : α → α → 𝕜} {C : ℝ}
    (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (hdiag : ∀ i, ‖K i i‖ ≤ C) (a b : α) : ‖K a b‖ ≤ C

entries.name: TauCeti.apply_one_le_apply_zero_of_sq_le_mul
entries.docstring:
The numerical core of the Hankel estimate: a bounded sequence of reals with `0 ≤ b 0` whose
squares satisfy the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality `b n ^ 2 ≤ b 0 * b (n + n)` cannot increase at the
first step. If it did, the ratio `r = b 1 / b 0` would exceed `1` and the doubling inequality would
push `b (2 ^ k)` past `b 0 * r ^ (2 ^ k)`, which is unbounded.
entries.snippet:
private lemma apply_one_le_apply_zero_of_sq_le_mul {b : ℕ → ℝ} {D : ℝ} (hb0 : 0 ≤ b 0)
    (hsq : ∀ n, b n ^ 2 ≤ b 0 * b (n + n)) (hbd : ∀ n, b n ≤ D) : b 1 ≤ b 0

entries.name: TauCeti.sub_nonneg_of_posSemidef_hankel
entries.docstring:
**A positive-semidefinite Hankel sequence bounded above does not increase at the first step.**
If `(m, n) ↦ a (m + n)` is positive semidefinite and the real parts of `a` are bounded above by `D`
— the entries are automatically real — then `a 1 ≤ a 0` in the `RCLike` order. Cauchy--Schwarz
alone gives `a n ^ 2 ≤ a 0 * a (2 n)`, and the bound rules out a ratio `a 1 / a 0` greater
than `1`.

entries.name: ContinuousLinearMap.norm_sub_apply_le_of_norm_le
entries.docstring:
Comparing two continuous linear maps of norm at most `K` at `x` costs at most `2 K ‖x - y‖`
more than comparing them at `y`. This is the shared estimate of the two density arguments below:
`y` is chosen in the dense subset, close to the arbitrary vector `x`.

entries.name: ContinuousLinearMap.tendsto_apply_of_dense
entries.docstring:
A uniformly bounded family of continuous linear maps that converges pointwise on a dense
subset converges pointwise everywhere.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub
entries.docstring:
A function `F : G → ℂ` on an additive commutative group is **positive definite** when, for
every finite family of scalars `c : Fin n → ℂ` and points `v : Fin n → G`, the Hermitian form
`∑_{i,j} c i · conj (c j) * F (v i - v j)` is a nonnegative real number (using the order on `ℂ`
for which `0 ≤ z` means `z` is real and nonnegative).

This is the classical translation-invariant condition, the one Bochner's theorem is stated in. It
is `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite` for the negation involution; see
`TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite`.
entries.snippet: def IsPositiveDefiniteSub (F : G → ℂ) : Prop

entries.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_forall_sum_nonneg
entries.docstring:
The defining finite-family characterization, for building a positive-definite function
directly from the quadratic-form condition.
entries.snippet:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_forall_sum_nonneg :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℂ) (v : Fin n → G),
      0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * F (v i - v j)

entries.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite
entries.docstring:
Subtraction-form positive definiteness is the generic involutive predicate for the negation
involution, read on the type synonym `TauCeti.WithNegStar`.
entries.snippet:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔
      IsPositiveDefinite fun a : WithNegStar G => F (WithNegStar.ofNegStar a)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.isPositiveDefinite
entries.docstring:
The generic involutive predicate attached to a subtraction-form positive-definite function.
This is the workhorse for transporting the generic API.
entries.snippet:
lemma isPositiveDefinite (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite fun a : WithNegStar G => F (WithNegStar.ofNegStar a)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.sum_nonneg
entries.docstring: Positive-definiteness holds for an arbitrary finite index type, not just `Fin n`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ) (v : ι → G) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * F (v i - v j)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.posSemidef
entries.docstring:
A subtraction-form positive-definite function gives the translation-invariant
positive-definite kernel `K(a, b) = F (a - b)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma posSemidef (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) :
    Matrix.PosSemidef fun a b : G => F (a - b)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.of_posSemidef
entries.docstring:
A function whose translation-invariant kernel `K(a, b) = F (a - b)` is positive definite is
positive definite.
entries.snippet:
lemma of_posSemidef (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef fun a b : G => F (a - b)) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub F

entries.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_posSemidef
entries.docstring:
The PD-function ↔ PD-kernel equivalence in its classical translation-invariant form: `F` is
positive definite if and only if the kernel `K(a, b) = F (a - b)` is positive definite.
entries.snippet:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_posSemidef :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔ Matrix.PosSemidef fun a b : G => F (a - b)

entries.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_isPositiveDefiniteSub
entries.docstring:
On a group whose own involution is negation, the generic involutive predicate and the
subtraction-form predicate agree.
entries.snippet:
lemma isPositiveDefinite_iff_isPositiveDefiniteSub [StarAddMonoid G]
    (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) : IsPositiveDefinite F ↔ IsPositiveDefiniteSub F

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_nonneg

entries.snippet: lemma map_zero_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) : 0 ≤ F 0

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_im

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_re_nonneg
entries.docstring: The real part of the value of a positive-definite function at `0` is nonnegative.
entries.snippet: lemma map_zero_re_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) : 0 ≤ (F 0).re

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_eq_ofReal_re

The value at the origin of a positive-definite function is the real number `(F 0).re`, viewed

entries.snippet: lemma map_zero_eq_ofReal_re (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) : F 0 = ((F 0).re : ℂ)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero

If a positive-definite function is nonzero at the origin, then the real part of that value is
strictly positive.
entries.snippet:
lemma map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (h0 : F 0 ≠ 0) :

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.conj_symm
entries.docstring: A positive-definite function is conjugate symmetric: `conj (F (b - a)) = F (a - b)`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma conj_symm (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (a b : G) : conj (F (b - a)) = F (a - b)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_neg

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.normSq_le
entries.docstring:
The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for a positive-definite function: the squared norm of any value
is bounded by the square of the value at the origin.
entries.snippet:
lemma normSq_le (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (a b : G) :
    Complex.normSq (F (a - b)) ≤ (F 0).re * (F 0).re

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.norm_apply_le_map_zero_re

entries.snippet: lemma norm_apply_le_map_zero_re (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (a : G) : ‖F a‖ ≤ (F 0).re

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.of_tendsto
entries.docstring: Positive definiteness is preserved under pointwise limits along a nontrivial filter.
entries.snippet:
lemma of_tendsto {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [NeBot l] {F : ι → G → ℂ} {H : G → ℂ}

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.normalize

Multiplying a positive-definite function by the reciprocal of its real value at the origin

Precomposing a Pontryagin character with `Multiplicative.ofAdd` gives a continuous function in

lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub
    (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    Continuous (fun g : G => (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ)) ∧

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_nonneg
entries.docstring:
Positive-definiteness holds for an arbitrary finite index type, not just `Fin n`: for every
finite family of scalars `c : ι → ℂ` and points `v : ι → M`, the Hermitian form
`∑_{i,j} c i · conj (c j) · F (v i + star (v j))` is a nonnegative real number.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ) (v : ι → M) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * F (v i + star (v j))

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.quadForm_two_nonneg
entries.docstring:
The `2 × 2` Hermitian sub-form of a positive-definite function at the points `a, b` with
coefficients `c₀, c₁` is nonnegative.
entries.snippet:
lemma quadForm_two_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a b : M) (c₀ c₁ : ℂ) :
    0 ≤ c₀ * conj c₀ * F (a + star a) + c₀ * conj c₁ * F (a + star b)
      + c₁ * conj c₀ * F (b + star a) + c₁ * conj c₁ * F (b + star b)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add_star_self_nonneg
entries.docstring:
A positive-definite function takes a real, nonnegative value at every "norm point"

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add_star_self_re_nonneg
entries.docstring:
The value of a positive-definite function at a "norm point" `a + star a` has nonnegative real

entries.snippet: lemma add_star_self_re_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a : M) : 0 ≤ (F (a + star a)).re

entries.docstring:
A positive-definite function is conjugate symmetric in the involution:

entries.docstring:
A positive-definite function `F` induces the positive-definite kernel `K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)`.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_posSemidef

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_expand_of_values
entries.snippet:
private lemma gram_three_add_star_expand_of_values
    {x y : E} {lam : ℂ} {c : Fin 3 → ℂ} {p : Fin 3 → E}
    (hc0 : c 0 = 1) (hc1 : c 1 = -1) (hc2 : c 2 = lam)
    (hp0 : p 0 = x) (hp1 : p 1 = y) (hp2 : p 2 = 0) (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0)
    (hyx : F (y + star x) = conj (F (x + star y)))
    (hnx : F (star x) = conj (F x)) (hny : F (0 + star y) = conj (F y)) : (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      c i * conj (c j) * F (p i + star (p j)))
      = F 0 - F (x + star y) + conj lam * F x - conj (F (x + star y)) + F 0
        - conj lam * F y + lam * conj (F x) - lam * conj (F y)
        + lam * conj lam * F 0

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_expand
entries.snippet:
private lemma gram_three_add_star_expand {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0)
    (hyx : F (y + star x) = conj (F (x + star y)))
    (hnx : F (star x) = conj (F x)) (hny : F (0 + star y) = conj (F y)) {lam : ℂ} :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      ![1, -1, lam] i * conj (![1, -1, lam] j) *
        F (![x, y, 0] i + star (![x, y, 0] j)))
      = F 0 - F (x + star y) + conj lam * F x - conj (F (x + star y)) + F 0
        - conj lam * F y + lam * conj (F x) - lam * conj (F y)
        + lam * conj lam * F 0

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_sub_re_complex_algebra
entries.snippet:
private lemma gram_three_sub_re_complex_algebra {r : ℝ} {z d lam : ℂ}
    (hlam : lam = -d / (r : ℂ)) (hr : 0 < r) :
    ((r : ℂ) - z + conj lam * d - conj z + (r : ℂ) + lam * conj d
        + lam * conj lam * (r : ℂ)).re
      = 2 * r - 2 * z.re - Complex.normSq d / r

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_re_algebra
entries.snippet:
private lemma gram_three_add_star_re_algebra (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0)
    (hyx : F (y + star x) = conj (F (x + star y)))
    (hnx : F (star x) = conj (F x)) (hny : F (0 + star y) = conj (F y)) {C d lam : ℂ}
    (hC : C = F 0) (hd : d = F x - F y) (hlam : lam = -d / C) (hCpos : 0 < (F 0).re) :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      ![1, -1, lam] i * conj (![1, -1, lam] j) *
        F (![x, y, 0] i + star (![x, y, 0] j))).re
      = 2 * (F 0).re - 2 * (F (x + star y)).re - Complex.normSq d / (F 0).re

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_re_eq
entries.snippet:
private lemma gram_three_add_star_re_eq (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0) {C d lam : ℂ}
    (hC : C = F 0) (hd : d = F x - F y) (hlam : lam = -d / C) (hCpos : 0 < (F 0).re) :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      ![1, -1, lam] i * conj (![1, -1, lam] j) *
        F (![x, y, 0] i + star (![x, y, 0] j))).re
      = 2 * (F 0).re - 2 * (F (x + star y)).re - Complex.normSq d / (F 0).re

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
entries.docstring: The local monoid-level real-part form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2
      ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ((F 0).re - (F (x + star y)).re)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
The local monoid-level norm-valued form of the standard positive-definite continuity
estimate.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_star_eq_neg
entries.docstring: The local real-part form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate.

entries.snippet:

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_star_eq_neg
entries.docstring: The local norm-valued form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate.

lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_star_eq_neg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)

The norm-valued form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate under a globally

entries.snippet:
lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero_of_forall_star_eq_neg
entries.docstring:
A positive-definite function on a seminormed additive group with the negation involution is
uniformly continuous as soon as it is continuous at the origin.
entries.snippet:
lemma uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero_of_forall_star_eq_neg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) :
    UniformContinuous F

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.real_smul
entries.docstring: Positive-definite functions are closed under multiplication by a nonnegative real scalar.
entries.snippet:
lemma real_smul {r : ℝ} {F : M → ℂ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => r • F x)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_smul
entries.docstring:
Finite nonnegative complex-weighted sums of positive-definite functions are positive
definite. This is the finite-mixture form used when the weights are already complex scalars with
nonnegative real value.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_const_mul
entries.docstring:
Finite nonnegative complex-weighted sums, written using multiplication rather than scalar
notation.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_real_smul
entries.docstring: Finite nonnegative real-weighted sums of positive-definite functions are positive definite.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_real_const_mul
entries.docstring:
Finite nonnegative real-weighted sums, written with the real weight coerced to `ℂ` and
multiplied in the codomain.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.pow
entries.docstring: Schur powers of a positive-definite function are positive definite.
entries.snippet:
lemma pow {F : M → ℂ} (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (n : ℕ) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => F x ^ n)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_smul_apply_of_apply_eq_one
entries.docstring:
If each summand in a finite complex-weighted sum is normalized at a point, then the sum's
value at that point is the sum of the weights.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_smul_apply_of_apply_eq_one {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {w : ι → ℂ}
    {F : ι → N → ℂ} {x : N} (hFx : ∀ i ∈ s, F i x = 1) : (∑ i ∈ s, w i • F i x) = ∑ i ∈ s, w i

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_smul_apply_eq_one
entries.docstring:
A finite complex-weighted sum of functions normalized at a point is normalized at that point
when the weights sum to `1`.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_const_mul_apply_of_apply_eq_one
entries.docstring:
If each summand in a finite complex-weighted sum is normalized at a point, then the sum's
multiplication-form value at that point is the sum of the weights.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_const_mul_apply_of_apply_eq_one {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {w : ι → ℂ}
    {F : ι → N → ℂ} {x : N} (hFx : ∀ i ∈ s, F i x = 1) : (∑ i ∈ s, w i * F i x) = ∑ i ∈ s, w i

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_const_mul_apply_eq_one
entries.docstring:
A finite complex-weighted sum, in multiplication form, of functions normalized at a point is
normalized at that point when the weights sum to `1`.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_real_smul_apply_of_apply_eq_one
entries.docstring:
If each summand in a finite real-weighted sum is normalized at a point, then the sum's value at
that point is the complex coercion of the sum of the real weights.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_real_smul_apply_eq_one
entries.docstring:
A finite real-weighted sum of functions normalized at a point is normalized at that point when

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_real_const_mul_apply_of_apply_eq_one
entries.docstring:
If each summand in a finite real-weighted sum is normalized at a point, then the sum's

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_smul_apply_zero_eq_one

If each summand in a finite real-weighted sum is normalized at the origin, then the sum's value

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsSpace
entries.docstring: The canonical Hilbert space of the translation-invariant kernel `K(a,b) = F(a-b)`.
entries.snippet: abbrev gnsSpace

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsVector
entries.docstring: The vector in the GNS space corresponding to a group element.
entries.snippet: def gnsVector (a : G) : hF.gnsSpace

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.inner_gnsVector
entries.docstring: The inner product of two GNS vectors is the original positive-definite kernel.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma inner_gnsVector (a b : G) : ⟪hF.gnsVector a, hF.gnsVector b⟫_ℂ = F (a - b)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.norm_gnsVector_sub_sq
entries.docstring: Squared distances between GNS vectors are controlled by the real part of the function.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma norm_gnsVector_sub_sq (a b : G) :
    ‖hF.gnsVector a - hF.gnsVector b‖ ^ 2 =
      2 * ((F 0).re - (F (a - b)).re)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsVector_dense
entries.docstring: The GNS vectors span a dense subspace.
entries.snippet:
lemma gnsVector_dense :
    (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range hF.gnsVector)).topologicalClosure = ⊤

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.translated_gnsVector_dense
entries.snippet:
private lemma translated_gnsVector_dense (g : G) :
    (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun a : G => hF.gnsVector (g + a))).topologicalClosure = ⊤

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsTranslation
entries.docstring:
Translation by `g` is a unitary operator on the canonical GNS Hilbert space. Its action on
the dense family of kernel vectors is `v(a) ↦ v(g+a)`.
entries.snippet: def gnsTranslation (g : G) : hF.gnsSpace ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] hF.gnsSpace

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsTranslation_gnsVector
entries.docstring: Translation acts on the canonical GNS vectors by addition.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma gnsTranslation_gnsVector (g a : G) :
    hF.gnsTranslation g (hF.gnsVector a) = hF.gnsVector (g + a)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsTranslation_zero
entries.docstring: The translation at zero is the identity operator.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma gnsTranslation_zero : hF.gnsTranslation 0 = LinearIsometryEquiv.refl ℂ hF.gnsSpace

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsTranslation_add
entries.docstring: GNS translations compose according to the group law.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma gnsTranslation_add (g k : G) :
    hF.gnsTranslation (g + k) = (hF.gnsTranslation k).trans (hF.gnsTranslation g)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsRepresentation
entries.docstring:
The GNS representation as a homomorphism from the multiplicative copy of `G` to the
unitary operators on its canonical Hilbert space.
entries.snippet: def gnsRepresentation : Multiplicative G →* (hF.gnsSpace ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] hF.gnsSpace)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsRepresentation_ofAdd
entries.docstring: The representation operator at `g` is translation by `g`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma gnsRepresentation_ofAdd (g : G) :
    hF.gnsRepresentation (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) = hF.gnsTranslation g

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsRepresentation_gnsVector
entries.docstring: The representation translates each GNS vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma gnsRepresentation_gnsVector (g a : G) :
    hF.gnsRepresentation (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) (hF.gnsVector a) =
      hF.gnsVector (g + a)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.eq_inner_gnsRepresentation
entries.docstring:
A positive-definite function is a matrix coefficient of its canonical unitary
representation.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_inner_gnsRepresentation (g : G) :
    F g = ⟪hF.gnsRepresentation (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) (hF.gnsVector 0),
      hF.gnsVector 0⟫_ℂ

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.continuous_gnsVector
entries.docstring:
Continuity of a positive-definite function at zero makes its canonical feature map
continuous. This is the regularity needed for a strongly continuous representation.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_gnsVector [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalAddGroup G]
    (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) : Continuous hF.gnsVector

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.continuous_gnsTranslation_gnsVector
entries.snippet:
private lemma continuous_gnsTranslation_gnsVector [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalAddGroup G]
    (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) (a : G) :
    Continuous (fun g : G => hF.gnsTranslation g (hF.gnsVector a))

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.continuous_gnsTranslation_apply
entries.docstring:
The GNS translation representation is strongly continuous: every vector has a continuous
orbit.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_gnsTranslation_apply [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalAddGroup G]
    (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) (x : hF.gnsSpace) :
    Continuous (fun g : G => hF.gnsTranslation g x)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.continuous_gnsRepresentation_apply
entries.docstring: The canonical unitary representation has continuous orbits.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_gnsRepresentation_apply [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalAddGroup G]
    (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) (x : hF.gnsSpace) :
    Continuous (fun g : Multiplicative G => hF.gnsRepresentation g x)

entries.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef
entries.docstring:
A function `F` on an involutive additive monoid is positive definite if and only if the
two-variable kernel `K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)` is positive definite.
entries.snippet:
lemma isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef :
    IsPositiveDefinite F ↔ Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a + star b))

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef_sub
entries.docstring:
Under the negation involution `a⋆ = -a`, a positive-definite function `F` gives the
translation-invariant positive-definite kernel `K(a, b) = F(a - b)`. This is the form in which
positive definiteness is usually stated on groups such as `ℝᵈ` or a real inner-product space.
entries.snippet:
lemma posSemidef_sub (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a - b))

entries.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef_sub
entries.docstring:
Under the negation involution `a⋆ = -a`, `F` is positive definite if and only if the
translation-invariant kernel `K(a, b) = F(a - b)` is positive definite.
entries.snippet:
lemma isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef_sub (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) :
    IsPositiveDefinite F ↔ Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a - b))

entries.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelOperator
entries.docstring:
A scalar kernel regarded as an operator-valued kernel on the one-dimensional Hilbert space
`𝕜`: the entry at `(a, b)` is left multiplication by `K a b`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def positiveDefiniteKernelOperator (K : α → α → 𝕜) :
    Matrix α α (𝕜 →L[𝕜] 𝕜)

entries.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelOperator_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma positiveDefiniteKernelOperator_apply (K : α → α → 𝕜) (a b : α) (z : 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelOperator K a b z = K a b * z

entries.name: TauCeti.posSemidef_positiveDefiniteKernelOperator
entries.docstring:
The operator-valued kernel obtained from a scalar positive-definite kernel is positive
semidefinite.  This is the bridge needed by Mathlib's `RKHS.OfKernel` construction.
entries.snippet:
lemma posSemidef_positiveDefiniteKernelOperator (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) :
    (positiveDefiniteKernelOperator K).PosSemidef

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.KolmogorovSpace
entries.docstring:
The canonical Hilbert space in the Kolmogorov decomposition of `K`.

This is an abbreviation because Mathlib's `RKHS.OfKernel` currently has to be an abbreviation in
order for its normed-group and inner-product instances to reduce.
entries.snippet: noncomputable abbrev KolmogorovSpace (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K)

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovFeature
entries.docstring:
The canonical feature map into the Kolmogorov space.  It sends `a` to the reproducing-kernel
vector at `a`, evaluated on the scalar `1`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def kolmogorovFeature (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (a : α) :
    KolmogorovSpace hK

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.inner_kolmogorovFeature
entries.docstring:
**Kolmogorov identity.** Inner products of the canonical feature vectors recover the
original kernel.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma inner_kolmogorovFeature (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (a b : α) :
    ⟪kolmogorovFeature hK a, kolmogorovFeature hK b⟫_𝕜 = K a b

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_kolmogorovFeature_sq
entries.docstring:
The squared norm of a canonical feature vector is the real part of the corresponding
diagonal kernel value.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma norm_kolmogorovFeature_sq (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (a : α) :
    ‖kolmogorovFeature hK a‖ ^ 2 = RCLike.re (K a a)

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_kolmogorovFeature_sub_sq
entries.docstring:
The squared distance between two canonical feature vectors, expressed entirely in terms of
the original kernel.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma norm_kolmogorovFeature_sub_sq (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (a b : α) :
    ‖kolmogorovFeature hK a - kolmogorovFeature hK b‖ ^ 2 =
      RCLike.re (K a a) - 2 * RCLike.re (K a b) + RCLike.re (K b b)

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovFeature_dense
entries.docstring:
The canonical feature vectors have dense linear span in the Kolmogorov space.  Thus the
construction is minimal: it contains no orthogonal summand invisible to the kernel.
entries.snippet:
lemma kolmogorovFeature_dense (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) :
    (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range (kolmogorovFeature hK))).topologicalClosure = ⊤

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.denseRange_featureCombination
entries.snippet:
private lemma denseRange_featureCombination (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) :
    DenseRange (Finsupp.linearCombination 𝕜 (kolmogorovFeature hK))

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovIsometry
entries.docstring:
The unique linear isometry from the canonical Kolmogorov space into any Hilbert-space
realization of `K`.  It sends each canonical feature vector to the corresponding vector in the
given realization.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def kolmogorovIsometry {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b) : KolmogorovSpace hK →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovIsometry_apply
entries.docstring:
The universal comparison isometry sends canonical feature vectors to the vectors of the
given realization.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma kolmogorovIsometry_apply {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b) (a : α) :
    kolmogorovIsometry hK φ hφ (kolmogorovFeature hK a) = φ a

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovIsometry_unique
entries.docstring:
A linear isometry out of the canonical Kolmogorov space is uniquely determined by its values
on the canonical feature vectors.
entries.snippet:
lemma kolmogorovIsometry_unique {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b) (T : KolmogorovSpace hK →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E)
    (hT : ∀ a, T (kolmogorovFeature hK a) = φ a) : T = kolmogorovIsometry hK φ hφ

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovIsometry_surjective
entries.docstring:
If the vectors in a realization of `K` have dense linear span, the universal comparison
isometry is surjective.
entries.snippet:
lemma kolmogorovIsometry_surjective {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b)
    (hφdense : (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range φ)).topologicalClosure = ⊤) :
    Function.Surjective (kolmogorovIsometry hK φ hφ)

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovEquiv
entries.docstring:
The canonical Kolmogorov space is linearly isometric to every other minimal realization of
the same kernel.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def kolmogorovEquiv {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b)
    (hφdense : (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range φ)).topologicalClosure = ⊤) :
    KolmogorovSpace hK ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] E

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovEquiv_apply
entries.docstring:
The equivalence with another minimal realization sends canonical feature vectors to the
vectors of that realization.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma kolmogorovEquiv_apply {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b)
    (hφdense : (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range φ)).topologicalClosure = ⊤) (a : α) :
    kolmogorovEquiv hK φ hφ hφdense (kolmogorovFeature hK a) = φ a

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto
entries.docstring:
Positive-definiteness is preserved under pointwise limits along a nontrivial filter. The
hypothesis on positive-definiteness is eventual, so this applies equally to nets that are
eventually positive definite.
entries.snippet:
lemma of_tendsto {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [NeBot l] {F : ι → M → ℂ} {G : M → ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ᶠ i in l, IsPositiveDefinite (F i))
    (hlim : ∀ x : M, Tendsto (fun i => F i x) l (𝓝 (G x))) :
    IsPositiveDefinite G

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_forall_tendsto
entries.docstring:
A pointwise limit of a family of positive-definite functions is positive definite. This is the
non-eventual form of `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto`.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_seq_tendsto
entries.docstring: Sequential pointwise limits of eventually positive-definite functions are positive definite.
entries.snippet:
lemma of_seq_tendsto {F : ℕ → M → ℂ} {G : M → ℂ} (hF : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, IsPositiveDefinite (F n))
    (hlim : ∀ x : M, Tendsto (fun n => F n x) atTop (𝓝 (G x))) :
    IsPositiveDefinite G

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendstoLocallyUniformly
entries.docstring:
A locally uniform limit of eventually positive-definite functions is positive definite.

Unlike continuity, positive-definiteness itself only needs pointwise convergence; local uniform
convergence is converted to pointwise convergence before applying
`TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto`.

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalizeScalar_nonneg
entries.docstring: The normalizing scalar `((F 0).re)⁻¹`, viewed as a complex number, is nonnegative.
entries.snippet:
private lemma normalizeScalar_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    0 ≤ (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalize
entries.docstring:
Multiplying a positive-definite function by the reciprocal of its real value at the origin
preserves positive-definiteness. If `F 0 = 0` this gives the zero scaling; the separate
`normalize_apply_zero` lemma below records the useful nonzero case.
entries.snippet:
lemma normalize (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F x)

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalize_apply_zero
entries.docstring: The normalized positive-definite function has value `1` at the origin.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma normalize_apply_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (h0 : F 0 ≠ 0) :
    (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F 0 = 1

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_add_star_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
At points satisfying `a + star a = 0`, the normalized positive-definite function is bounded
by `1`. When `F 0 = 0` the normalizing scalar is `0`, so the bound holds trivially.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_add_star_eq_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (a : M) (ha : a + star a = 0) :
    ‖(((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F a‖ ≤ 1

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_star_eq_neg
entries.docstring:
Under the negation involution, the normalized positive-definite function is bounded by `1` at
every point.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_star_eq_neg (hH : IsPositiveDefinite H)
    (a : G) (hstar_a : star a = -a) :
    ‖(((H 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * H a‖ ≤ 1

entries.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_forall_star_eq_neg
entries.docstring:
If the involution is negation everywhere, the normalized positive-definite function is
uniformly bounded by `1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_forall_star_eq_neg (hH : IsPositiveDefinite H)
    (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) (a : G) :
    ‖(((H 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * H a‖ ≤ 1

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.isPositiveDefiniteSub_pontryaginMeasureTransform
entries.docstring: The transform of a finite positive measure on the dual is positive definite.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.isPositiveDefiniteSub_pontryaginMeasureTransform
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform

entries.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.norm_pontryaginMeasureTransform_le
entries.docstring: The absolute value of a measure transform is bounded by the measure's total mass.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.norm_pontryaginMeasureTransform_le
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) (g : G) :
    ‖μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform g‖ ≤ μ.toMeasure.real Set.univ

entries.name: Submodule.inf_ne_bot_of_finrank_lt
entries.docstring:
Two subspaces whose dimensions sum to more than the dimension of the ambient
space have nontrivial intersection.
entries.snippet:
lemma inf_ne_bot_of_finrank_lt [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] {V W : Submodule 𝕜 E}
    (h : finrank 𝕜 E < finrank 𝕜 V + finrank 𝕜 W) : V ⊓ W ≠ ⊥

entries.name: TauCeti.posSemidef_of_support_posSemidef
entries.snippet:
private lemma posSemidef_of_support_posSemidef {R : Type u}
    [Ring R] [PartialOrder R] [StarRing R] (K : α → α → R)
    (hHerm : (Matrix.of fun a b => K a b).IsHermitian) (hgram : ∀ x : α →₀ R,
      (Matrix.of fun i j : x.support => K (i : α) (j : α)).PosSemidef) :
    (Matrix.of fun a b => K a b).PosSemidef

entries.name: TauCeti.posSemidef_rankOne
TauCeti.posSemidef_const_one
entries.docstring: The constant matrix with value `1` is positive semidefinite.

entries.name: TauCeti.posSemidef_const_of_nonneg
entries.docstring: A nonnegative constant gives a positive-semidefinite constant matrix.

entries.name: TauCeti.posSemidef_iff_finite_sum
entries.docstring:
The quadratic-form characterization of an arbitrary-index positive-semidefinite matrix:
conjugate symmetry and nonnegativity on every finite family, allowing repeated indices.
entries.snippet:
lemma posSemidef_iff_finite_sum {R : Type u} [Ring R] [PartialOrder R] [StarRing R]
    {K : α → α → R} :
    Matrix.PosSemidef K ↔
      (∀ a b, star (K a b) = K b a) ∧
        ∀ {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (v : ι → α) (x : ι → R),
          0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, star (x i) * K (v i) (v j) * x j

entries.name: TauCeti.posSemidef_schur_finset_prod
entries.docstring: Finite pointwise Schur products of positive-semidefinite matrices are positive semidefinite.

entries.name: TauCeti.posSemidef_prod_union
entries.docstring:
For weights `w` in `[0, 1]` and finite sets `L i`, the matrix
`(i, j) ↦ ∏_{a ∈ L i ∪ L j} w a` is positive semidefinite.
entries.snippet:
lemma posSemidef_prod_union {ι : Type w} [DecidableEq α] (L : ι → Finset α)
    {w : α → ℝ} (hw₀ : ∀ a, 0 ≤ w a) (hw₁ : ∀ a, w a ≤ 1) :
    Matrix.PosSemidef (fun i j => ∏ a ∈ L i ∪ L j, w a)

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.hadamard_pow
entries.docstring: Schur powers of a positive-semidefinite matrix are positive semidefinite.

entries.name: ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable_of_measure_ne_top
entries.docstring:
For a measure that is inner regular with respect to compact sets on sets of finite measure, a
function continuous on a measurable set `s` of finite measure is a.e. strongly measurable for the
restriction of the measure to `s`.

entries.name: Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable_of_sigmaFinite
entries.docstring:
A continuous function is a.e. strongly measurable for a σ-finite measure that is inner regular
with respect to compact sets on sets of finite measure. Compare `Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable`,
which asks for second countability of the source or the target instead.
entries.snippet:
lemma Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable_of_sigmaFinite [SigmaFinite μ] {f : α → β}
    (hf : Continuous f) : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ

entries.name: MeasureTheory.AEFinStronglyMeasurable.aestronglyMeasurable_smul
entries.docstring:
The product of an a.e. finitely strongly measurable function `f`, for instance an integrable
one, and a continuous function `g` is a.e. strongly measurable, for a measure that is inner regular
with respect to compact sets on sets of finite measure. No σ-finiteness of the measure and no
second countability is needed: `f` vanishes outside a σ-finite set, on which `g` is a.e. strongly
measurable by `Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable_of_sigmaFinite`.
entries.snippet:
lemma MeasureTheory.AEFinStronglyMeasurable.aestronglyMeasurable_smul {𝕜 : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace 𝕜] [T2Space 𝕜] [Zero 𝕜] [Zero β] [SMulWithZero 𝕜 β] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 β]
    {f : α → 𝕜} (hf : AEFinStronglyMeasurable f μ) {g : α → β} (hg : Continuous g) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ f x • g x) μ

entries.name: TauCeti.norm_integral_smul_sub_le
entries.docstring:
**The approximate-identity estimate.** If an `L¹` class `f` has unit integral and vanishes
almost everywhere outside `U`, and `φ` stays within `ε` of `y` on `U`, then the integral of `φ`
against `f` is within `ε * ‖f‖` of `y`. The integrand `f • φ` is assumed almost everywhere
strongly measurable.

entries.name: TauCeti.tendsto_integral_smul_of_tendsto
entries.docstring:
**`L¹` peak functions integrate a function to its limit at the peak.** Let `f i` be `L¹`
classes which eventually have unit integral and `L¹` norm at most `C`, and which concentrate at
`x₀`: for every neighbourhood `U` of `x₀`, eventually `f i` vanishes almost everywhere outside `U`.
Then `∫ x, f i x • φ x ∂μ` tends to `a` for every `φ` tending to `a` at `x₀` whose products
`f i • φ` are eventually almost everywhere strongly measurable.

entries.name: TauCeti.exists_integral_eq_one_norm_eq_one
entries.docstring:
**`L¹` peak functions exist.** For a measure positive on nonempty open sets and finite on some
neighbourhood of each point, every neighbourhood `U` of a point carries an `L¹` class of unit
integral and unit `L¹` norm vanishing almost everywhere outside `U`: the indicator of a
neighbourhood of finite measure inside `U`, normalized by that measure.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_integral_eq_one_norm_eq_one [TopologicalSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α]
    [μ.IsOpenPosMeasure] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] {x₀ : α} {U : Set α} (hU : U ∈ 𝓝 x₀) :
    ∃ f : α →₁[μ] 𝕜, ∫ x, f x ∂μ = 1 ∧ ‖f‖ = 1 ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∉ U → f x = 0

entries.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.ext_of_forall_mem_submonoid_integral_eq_of_polish
entries.docstring:
**A separating submonoid of test functions determines a finite measure.** Two finite Borel
measures on a Polish space that give the same integral to every member of a submonoid `S` of the
real bounded continuous functions are equal, provided the members of `S` separate points.
entries.snippet:
lemma ext_of_forall_mem_submonoid_integral_eq_of_polish [PolishSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {P P' : Measure E} [IsFiniteMeasure P] [IsFiniteMeasure P'] {S : Submonoid (E →ᵇ ℝ)}
    (hS : ∀ ⦃x y : E⦄, x ≠ y → ∃ g ∈ S, g x ≠ g y)
    (heq : ∀ g ∈ S, ∫ x, g x ∂P = ∫ x, g x ∂P') : P = P'

entries.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.abs_integral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_sub_le_of_isTightMeasureSet_of_borel
entries.snippet:
private lemma abs_integral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_sub_le_of_isTightMeasureSet_of_borel
    [BorelSpace E]
    (hP : IsTightMeasureSet {P}) (hP' : IsTightMeasureSet {P'}) (f : E →ᵇ ℝ)
    {A : Subalgebra ℝ (E →ᵇ ℝ)} (hA : (A.map (toContinuousMapₐ ℝ)).SeparatesPoints)
    (heq : ∀ g ∈ A, ∫ x, (g : E → ℝ) x ∂P = ∫ x, (g : E → ℝ) x ∂P') {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    |∫ x, mulExpNegMulSq ε (f x) ∂P - ∫ x, mulExpNegMulSq ε (f x) ∂P'| ≤ 6 * √ε

entries.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.abs_integral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_sub_le_of_isTightMeasureSet
entries.docstring:
If two tight finite measures on a Hausdorff space integrate every member of a point-separating
real subalgebra `A` of `E →ᵇ ℝ` equally, then their integrals of `mulExpNegMulSq ε ∘ f` differ by
at most `6 √ε`. This is the tight form of Mathlib's `dist_integral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_le`, which
assumes a complete second-countable pseudo-metric space instead.
entries.snippet:
lemma abs_integral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_sub_le_of_isTightMeasureSet
    (hP : IsTightMeasureSet {P}) (hP' : IsTightMeasureSet {P'}) (f : E →ᵇ ℝ)
    {A : Subalgebra ℝ (E →ᵇ ℝ)} (hA : (A.map (toContinuousMapₐ ℝ)).SeparatesPoints)
    (heq : ∀ g ∈ A, ∫ x, (g : E → ℝ) x ∂P = ∫ x, (g : E → ℝ) x ∂P') {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    |∫ x, mulExpNegMulSq ε (f x) ∂P - ∫ x, mulExpNegMulSq ε (f x) ∂P'| ≤ 6 * √ε

entries.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_of_opens
entries.snippet:
private lemma tendsto_integral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_of_opens (f : E →ᵇ ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun ε => ∫ x, mulExpNegMulSq ε (f x) ∂P) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂P))

entries.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.integral_eq_of_forall_mem_subalgebra_integral_eq_of_isTightMeasureSet
entries.docstring:
**A separating subalgebra determines the integrals of tight measures.** Two tight finite
measures on a Hausdorff space that integrate every member of a point-separating star
subalgebra `A` of `E →ᵇ 𝕜` equally give the same integral to every real bounded continuous
function.
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_eq_of_forall_mem_subalgebra_integral_eq_of_isTightMeasureSet {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
    (hP : IsTightMeasureSet {P}) (hP' : IsTightMeasureSet {P'})
    {A : StarSubalgebra 𝕜 (E →ᵇ 𝕜)} (hA : (A.map (toContinuousMapStarₐ 𝕜)).SeparatesPoints)
    (heq : ∀ g ∈ A, ∫ x, (g : E → 𝕜) x ∂P = ∫ x, (g : E → 𝕜) x ∂P') (f : E →ᵇ ℝ) :
    ∫ x, f x ∂P = ∫ x, f x ∂P'

entries.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.ext_of_forall_mem_subalgebra_integral_eq_of_innerRegular
entries.docstring:
**A separating subalgebra determines a finite inner regular measure.** On a locally compact
Hausdorff space, two finite inner regular (equivalently, for finite Borel measures there, regular)
measures that integrate every member of a point-separating star subalgebra `A` of `E →ᵇ 𝕜`
equally are equal. Unlike
`MeasureTheory.ext_of_forall_mem_subalgebra_integral_eq_of_polish`, no metrizability or
countability is assumed.
entries.snippet:
lemma ext_of_forall_mem_subalgebra_integral_eq_of_innerRegular {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
    [BorelSpace E] [LocallyCompactSpace E] [P.InnerRegular] [P'.InnerRegular]
    {A : StarSubalgebra 𝕜 (E →ᵇ 𝕜)} (hA : (A.map (toContinuousMapStarₐ 𝕜)).SeparatesPoints)
    (heq : ∀ g ∈ A, ∫ x, (g : E → 𝕜) x ∂P = ∫ x, (g : E → 𝕜) x ∂P') : P = P'

entries.name: TauCeti.innerRegular_map_of_continuousOn
entries.docstring:
A measurable map continuous on a measurable set of full measure preserves inner regularity.
No separation, countability or finiteness assumption is required.
entries.snippet:
lemma innerRegular_map_of_continuousOn {μ : Measure α} [μ.InnerRegular]
    {f : α → β} {s : Set α} (hf : Measurable f) (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f s) (hmem : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ s) :
    (Measure.map f μ).InnerRegular

entries.name: TauCeti.comap_val_smallSets_neBot
entries.docstring:
**A filter indexes a nontrivial net by its own members.** A net indexed by the members of a
filter `l` converges along this filter, the members read through `Filter.smallSets`, so that
`∀ᶠ s in _, p s` says that `p` holds for every small enough member of `l`; it is not the bottom
filter, every member of `l` being an index below itself.
entries.snippet:
lemma comap_val_smallSets_neBot {α : Type*} (l : Filter α) :
    NeBot (comap (Subtype.val : {s : Set α // s ∈ l} → Set α) l.smallSets)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedAlgebra
entries.docstring: The closed unital star algebra generated by the integrated operators of `π`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedAlgebra :
    StarSubalgebra ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedAlgebra_def
entries.docstring: The integrated algebra is the closure of the star algebra generated by the integrated form.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedAlgebra_def :
    π.integratedAlgebra hcont hbdd μ =
      (StarAlgebra.adjoin ℂ
        (Set.range (π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ))).topologicalClosure

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_mem_integratedAlgebra
entries.docstring: Every integrated operator belongs to the integrated algebra.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_mem_integratedAlgebra
    (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) :
    π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f ∈ π.integratedAlgebra hcont hbdd μ

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra
entries.docstring: The integrated form with values in its closed star algebra.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra :
    (G →₁[μ] ℂ) →L[ℂ] π.integratedAlgebra hcont hbdd μ

entries.name: ContRepresentation.coe_integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra
entries.docstring: Coercing the algebra-valued integrated form recovers the original integrated operator.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.coe_integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) :
    (π.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra hcont hbdd μ f : H →L[ℂ] H) =
      π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f

entries.name: ContRepresentation.star_integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra
entries.docstring:
The algebra-valued integrated form of a unitary representation takes the involuted weight
to the star of the integrated operator.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.star_integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra
    [MeasurableNeg G] [μ.IsNegInvariant] (hπ : ContRepresentation.IsUnitary π)
    (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) :
    star (π.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra hcont hbdd μ f) =
      π.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra hcont hbdd μ
        (star (Lp.compMeasurePreserving Neg.neg (Measure.measurePreserving_neg μ) f))

entries.name: ContRepresentation.isClosed_integratedAlgebra
entries.docstring: The integrated algebra is closed in the operator norm.
entries.snippet:
@[instance]
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.isClosed_integratedAlgebra :
    IsClosed (π.integratedAlgebra hcont hbdd μ : Set (H →L[ℂ] H))

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedAlgebra_le_iff
entries.docstring:
A closed star subalgebra contains the integrated algebra exactly when it contains every
integrated operator.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedAlgebra_le_iff (B : StarSubalgebra ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (hB : IsClosed (B : Set (H →L[ℂ] H))) :
    π.integratedAlgebra hcont hbdd μ ≤ B ↔
      ∀ f : G →₁[μ] ℂ, π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f ∈ B

entries.name: ContRepresentation.comp_integratedOperatorL1_mem_integratedAlgebra
entries.docstring: A group translate of an integrated operator still belongs to the integrated algebra.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.comp_integratedOperatorL1_mem_integratedAlgebra
    (g : G) (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) :
    π (.ofAdd g) ∘L π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f ∈
      π.integratedAlgebra hcont hbdd μ

entries.name: ContRepresentation.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring: Translated integrated operators, as elements of the integrated algebra.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.ContRepresentation.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1
    (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) (g : G) : π.integratedAlgebra hcont hbdd μ

entries.name: ContRepresentation.coe_translatedIntegratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring: The underlying operator of a translated integrated operator is `π(g) π(f)`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.coe_translatedIntegratedOperatorL1
    (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) (g : G) :
    (π.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f g : H →L[ℂ] H) =
      π (.ofAdd g) ∘L π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f

entries.name: ContRepresentation.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1_eq
entries.docstring:
A translated integrated operator is the algebra-valued integrated form of the translated
weight.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1_eq
    (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) (g : G) :
    π.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f g =
      π.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra hcont hbdd μ
        (Lp.compMeasurePreserving (fun x ↦ -g + x) (measurePreserving_add_left μ (-g)) f)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1_zero
entries.docstring: Translation by zero recovers the algebra-valued integrated form.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1_zero (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) :
    π.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f 0 =
      π.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra hcont hbdd μ f

entries.name: ContRepresentation.continuous_translatedIntegratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring:
Translated integrated operators depend continuously on the group element in the norm of the
integrated algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.continuous_translatedIntegratedOperatorL1
    [IsTopologicalAddGroup G] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) :
    Continuous (π.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra_convolution
entries.docstring: The algebra-valued integrated form takes convolution of weights to multiplication.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra_convolution {f₁ f₂ : G → ℂ}
    (hf₁ : Integrable f₁ μ) (hf₂ : Integrable f₂ μ) :
    π.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra hcont hbdd μ
        ((hf₁.integrable_convolution (ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℂ ℂ) hf₂).toL1 _) =
      π.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra hcont hbdd μ (hf₁.toL1 f₁) *
        π.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra hcont hbdd μ (hf₂.toL1 f₂)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1_convolution
entries.docstring: Translating the integrated form of a convolution translates the first factor in its product.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1_convolution
    [μ.IsAddLeftInvariant] {f₁ f₂ : G → ℂ} (hf₁ : Integrable f₁ μ) (hf₂ : Integrable f₂ μ)
    (g : G) :
    π.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ
        ((hf₁.integrable_convolution (ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℂ ℂ) hf₂).toL1 _) g =
      π.translatedIntegratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ (hf₁.toL1 f₁) g *
        π.integratedOperatorL1ToAlgebra hcont hbdd μ (hf₂.toL1 f₂)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.isMulCommutative_integratedAlgebra
entries.docstring:
For a unitary abelian-group representation, the closed algebra of integrated operators is
commutative.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.isMulCommutative_integratedAlgebra
    (hπ : ContRepresentation.IsUnitary π) :
    IsMulCommutative (π.integratedAlgebra hcont hbdd μ)

entries.name: TauCeti.integrable_smul_apply
entries.docstring: The integrand of the integrated form is integrable.

entries.name: TauCeti.norm_integral_smul_apply_le
entries.docstring:
The integral of the integrand of the integrated form is bounded by the `L¹` norm of the
weight.

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring:
The **integrated form** of a strongly continuous, uniformly bounded representation `π` of an
additive group `G` (written multiplicatively as `Multiplicative G`): the bounded operator
`π(f) = ∫ g, f g • π g ∂μ` attached to an integrable weight `f`, defined pointwise by the Bochner
integral `π(f) v = ∫ g, f g • π g v ∂μ` of the continuous orbit `g ↦ π g v`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1
    (hcont : ∀ v, Continuous fun g : G ↦ π (.ofAdd g) v)
    (hbdd : ∃ C, ∀ g, ‖π g‖ ≤ C) (μ : Measure G) [μ.InnerRegularCompactLTTop] :
    (G →₁[μ] 𝕜) →L[𝕜] E →L[𝕜] E

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_apply
entries.docstring: The integrated form acts on a vector by integrating its orbit against the weight.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_apply (f : G →₁[μ] 𝕜) (v : E) :
    π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f v = ∫ g, f g • π (.ofAdd g) v ∂μ

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_toL1
entries.docstring: The integrated form of the class of an integrable function.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_toL1 {f : G → 𝕜} (hf : Integrable f μ)
    (v : E) :
    π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ (hf.toL1 f) v = ∫ g, f g • π (.ofAdd g) v ∂μ

entries.name: ContRepresentation.norm_integratedOperatorL1_le
entries.docstring:
The integrated form is bounded by the uniform bound of the representation times the `L¹`
norm of the weight.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.norm_integratedOperatorL1_le {C : ℝ} (hC : ∀ g, ‖π g‖ ≤ C)
    (f : G →₁[μ] 𝕜) :
    ‖π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f‖ ≤ C * ‖f‖

entries.name: ContRepresentation.comp_integratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring:
Translating the weight on the left by `h` amounts to composing the integrated form with
`π h`.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.comp_integratedOperatorL1 [CompleteSpace E] [MeasurableAdd G]
    [μ.IsAddLeftInvariant] (h : G) (f : G →₁[μ] 𝕜) :
    π (.ofAdd h) ∘L π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f =
      π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ
        (Lp.compMeasurePreserving (fun g ↦ -h + g) (measurePreserving_add_left μ (-h)) f)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.continuous_comp_integratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring:
Although `π` is only strongly continuous, `h ↦ π h ∘L π(f)` is continuous in the operator norm:
by `comp_integratedOperatorL1` it is the integrated form of the left translates of `f`, which
depend continuously on `h` in `L¹`.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.continuous_comp_integratedOperatorL1 [CompleteSpace E]
    [IsTopologicalAddGroup G] [MeasurableAdd G] [μ.IsAddLeftInvariant] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ]
    (f : G →₁[μ] 𝕜) :
    Continuous fun h : G ↦ π (.ofAdd h) ∘L π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f

entries.name: ContRepresentation.commute_integratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring:
Every action operator of a representation of an abelian group commutes with its
integrated operators. No invariance hypothesis on the measure is needed.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.commute_integratedOperatorL1
    (g : Multiplicative G) (f : G →₁[μ] 𝕜) :
    Commute (π g) (π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_commute
entries.docstring: Integrated operators of an abelian-group representation commute for any measure.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_commute (f₁ f₂ : G →₁[μ] 𝕜) :
    Commute (π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f₁)
      (π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f₂)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_convolution
entries.docstring:
The integrated form turns convolution of weights into composition of operators:
`π(f₁ ⋆ f₂) = π(f₁) ∘L π(f₂)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.integratedOperatorL1_convolution {f₁ f₂ : G → 𝕜}
    (hf₁ : Integrable f₁ μ) (hf₂ : Integrable f₂ μ) :
    π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ
        ((hf₁.integrable_convolution (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 𝕜) hf₂).toL1 _) =
      π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ (hf₁.toL1 f₁) ∘L
        π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ (hf₂.toL1 f₂)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.inner_integratedOperatorL1_apply
entries.docstring:
Matrix coefficients of the integrated form are the integrals of the matrix coefficients of the
representation against the weight.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.inner_integratedOperatorL1_apply (f : G →₁[μ] 𝕜) (w v : E) :
    ⟪w, π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f v⟫_𝕜 = ∫ g, f g * ⟪w, π (.ofAdd g) v⟫_𝕜 ∂μ

entries.name: ContRepresentation.adjoint_integratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring:
The adjoint of the integrated form of a unitary representation is the integrated form of the
involuted weight `g ↦ conj (f (-g))`.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.adjoint_integratedOperatorL1 [MeasurableNeg G]
    [μ.IsNegInvariant] (hπ : ContRepresentation.IsUnitary π) (f : G →₁[μ] 𝕜) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f) =
      π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ
        (star (Lp.compMeasurePreserving Neg.neg (Measure.measurePreserving_neg μ) f))

entries.name: ContRepresentation.isStarNormal_integratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring: The integrated operators of a unitary abelian-group representation are normal.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.isStarNormal_integratedOperatorL1
    (hπ : ContRepresentation.IsUnitary π) (f : G →₁[μ] 𝕜) :
    IsStarNormal (π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.tendsto_integratedOperatorL1_apply
entries.docstring:
**Approximate identities for the integrated form.** If the weights `f i` eventually have unit
integral and `L¹` norm at most `C`, and concentrate at `0` (for every neighbourhood `U` of `0`,
eventually `f i` vanishes almost everywhere outside `U`), then `π(f i)` tends strongly to the
identity: `π(f i) v → v` for every `v`.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.tendsto_integratedOperatorL1_apply {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι}
    {f : ι → G →₁[μ] 𝕜} {C : ℝ} (hf : ∀ᶠ i in l, ∫ g, f i g ∂μ = 1)
    (hfC : ∀ᶠ i in l, ‖f i‖ ≤ C)
    (hf₀ : ∀ U ∈ 𝓝 (0 : G), ∀ᶠ i in l, ∀ᵐ g ∂μ, g ∉ U → f i g = 0) (v : E) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ (f i) v) l (𝓝 v)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.mem_closure_range_integratedOperatorL1_apply
entries.docstring:
**The integrated form is nondegenerate.** For a measure positive on nonempty open sets and
finite on some neighbourhood of each point, such as a Haar measure on a locally compact group, every
vector `v` is a limit of vectors `π(f) v`.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.mem_closure_range_integratedOperatorL1_apply
    [μ.IsOpenPosMeasure] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] (v : E) :
    v ∈ closure (Set.range fun f : G →₁[μ] 𝕜 ↦ π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f v)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.existsUnique_pontryaginDual_of_integratedOperatorL1
entries.docstring:
A nonvanishing character of an algebra containing the integrated form of a strongly
continuous unitary representation detects a unique continuous group character. Its value is
the multiplier on every integrated operator, independently of the witnessing weight.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.ContRepresentation.existsUnique_pontryaginDual_of_integratedOperatorL1
    (π : ContRepresentation ℂ (Multiplicative G) H)
    {hcont : ∀ v, Continuous fun g : G => π (.ofAdd g) v}
    (hbdd : ∃ C, ∀ g, ‖π g‖ ≤ C)
    (hπ : ContRepresentation.IsUnitary π)
    (A : StarSubalgebra ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)) [CompleteSpace A] :
    ∀ (hA : ∀ f : G →₁[μ] ℂ, π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f ∈ A)
    (ω : characterSpace ℂ A),
    (∃ f : G →₁[μ] ℂ, ω ⟨π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f, hA f⟩ ≠ 0) →
    ∃! χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), ∀ (g : G) (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ),
      ω ⟨π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ
          (Lp.compMeasurePreserving (fun t => -g + t)
            (measurePreserving_add_left μ (-g)) f), hA _⟩ =
        (χ (.ofAdd g) : ℂ) * ω ⟨π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f, hA f⟩

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedCharacterSet
entries.docstring:
The characters of an algebra containing the integrated form which do not annihilate every
integrated operator.  When `π` is unitary, these are exactly the algebra characters from which
the representation detects a point of the Pontryagin dual.
entries.snippet: def integratedCharacterSet : Set (characterSpace ℂ A)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.mem_integratedCharacterSet_iff
entries.docstring: Membership in the integrated-character set means nonvanishing on some integrated operator.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma mem_integratedCharacterSet_iff (ω : characterSpace ℂ A) :
    ω ∈ π.integratedCharacterSet hcont hbdd A hA ↔
      ∃ f : G →₁[μ] ℂ, ω ⟨π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f, hA f⟩ ≠ 0

entries.name: ContRepresentation.isOpen_integratedCharacterSet
entries.docstring: The integrated-character set is open in the character space.
entries.snippet:
lemma isOpen_integratedCharacterSet :
    IsOpen (π.integratedCharacterSet hcont hbdd A hA)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual
entries.docstring:
The continuous group character detected by an algebra character that does not annihilate the
integrated form.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual
    (ω : π.integratedCharacterSet hcont hbdd A hA) : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual_spec
entries.docstring:
The defining multiplier identity for the group character detected by an integrated
character.
entries.snippet:
lemma integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual_spec
    (ω : π.integratedCharacterSet hcont hbdd A hA) (g : G) (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ) :
    ω.1
        ⟨π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ
          (Lp.compMeasurePreserving (fun t => -g + t)
            (measurePreserving_add_left μ (-g)) f), hA _⟩ =
      (π.integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual hcont hbdd A hA hπ ω (.ofAdd g) : ℂ) *
        ω.1 ⟨π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f, hA f⟩

entries.name: ContRepresentation.coe_integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual_apply_eq_div
entries.docstring: Local quotient formula for the group character detected by an integrated character.
entries.snippet:
lemma coe_integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual_apply_eq_div
    (ω : π.integratedCharacterSet hcont hbdd A hA) (g : G) (f : G →₁[μ] ℂ)
    (hf : ω.1 ⟨π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f, hA f⟩ ≠ 0) :
    (π.integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual hcont hbdd A hA hπ ω (.ofAdd g) : ℂ) =
      ω.1 ⟨π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ
        (Lp.compMeasurePreserving (fun t => -g + t)
          (measurePreserving_add_left μ (-g)) f), hA _⟩ /
        ω.1 ⟨π.integratedOperatorL1 hcont hbdd μ f, hA f⟩

entries.name: ContRepresentation.continuous_integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual
entries.docstring:
The group character detected by a nonvanishing integrated character depends continuously on
the algebra character.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual :
    Continuous (π.integratedCharacterToPontryaginDual hcont hbdd A hA hπ)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.subrepresentation
entries.docstring:
The restriction of a continuous representation to an invariant submodule. This is the
continuous counterpart of `Representation.subrepresentation`.
entries.snippet:
def subrepresentation (π : ContRepresentation R G V) (W : Submodule R V)
    (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) : ContRepresentation R G W

entries.name: ContRepresentation.coe_subrepresentation_apply
entries.docstring: The restricted action is the ambient action, read on the underlying vectors.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma coe_subrepresentation_apply (g : G) (v : W) :
    ((subrepresentation π W hW g v : W) : V) = π g (v : V)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.subrepresentationInclusion
entries.docstring:
The inclusion of a subrepresentation into its ambient continuous representation, packaged as a
continuous intertwiner.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def subrepresentationInclusion
    (π : ContRepresentation R G V) (σ : Subrepresentation π.toRepresentation) :
    ContIntertwiningMap
      (subrepresentation π σ.toSubmodule
        (fun g _ hv ↦ σ.apply_mem_toSubmodule g hv)) π

entries.name: ContRepresentation.subrepresentationInclusion_apply
entries.docstring: The subrepresentation inclusion sends a vector to the same vector in the ambient space.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma subrepresentationInclusion_apply (π : ContRepresentation R G V)
    (σ : Subrepresentation π.toRepresentation) (v : σ.toSubmodule) :
    π.subrepresentationInclusion σ v = (v : V)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.mem_invariants_subrepresentation
entries.docstring:
A vector of an invariant submodule is invariant for the restricted representation exactly when
it is invariant for the ambient one: the restricted action is the ambient action.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_invariants_subrepresentation {x : W} :
    x ∈ (subrepresentation π W hW).invariants ↔ (x : V) ∈ π.invariants

entries.name: ContRepresentation.toRepresentation_subrepresentation
entries.docstring:
The underlying representation of a restricted continuous representation is the restriction of
the underlying representation.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toRepresentation_subrepresentation :
    (subrepresentation π W hW).toRepresentation
      = π.toRepresentation.subrepresentation W fun g _ hv => hW g _ hv

entries.name: Subrepresentation.toRepresentation_subrepresentation_toSubmodule
entries.docstring:
Restricting `π` to the submodule a subrepresentation `σ` of `π.toRepresentation` carries has
`σ.toRepresentation` as its underlying representation: both restrict the ambient action to the
same submodule.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.Subrepresentation.toRepresentation_subrepresentation_toSubmodule
    (σ : Subrepresentation π.toRepresentation) :
    (subrepresentation π σ.toSubmodule
      (fun g _ hv ↦ σ.apply_mem_toSubmodule g hv)).toRepresentation = σ.toRepresentation

entries.name: ContRepresentation.quotient
entries.docstring:
A continuous representation descended to the quotient by an invariant submodule, which
carries the quotient topology. This is the continuous counterpart of `Representation.quotient`.
entries.snippet:
def quotient (π : ContRepresentation R G V) (W : Submodule R V)
    (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) : ContRepresentation R G (V ⧸ W)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.quotient_apply_mk
entries.docstring: The descended action on the class of `v` is the class of the ambient action on `v`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma quotient_apply_mk (g : G) (v : V) :
    quotient π W hW g (Submodule.Quotient.mk v) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (π g v)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.toRepresentation_quotient
entries.docstring:
The underlying representation of a descended continuous representation is the descended
underlying representation.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toRepresentation_quotient :
    (quotient π W hW).toRepresentation
      = π.toRepresentation.quotient W fun g _ hv => hW g _ hv

entries.name: ContRepresentation.continuous_subrepresentation
entries.docstring:
Restricting a continuous representation to an invariant submodule preserves continuity: from
continuity of `g ↦ π g` as a map into the continuous linear endomorphisms of `V`, the restricted
action `g ↦ subrepresentation π W hW g` is continuous into those of `W`. This supplies the
continuity argument that `matrixCoeff` and the rest of the continuous-representation API take
explicitly, so a subrepresentation can be used wherever a continuous representation is expected.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_subrepresentation (hπ : Continuous π) :
    Continuous (subrepresentation π W hW)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.self_inv_apply
entries.docstring:
Applying a continuous group representation at an element and then at its inverse cancels.

This restates `Representation.self_inv_apply` for the continuous action coercion, which `simp` does
not otherwise reach; it is an implementation detail of the inverse-transfer proofs below.
entries.snippet:
private lemma self_inv_apply (π : ContRepresentation R G V) (g : G) (v : V) :
    π g (π g⁻¹ v) = v

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary
entries.docstring:
A continuous representation is unitary when every action operator preserves the inner
product.
entries.snippet: def IsUnitary (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) : Prop

entries.name: ContRepresentation.isUnitary_iff_norm_map
entries.docstring: A representation is unitary exactly when every action map preserves norms.
entries.snippet:
lemma isUnitary_iff_norm_map (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) :
    IsUnitary π ↔ ∀ g v, ‖π g v‖ = ‖v‖

entries.name: ContRepresentation.isUnitary_iff_isometry
entries.docstring: A representation is unitary exactly when every action map is an isometry.
entries.snippet:
lemma isUnitary_iff_isometry (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) :
    IsUnitary π ↔ ∀ g, Isometry (π g)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.inner_map_map
entries.docstring: A unitary representation preserves the inner product.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma inner_map_map (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v w : V) :
    ⟪π g v, π g w⟫_𝕜 = ⟪v, w⟫_𝕜

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.norm_map
entries.docstring: Every action map of a unitary representation preserves norms.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma norm_map (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v : V) :
    ‖π g v‖ = ‖v‖

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.norm_le_one
entries.docstring: Every action operator of a unitary representation has operator norm at most `1`.
entries.snippet: lemma norm_le_one (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) : ‖π g‖ ≤ 1

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.exists_norm_le
entries.docstring:
The action operators of a unitary representation are uniformly bounded, in the form taken
by the integrated-form API.
entries.snippet: lemma exists_norm_le (hπ : IsUnitary π) : ∃ C, ∀ g, ‖π g‖ ≤ C

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.isometry
entries.docstring: Every action map of a unitary representation is an isometry.
entries.snippet: lemma isometry (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) : Isometry (π g)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.injective
entries.docstring: Every action map of a unitary representation is injective.
entries.snippet: lemma injective (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) : Function.Injective (π g)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.restrict
entries.docstring: Restriction along a monoid homomorphism preserves unitarity.
entries.snippet:
lemma restrict {H : Type*} [Monoid H] (hπ : IsUnitary π) (φ : H →* G) :
    IsUnitary (π.restrict φ)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.subrepresentation
entries.docstring: The restriction of a unitary representation to an invariant submodule is unitary.
entries.snippet:
lemma subrepresentation (hπ : IsUnitary π) {W : Submodule 𝕜 V}
    (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) : IsUnitary (subrepresentation π W hW)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.norm_inner_map_le
entries.docstring:
A matrix coefficient of a unitary representation is bounded by the product of the vector
norms.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_inner_map_le (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v w : V) :
    ‖⟪π g v, w⟫_𝕜‖ ≤ ‖v‖ * ‖w‖

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.adjoint_comp_self
entries.docstring: The adjoint of a unitary action operator is a left inverse.
entries.snippet:
lemma adjoint_comp_self (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) :
    (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π g)).comp (π g) = 1

entries.name: ContRepresentation.isUnitary_trivial
entries.docstring: The trivial continuous representation is unitary.
entries.snippet:
lemma isUnitary_trivial :
    IsUnitary (ContRepresentation.trivial 𝕜 G V)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.isUnitary_iff_mem_unitary
entries.docstring:
For a group representation, inner-product preservation is equivalent to every action operator
belonging to Mathlib's unitary submonoid.
entries.snippet:
lemma isUnitary_iff_mem_unitary (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) :
    IsUnitary π ↔ ∀ g, π g ∈ unitary (V →L[𝕜] V)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.mem_unitary
entries.docstring:
Every action operator of a unitary group representation belongs to Mathlib's `unitary`
submonoid.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_unitary (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) :
    π g ∈ unitary (V →L[𝕜] V)

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.self_comp_adjoint
entries.docstring: The adjoint of a unitary action operator is a right inverse.
entries.snippet:
lemma self_comp_adjoint (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) :
    (π g).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π g)) = 1

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.inner_map_left
entries.docstring:
Moving a unitary action from the first inner-product argument to the second replaces the group
element by its inverse.
entries.snippet:
lemma inner_map_left (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v w : V) :
    ⟪π g v, w⟫_𝕜 = ⟪v, π g⁻¹ w⟫_𝕜

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.inner_map_right
entries.docstring:
Moving a unitary action from the second inner-product argument to the first replaces the group
element by its inverse.
entries.snippet:
lemma inner_map_right (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v w : V) :
    ⟪v, π g w⟫_𝕜 = ⟪π g⁻¹ v, w⟫_𝕜

entries.name: ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.adjoint_eq_inv
entries.docstring: The adjoint of a unitary action operator is the action of the inverse group element.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma adjoint_eq_inv (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π g) = π g⁻¹

entries.name: ContinuousMonoidHom.instPolishSpace
entries.docstring:
Continuous homomorphisms from a second-countable locally compact monoid to a Polish
topological monoid form a Polish space in the compact-open topology.
entries.snippet:
instance _root_.ContinuousMonoidHom.instPolishSpace {A B : Type*}
    [Monoid A] [TopologicalSpace A] [LocallyCompactSpace A] [SecondCountableTopology A]
    [Monoid B] [TopologicalSpace B] [ContinuousMul B] [PolishSpace B] :
    PolishSpace (A →ₜ* B)

entries.name: TauCeti.instPolishSpacePontryaginDual
entries.docstring: The Pontryagin dual of a second-countable locally compact monoid is Polish.
entries.snippet:
instance instPolishSpacePontryaginDual {A : Type*} [Monoid A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    [LocallyCompactSpace A] [SecondCountableTopology A] : PolishSpace (PontryaginDual A)

entries.name: TauCeti.circleEquivPontryaginDualInt
entries.docstring:
The unit circle is the Pontryagin dual of `ℤ`: the point `z` corresponds to the character
`n ↦ zⁿ`, and a character corresponds to its value at `1`.
entries.snippet: def circleEquivPontryaginDualInt : Circle ≃ₜ* PontryaginDual (Multiplicative ℤ) where

entries.name: TauCeti.circleEquivPontryaginDualInt_apply_apply
entries.docstring: The character attached to `z` sends `n` to `zⁿ`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma circleEquivPontryaginDualInt_apply_apply (z : Circle) (n : Multiplicative ℤ) :
    circleEquivPontryaginDualInt z n = z ^ n.toAdd

entries.name: TauCeti.circleEquivPontryaginDualInt_symm_apply
entries.docstring: The point of the circle attached to a character of `ℤ` is its value at `1`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma circleEquivPontryaginDualInt_symm_apply (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative ℤ)) :
    circleEquivPontryaginDualInt.symm χ = χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)

entries.name: lTensor_map_id_comm
entries.docstring: An endomorphism of the second tensor factor commutes with one of the first.
entries.snippet:
lemma lTensor_map_id_comm {k : Type} [CommSemiring k] {W X : Type} [AddCommMonoid W]
    [Module k W] [AddCommMonoid X] [Module k X] (f : X →ₗ[k] X) (g : W →ₗ[k] W)
    (t : W ⊗[k] X) :
    (LinearMap.lTensor W f) (TensorProduct.map g LinearMap.id t) =
      TensorProduct.map g LinearMap.id ((LinearMap.lTensor W f) t)

entries.name: congr_assoc_map_id_comm
entries.docstring:
Reassociating and recombining the last two tensor factors commutes with an
  endomorphism of the first.
entries.snippet:
lemma congr_assoc_map_id_comm {k : Type} [CommSemiring k] {W X Y Z : Type} [AddCommMonoid W]
    [Module k W] [AddCommMonoid X] [Module k X] [AddCommMonoid Y] [Module k Y]
    [AddCommMonoid Z] [Module k Z] (E : X ⊗[k] Y ≃ₗ[k] Z) (g : W →ₗ[k] W)
    (t : (W ⊗[k] X) ⊗[k] Y) :
    (TensorProduct.congr (LinearEquiv.refl k W) E) (TensorProduct.assoc k W X Y
        (TensorProduct.map (TensorProduct.map g LinearMap.id) LinearMap.id t)) =
      TensorProduct.map g LinearMap.id
        ((TensorProduct.congr (LinearEquiv.refl k W) E) (TensorProduct.assoc k W X Y t))

entries.name: QED.indexList
entries.docstring:
The canonical sorted list of a multiset of spacetime directions, sorted
  through `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 ≃ Fin 4`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def indexList (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)

entries.name: QED.indexList_zero
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma indexList_zero : indexList 0 = []

entries.name: QED.indexList_singleton
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma indexList_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : indexList {μ} = [μ]

entries.name: QED.mem_indexList
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_indexList {t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} {a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3} :
    a ∈ indexList t ↔ a ∈ t

entries.name: QED.indexList_length
entries.snippet:
lemma indexList_length (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    (indexList t).length = Multiset.card t

entries.name: QED.classRep
entries.docstring:
The canonical representative of a nonempty multiset of spacetime
  directions: the head of its canonical sorted list.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def classRep (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3

entries.name: QED.classRep_mem
entries.snippet: lemma classRep_mem {t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} (ht : t ≠ 0) : classRep t ∈ t

entries.name: QED.derivSum
entries.docstring:
The Lorentz transport of a family indexed by derivative multisets along a
  list of derivative directions: each direction in the list is summed against
  a row of `Λ⁻¹`, and the chosen directions accumulate in the multiset
  argument of the continuation `k`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def derivSum {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M]
    (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) :
    List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) → M
  | [], k => k 0
