entries.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeGroupI.truncation_eq_one_of_mem_truncationKer
entries.docstring:
Maurer–Cartan triangularity for the Standard Model: a jet trivial to order `n` in the
  sense of the Maurer–Cartan filtration truncates to the identity at order `n`. On each
  factor the radial relation `∂_ρ U = −i ω_ρ(U) U` and the Euler vanishing principle
  propagate the vanishing of the Maurer–Cartan coefficients below degree `n` to the
  vanishing of the coefficients of `U` in nonzero degree up to `n`.
entries.snippet:
lemma truncation_eq_one_of_mem_truncationKer {U : JetGaugeGroupI} {n : ℕ}
    (hU : U ∈ localGaugeData.truncationKer n) : truncation n U = 1

entries.name: StandardModel.localGaugeData
entries.docstring:
The Standard Model gauge group as local gauge data, for the jet gauge group
  `JetGaugeGroupI` and its Lie algebra `JetGaugeAlgebra` over the global group
  `GaugeGroupI` and gauge algebra `GaugeAlgebra`. It is the gauge data
  `StandardModel.Model.gaugeData` that the model table assembles from the factor list
  `[.SU 3, .SU 2, .U1]` by `LocalGaugeData.ofFactors`; the carriers of that assembly are
  `JetGaugeGroupI` and `JetGaugeAlgebra` on the nose, and each data field is definitionally
  the existing Standard Model construction (the rules of section B are all `rfl`).
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def localGaugeData :
    LocalGaugeData GaugeGroupI GaugeAlgebra JetGaugeGroupI JetGaugeAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.instFreeLocalGaugeData
entries.docstring:
The Standard Model package is free. It is the local gauge data of the factors
  `SU(3)`, `SU(2)` and `U(1)`, each free, and freeness passes to products:
  `LocalGaugeData.instFreeOfFactors`. The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data are therefore free
  coordinates on its pure jets, by `LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_bijective`.
entries.snippet: instance instFreeLocalGaugeData : localGaugeData.Free

entries.name: StandardModel.localGaugeData_adjointCoeff_apply
entries.docstring: The adjoint Taylor coefficients of the package, written out in Standard Model terms.

@[simp]
lemma localGaugeData_adjointCoeff_apply (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))

entries.name: StandardModel.localGaugeData_adjointCoeff_toSU3Matrix
entries.docstring: The `su(3)` component of the adjoint Taylor coefficients.

      = ((U.1.1 * b.toSU3Matrix.map (MvPowerSeries.C : ℂ → SpaceTimeAlgebra) *
          star U.1.1).map fun f =>
          MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv p f))

entries.name: StandardModel.instFaithfulLocalGaugeData
entries.docstring:
The Standard Model package is faithful: an element of the jet gauge algebra is
  determined by the base-point values of its iterated derivatives, and a jet whose
  Maurer–Cartan form vanishes is the constant jet of its value. Both are statements about
  power series, proved from the matrix definitions in
  `JetGaugeAlgebra.ext_of_eval_iteratedDeriv` and `maurerCartanForm_eq_zero_iff_ofConstant`.
  Unlike the package itself this is a property of it and not a choice, so it is an
  instance.
entries.snippet: instance instFaithfulLocalGaugeData : localGaugeData.Faithful

entries.name: StandardModel.maurerCartanForm
entries.docstring:
The Maurer–Cartan form `ω_μ(U) := i (∂_μ U) U⁻¹` of the jet gauge group, valued
  in the jet gauge algebra.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def maurerCartanForm (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetGaugeAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.maurerCartanForm_toSU3Matrix
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma maurerCartanForm_toSU3Matrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (maurerCartanForm U μ).toSU3Matrix =
      Complex.I • (U.1.1.map (pderiv μ) * star U.1.1)

entries.name: StandardModel.maurerCartanForm_toSU2Matrix
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma maurerCartanForm_toSU2Matrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (maurerCartanForm U μ).toSU2Matrix =
      Complex.I • (U.2.1.1.map (pderiv μ) * star U.2.1.1)

entries.name: StandardModel.maurerCartanForm_toU1Value
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma maurerCartanForm_toU1Value (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (maurerCartanForm U μ).toU1Value =
      Complex.I • (pderiv μ U.2.2.1 * star U.2.2.1)

entries.name: StandardModel.maurerCartanForm_one
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma maurerCartanForm_one : maurerCartanForm (1 : JetGaugeGroupI) = 0

entries.name: StandardModel.maurerCartanForm_ofConstant
entries.snippet:
lemma maurerCartanForm_ofConstant (U₀ : GaugeGroupI) :
    maurerCartanForm (JetGaugeGroupI.ofConstant U₀) = 0

entries.name: StandardModel.maurerCartanForm_cocycle
entries.snippet:
lemma maurerCartanForm_cocycle (U V : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    maurerCartanForm (U * V) μ = maurerCartanForm U μ + adjoint U (maurerCartanForm V μ)

entries.name: StandardModel.deriv_zero_of_maurerCartanForm_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_zero_of_maurerCartanForm_zero (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (h : maurerCartanForm U = 0) :
    ∀ μ, U.deriv μ = 0

entries.name: StandardModel.maurerCartanForm_eq_zero_iff_ofConstant
entries.snippet:
lemma maurerCartanForm_eq_zero_iff_ofConstant (U : JetGaugeGroupI) :
    maurerCartanForm U = 0 ↔ ∃ c, U = JetGaugeGroupI.ofConstant c

entries.name: StandardModel.maurerCartanForm_structure
entries.docstring:
The structural (Maurer–Cartan) equation, basis-independently: the Maurer–Cartan
  form is flat,

  `∂_μ ω_ν − ∂_ν ω_μ + ⁅ω_μ, ω_ν⁆ = 0`.

  In components with respect to a basis of the jet gauge algebra this is
  `∂_μ ω^a_ν − ∂_ν ω^a_μ = ∑_{b c} f^a_{b c} · ω^b_μ · ω^c_ν`. On each matrix
  factor the second-derivative terms cancel by symmetry of mixed partials, the
  derivative of `A†` is rewritten through the differentiated unitarity relation,
  and the surviving first-order terms form the commutator; on the abelian `U(1)`
  factor the commutator is absent and only the symmetry of mixed partials
  remains.
entries.snippet:
lemma maurerCartanForm_structure (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    deriv μ (maurerCartanForm U ν) - deriv ν (maurerCartanForm U μ) +
      ⁅maurerCartanForm U μ, maurerCartanForm U ν⁆ = 0

entries.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.deriv_ofConstant
entries.docstring:
The constant inclusion has vanishing formal derivative: constants have no
  spacetime dependence.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma JetGaugeAlgebra.deriv_ofConstant (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    deriv μ (ofConstant a) = 0

entries.name: StandardModel.deriv_adjointMap
entries.docstring:
The formal derivative intertwines the adjoint action through the Maurer–Cartan
  form: `∂_μ (Ad_U x) = Ad_U (∂_μ x) − ⁅ω_μ(U), Ad_U x⁆`. On the matrix factors this
  is the Leibniz rule with the derivative of `U†` rewritten through the
  differentiated unitarity relation; on the abelian `u(1)` factor the adjoint action
  is trivial and the bracket is absent.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_adjointMap (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    deriv μ (adjointMap U x) =
      adjointMap U (deriv μ x) - ⁅maurerCartanForm U μ, adjointMap U x⁆

entries.name: StandardModel.su2Epsilon
entries.docstring:
The antisymmetric symbol `ε_{ab}` on two `su(2)` fundamental indices: the Levi-Civita
  symbol of `Fin 2`, normalized by `ε 0 1 = 1`.
entries.snippet: def su2Epsilon (a b : Fin 2) : ℂ

entries.name: StandardModel.sum_su2Epsilon_mul
entries.docstring:
Every element of `SU(2)` fixes the antisymmetric symbol: contracted against two rows of
  `U` it gives `det U` times itself (`sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod`), and `det U = 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_su2Epsilon_mul (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (b c : Fin 2) :
    ∑ x : Fin 2, ∑ y : Fin 2, su2Epsilon x y * (U.1 b x * U.1 c y) = su2Epsilon b c

entries.name: StandardModel.su2_star_eq_adjugate
entries.docstring: The conjugate transpose of an `SU(2)` matrix is its adjugate.
entries.snippet:
lemma su2_star_eq_adjugate (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    star U.1 = Matrix.adjugate U.1

entries.name: StandardModel.su2_conj_apply
entries.docstring:
The conjugate of an entry of an `SU(2)` matrix is the transposed entry of its
  adjugate.
entries.snippet:
lemma su2_conj_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (i j : Fin 2) :
    conj (U.1 i j) = Matrix.adjugate U.1 j i

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetActionMatrix_map_cc_foldl

    ((jetActionMatrix a).map fun f =>

      = actionMatrix (JetGaugeAlgebra.eval (JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv p a))

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.pderivWeak_comp_foldWeak
StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetValLinEquiv_jetDeriv
entries.docstring:
The identification of Higgs-doublet jets intertwines the formal derivative with the
  entrywise derivative on the weak coordinates.
entries.snippet:
private lemma jetValLinEquiv_jetDeriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] HiggsVec) :
    jetValLinEquiv (jetDeriv μ z)
      = pderivWeak μ (jetValLinEquiv z)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetValLinEquiv_jetIteratedDeriv
entries.docstring:
The identification of Higgs-doublet jets intertwines the iterated formal derivative
  with the entrywise iterated derivative on the weak coordinates.
entries.snippet:
private lemma jetValLinEquiv_jetIteratedDeriv (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] HiggsVec) :
    jetValLinEquiv (jetIteratedDeriv x z)
      = foldWeak x (jetValLinEquiv z)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetEval_eq
entries.docstring: The base-point evaluation of a Higgs-doublet jet through the weak coordinates.
entries.snippet:
private lemma jetEval_eq (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] HiggsVec) :
    jetEval z = ccWeak (jetValLinEquiv z)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetGaugeMatrix_map_pderiv
entries.docstring:
**The derivative identity** for the weak matrix of the jet gauge action: the
  formal derivative of the weak matrix is minus the jet action matrix of the
  Maurer–Cartan form times the weak matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma jetGaugeMatrix_map_pderiv (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (jetGaugeMatrix U).map (fun f => pderiv μ f)
      = -(jetActionMatrix (maurerCartanForm U μ) * jetGaugeMatrix U)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetGaugeMatrix_mul_jetActionMatrix
entries.docstring:
**The equivariance identity** for the weak matrix of the jet gauge action: the
  weak matrix intertwines the constant jet action matrix with its adjoint
  transform.
entries.snippet:
lemma jetGaugeMatrix_mul_jetActionMatrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    jetGaugeMatrix U * jetActionMatrix (JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant c)
      = jetActionMatrix (JetGaugeAlgebra.adjointMap U (JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant c))
        * jetGaugeMatrix U

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repCoeff_eq
entries.docstring:
**The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet gauge action** on the Higgs
  doublet are the weak endomorphisms of the base-point Taylor coefficients of the
  weak matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma repCoeff_eq (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff repJetGaugeGroupI U x
      = weakEnd ((jetGaugeMatrix U).map fun f =>
          constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f))

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.weakEnd_one
entries.docstring: The weak endomorphism of the identity matrix is the identity.
entries.snippet: lemma weakEnd_one : weakEnd 1 = LinearMap.id

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one
entries.docstring:
At the base point, a gauge jet with trivial value acts trivially: the zeroth
  Taylor coefficient of the jet gauge action is the identity.
entries.snippet:
lemma repCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one {U : JetGaugeGroupI} (hU : U.eval = 1) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff repJetGaugeGroupI U 0 = LinearMap.id

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.isInfinitesimalActionOf
entries.docstring:
**The `(1, 2)_{3}` action of the gauge algebra is the infinitesimal action
  underlying the jet gauge action on the Higgs doublet**: its base-point Taylor
  coefficients obey the Maurer–Cartan Leibniz law and intertwine the action with the
  adjoint transports.
entries.snippet:
lemma isInfinitesimalActionOf :
    localGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf gaugeAlgebraAction repJetGaugeGroupI

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.gaugeAlgebraAction_comm_repLorentz
entries.docstring:
The infinitesimal gauge action on the Higgs commutes with the Lorentz action, which is
  trivial.
entries.snippet:
lemma gaugeAlgebraAction_comm_repLorentz (c : GaugeAlgebra) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : HiggsVec) :
    HiggsVec.gaugeAlgebraAction c ((Representation.trivial ℂ SL(2,ℂ) HiggsVec) Λ v) =
      (Representation.trivial ℂ SL(2,ℂ) HiggsVec) Λ (HiggsVec.gaugeAlgebraAction c v)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsJetAlgebra
entries.docstring:
**The jet algebra of the Higgs field**: the bosonic algebra of the `HiggsVec`-valued
  Higgs field. Its generators are the component functions `∂_s H_α` and `∂_s H̄_α`, and
  they commute — the Higgs is a boson.
entries.snippet: abbrev HiggsJetAlgebra : Type

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsJetAlgebra.ofHiggs
entries.docstring: The component functions of the Higgs field inside its jet algebra.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def ofHiggs : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec →ₗ[ℂ] HiggsJetAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsJetAlgebra.ofConjHiggs
entries.docstring: The conjugate component functions of the Higgs field inside its jet algebra.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def ofConjHiggs :
    Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec) →ₗ[ℂ] HiggsJetAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsJetAlgebra.repLorentzGroup
entries.docstring:
The Lorentz action on the jet algebra of the Higgs field: the Higgs is a Lorentz
  scalar, so the Lorentz group acts on the component functions only through their
  derivative labels.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def repLorentzGroup : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) HiggsJetAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsJetAlgebra.repJetGaugeGroupI
entries.docstring:
The jet gauge action on the jet algebra of the Higgs field, lifted from the fibrewise
  action on its jets.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def repJetGaugeGroupI : Representation ℂ JetGaugeGroupI HiggsJetAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsJetAlgebra.repGaugeGroupI
entries.docstring:
The action of the constant — global — gauge transformations on the jet algebra of the
  Higgs field.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def repGaugeGroupI : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI HiggsJetAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsJetAlgebra.massWeightScale
entries.docstring:
The mass-dimension scaling on the jet algebra of the Higgs field: the Higgs has mass
  dimension one, that is mass weight two, and each derivative adds mass weight two.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def massWeightScale (c : ℂ) : HiggsJetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] HiggsJetAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsJetAlgebra.massWeightScale_ofHiggs
entries.docstring: The Higgs field carries mass weight two — mass dimension one.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma massWeightScale_ofHiggs (c : ℂ) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) :
    massWeightScale c (ofHiggs φ) = c ^ 2 • ofHiggs φ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsJetAlgebra.massWeightScale_jetDeriv
entries.docstring: A derivative of the Higgs field adds mass weight two.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightScale_jetDeriv (c : ℂ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : HiggsJetAlgebra) :
    massWeightScale c (BosonicAlgebra.jetDeriv μ x)
      = c ^ 2 • BosonicAlgebra.jetDeriv μ (massWeightScale c x)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetValLinEquiv
entries.docstring:
Absorbs the jet ring into the weak index: a jet of the Higgs field is the same thing
as a `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-valued weak doublet,

  `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] HiggsVec ≃ EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 2)`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def jetValLinEquiv :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] HiggsVec ≃ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 2)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetValLinEquiv_tmul
entries.snippet:
lemma jetValLinEquiv_tmul (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (v : HiggsVec) :
    jetValLinEquiv (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) = WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => v.ofLp i • f

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetValLinEquiv_smul
entries.docstring:
The identification of the jets of the Higgs field is `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-linear: multiplying a
  jet by a scalar jet multiplies each of its weak components.
entries.snippet:
lemma jetValLinEquiv_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] HiggsVec) :
    jetValLinEquiv (χ • z) = χ • jetValLinEquiv z

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetValLinEquiv_symm_smul
entries.snippet:
lemma jetValLinEquiv_symm_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (y : EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 2)) :
    jetValLinEquiv.symm (χ • y) = χ • jetValLinEquiv.symm y

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetGaugeMatrix
entries.docstring:
The matrix of jets through which a jet of gauge transformations acts on the Higgs
  doublet: the `SU(2)` power-series matrix scaled by the hypercharge power series
  `u ^ 3`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def jetGaugeMatrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) SpaceTimeAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetGaugeMatrix_one
entries.snippet: lemma jetGaugeMatrix_one : jetGaugeMatrix 1 = 1

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.jetGaugeMatrix_mul
entries.snippet:
lemma jetGaugeMatrix_mul (U₁ U₂ : JetGaugeGroupI) :
    jetGaugeMatrix (U₁ * U₂) = jetGaugeMatrix U₁ * jetGaugeMatrix U₂

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repJetGaugeGroupI
entries.docstring:
The `2_{3}` action of the jet gauge group on the jets of the Higgs field. Through
`jetValLinEquiv` the weak matrix of the gauge jet, carrying the `3` hypercharge phase
`u ^ 3`, acts `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-linearly by matrix-vector multiplication.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def repJetGaugeGroupI :
    Representation ℂ JetGaugeGroupI (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] HiggsVec) where

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repJetGaugeGroupI_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma repJetGaugeGroupI_apply (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] HiggsVec) :
    repJetGaugeGroupI U z =
      jetValLinEquiv.symm
        (Matrix.toLpLinAlgEquiv 2 (jetGaugeMatrix U) (jetValLinEquiv z))

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repJetGaugeGroupI_smul
entries.docstring:
**The jet gauge action on the jets of the Higgs field is fibrewise**: it commutes
  with multiplication by scalar jets, acting on the values of the field over the identity
  on spacetime. This is the hypothesis under which the action lifts to the bosonic
  algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma repJetGaugeGroupI_smul (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] HiggsVec) :
    repJetGaugeGroupI U (χ • z) = χ • repJetGaugeGroupI U z

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repJetGaugeGroupI_ofConstant
entries.docstring:
On jets of constant gauge transformations the jet action reduces to the global gauge
action on the fibre: the action `HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI` on the Higgs factor, and the
trivial action on the jet ring.
entries.snippet:
lemma repJetGaugeGroupI_ofConstant (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    repJetGaugeGroupI (JetGaugeGroupI.ofConstant g) =
      TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (repGaugeGroupI g)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField
entries.docstring:
The Higgs field as a matter field of `StandardModel.localGaugeData`, valued in
  `HiggsVec`, in the `2_{3}` representation of the gauge group, a Lorentz scalar, of mass
  weight two, declared bosonic.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def matterField : MatterField localGaugeData where

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_V
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma matterField_V : matterField.V = HiggsVec

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_repLorentz
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma matterField_repLorentz :
    matterField.repLorentz = Representation.trivial ℂ SL(2,ℂ) HiggsVec

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_repJet
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma matterField_repJet : matterField.repJet = repJetGaugeGroupI

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_repAlgebra
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma matterField_repAlgebra : matterField.repAlgebra = gaugeAlgebraAction

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_massWeight
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma matterField_massWeight : matterField.massWeight = 2

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_pureJetsActTrivially
entries.docstring: Pure gauge jets act trivially on the Higgs at the base point.
entries.snippet: lemma matterField_pureJetsActTrivially : matterField.PureJetsActTrivially

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_gaugeLorentzCompatible
entries.docstring: The gauge action on the Higgs commutes with its (trivial) Lorentz action.
entries.snippet: lemma matterField_gaugeLorentzCompatible : matterField.GaugeLorentzCompatible

entries.name: StandardModel.gaugeLorentzMaps
entries.docstring:
The gauge and Lorentz groups read as a single family of linear maps, indexed by their
  disjoint union.
entries.snippet: def gaugeLorentzMaps : GaugeGroupI ⊕ SL(2,ℂ) → B →ₗ[ℂ] B

entries.name: StandardModel.isStableUnder_gaugeLorentzMaps_iff
entries.docstring:
A submodule stable under both groups is stable under the combined family, and
  conversely.
entries.snippet:
lemma isStableUnder_gaugeLorentzMaps_iff {V : Submodule ℂ B} :
    IsStableUnder (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) V
      ↔ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ V, repGauge g y ∈ V)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ V, repLorentz Λ y ∈ V

entries.name: StandardModel.forall_gaugeLorentzMaps_eq_self_iff
entries.docstring: An element fixed by both groups is fixed by the combined family, and conversely.
entries.snippet:
lemma forall_gaugeLorentzMaps_eq_self_iff {x : B} :
    (∀ p, gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz p x = x)
      ↔ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x) ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz Λ x = x

entries.name: StandardModel.isFixedBy_gaugeLorentzMaps_iff
entries.docstring:
A submodule fixed pointwise by both groups is fixed pointwise by the combined family, and
  conversely.
entries.snippet:
lemma isFixedBy_gaugeLorentzMaps_iff {V : Submodule ℂ B} :
    IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) V
      ↔ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ V, repGauge g y = y)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ V, repLorentz Λ y = y

entries.name: StandardModel.ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
entries.docstring:
The classification endpoint `ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_forall_eq_self_iff` for the
  gauge and Lorentz groups together, with the two invariances and the two stabilities stated
  separately.
entries.snippet:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff {V W S : Submodule ℂ B}
    (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) V W) (hWV : W ≤ V)
    (hW : IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) W)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz Λ y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ V ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x) ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz Λ x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz Λ y = y) ∧ x - y ∈ W

entries.name: StandardModel.ReducesInvariantsTo.ofGauge
entries.docstring: A gauge reduction is a reduction for the gauge and Lorentz groups together.

entries.name: StandardModel.ReducesInvariantsTo.ofSU3
entries.docstring:
A reduction for the colour factor is a reduction for the gauge and Lorentz groups
  together.

entries.name: StandardModel.ReducesInvariantsTo.ofSU2
entries.docstring:
A reduction for the isospin factor is a reduction for the gauge and Lorentz groups
  together.

entries.name: StandardModel.ReducesInvariantsTo.ofLorentz
entries.docstring: A Lorentz reduction is a reduction for the gauge and Lorentz groups together.

entries.name: StandardModel.gaugeLorentzMaps_mul
entries.docstring:
The two groups read as one family of maps respect multiplication, each of the two
  representations doing so.
entries.snippet:
lemma gaugeLorentzMaps_mul
    (hG : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repGauge g (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge g b₁ * repGauge g b₂)
    (hL : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂)
    (p : GaugeGroupI ⊕ SL(2,ℂ)) (a b : B) :
    gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz p (a * b)
      = gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz p a
        * gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz p b

entries.name: StandardModel.su3_inv_apply
entries.docstring:
The entries of the inverse of an `SU(3)` element are the conjugated transposed
  entries, the inverse of a unitary matrix being its conjugate transpose.
entries.snippet:
lemma su3_inv_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (a b : Fin 3) :
    (U⁻¹).1 a b = conj (U.1 b a)

entries.name: StandardModel.su2_inv_apply
entries.docstring:
The entries of the inverse of an `SU(2)` element are the conjugated transposed
  entries.
entries.snippet:
lemma su2_inv_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (a b : Fin 2) :
    (U⁻¹).1 a b = conj (U.1 b a)

entries.name: StandardModel.unitary_inv_coe
entries.docstring: The inverse of a unitary scalar is its conjugate.
entries.snippet: lemma unitary_inv_coe (t : unitary ℂ) : ((t⁻¹ : unitary ℂ) : ℂ) = star (t : ℂ)

entries.name: StandardModel.inv_su3Elt
entries.docstring:
The inverse of a colour gauge transformation is the colour transformation of the
  inverse.
entries.snippet:
lemma inv_su3Elt (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI)⁻¹ = ((U⁻¹, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI)

entries.name: StandardModel.inv_su2Elt
entries.docstring:
The inverse of an isospin gauge transformation is the isospin transformation of the
  inverse.
entries.snippet:
lemma inv_su2Elt (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI)⁻¹ = ((1, V⁻¹, 1) : GaugeGroupI)

entries.name: StandardModel.inv_u1Elt
entries.docstring:
The inverse of a hypercharge gauge transformation is the hypercharge transformation of
  the inverse.
entries.snippet:
lemma inv_u1Elt (t : unitary ℂ) :
    ((1, 1, t) : GaugeGroupI)⁻¹ = ((1, 1, t⁻¹) : GaugeGroupI)

entries.name: StandardModel.forall_repGauge_eq_self
entries.docstring:
A gauge transformation is the product of its colour, isospin and hypercharge parts, so
  an element fixed by each of the three factors separately is gauge invariant.
entries.snippet:
lemma forall_repGauge_eq_self {B : Type*} [AddCommGroup B] [Module ℂ B]
    {rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B} {x : B}
    (h3 : ∀ U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ, rep (U, 1, 1) x = x)
    (h2 : ∀ V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ, rep (1, V, 1) x = x)
    (h1 : ∀ t : unitary ℂ, rep (1, 1, t) x = x) (g : GaugeGroupI) : rep g x = x

entries.name: StandardModel.isStableUnder_range_repGauge
entries.docstring:
The range of a symbol map is carried into itself by the gauge group: the symbol is
  equivariant, so a gauge transformation only moves the dual vector it is evaluated at.
entries.snippet:
lemma isStableUnder_range_repGauge {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℂ M]
    {repGauge : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B} {ρ : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI M}
    {F : Module.Dual ℂ M →ₗ[ℂ] B} (hF : ∀ g φ, repGauge g (F φ) = F (ρ.dual g φ)) :
    ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ LinearMap.range F, repGauge g y ∈ LinearMap.range F

entries.name: StandardModel.isStableUnder_range_repLorentz
entries.docstring:
The range of an underived symbol map is carried into itself by the Lorentz group: with
  no derivative slots to mix, the transformation law moves the dual vector alone.

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector
entries.docstring:
The ten fermion families and their covariant derivatives as a sector of the
  algebra `B`: gauge transformation through the dual of the species representations
  (conjugate for the barred fields), the Lorentz transformation of the towers, and
  the mass weights `3 + 2 * n`.
entries.snippet:
structure IsFermionSector (B : Type) [Ring B] [Algebra ℂ B]
    (repGauge : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B)
    (repGauge_mul : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repGauge g (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge g b₁ * repGauge g b₂)
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B)
    (repLorentz_mul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂)
    (d : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ DownSinglet →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (bard : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule DownSinglet) →ₗ[ℂ]
      B)
    (u : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ UpSinglet →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (baru : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule UpSinglet) →ₗ[ℂ]
      B)
    (Q : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ QuarkDoublet →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (barQ : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule QuarkDoublet)
      →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (L : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ LeptonDoubletV →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (barL : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule LeptonDoubletV)
      →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (e : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ LeptonSinglet →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (bare : {n : ℕ} → Fin 3 → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule LeptonSinglet)
      →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (massWeightPoly : B →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial B) : Prop where
  repGauge_d : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ DownSinglet),
    repGauge g (d i l φ) = d i l (DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.dual g φ)
  repGauge_bard : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule DownSinglet)),
    repGauge g (bard i l φ) = bard i l (DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual g φ)
  repGauge_u : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ UpSinglet),
    repGauge g (u i l φ) = u i l (UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.dual g φ)
  repGauge_baru : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule UpSinglet)),
    repGauge g (baru i l φ) = baru i l (UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual g φ)
  repGauge_Q : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ QuarkDoublet),
    repGauge g (Q i l φ) = Q i l (QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI.dual g φ)
  repGauge_barQ : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule QuarkDoublet)),
    repGauge g (barQ i l φ) = barQ i l (QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual g φ)
  repGauge_L : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ LeptonDoubletV),
    repGauge g (L i l φ) = L i l (LeptonDoubletV.repGaugeGroupI.dual g φ)
  repGauge_barL : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule LeptonDoubletV)),
    repGauge g (barL i l φ) = barL i l (LeptonDoubletV.repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual g φ)
  repGauge_e : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ LeptonSinglet),
    repGauge g (e i l φ) = e i l (LeptonSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.dual g φ)
  repGauge_bare : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
      (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule LeptonSinglet)),
    repGauge g (bare i l φ) = bare i l (LeptonSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual g φ)
  repLorentz_d : ∀ i, IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz
    DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup (d i)
  repLorentz_bard : ∀ i, IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz
    DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup.conj (bard i)
  repLorentz_u : ∀ i, IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz
    UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup (u i)
  repLorentz_baru : ∀ i, IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz

  derivatives.

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.derivSubmodule
entries.docstring:
The submodule of `B` generated by the fermion symbols carrying exactly `n`
  covariant derivatives: the join, over the families and derivative slots, of the
  ranges of the ten species' symbol maps.
entries.snippet:
@[nolint unusedArguments]
noncomputable def derivSubmodule
  (h : IsFermionSector B repGauge hrepGauge_mul repLorentz hrepLorentz_mul
      d bard u baru Q barQ L barL e bare massWeightPoly) (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ B

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.derivSubmodule_eq_span
entries.docstring: The derivative submodule as the span of the fermion symbol values.
entries.snippet:
lemma derivSubmodule_eq_span (n : ℕ) :
    h.derivSubmodule n = Submodule.span ℂ
      (⋃ (i : Fin 3) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
        Set.range (d i l) ∪ Set.range (bard i l) ∪
        Set.range (u i l) ∪ Set.range (baru i l) ∪
        Set.range (Q i l) ∪ Set.range (barQ i l) ∪
        Set.range (L i l) ∪ Set.range (barL i l) ∪
        Set.range (e i l) ∪ Set.range (bare i l))

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.anticomm_of_mem_derivSubmodule
entries.docstring:
Any two elements of the fermion derivative submodules anticommute: the pairwise
  anticommutation of the symbols extends bilinearly to the spans.

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.derivSubmodule_mul_comm
entries.docstring:
The fermion derivative submodules commute with one another as submodules: the
  sign from anticommutation is absorbed by the span.
entries.snippet:
lemma derivSubmodule_mul_comm (n m : ℕ) :
    h.derivSubmodule n * h.derivSubmodule m = h.derivSubmodule m * h.derivSubmodule n

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.rep_dComponent
entries.docstring:
The gauge transformation of a down-singlet component: the colour index mixes by the
  transposed `SU(3)` matrix of `g⁻¹`, scaled by the conjugate hypercharge factor.
entries.snippet:
lemma rep_dComponent (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGauge g (h.dComponent i l j) =
      ∑ c, (star (g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 2 * (g⁻¹).toSU3.1 j.2 c) • h.dComponent i l (j.1, c)

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight
entries.docstring:
**The gauge weight decomposition of the fermion derivative submodules**, for any
  number of covariant derivatives: the join, over families, derivative slots and the
  ten species, of the spans of the symbol components, each of pure gauge weight.

  This is an instance: its statement mentions `h`, so unification against the goal
  recovers the sector and with it all the implicit data of `IsFermionSector`.  The
  `rangeGaugeWeight*` decompositions above cannot be instances for exactly that
  reason — their statements name only the symbol maps, leaving the rest of the
  structure's parameters undetermined.
entries.snippet:
@[implicit_reducible]
noncomputable instance derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight (n : ℕ) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge (h.derivSubmodule n)

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.fermionGaugeWeights

The gauge weights carried by the fermion symbols: for each species the image of
  its value weights, negated for the unbarred species (the symbols pair with the dual
  of the value space) and taken as they are for the barred ones.
entries.snippet: def fermionGaugeWeights : Finset GaugeWeight

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_zero_eq
entries.docstring: Weight zero is the scalars: every fermion tower has positive weight.
entries.snippet: lemma massWeightSubmodule_zero_eq : h.massWeightSubmodule 0 = 1

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq
entries.docstring:
The weight recursion: an element of positive mass weight `i` is a sum of single
  fermion towers of weight `i` and of products of two elements of lower positive weights
  summing to `i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    h.massWeightSubmodule i
      = (⨆ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun k : Fin i => 3 + 2 * (k : ℕ) = i),
          h.derivSubmodule (k : ℕ))
        ⊔ (⨆ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin i × Fin i => (p.1 : ℕ) + (p.2 : ℕ) = i),
            h.massWeightSubmodule (p.1 : ℕ) * h.massWeightSubmodule (p.2 : ℕ))

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul
entries.docstring:
Removing the leftmost fermion tower: an element of positive weight `w` is a sum of
  products of a tower `∇ⁿψ` of weight `3 + 2 * n ≤ w` with an element of the remaining
  weight.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul (w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) :
    h.massWeightSubmodule w
      = ⨆ n ∈ (Finset.range (w + 1)).filter (fun n => 3 + 2 * n ≤ w),
          h.derivSubmodule n * h.massWeightSubmodule (w - (3 + 2 * n))

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq_bot
entries.docstring:
The weights `1`, `2` and `4` are empty: the tower weights `3, 5, 7, …` and their sums
  only reach `0`, `3` and every weight from `5` on.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_bot {w : ℕ} (hw : ¬ (w = 0 ∨ w = 3 ∨ 5 ≤ w)) :
    h.massWeightSubmodule w = ⊥

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_one_eq

entries.snippet: lemma massWeightSubmodule_one_eq : h.massWeightSubmodule 1 = ⊥

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_two_eq

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_three_eq
entries.docstring: Weight three is the underived fermion towers: `ψ` leaves weight zero.

    h.massWeightSubmodule 3 = h.derivSubmodule 0

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_four_eq
entries.docstring: There is nothing of weight four.
entries.snippet: lemma massWeightSubmodule_four_eq : h.massWeightSubmodule 4 = ⊥

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_five_eq
entries.docstring:
Weight five is the once-derived fermion towers: `ψ` would leave weight two, which is
  empty, and `∇ψ` leaves weight zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_five_eq :
    h.massWeightSubmodule 5 = h.derivSubmodule 1

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_six_eq
entries.docstring:
Weight six is the products of two underived fermion towers: `ψ` leaves weight three,
  which is `ψ`, and `∇ψ` would leave weight one, which is empty.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_six_eq :
    h.massWeightSubmodule 6 = h.derivSubmodule 0 * h.derivSubmodule 0

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_seven_eq
entries.docstring:
Weight seven is the twice-derived fermion towers: `ψ` and `∇ψ` would leave weights
  four and two, which are empty, and `∇∇ψ` leaves weight zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_seven_eq :
    h.massWeightSubmodule 7 = h.derivSubmodule 2

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq
entries.docstring:
Weight eight is the products of an underived and a once-derived fermion tower, the
  kinetic-term sector: `ψ` leaves `∇ψ`, `∇ψ` leaves `ψ`, and `∇∇ψ` would leave weight one,
  which is empty. The two orders agree by `derivSubmodule_mul_comm`.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq :
    h.massWeightSubmodule 8 = h.derivSubmodule 0 * h.derivSubmodule 1

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.zero_not_mem_fermionGaugeWeights
entries.docstring:
Every gauge weight carried by a fermion symbol has nonzero hypercharge: each of the
  ten species has a fixed nonzero hypercharge, independent of colour, isospin and
  family, and the barred species carry the negative of the unbarred one. So the zero
  weight never occurs.
entries.snippet: lemma zero_not_mem_fermionGaugeWeights : (0 : GaugeWeight) ∉ fermionGaugeWeights

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_zero
entries.docstring:
The weight-zero piece of the fermion derivative submodules is trivial: unlike
  the gauge sector, no single fermion symbol is a gauge singlet, since every one of the
  ten species carries a fixed nonzero hypercharge. A gauge-invariant combination needs
  at least two fermion insertions, which is why it is the mass weights six and eight,
  the products of two towers, that carry the interesting weight-zero content.
entries.snippet:
lemma derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_zero (n : ℕ) :
    (h.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight n).piece 0 = ⊥

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.piece_sup_mul
entries.docstring:
If the left factor of a product decomposition is a join `VA ⊔ VB`, its weight-`w`
  piece splits along the join.
entries.snippet:
lemma piece_sup_mul {VA VB VC : Submodule ℂ B}
    (dA : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VA) (dB : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VB)
    (dC : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VC) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup (d := dA) (d' := dB))
        (d' := dC)).piece w
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA) (d' := dC)).piece w
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dB) (d' := dC)).piece w

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.piece_mul_sup
entries.docstring:
If the right factor of a product decomposition is a join `VA ⊔ VB`, its weight-`w`
  piece splits along the join.
entries.snippet:
lemma piece_mul_sup {VA VB VC : Submodule ℂ B}
    (dC : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VC) (dA : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VA)
    (dB : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VB) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dC)
        (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup (d := dA) (d' := dB))).piece w
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dC) (d' := dA)).piece w
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dC) (d' := dB)).piece w

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mul_piece_zero_eq_bot_of_hypercharge
entries.docstring:
Two decompositions with constant, non-cancelling hypercharge across their whole
  supports have a trivial product at weight zero: a weight from one can never cancel
  a weight from the other.

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.speciesGaugeWeight
entries.docstring:
The gauge weight decomposition of one family's full set of symbols at fixed
  derivative slots, matching the recipe of `derivSubmodule` itself: the join of the
  ten species' ranges.
entries.snippet:
@[implicit_reducible]
noncomputable def speciesGaugeWeight (f : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge
      (LinearMap.range (d f l) ⊔ LinearMap.range (bard f l) ⊔
        LinearMap.range (u f l) ⊔ LinearMap.range (baru f l) ⊔
        LinearMap.range (Q f l) ⊔ LinearMap.range (barQ f l) ⊔
        LinearMap.range (L f l) ⊔ LinearMap.range (barL f l) ⊔
        LinearMap.range (e f l) ⊔ LinearMap.range (bare f l))

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero
entries.docstring:
The weight-zero piece of the product of two families' full symbol sets collapses
  to the ten conjugate pairings: every other combination of species has hypercharges
  that cannot cancel.
entries.snippet:
lemma speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero {n m : ℕ} (f f' : Fin 3) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (l' : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.speciesGaugeWeight f l)
        (d' := h.speciesGaugeWeight f' l')).piece 0
      =
      (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightD f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarD f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarD f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightD f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightU f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarU f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarU f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightU f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightQ f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightQ f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightL f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarL f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarL f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightL f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightE f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarE f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarE f l)
            (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightE f' l')).piece 0

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix_piece_zero
entries.docstring:
The weight-zero piece at mass weight six, written out in the mass terms
  themselves: the join, over pairs of families, of the ten ways to pair each
  species with its own conjugate. Every other pairing of species has hypercharges
  that cannot cancel, by `speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero`.

lemma massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix_piece_zero :
    (h.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix).piece 0
      = ⨆ (f : Fin 3) (f' : Fin 3),
        (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightD f ![])
              (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarD f' ![])).piece 0
          ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarD f ![])
              (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightD f' ![])).piece 0
          ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightU f ![])
              (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarU f' ![])).piece 0
          ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarU f ![])
              (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightU f' ![])).piece 0

          ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f ![])
              (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightQ f' ![])).piece 0
          ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightL f ![])
              (d' := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarL f' ![])).piece 0
          ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightBarL f ![])

          ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := h.rangeGaugeWeightE f ![])

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mem_of_invariant_of_mem_derivSubmodule_sup
entries.docstring:
A gauge-invariant element of `h.derivSubmodule n ⊔ S`, for any submodule `S` closed under
  the gauge action, already lies in `S`. The fermionic part carries no gauge singlet, since
  each of the ten species has a fixed nonzero hypercharge, so it cannot survive; what is left
  is the part in `S`. Compare `derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_zero`.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_of_invariant_of_mem_derivSubmodule_sup {n : ℕ} {S : Submodule ℂ B}
    (hS : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (y : B), y ∈ S → repGauge g y ∈ S)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ h.derivSubmodule n ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x) : x ∈ S

lemma mem_of_mem_massWeightSubmoduleOne_sup {S : Submodule ℂ B}

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.sum_deriv_one
entries.docstring: A sum over the assignments of one derivative direction is a single sum.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_deriv_one {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : (Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ p : Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f p = ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f ![x]

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.repLorentz_symbol_deriv_one
entries.docstring:
The Lorentz transformation of a symbol with one covariant derivative: the derivative
  slot moves by the columns of the Lorentz matrix and the value index by the
  contragredient action.
entries.snippet:
lemma repLorentz_symbol_deriv_one {V : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V}
    {X : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hX : IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz rep X) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repLorentz Λ (X ![μ] φ)
      = ∑ ν, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • X ![ν] (rep.dual Λ φ)

entries.docstring:
A product of a component with a fundamental colour index and one with an
  anti-fundamental colour index carries one colour index of each kind.
entries.snippet:
lemma isSU3FundamentalAntiFundamental_mul
    (hmul : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repGauge g (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge g b₁ * repGauge g b₂)
    {A C : Fin 3 → B}
    (hA : ∀ (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (c : Fin 3),
      repGauge ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (A c) = ∑ a, U.1 a c • A a)
    (hC : ∀ (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (c : Fin 3),
      repGauge ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (C c) = ∑ a, conj (U.1 a c) • C a) :
    IsSU3FundamentalAntiFundamental B repGauge (fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 3 => A (l 0) * C (l 1))

    (hmul : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repGauge g (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge g b₁ * repGauge g b₂)
    {A C : Fin 2 → B}
    (hA : ∀ (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (w : Fin 2),
      repGauge ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (A w) = ∑ a, conj (V.1 a w) • A a)
    (hC : ∀ (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (w : Fin 2),
      repGauge ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (C w) = ∑ a, V.1 a w • C a) :
    IsSU2FundamentalAntiFundamental B repGauge (fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 2 => A (l 1) * C (l 0))

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.repGauge_mul_fixed
entries.docstring:
A product of two components that a gauge transformation fixes is fixed by it: the
  form in which a block whose symbols carry no colour, or no isospin, supplies the
  corresponding stage.
entries.snippet:
lemma repGauge_mul_fixed
    (hmul : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repGauge g (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge g b₁ * repGauge g b₂)
    {g : GaugeGroupI} {a c : B} (ha : repGauge g a = a) (hc : repGauge g c = c) :
    repGauge g (a * c) = a * c

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.repGauge_mul_smul_fixed
entries.docstring:
A product of two components that a gauge transformation scales by reciprocal scalars
  is fixed by it: the form in which the hypercharges of a species and its conjugate
  cancel.
entries.snippet:
lemma repGauge_mul_smul_fixed
    (hmul : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repGauge g (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge g b₁ * repGauge g b₂)
    {g : GaugeGroupI} {z z' : ℂ} {a c : B} (hz : z * z' = 1)
    (ha : repGauge g a = z • a) (hc : repGauge g c = z' • c) :
    repGauge g (a * c) = a * c

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.isVectorDualLeftRightWeyl_sum
entries.docstring:
A finite sum of families carrying one four-vector index and a pair of dual
  opposite-chirality Weyl indices is such a family again: the colour and isospin
  contractions are Lorentz spectators.

lemma isVectorDualLeftRightWeyl_sum {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    {T : ι → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B}
    (hT : ∀ i, IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz (ofDualVectorComponents (T i))) :
    IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz (ofDualVectorComponents fun p => ∑ i, T i p)

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.unitary_mul_star_coe
entries.docstring:
A unitary scalar times its conjugate is one, in the order the hypercharge cancellation
  of a species against its conjugate needs.
entries.snippet: lemma unitary_mul_star_coe (t : unitary ℂ) : (t : ℂ) * star (t : ℂ) = 1

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.unitary_star_mul_coe
entries.docstring: The conjugate of a unitary scalar times itself is one.
entries.snippet: lemma unitary_star_mul_coe (t : unitary ℂ) : star (t : ℂ) * (t : ℂ) = 1

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.KineticBlock
entries.docstring:
One kinetic block of the fermion sector, together with the three classifications its
  indices admit. The block is indexed by the derivative direction, the pair of spinor
  indices in the order `(undotted, dotted)`, the pair of colour indices and the pair of
  isospin indices, each pair in the order `(fundamental, anti-fundamental)`.
entries.snippet:
structure KineticBlock where
  blk : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Fin 2 → Fin 2 → B
  colourStep : ∀ (q : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l : Fin 2 × Fin 2) (w w' : Fin 2),
    InvariantReductionToSpan (fun U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ => repGauge (U, 1, 1))
      (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun n : Fin 2 → Fin 3 => blk q l (n 0) (n 1) w w'))
  colourStep_mem : ∀ q l w w', (colourStep q l w w').spanningVector
    ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun n : Fin 2 → Fin 3 => blk q l (n 0) (n 1) w w')
  isospinStep : ∀ (q : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l : Fin 2 × Fin 2),
    InvariantReductionToSpan (fun V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ => repGauge (1, V, 1))
      (Submodule.span ℂ
        (Set.range fun n : Fin 2 → Fin 2 => (colourStep q l (n 0) (n 1)).spanningVector))
  isospinStep_mem : ∀ q l, (isospinStep q l).spanningVector
    ∈ Submodule.span ℂ
      (Set.range fun n : Fin 2 → Fin 2 => (colourStep q l (n 0) (n 1)).spanningVector)
  lorentzStep : InvariantReductionToSpan (fun Λ : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz Λ)
    (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun p : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 =>
      (isospinStep p.1 p.2).spanningVector))
  lorentzStep_mem : lorentzStep.spanningVector
    ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun p : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 =>
      (isospinStep p.1 p.2).spanningVector)
  hyper : ∀ (t : unitary ℂ) q l c c' w w',
    repGauge ((1, 1, t) : GaugeGroupI) (blk q l c c' w w') = blk q l c c' w w'

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.KineticBlock.kineticTerm
entries.docstring:
The kinetic term of a block: the conjugate Pauli contraction of its doubly contracted
  form, which is `ψ̄ σ̄^μ ∂_μ ψ` with the colour and isospin indices already joined.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def kineticTerm : B

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.KineticBlock.blockSpan
entries.docstring:

entries.snippet: noncomputable def blockSpan : Submodule ℂ B

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.KineticBlock.reducesInvariantsTo
entries.docstring: The three stages in sequence: the block span reduces to the span of the kinetic term.
entries.snippet:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) K.blockSpan (ℂ ∙ K.kineticTerm)

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.KineticBlock.kineticTerm_mem

  contraction lies in the span of the objects of the stage before it.

lemma kineticTerm_mem {V : Submodule ℂ B}

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.KineticBlock.repGauge_su3_kineticTerm
entries.docstring:
The kinetic term is fixed by the colour factor: the colour contractions are, and every
  later stage stays inside their span.
entries.snippet:
lemma repGauge_su3_kineticTerm (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    repGauge ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) K.kineticTerm = K.kineticTerm

entries.snippet:
lemma repGauge_u1_kineticTerm (t : unitary ℂ) :

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.KineticBlock.repGauge_kineticTerm
entries.docstring:

  colour, isospin and hypercharge parts, and each fixes it.
entries.snippet: lemma repGauge_kineticTerm (g : GaugeGroupI) : repGauge g K.kineticTerm = K.kineticTerm

  vector dual left-right Weyl family.
entries.snippet:

    repLorentz Λ K.kineticTerm = K.kineticTerm

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.isStableUnder_iSup_range_deriv_one
entries.docstring:
The join, over the derivative direction, of the ranges of a once-derived symbol map is
  carried into itself by the Lorentz group: a Lorentz transformation mixes the derivative
  slot into the other directions and moves the covector, and both stay inside the join.

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.isStableUnder_range_underived
entries.docstring: The range of an underived symbol map is carried into itself by both groups.
entries.snippet:
lemma isStableUnder_range_underived {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℂ M]
    {ρG : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI M} {ρL : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) M}
    {F : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ M →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hG : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ M),
      repGauge g (F (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) φ)
        = F (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (ρG.dual g φ))
    (hL : IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz ρL F) :
    IsStableUnder (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz)
      (LinearMap.range (F (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)))

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.isStableUnder_iSup_range_derived
entries.docstring:
The join, over the derivative direction, of the ranges of a once-derived symbol map is
  carried into itself by both groups.
entries.snippet:
lemma isStableUnder_iSup_range_derived {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℂ M]
    {ρG : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI M} {ρL : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) M}
    {F : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ M →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hG : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ M),
      repGauge g (F ![μ] φ) = F ![μ] (ρG.dual g φ))
    (hL : IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz ρL F) :
    IsStableUnder (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz)
      (⨆ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, LinearMap.range (F ![μ]))

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.reducesInvariantsTo_kineticSpan
entries.docstring:
The fermion sector at mass weight eight reduces, for the gauge and Lorentz groups

  lies in the ten block submodules, and those reduce to the kinetic terms.

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
entries.docstring:
The classification of mass weight eight as an equivalence, in the shape of the
  sibling sectors: an element of `massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S` is fixed by both groups
  exactly when it is a combination of the kinetic terms up to a remainder in `S` fixed by
  both groups.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ h.kineticSpan

A two-element family `X` of elements of `B` carries a dual undotted spinor index: it

entries.docstring:
A two-element family `Y` of elements of `B` carries a dual dotted spinor index: it

  conjugate of the undotted law.
entries.snippet: def IsDualRightWeyl (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B) (Y : Fin 2 → B) : Prop

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.IsVectorDualLeftWeyl
entries.docstring:
A family `X` carrying one four-vector index and one dual undotted spinor index: the
  once-derived form of `IsDualLeftWeyl`, the derivative slot moving by the columns of the
  Lorentz matrix. Only the value index of a fermion symbol is dualised, so the derivative
  slot keeps the plain Lorentz law.
entries.snippet:
def IsVectorDualLeftWeyl (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B)
    (X : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 → B) : Prop

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.IsVectorDualRightWeyl
entries.docstring:
A family `Y` carrying one four-vector index and one dual dotted spinor index: the
  once-derived form of `IsDualRightWeyl`.
entries.snippet:
def IsVectorDualRightWeyl (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B)
    (Y : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 → B) : Prop

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.isDualLeftRightWeyl_mul
entries.docstring: An undotted family times a dotted one is a dual left-right Weyl family.
entries.snippet:
lemma isDualLeftRightWeyl_mul {X Y : Fin 2 → B} (hX : IsDualLeftWeyl repLorentz X)
    (hY : IsDualRightWeyl repLorentz Y) :
    IsDualLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz
      (ofPairComponents (k := .downL) (k' := .downR) fun a b => X a * Y b)

A dotted family times an undotted one is a dual left-right Weyl family, the two
  spinor slots exchanged.

lemma isDualLeftRightWeyl_mul_swap {X Y : Fin 2 → B} (hX : IsDualRightWeyl repLorentz X)
    (hY : IsDualLeftWeyl repLorentz Y) :
    IsDualLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz
      (ofPairComponents (k := .downL) (k' := .downR) fun a b => X b * Y a)

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.isVectorDualLeftRightWeyl_mul
entries.docstring:
An undotted family times a once-derived dotted one is a vector dual left-right Weyl
  family: the derivative supplies the four-vector index.

lemma isVectorDualLeftRightWeyl_mul {X : Fin 2 → B} {Y : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 → B}
    (hX : IsDualLeftWeyl repLorentz X) (hY : IsVectorDualRightWeyl repLorentz Y) :
    IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz

A dotted family times a once-derived undotted one is a vector dual left-right Weyl

    (hX : IsDualRightWeyl repLorentz X) (hY : IsVectorDualLeftWeyl repLorentz Y) :

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span
entries.docstring:
A finite join of the spans of dual left-right Weyl families carries no Lorentz
  invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule: such a family has no invariant, so each span
  reduces to `⊥`, and `ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup` combines the reductions. A Lorentz
  invariant of the join together with `S` lies in `S`.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span {ι : Type} [DecidableEq ι]
    {T : ι → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B} (hT : ∀ i, IsDualLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz
      (ofPairComponents (k := .downL) (k' := .downR) fun a b => T i (a, b)))
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (s : Finset ι)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ (⨆ i ∈ s, ⨆ l, ℂ ∙ T i l) ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span
entries.docstring:
The version of `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span` joining over a
  whole finite index type.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    [DecidableEq ι] {T : ι → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B}
    (hT : ∀ i, IsDualLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz
      (ofPairComponents (k := .downL) (k' := .downR) fun a b => T i (a, b))) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ (⨆ i, ⨆ l, ℂ ∙ T i l) ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

inductive RightIdx
  | d (f : Fin 3) (c : Fin 3)
  | u (f : Fin 3) (c : Fin 3)
  | barQ (f : Fin 3) (c : Fin 3) (s : Fin 2)
  | barL (f : Fin 3) (s : Fin 2)
  | e (f : Fin 3)
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

      hrepLorentz_mul d bard u baru Q barQ L barL e bare massWeightPoly)

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mul_le_iSup_span_pair
entries.docstring:
If `V` lies in the join of the lines through an undotted family and `W` in the join
  for a dotted one, the product lies in the join of the spans of the pair families.
entries.snippet:
lemma mul_le_iSup_span_pair {ι κ : Type} {X : ι → Fin 2 → B} {Y : κ → Fin 2 → B}
    {V W : Submodule ℂ B} (hV : V ≤ ⨆ (i : ι) (a : Fin 2), ℂ ∙ X i a)
    (hW : W ≤ ⨆ (j : κ) (a : Fin 2), ℂ ∙ Y j a) :
    V * W ≤ ⨆ (p : ι × κ) (l : Fin 2 × Fin 2), ℂ ∙ (X p.1 l.1 * Y p.2 l.2)

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mul_le_iSup_span_pair_swap
entries.docstring:
The mirror of `mul_le_iSup_span_pair` with the two spinor slots exchanged, for a
  product whose left factor is the dotted one.
entries.snippet:
lemma mul_le_iSup_span_pair_swap {ι κ : Type} {X : ι → Fin 2 → B} {Y : κ → Fin 2 → B}
    {V W : Submodule ℂ B} (hV : V ≤ ⨆ (i : ι) (a : Fin 2), ℂ ∙ X i a)
    (hW : W ≤ ⨆ (j : κ) (a : Fin 2), ℂ ∙ Y j a) :
    V * W ≤ ⨆ (p : ι × κ) (l : Fin 2 × Fin 2), ℂ ∙ (X p.1 l.2 * Y p.2 l.1)

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.sixFamily
entries.docstring:
The mass-weight six families: a product of two underived components of opposite
  chirality, in either order.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def sixFamily (h : IsFermionSector B repGauge hrepGauge_mul repLorentz
      hrepLorentz_mul d bard u baru Q barQ L barL e bare massWeightPoly) :
    (LeftIdx × RightIdx) ⊕ (RightIdx × LeftIdx) → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B
  | .inl p => fun l => h.leftComp ![] p.1 l.1 * h.rightComp ![] p.2 l.2
  | .inr p => fun l => h.rightComp ![] p.1 l.2 * h.leftComp ![] p.2 l.1

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix_piece_zero_le
entries.docstring:
The weight-zero piece at mass weight six lies in the span of the mass-weight six
  families: each of the ten conjugate pairings is a product of an undotted range with a
  dotted one, in one order or the other.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix_piece_zero_le :
    (h.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix).piece 0 ≤ h.sixSpan

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mem_of_invariant_of_mem_massWeightSubmoduleSix_sup
entries.docstring:
Mass weight six carries no invariant modulo a stable submodule: there is no Dirac
  mass term. A gauge- and Lorentz-invariant element of `massWeightSubmodule 6 ⊔ S` lies
  in `S`, gauge invariance cutting the hundred pairings of two fermion symbols down to
  the ten conjugate ones and Lorentz invariance killing each of those, its two spinor
  indices being of opposite chirality.

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mem_of_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup
entries.docstring:
Between mass weight zero and mass weight eight the fermion sector carries no
  invariant: an element of `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` for `0 < w < 8` fixed by both
  groups lies in `S`. Weights one, two and four are trivial, weights three, five and
  seven carry no gauge singlet, and weight six is the missing Dirac mass term.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_of_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup (w : ℕ) (hw0 : 0 < w)
    (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S)
    (hG : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
entries.docstring:
The classification below mass weight eight as an equivalence, in the shape of
  `mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`: an element of
  `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` for `0 < w < 8` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is
  itself an element of `S` fixed by both groups. The span of invariants that the weight
  eight statement leaves over is here the trivial one, so `x - y` lies in it exactly when
  `x = y`.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x = y

entries.name: StandardModel.IsFermionSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
entries.docstring:
The same classification without the existential: below mass weight eight an element
  of `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of `S` fixed by both
  groups, and conversely.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)

entries.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector
entries.docstring:
The field strength and its covariant derivatives as a sector of the algebra `B`:
  gauge transformation through the adjoint action, the Lorentz transformation of the
  towers with two explicit covector indices, and the mass weights `2 * (2 + n)`.
entries.snippet:
structure IsGaugeSector (B : Type) [Ring B] [Algebra ℂ B]
    (repGauge : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B)
    (repGauge_mul : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repGauge g (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge g b₁ * repGauge g b₂)
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B)
    (repLorentz_mul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂)
    (F : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) →
      Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (massWeightPoly : B →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial B) : Prop where
  repGauge_F : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra),
    repGauge g (F l μ ν φ) = F l μ ν ((GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ)
  repLorentz_F : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra),
    repLorentz Λ (F l μ ν φ) =
      ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
        (∏ i, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 (p i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) •
      ∑ a, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
      ∑ b, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 b ν : ℝ) : ℂ) • F p a b φ
  massWeight_F : ∀ {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) φ,
    massWeightPoly (F l μ ν φ) = Polynomial.monomial (2 * (2 + n)) (F l μ ν φ)
  F_comm_F : ∀ {n m : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) (l' : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (μ' ν' : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (ψ' : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra),
    Commute (F l μ ν ψ) (F l' μ' ν' ψ')
  F_antisymm : ∀ {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra),
    F l ν μ φ = - F l μ ν φ

entries.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.gaugeAlgebra
entries.docstring: The algebra generated by the field strength and all its covariant derivatives.
entries.snippet:
@[nolint unusedArguments]
def gaugeAlgebra (_h : IsGaugeSector B repGauge hrepGauge_mul repLorentz hrepLorentz_mul
    F massWeightPoly) : Subalgebra ℂ B

entries.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.gluonField
entries.docstring:
The gluon contribution to the field strength (and its covariant derivatives): the
  field-strength symbol evaluated on the coordinate dual to the `a`-th Gell-Mann
  direction of the standard basis of the gauge algebra, i.e. the `su(3)` factor.

@[nolint unusedArguments]
noncomputable def gluonField (h : IsGaugeSector B repGauge hrepGauge_mul repLorentz hrepLorentz_mul
      F massWeightPoly) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (a : Fin 8) : B

entries.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.wField
entries.docstring:
The `W`-boson contribution to the field strength (and its covariant derivatives):
  the field-strength symbol evaluated on the coordinate dual to the `i`-th Pauli
  direction of the standard basis of the gauge algebra, i.e. the `su(2)` factor.
entries.snippet:
@[nolint unusedArguments]
noncomputable def wField (h : IsGaugeSector B repGauge hrepGauge_mul repLorentz hrepLorentz_mul
      F massWeightPoly) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (i : Fin 3) : B
