entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule
entries.docstring:
All elements of the field algebra of mass weight exactly `n`: the intersection of the
  algebra generated by the bare symbols with the part on which `massWeightPoly` is the
  monomial `X ^ n`. This is the jet-form counterpart of
  `CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmodule
    (h : AlgebraRealization B repJet repLorentz massWeightPoly) (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ B

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightPoly_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
entries.docstring:
On the mass-weight submodule of weight `n` the map `massWeightPoly` is the monomial
  `X ^ n`, which is what the kernel condition says.

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule_le_fieldAlgebra
entries.docstring: Each graded piece lies in the field algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_le_fieldAlgebra (w : ℕ) :
    h.massWeightSubmodule w ≤ h.fieldAlgebra.toSubmodule

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE
entries.docstring:
The elements of the field algebra of mass weight at most `w`: the join of the
  mass-weight submodules of weight `0` through `w`. This is where a Lagrangian lives, a
  sum of terms of every mass dimension up to a cut-off rather than of a single one.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ B

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE
entries.docstring: Each graded piece of weight at most `w` sits inside the filtration at `w`.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE {k w : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ w) :
    h.massWeightSubmodule k ≤ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE
entries.docstring: An element of a graded piece of weight at most `w` lies in the filtration at `w`.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE {k w : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ w) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule k) : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE_le
entries.docstring:
A submodule containing every graded piece of weight at most `w` contains the
  filtration at `w`: the join is taken over exactly those pieces.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_le {w : ℕ} {V : Submodule ℂ B}
    (hV : ∀ k ≤ w, h.massWeightSubmodule k ≤ V) : h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ≤ V

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE_mono
entries.docstring: The filtration grows with the bound.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_mono {w w' : ℕ} (hw : w ≤ w') :
    h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ≤ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w'

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE_le_fieldAlgebra
entries.docstring: The filtration lies in the field algebra, being a join of pieces that do.
entries.snippet:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_le_fieldAlgebra (w : ℕ) :
    h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ≤ h.fieldAlgebra.toSubmodule

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covAlgebra_le_fieldAlgebra
entries.docstring:
The covariant subalgebra sits inside the field algebra: the field-strength tower is a
  polynomial in the gauge-field symbols, and the matter towers generate the same algebra
  as the bare matter symbols.
entries.snippet: lemma covAlgebra_le_fieldAlgebra : h.covAlgebra ≤ h.fieldAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covAlgebra_toSubmodule_le_fieldAlgebra
entries.docstring: The covariant subalgebra as a submodule sits inside the field algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma covAlgebra_toSubmodule_le_fieldAlgebra :
    h.covAlgebra.toSubmodule ≤ h.fieldAlgebra.toSubmodule

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.toCovAlgebraRealization_fieldAlgebra
entries.docstring:
The field algebra of the covariant form of the theory is the covariant subalgebra:
  the two are generated by the same set of covariant towers.
entries.snippet:
lemma toCovAlgebraRealization_fieldAlgebra :
    h.toCovAlgebraRealization.fieldAlgebra = h.covAlgebra

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covMassWeightSubmodule_eq
entries.docstring:
A covariant weight piece is a weight piece that happens to be covariant: the two
  submodules cut the same kernel of `massWeightPoly` out of the two algebras, and one
  algebra sits inside the other.
entries.snippet:
lemma covMassWeightSubmodule_eq (w : ℕ) :
    h.toCovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule w
      = h.massWeightSubmodule w ⊓ h.covAlgebra.toSubmodule

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covMassWeightSubmodule_le
entries.docstring: A covariant weight piece lies in the weight piece of the field algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma covMassWeightSubmodule_le (w : ℕ) :
    h.toCovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule w ≤ h.massWeightSubmodule w

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covMassWeightSubmoduleLE_le
entries.docstring: The covariant filtration lies in the filtration of the field algebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma covMassWeightSubmoduleLE_le (w : ℕ) :
    h.toCovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ≤ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covMassWeightSubmoduleLE_le_covAlgebra
entries.docstring: The covariant filtration lies in the covariant subalgebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma covMassWeightSubmoduleLE_le_covAlgebra (w : ℕ) :
    h.toCovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ≤ h.covAlgebra.toSubmodule

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.eq_sum_coeff_massWeightPoly
entries.docstring:
The weight decomposition of an element of the filtration is canonical: an element of
  mass weight at most `w` is the sum of the coefficients of `X ^ 0, …, X ^ w` in its image
  under `massWeightPoly`. Both sides are linear in the element, so it is enough to check
  it on a single graded piece, where `massWeightPoly` is a monomial.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_sum_coeff_massWeightPoly {w : ℕ} {x : B} (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w) :
    x = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (w + 1), (massWeightPoly x).coeff k

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.mem_covMassWeightSubmoduleLE
entries.docstring:
A covariant element of the filtration lies in the covariant filtration. Its weight
  components are the coefficients of `massWeightPoly`, and reading off a coefficient does
  not leave the covariant algebra: on the covariant algebra the coefficient of `X ^ k`
  lands in the span of the covariant words of weight `k`.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_covMassWeightSubmoduleLE {w : ℕ} {x : B} (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w)
    (hcov : x ∈ h.covAlgebra) : x ∈ h.toCovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covStandardModelSpanLE_le_covAlgebra
entries.docstring: The span of the covariant filtration lies in the covariant subalgebra.
entries.snippet:
lemma covStandardModelSpanLE_le_covAlgebra (w : ℕ) :
    h.toCovAlgebraRealization.standardModelSpanLE w ≤ h.covAlgebra.toSubmodule

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.forall_repJet_of_mem_covStandardModelSpanLE
entries.docstring:
Every element of the span of the covariant filtration is invariant under the whole jet
  gauge group, not just the global one: it is covariant and globally invariant, which is
  what the reduction theorem asks for.

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff
entries.docstring:
The classification of the Standard Model up to mass dimension four in its jet form: an
  element of `massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S`, for `S` a covariant submodule stable under the
  jet gauge group and the Lorentz group, is fixed by both groups exactly when it lies in
  the span of the covariant filtration up to a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups.

  The hypothesis `hScov` has no counterpart in the covariant statement. It is what repairs
  a decomposition `x = v + s`: the reduction puts `x` in the covariant algebra, and `v` is
  then covariant only because `s` is. Jet-gauge stability of `S` gives global stability for
  free, `repGlobal` being `repJet` at a constant jet.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repJet U y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz Λ y ∈ S)
    (hScov : S ≤ h.covAlgebra.toSubmodule) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, repJet U x = x)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz Λ x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, repJet U y = y)
          ∧ (∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz Λ y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ h.toCovAlgebraRealization.standardModelSpanLE 8

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian
entries.docstring:
The invariant content of the Standard Model up to mass dimension four, in its jet
  form. An element of `massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S`, for `S` a covariant submodule stable
  under both groups, is fixed by the jet gauge group and the Lorentz group exactly when it
  is a combination of
  the constant term, of mass dimension zero,
  the Higgs mass term `H† H`, of mass dimension two (`HiggsAlgebraCovRealization.dotSpan`),
  and the dimension-four span — the four Lorentz contractions of the three `F·F` trace
  families and of the twice-derived hypercharge field strength, among them the gauge
  kinetic and theta terms (`IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan`), the Higgs
  kinetic term, its quartic potential and its two box terms
  (`HiggsAlgebraCovRealization.lorentzContractionEightSpan`), the kinetic terms of the ten fermion
  species over the nine family pairs (`IsFermionSector.kineticSpan`), and the six Yukawa
  couplings over the nine family pairs (`yukawaSpan`) —
  up to a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups, and nothing else.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repJet U y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz Λ y ∈ S)
    (hScov : S ≤ h.covAlgebra.toSubmodule) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, repJet U x = x)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz Λ x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, repJet U y = y)
          ∧ (∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz Λ y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ (1 : Submodule ℂ B) ⊔ (h.toCovAlgebraRealization.isHiggsSector.dotSpan 0 0
              ⊔ (h.toCovAlgebraRealization.isGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
                    ⊔ h.toCovAlgebraRealization.isHiggsSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
                  ⊔ (h.toCovAlgebraRealization.isFermionSector.kineticSpan
                    ⊔ h.toCovAlgebraRealization.yukawaSpan)))

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_and_invariant_iff
entries.docstring:
The invariants of the filtration, with nothing set aside: an element of mass weight at
  most eight is fixed by the jet gauge group and the Lorentz group exactly when it lies in
  the span of the covariant filtration.  This is
  `mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff` at `S = ⊥`, where the stability
  and covariance hypotheses hold vacuously.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_and_invariant_iff (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ∧ (∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, repJet U x = x)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz Λ x = x)
      ↔ x ∈ h.toCovAlgebraRealization.standardModelSpanLE 8

entries.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian
entries.docstring:
The invariant content of the Standard Model up to mass dimension four, with nothing set
  aside: an element of mass weight at most eight is fixed by the jet gauge group and the
  Lorentz group exactly when it is a combination of the constant term, the Higgs mass term
  `H† H`, and the Standard-Model Lagrangian of mass dimension four, and nothing else.
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ∧ (∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, repJet U x = x)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz Λ x = x)
      ↔ x ∈ (1 : Submodule ℂ B) ⊔ (h.toCovAlgebraRealization.isHiggsSector.dotSpan 0 0
          ⊔ (h.toCovAlgebraRealization.isGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
                ⊔ h.toCovAlgebraRealization.isHiggsSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
              ⊔ (h.toCovAlgebraRealization.isFermionSector.kineticSpan
                ⊔ h.toCovAlgebraRealization.yukawaSpan)))

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.preGNSAut
entries.docstring: The map `[a] ↦ [σ a]` on the pre-Hilbert space of a state.

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofPreGNS_preGNSAut
entries.snippet:
lemma ofPreGNS_preGNSAut (x : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS) :
    ω.toPositiveLinearMap.ofPreGNS (preGNSAut ω σ x) = σ (ω.toPositiveLinearMap.ofPreGNS x)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.inner_preGNSAut

entries.snippet:
lemma inner_preGNSAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x y : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS) :
    ⟪preGNSAut ω σ x, preGNSAut ω σ y⟫_ℂ = ⟪x, y⟫_ℂ

lemma norm_preGNSAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS) :
    ‖preGNSAut ω σ x‖ = ‖x‖

entries.snippet:
def preGNSAutCLM (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) :

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsAut
entries.docstring: The unitary operator on the GNS space implementing a symmetry that preserves the state.
entries.snippet: def gnsAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS

    star (gnsAut (hα g)) * gnsAut (hα g) = 1

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.star_gnsAut
entries.snippet: lemma star_gnsAut (g : Multiplicative G) : star (gnsAut (hα g)) = gnsAut (hα g⁻¹)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary
entries.docstring:
**Translations of an invariant state are unitarily implemented**: the unitary operator on the
GNS space implementing the symmetry `α g`.
entries.snippet: def gnsUnitary (g : Multiplicative G) : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitaryRep
entries.docstring: **The unitary representation of a symmetry group on the GNS space of an invariant state.**
entries.snippet: def gnsUnitaryRep : Multiplicative G →* unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS) where

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary_cyclicVector
entries.docstring: The implementing unitary fixes the cyclic vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma gnsUnitary_cyclicVector (g : Multiplicative G) :
    ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS) ω.gnsCyclicVector =
      ω.gnsCyclicVector

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary_gnsRep_cyclicVector
entries.docstring: The implementing unitary carries `π(a) Ω` to `π(α_g a) Ω`.
entries.snippet:
lemma gnsUnitary_gnsRep_cyclicVector (g : Multiplicative G) (a : A) :
    ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)
        (ω.gnsRep a ω.gnsCyclicVector) = ω.gnsRep (α g a) ω.gnsCyclicVector

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary_comp_gnsRep
entries.docstring:
The implementing unitaries intertwine the GNS representation with the symmetry:
`U_g π(a) = π(α_g a) U_g`.
entries.snippet:
lemma gnsUnitary_comp_gnsRep (g : Multiplicative G) (a : A) :
    ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS) * ω.gnsRep a =
      ω.gnsRep (α g a) * ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.inner_gnsRep_cyclicVector_gnsUnitary
entries.docstring:
The matrix coefficients of the GNS vectors `π(a) Ω` are the correlation functions of the
state: `⟪π(a) Ω, U_g π(a) Ω⟫ = ω(a⋆ α_g(a))`.
entries.snippet:
lemma inner_gnsRep_cyclicVector_gnsUnitary (g : Multiplicative G) (a : A) :
    ⟪ω.gnsRep a ω.gnsCyclicVector,
      ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)
        (ω.gnsRep a ω.gnsCyclicVector)⟫_ℂ = ω (star a * α g a)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsStructureFactor
entries.docstring:
The momentum distribution of the excitation `π(a) Ω` created by the observable `a` from the
invariant state: the distribution of the vector `π(a) Ω` over the characters of the symmetry
group.
entries.snippet: def gnsStructureFactor (a : A) : Measure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.«instance@ad22a426»
entries.snippet: instance (a : A) : IsFiniteMeasure (gnsStructureFactor hα a)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.integral_gnsStructureFactor
entries.docstring:
**The Fourier transform of the momentum distribution is the correlation function**:
`∫ χ(g) dμ_a(χ) = ω(a⋆ α_g(a))`.
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_gnsStructureFactor (a : A) (g : Multiplicative G) :
    ∫ χ, ((χ g : Circle) : ℂ) ∂gnsStructureFactor hα a = ω (star a * α g a)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsStructureFactor_univ
entries.docstring: The total momentum weight of the excitation `π(a) Ω` is `ω(a⋆ a)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma gnsStructureFactor_univ (a : A) :
    (gnsStructureFactor hα a).real Set.univ = (ω (star a * a)).re

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsCyclicVector_mem_sector
entries.docstring:
The cyclic vector of an invariant state has momentum zero: its spectral measure is carried
by the trivial character.
entries.snippet:
lemma gnsCyclicVector_mem_sector :
    ω.gnsCyclicVector ∈ ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.sector (toEnd (gnsUnitaryRep hα))
      (fun g => (((1 : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) g : Circle) : ℂ))

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.projection_one_gnsCyclicVector
entries.docstring:
**The vacuum has momentum zero.** For a countable symmetry group the spectral projection of
the trivial character fixes the cyclic vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma projection_one_gnsCyclicVector [Countable G] :
    projection (gnsUnitaryRep hα) {(1 : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))} ω.gnsCyclicVector =
      ω.gnsCyclicVector

entries.name: Matrix.PosDef.normalizer
entries.docstring:
A matrix `T` with `T A Tᴴ = 1` for a positive definite `A`: the inverse square roots of the
eigenvalues of `A` times the adjoint of its eigenvector unitary.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def PosDef.normalizer {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef) : Matrix n n ℂ

entries.name: Matrix.PosDef.normalizer_mul_mul_conjTranspose
entries.snippet:
lemma PosDef.normalizer_mul_mul_conjTranspose {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef) :
    hA.normalizer * A * hA.normalizerᴴ = 1

entries.name: Matrix.IsHermitian.abs_eigenvalues_le_one
entries.docstring:
The eigenvalues of a hermitian `K` with `1 − K` and `1 + K` positive semidefinite lie in
`[−1, 1]`.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsHermitian.abs_eigenvalues_le_one {K : Matrix n n ℂ} (hK : K.IsHermitian)
    (hm : (1 - K).PosSemidef) (hp : (1 + K).PosSemidef) (i : n) : |hK.eigenvalues i| ≤ 1

entries.name: Matrix.PosDef.norm_det_le_re_det
entries.docstring:
If `A` is positive definite, `B` hermitian and `A − B`, `A + B` positive semidefinite, then
`‖det B‖ ≤ re (det A)`: conjugating by the normalizer of `A` puts `B` between `−1` and `1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma PosDef.norm_det_le_re_det {A B : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.IsHermitian)
    (h₁ : (A - B).PosSemidef) (h₂ : (A + B).PosSemidef) : ‖B.det‖ ≤ (A.det).re

entries.name: Matrix.map_ofReal_add_smul_one
entries.snippet:
lemma map_ofReal_add_smul_one (S : Matrix n n ℝ) (ε : ℝ) :
    (S + ε • 1).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) = S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) + (ε : ℂ) • 1

entries.name: Matrix.abs_det_le_det_of_posSemidef
entries.docstring:
For real `S` and `W`, if `S − iW` and `S + iW` are positive semidefinite then
`|det W| ≤ det S`.
entries.snippet:
lemma abs_det_le_det_of_posSemidef {S W : Matrix n n ℝ}
    (h₁ : (S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) - Complex.I • W.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)).PosSemidef)
    (h₂ : (S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) + Complex.I • W.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)).PosSemidef) :
    |W.det| ≤ S.det

entries.name: Matrix.IsHermitian.mul_self_eq_one
entries.docstring: A hermitian `K` with eigenvalues in `[−1, 1]` and `‖det K‖ = 1` squares to the identity.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsHermitian.mul_self_eq_one {K : Matrix n n ℂ} (hK : K.IsHermitian)
    (hle : ∀ i, |hK.eigenvalues i| ≤ 1) (h1 : ‖K.det‖ = 1) : K * K = 1

entries.name: Matrix.PosDef.inv_eq_conjTranspose_normalizer_mul
entries.docstring: The normalizer of a positive definite `A` is invertible, and `A⁻¹ = Tᴴ T`.
entries.snippet:
lemma PosDef.inv_eq_conjTranspose_normalizer_mul {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef) :
    A⁻¹ = hA.normalizerᴴ * hA.normalizer

entries.name: Matrix.PosDef.add_mul_inv_mul_sub_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
**The equality case.** If `A` is positive definite, `B` hermitian, `A ∓ B` positive
semidefinite and `‖det B‖ = re (det A)`, then `(A + B) A⁻¹ (A − B) = 0`: every eigenvalue of the
normalized `B` is `±1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma PosDef.add_mul_inv_mul_sub_eq_zero {A B : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef)
    (hB : B.IsHermitian) (h₁ : (A - B).PosSemidef) (h₂ : (A + B).PosSemidef)
    (heq : ‖B.det‖ = (A.det).re) : (A + B) * A⁻¹ * (A - B) = 0

entries.name: Matrix.PosDef.card_le_finrank_ker_add_finrank_ker
entries.docstring:
At equality the kernels of `A + B` and `A − B` together have dimension at least `n`: every
vector is `A⁻¹ (A − B) x / 2 + A⁻¹ (A + B) x / 2`.
entries.snippet:
lemma PosDef.card_le_finrank_ker_add_finrank_ker {A B : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef)
    (hB : B.IsHermitian) (h₁ : (A - B).PosSemidef) (h₂ : (A + B).PosSemidef)
    (heq : ‖B.det‖ = (A.det).re) :
    Fintype.card n ≤ Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker (A + B).mulVecLin) +
      Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker (A - B).mulVecLin)

entries.name: Matrix.finrank_ker_transpose
entries.docstring: `G` and `Gᵀ` have kernels of the same dimension.
entries.snippet:
lemma finrank_ker_transpose (G : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker Gᵀ.mulVecLin) =
      Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker G.mulVecLin)

entries.name: Matrix.card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker
entries.docstring:
**Equality in Robertson's determinant relation.** Let `G = S + iW` be positive semidefinite
with `Gᵀ = S − iW`, for real `S` and `W`. If `|det W| = det S ≠ 0`, the kernel of `G` has at
least half the dimension.
entries.snippet:
lemma card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker {G : Matrix n n ℂ} {S W : Matrix n n ℝ} (hG : G.PosSemidef)
    (hGS : G = S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) + Complex.I • W.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ))
    (hGT : Gᵀ = S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) - Complex.I • W.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)) (hW : W.det ≠ 0)
    (heq : |W.det| = S.det) :
    Fintype.card n ≤ 2 * Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker G.mulVecLin)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.covarianceMatrix
entries.docstring: The covariance matrix `Σ_jk = cov(a_j, a_k)` of a family of observables.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def covarianceMatrix (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) : Matrix ι ι ℝ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.bracketMatrix
entries.docstring: The matrix `Ω_jk = ω⟨⁅a_j, a_k⁆⟩` of expectations of brackets of a family of observables.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def bracketMatrix (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) : Matrix ι ι ℝ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.centeredGNSVector
entries.docstring: The GNS vectors of the centered observables.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def centeredGNSVector (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gram_centeredGNSVector
entries.docstring: `Σ + iΩ` is the Gram matrix of the GNS vectors of the centered observables.
entries.snippet:
lemma gram_centeredGNSVector (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) :
    gram ℂ (fun j => centeredGNSVector ω (a j)) =
      (covarianceMatrix ω a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) +
        Complex.I • (bracketMatrix ω a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.transpose_gram_centeredGNSVector
entries.docstring: `Σ − iΩ` is the transpose of the Gram matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma transpose_gram_centeredGNSVector (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) :
    (gram ℂ (fun j => centeredGNSVector ω (a j)))ᵀ =
      (covarianceMatrix ω a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) -
        Complex.I • (bracketMatrix ω a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_det
entries.docstring:
**Robertson's uncertainty relation for several observables**: for every state and every
finite family of observables, `|det Ω| ≤ det Σ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma robertson_det [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) :
    |(bracketMatrix ω a).det| ≤ (covarianceMatrix ω a).det

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily
entries.docstring: A commuting family of bounded operators closed under adjoints.
entries.snippet:
structure CommutingStarFamily where
  carrier : Set (H →L[ℂ] H)
  commute : ∀ a ∈ carrier, ∀ b ∈ carrier, Commute a b
  star_mem : ∀ a ∈ carrier, star a ∈ carrier

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.isStarNormal_of_mem
entries.snippet: lemma isStarNormal_of_mem {a : H →L[ℂ] H} (ha : a ∈ F.carrier) : IsStarNormal a

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.isMulCommutative_adjoin
entries.snippet: instance isMulCommutative_adjoin : IsMulCommutative (StarAlgebra.adjoin ℂ F.carrier)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.algebra
entries.docstring: The closed ⋆-subalgebra of the bounded operators generated by a commuting ⋆-family.
entries.snippet: def algebra : StarSubalgebra ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.carrier_subset_algebra
entries.snippet: lemma carrier_subset_algebra : F.carrier ⊆ F.algebra

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.isClosed_algebra
entries.snippet: instance isClosed_algebra : IsClosed (F.algebra : Set (H →L[ℂ] H))

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.isMulCommutative_algebra
entries.snippet: instance isMulCommutative_algebra : IsMulCommutative F.algebra

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.commCStarAlgebraAlgebra
entries.docstring: The algebra generated by a commuting ⋆-family is a commutative C⋆-algebra.
entries.snippet: instance commCStarAlgebraAlgebra : CommCStarAlgebra F.algebra where

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.commute_of_forall_mem_carrier
entries.snippet:
lemma commute_of_forall_mem_carrier {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : ∀ a ∈ F.carrier, Commute a T)
    {b : H →L[ℂ] H} (hb : b ∈ F.algebra) : Commute b T

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.«instance@8309d561»
entries.snippet: instance : MeasurableSpace (characterSpace ℂ F.algebra)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.«instance@c86bbae7»
entries.snippet: instance : BorelSpace (characterSpace ℂ F.algebra)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.starHom
entries.docstring:
The inclusion of the algebra as a representation of the continuous functions on its character
space, by Gelfand duality.
entries.snippet: def starHom : C(characterSpace ℂ F.algebra, ℂ) →⋆ₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.starHom_gelfandStarTransform
entries.snippet:
lemma starHom_gelfandStarTransform (a : F.algebra) :
    F.starHom (gelfandStarTransform F.algebra a) = a

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.starHom_mem_algebra
entries.snippet: lemma starHom_mem_algebra (f : C(characterSpace ℂ F.algebra, ℂ)) : F.starHom f ∈ F.algebra

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.spectralMeasure
entries.docstring:
The joint spectral measure of a commuting ⋆-family, on the character space of the
C⋆-algebra it generates.
entries.snippet: def spectralMeasure : WOTSpectralMeasure (characterSpace ℂ F.algebra) H

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.boundedIntegral_gelfandStarTransform
entries.docstring:
Every operator of the algebra generated by the family is the integral of its Gelfand
transform against the joint spectral measure.
entries.snippet:
lemma boundedIntegral_gelfandStarTransform [Nonempty (characterSpace ℂ F.algebra)]
    (a : F.algebra) :
    ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM
      (WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral F.spectralMeasure (gelfandStarTransform F.algebra a)
        (gelfandStarTransform F.algebra a).continuous.measurable
        (boundedIntegral_bound_of_continuous _)) = a

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.CommutingStarFamily.spectralMeasure_commute
entries.docstring: The joint spectral measure commutes with every bounded operator commuting with the family.
entries.snippet:
lemma spectralMeasure_commute {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : ∀ a ∈ F.carrier, Commute a T) (S : Set _) :
    F.spectralMeasure S * ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T =
      ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T * F.spectralMeasure S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.inner_rankOne_self_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma inner_rankOne_self_apply (v φ : H) :
    ⟪φ, rankOne ℂ v v φ⟫_ℂ = (‖⟪v, φ⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2 : ℝ)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.inner_sum_rankOne_self_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma inner_sum_rankOne_self_apply (b : X → H) (φ : H) :
    ⟪φ, (∑ y, rankOne ℂ (b y) (b y)) φ⟫_ℂ = (∑ y, ‖⟪b y, φ⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2 : ℝ)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isPositive_one_sub_sum_rankOne
entries.docstring: By Bessel's inequality, `1 - ∑ y, |b y⟩⟨b y|` is positive for an orthonormal family `b`.
entries.snippet:
lemma isPositive_one_sub_sum_rankOne {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) :
    (1 - ∑ y, rankOne ℂ (b y) (b y)).IsPositive

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.rankOneObservable
entries.docstring: The rank-one observable `|v⟩⟨v|`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def rankOneObservable (v : H) : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.coe_rankOneObservable
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma coe_rankOneObservable (v : H) :
    (rankOneObservable v : H →L[ℂ] H) = rankOne ℂ v v

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.rankOneObservable_nonneg
entries.docstring: The rank-one observable `|v⟩⟨v|` is positive.
entries.snippet: lemma rankOneObservable_nonneg (v : H) : 0 ≤ rankOneObservable v

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.orthonormalObservable
entries.docstring:
The observable of the outcome `x` in the measurement in the family `b`: `|b x⟩⟨b x|`, plus
the remainder `1 - ∑ y, |b y⟩⟨b y|` when `x = x₀`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def orthonormalObservable (b : X → H) (x₀ x : X) : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.coe_orthonormalObservable
entries.docstring: The operator underlying the observable of the outcome `x`.
entries.snippet:
lemma coe_orthonormalObservable (b : X → H) (x₀ x : X) :
    (orthonormalObservable b x₀ x : H →L[ℂ] H) =
      rankOne ℂ (b x) (b x) + if x = x₀ then 1 - ∑ y, rankOne ℂ (b y) (b y) else 0

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.sum_orthonormalObservable
entries.docstring: The outcome observables add up to `1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_orthonormalObservable (b : X → H) (x₀ : X) :
    ∑ x, orthonormalObservable b x₀ x = 1

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.orthonormalObservable_nonneg
entries.docstring: The outcome observables of an orthonormal family are positive.
entries.snippet:
lemma orthonormalObservable_nonneg {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ x : X) :
    0 ≤ orthonormalObservable b x₀ x

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.orthonormalEffect
entries.docstring: The outcome effects of the measurement in an orthonormal family.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def orthonormalEffect {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ x : X) :
    Effect (Observable (H →L[ℂ] H))

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.coe_orthonormalEffect
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma coe_orthonormalEffect {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ x : X) :
    (orthonormalEffect hb x₀ x : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) = orthonormalObservable b x₀ x

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.ofOrthonormal
entries.docstring:
The measurement in the orthonormal family `b`: the outcome `x` has effect `|b x⟩⟨b x|`, and
the outcome `x₀` also registers the orthogonal complement of the span of the family.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def ofOrthonormal {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ : X) :
    Measurement X (Observable (H →L[ℂ] H))

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.coe_ofOrthonormal_singleton
entries.docstring:
The outcome `x` of the measurement in an orthonormal family has the observable
`orthonormalObservable b x₀ x`.
entries.snippet:
lemma coe_ofOrthonormal_singleton {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ x : X)
    (hx : MeasurableSet {x}) :
    (ofOrthonormal hb x₀ {x} hx : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) = orthonormalObservable b x₀ x

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.expectation_ofOrthonormal_singleton
entries.docstring:
The Born rule for the measurement in an orthonormal family: on a unit vector `φ`, the
outcome `x` has probability `‖⟪b x, φ⟫‖ ^ 2`, plus `1 - ∑ y, ‖⟪b y, φ⟫‖ ^ 2` when `x = x₀`.
entries.snippet:
lemma expectation_ofOrthonormal_singleton [MeasurableSingletonClass X] {b : X → H}
    (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ : X) {φ : H} (hφ : ‖φ‖ = 1) (x : X) :
    (ofVec hφ)⟨ofOrthonormal hb x₀ {x} (measurableSet_singleton x)⟩ =
      ‖⟪b x, φ⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2 + if x = x₀ then 1 - ∑ y, ‖⟪b y, φ⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2 else 0

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec_smul
entries.docstring: Vector states do not see a global phase: `ofVec (c • ψ) = ofVec ψ` for `‖c‖ = 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec_smul {ψ : H} (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) {c : 𝕜} (hc : ‖c‖ = 1)
    (h' : ‖c • ψ‖ = 1) :
    UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec (𝕜 := 𝕜) h' = UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec (𝕜 := 𝕜) h

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.norm_inner_lt_one_of_ofVec_ne
entries.docstring: Unit vectors with different vector states are not parallel: `‖⟪ψ, φ⟫‖ < 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma UnitalPositiveLinearMap.norm_inner_lt_one_of_ofVec_ne {ψ φ : H} (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
    (hφ : ‖φ‖ = 1) (h : ofVec (𝕜 := 𝕜) hψ ≠ ofVec (𝕜 := 𝕜) hφ) : ‖⟪ψ, φ⟫_𝕜‖ < 1

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.fluctuation
entries.docstring: The fluctuation vector `a ψ - ⟨a⟩ ψ` of an observable in a vector state.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def fluctuation (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gram_fluctuation
entries.docstring: In a vector state, `Σ + iΩ` is the Gram matrix of the fluctuation vectors.
entries.snippet:
lemma gram_fluctuation (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a : ι → Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    gram ℂ (fun j => fluctuation h (a j)) =
      (covarianceMatrix (ofVec h) a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) +
        Complex.I • (bracketMatrix (ofVec h) a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.transpose_gram_fluctuation
entries.docstring: In a vector state, `Σ − iΩ` is the transpose of the Gram matrix of the fluctuation vectors.
entries.snippet:
lemma transpose_gram_fluctuation (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a : ι → Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    (gram ℂ (fun j => fluctuation h (a j)))ᵀ =
      (covarianceMatrix (ofVec h) a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) -
        Complex.I • (bracketMatrix (ofVec h) a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gram_mulVec_eq_zero_iff
entries.docstring: The kernel of a Gram matrix is the space of linear relations among the vectors.
entries.snippet:
lemma gram_mulVec_eq_zero_iff [Fintype ι] (v : ι → H) (c : ι → ℂ) :
    gram ℂ v *ᵥ c = 0 ↔ ∑ j, c j • v j = 0

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker_gram_fluctuation
entries.docstring:
**Equality in Robertson's relation for several observables.** In a vector state with
`|det Ω| = det Σ ≠ 0`, the fluctuation vectors of the family satisfy linear relations
`∑ j, c j • (a_j ψ - ⟨a_j⟩ ψ) = 0` forming a space of at least half the size of the family.
entries.snippet:
lemma card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker_gram_fluctuation [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
    (a : ι → Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (hΩ : (bracketMatrix (ofVec h) a).det ≠ 0)
    (heq : |(bracketMatrix (ofVec h) a).det| = (covarianceMatrix (ofVec h) a).det) :
    Fintype.card ι ≤
      2 * Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker (gram ℂ fun j => fluctuation h (a j)).mulVecLin)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_commute
entries.docstring:
An operator commuting with every spectral projection commutes with every bounded integral
against the spectral measure.
entries.snippet:
lemma boundedIntegral_commute [Nonempty α] {T : H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hT : ∀ S, μS S * ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T = ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T * μS S)
    {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hbf : ∃ C, ∀ z, ‖f z‖ ≤ C) :
    ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (boundedIntegral μS f hf hbf) * T =
      T * ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (boundedIntegral μS f hf hbf)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.integralCLM

entries.snippet: def integralCLM (f : C(X, ℂ)) : H →L[ℂ] H

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bound_of_continuous
entries.snippet: lemma bound_of_continuous (f : C(X, ℂ)) : ∃ C, ∀ z, ‖f z‖ ≤ C

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.integralCLM_eq_of_forall_eq
entries.docstring: The integral of a measurable bounded function that agrees with a continuous function.
entries.snippet:
lemma integralCLM_eq_of_forall_eq (f : C(X, ℂ)) {F : X → ℂ} (hF : Measurable F)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.continuousCalculus
entries.docstring:
**The continuous functional calculus of a spectral measure**: `f ↦ ∫ f dP` is a unital
⋆-homomorphism from the continuous functions to the bounded operators.
entries.snippet: def continuousCalculus : C(X, ℂ) →⋆ₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H) where

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomCommutant
entries.docstring: The commutant of the range of `Φ`, a ⋆-subalgebra of the bounded operators.
entries.snippet: def starHomCommutant : StarSubalgebra ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.mem_starHomCommutant_iff
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_starHomCommutant_iff {T : H →L[ℂ] H} :
    T ∈ starHomCommutant Φ ↔ ∀ f : C(X, ℂ), Commute (Φ f) T

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomCommutant_isClosed
entries.snippet: instance starHomCommutant_isClosed : IsClosed (starHomCommutant Φ : Set (H →L[ℂ] H))

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_commute_of_commute
entries.docstring:
**The spectral operators commute with the commutant**: every bounded operator commuting with
the range of `Φ` commutes with each spectral operator of `Φ`. A bounded operator commuting with the
range is a combination of four unitary operators in the C⋆-algebra of such operators, and the
spectral operators commute with unitaries commuting with the range.

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_commute_of_commute
entries.docstring:
**The spectral measure commutes with the commutant**: every bounded operator commuting with
the range of `Φ` commutes with each spectral projection of `Φ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_commute_of_commute {T : H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hT : ∀ f : C(X, ℂ), Commute (Φ f) T) (S : Set X) :
    starHomSpectralMeasure Φ S * ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T =
      ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T * starHomSpectralMeasure Φ S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.reCompact
entries.docstring:
The real part of a continuous complex function on a compact space, as a compactly supported
continuous real function.
entries.snippet: def reCompact (f : C(X, ℂ)) : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.imCompact
entries.docstring:
The imaginary part of a continuous complex function on a compact space, as a compactly
supported continuous real function.
entries.snippet: def imCompact (f : C(X, ℂ)) : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex_reCompact_add_I_smul
entries.snippet:
lemma realToComplex_reCompact_add_I_smul (f : C(X, ℂ)) :
    realToComplex (reCompact f) + Complex.I • realToComplex (imCompact f) = f

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_diagonalMeasure
entries.docstring:
The diagonal measure `S ↦ ‖E(S) x‖²` of the spectral measure of `Φ` is the Riesz measure of
the vector state of `x`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_diagonalMeasure (x : H) :
    (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ).diagonalMeasure x = starHomScalarMeasure Φ x

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.integral_starHomScalarMeasure_real
entries.docstring:
The integral of a real continuous function against the Riesz measure of the vector state of
`x` is the expectation of its operator.
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_starHomScalarMeasure_real (u : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ) (x : H) :
    ∫ z, (u z : ℂ) ∂starHomScalarMeasure Φ x = ⟪x, starHomRealOperator Φ u x⟫_ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.integral_starHomScalarMeasure
entries.docstring:
The vector state of `x` in the representation `Φ` is integration against its Riesz measure:
`⟪x, Φ f x⟫ = ∫ f dμₓ` for every continuous `f`.
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_starHomScalarMeasure (f : C(X, ℂ)) (x : H) :
    ∫ z, f z ∂starHomScalarMeasure Φ x = ⟪x, Φ f x⟫_ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.boundedIntegral_bound_of_continuous
entries.snippet: lemma boundedIntegral_bound_of_continuous (f : C(X, ℂ)) : ∃ C, ∀ z, ‖f z‖ ≤ C

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral_real
entries.docstring:
The bounded integral of a real continuous function against the spectral measure of `Φ` is
`Φ` of that function.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral_real (u : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ) :
    ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM
      (WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ)
        (fun z => (u z : ℂ)) (by fun_prop) ⟨‖u.toContinuousMap‖, fun z => by
          simpa using u.toContinuousMap.norm_coe_le_norm z⟩) = starHomRealOperator Φ u

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral
entries.docstring:
**The spectral measure of `Φ` reconstructs `Φ`**: the bounded integral of a continuous
function `f` against `starHomSpectralMeasure Φ` is `Φ f`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral (f : C(X, ℂ)) :
    ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM
      (WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ) f f.continuous.measurable
        (boundedIntegral_bound_of_continuous f)) = Φ f

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral_map
entries.docstring:
**Change of spectral variable**: integrating a bounded measurable function `g` against the
pushforward of the spectral measure of `Φ` along a measurable map `f` is integrating `g ∘ f`
against the spectral measure itself.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral_map {β : Type*} [MeasurableSpace β] [Nonempty β]
    {f : X → β} (hf : Measurable f) {g : β → ℂ} (hg : Measurable g)
    (hbg : ∃ C, ∀ b, ‖g b‖ ≤ C) :
    WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral ((starHomSpectralMeasure Φ).map f hf) g hg hbg =
      WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ) (g ∘ f) (hg.comp hf)
        (by obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hbg; exact ⟨C, fun z => hC (f z)⟩)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex
entries.docstring:
Regard a real-valued continuous function on the spectrum of a normal operator as a complex
valued one.  Keeping this map explicit prevents the real/complex scalar changes in the Riesz
construction from being hidden in coercions.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def realToComplex
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    C(X, ℂ)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma realToComplex_apply
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (z : X) :
    realToComplex f z = f z

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex_add
entries.snippet:
lemma realToComplex_add
    (f g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    realToComplex (f + g) =
      realToComplex f + realToComplex g

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex_smul
entries.snippet:
lemma realToComplex_smul (r : ℝ)
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    realToComplex (r • f) =
      (r : ℂ) • realToComplex f

The operator obtained by applying the complex continuous functional calculus to a real test

entries.snippet:

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomRealOperator_isSelfAdjoint
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomRealOperator_isSelfAdjoint

entries.snippet:
lemma starHomRealOperator_nonneg

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarFunctional
entries.docstring:
The vector state of the continuous functional calculus, restricted to real test functions.
The positivity proof is the square-root argument above; this is the exact input required by
Riesz--Markov.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def starHomScalarFunctional (x : H) :
    CompactPositiveFunctional (X := X) where

entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarFunctional_apply (x : H)
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    (starHomScalarFunctional Φ x).functional f =
      RCLike.re ⟪x, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫_ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure
entries.docstring: The scalar spectral measure supplied by Riesz--Markov for the vector state at `x`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def starHomScalarMeasure (x : H) : Measure (X)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_regular
entries.snippet: instance starHomScalarMeasure_regular (x : H) : (starHomScalarMeasure Φ x).Regular

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_isFinite
entries.snippet: instance starHomScalarMeasure_isFinite (x : H) : IsFiniteMeasure (starHomScalarMeasure Φ x)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_integral
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_integral (x : H)
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    ∫ z, f z ∂starHomScalarMeasure Φ x =
      RCLike.re ⟪x, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫_ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_integral_complex
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_integral_complex (x : H)
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    ((∫ z, f z ∂starHomScalarMeasure Φ x : ℝ) : ℂ) =
      ⟪starHomRealOperator Φ f x, x⟫_ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomRealIntegral
entries.docstring: The integral of a real function against the polarized measure.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def polarizedStarHomRealIntegral
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x y : H) : ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomRealIntegral_eq_inner
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomRealIntegral_eq_inner
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x y : H) :
    polarizedStarHomRealIntegral Φ f x y =
      ⟪y, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫_ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_parallelogram
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_parallelogram (x y : H) :
    starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + y) + starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x - y) =
      (starHomScalarMeasure Φ x + starHomScalarMeasure Φ x) +
        (starHomScalarMeasure Φ y + starHomScalarMeasure Φ y)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_neg
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_neg (x : H) :
    starHomScalarMeasure Φ (-x) = starHomScalarMeasure Φ x

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_I_smul
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_I_smul (x : H) :
    starHomScalarMeasure Φ (Complex.I • x) = starHomScalarMeasure Φ x

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure
entries.docstring: The complex measure `⟪y, E(·) x⟫`, obtained by polarizing the four measures `⟪v, E(·) v⟫`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure (x y : H) : ComplexMeasure (X)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_isFiniteMeasure
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_isFiniteMeasure (x y : H) :
    IsFiniteMeasure
      (polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y).variation

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_complexIntegral
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_complexIntegral
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x y : H) :
    ∫ᵛ z, (f z : ℂ) ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℂ (E := ℂ);
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y] =
      polarizedStarHomRealIntegral Φ f x y

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_complexIntegral_eq_inner
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_complexIntegral_eq_inner
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x y : H) :
    ∫ᵛ z, (f z : ℂ) ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℂ (E := ℂ);
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y] =
      ⟪y, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫_ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_apply {x y : H}
    {S : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S =
      ((1 / 4 : ℝ) *
          ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + y)).real S -
            (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x - y)).real S) : ℂ) +
        Complex.I * ((1 / 4 : ℝ) *
          ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + Complex.I • y)).real S -
            (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x - Complex.I • y)).real S) : ℂ)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_parallelogram
entries.docstring:
The real-valued version of the parallelogram law, at a fixed (not necessarily measurable)
set `S`.  This is the algebraic engine behind the sesquilinearity proofs below.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_parallelogram (a b : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + b)).real S + (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - b)).real S =
      2 * (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S + 2 * (starHomScalarMeasure Φ b).real S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_neg
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_neg (a : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (-a)).real S = (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_I_smul
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_I_smul (a : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (Complex.I • a)).real S = (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_nonneg
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_nonneg (a : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    0 ≤ (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_univ
entries.docstring:
The Riesz measure for the vector state at `x` has total mass `‖x‖ ^ 2`: the vector-state
counterpart of `Φ 1 = 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_univ (x : H) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ x).real Set.univ = ‖x‖ ^ 2

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_le_univ
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_le_univ (a : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S ≤ ‖a‖ ^ 2

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_symm
entries.docstring:
The real polarization `Q(a + b) - Q(a - b)` of the diagonal measures is symmetric in `a` and
`b`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_symm (a b : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + b)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - b)).real S =
      (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (b + a)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (b - a)).real S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_left
entries.docstring:
First-argument additivity of the real polarization `Q(a+b) - Q(a-b)`, established by pure
algebra from the parallelogram law (`starHomScalarMeasure_real_parallelogram`); no continuity is
needed for this step, matching the classical Jordan--von Neumann polarization argument
(`Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.OfNorm`).
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_left (x y z : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + y + z)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + y - z)).real S =
      ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + z)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x - z)).real S) +
        ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (y + z)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (y - z)).real S)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_right
entries.docstring:
Second-argument additivity of the real polarization, obtained from first-argument additivity
(`starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_left`)
  via the symmetry `starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_symm`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_right (a b c : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + (b + c))).real S -
        (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - (b + c))).real S =
      ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + b)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - b)).real S) +
        ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + c)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - c)).real S)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_add_right
entries.docstring:
Additivity of the polarized measure in its second (right) vector argument, for a fixed
measurable set `S`.  This is the sesquilinearity step promised in the module docstring: it
follows from the parallelogram law by pure algebra, with no continuity or Riesz-representation
machinery required.
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_add_right (x y₁ y₂ : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x (y₁ + y₂) S =
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y₁ S +
        polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y₂ S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_add_left
entries.docstring:
Additivity of the polarized measure in its first (left) vector argument, for a fixed
measurable set `S`.
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_add_left (x₁ x₂ y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ (x₁ + x₂) y S =
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x₁ y S +
        polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x₂ y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_I_smul_right
entries.docstring: Multiplying the second vector by `i` multiplies the polarized measure by `-i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_I_smul_right (x y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x (Complex.I • y) S =
      -Complex.I * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_I_smul_left
entries.docstring: Multiplying the first vector by `i` multiplies the polarized measure by `i`.
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_I_smul_left (x y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ (Complex.I • x) y S =
      Complex.I * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_norm_le
entries.docstring:
A crude but sufficient bound on the polarized measure, from the parallelogram law and
`starHomScalarMeasure_real_le_univ`.
   This is enough to see `(x, y) ↦ polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ
x y S` is jointly bounded, the input a Riesz-representation argument needs.

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_right
entries.docstring: The polarized measure is real homogeneous in the second vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_right (x y : H) (r : ℝ) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x (r • y) S =
      (r : ℂ) * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_left
entries.docstring:
Real-scalar homogeneity in the left (first) argument, the counterpart of
`polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_right` needed for conjugate-linearity in `x` (real scalars
are self-conjugate, so the same statement serves both roles).
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_left (x y : H) (r : ℝ) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ (r • x) y S =
      (r : ℂ) * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_smul_left
entries.docstring: Full `ℂ`-linearity of the polarized measure in its first (left) argument.
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_smul_left (c : ℂ) (x y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ (c • x) y S =
      c * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_smul_right
entries.docstring: Full conjugate-`ℂ`-linearity of the polarized measure in its second (right) argument.
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_smul_right (c : ℂ) (x y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x (c • y) S =
      (starRingEnd ℂ c) * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_zero_left
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_zero_left (y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) : polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ 0 y S = 0

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_zero_right
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_zero_right (x : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) : polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x 0 S = 0

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_norm_le_mul
entries.docstring: The polarized measure is bounded by `‖x‖ ‖y‖`.

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSesquilinearFormAux
entries.docstring:
The algebraic (not-yet-continuous) sesquilinear form representing `S`, conjugate-linear in the
first argument and linear in the second — the convention Mathlib's
`InnerProductSpace.continuousLinearMapOfBilin` expects.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def starHomSesquilinearFormAux (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    H →ₛₗ[starRingEnd ℂ] H →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSesquilinearFormAux_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSesquilinearFormAux_apply (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) (x y : H) :
    starHomSesquilinearFormAux Φ S hS x y =
      starRingEnd ℂ (polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSesquilinearForm
entries.docstring:
The continuous sesquilinear form, in the shape `InnerProductSpace.continuousLinearMapOfBilin`
consumes.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def starHomSesquilinearForm (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    H →L⋆[ℂ] H →L[ℂ] ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSesquilinearForm_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma starHomSesquilinearForm_apply (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) (x y : H) :
    starHomSesquilinearForm Φ S hS x y =
      starRingEnd ℂ (polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperatorAux
entries.docstring: The Riesz-represented operator at the measurable set `S`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def starHomSpectralOperatorAux (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    H →L[ℂ] H

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperatorAux_inner
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperatorAux_inner (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) (x y : H) :
    ⟪y, starHomSpectralOperatorAux Φ S hS x⟫_ℂ =
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator
entries.docstring:
The Riesz-represented operator on every set, `0` off the measurable sets so that this
directly matches `MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure`'s `not_measurable'` convention.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def starHomSpectralOperator (S : Set (X)) : H →L[ℂ] H

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_inner
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_inner (S : Set (X)) (x y : H) :
    ⟪y, starHomSpectralOperator Φ S x⟫_ℂ = polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_apply_eq_zero_of_not_measurableSet
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_apply_eq_zero_of_not_measurableSet {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : ¬MeasurableSet S) : starHomSpectralOperator Φ S = 0

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_eq_negI_smul
entries.docstring:
The `Complex.I`-inversion companion of `starHomScalarMeasure_real_I_smul`: rewrites a Riesz
measure at `v` as the Riesz measure at `(-I) • v`.  This is the algebraic engine behind
Hermitian symmetry of the polarized measure below.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_eq_negI_smul (v : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ v).real S = (starHomScalarMeasure Φ ((-Complex.I) • v)).real S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_conj_symm
entries.docstring:
Hermitian symmetry of the polarized measure: `B(y,x,S) = conj (B(x,y,S))`, matching the
convention that `B` is exactly `⟪y, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫` in the limit and inner products
are conjugate-symmetric.  This is the input `starHomSpectralOperator_isSelfAdjoint` needs.
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_conj_symm (x y : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ y x S =
      starRingEnd ℂ (polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_isSelfAdjoint
entries.docstring:
`starHomSpectralOperator Φ S` is self-adjoint, for every `S` (measurable or not — the
non-measurable case is trivial since the operator is `0`).  This follows from
`polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_conj_symm` via `LinearMap.IsSymmetric`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_isSelfAdjoint (S : Set (X)) :
    IsSelfAdjoint (starHomSpectralOperator Φ S)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_univ
entries.docstring: The polarized measure of the whole spectrum is `⟪y, x⟫`.
entries.snippet:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_univ (x y : H) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y Set.univ = ⟪y, x⟫_ℂ

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_univ_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_univ_apply (x : H) :
    starHomSpectralOperator Φ Set.univ x = x

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_univ
entries.snippet: lemma starHomSpectralOperator_univ : starHomSpectralOperator Φ Set.univ = 1

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_inner_self
entries.docstring: On the diagonal, `⟪x, E(S) x⟫` is the diagonal measure of `S`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_inner_self {S : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) (x : H) :
    ⟪x, starHomSpectralOperator Φ S x⟫_ℂ = ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ x).real S : ℂ)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_reApplyInnerSelf
entries.docstring:
`reApplyInnerSelf` version of `starHomSpectralOperator_inner_self`, in the exact shape
`ContinuousLinearMap.IsPositive` consumes.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_reApplyInnerSelf {S : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S)
    (x : H) :
    (starHomSpectralOperator Φ S).reApplyInnerSelf x = (starHomScalarMeasure Φ x).real S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_isPositive
entries.docstring: `starHomSpectralOperator Φ S` is a positive operator, for measurable `S`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_isPositive {S : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.IsPositive (starHomSpectralOperator Φ S)

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_nonneg
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_nonneg {S : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    0 ≤ starHomSpectralOperator Φ S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_mono
entries.docstring:
`starHomSpectralOperator Φ S` is monotone in `S`, for measurable sets, in the Loewner order on
`H →L[ℂ] H`.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_mono {S T : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S)
    (hT : MeasurableSet T) (hST : S ⊆ T) :
    starHomSpectralOperator Φ S ≤ starHomSpectralOperator Φ T

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_le_one
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_le_one {S : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    starHomSpectralOperator Φ S ≤ 1

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_empty
entries.snippet: lemma starHomSpectralOperator_empty : starHomSpectralOperator Φ ∅ = 0

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_add_of_disjoint
entries.docstring: Finite additivity of `starHomSpectralOperator` on disjoint measurable sets.
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_add_of_disjoint {S T : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S)
    (hT : MeasurableSet T) (hdisj : Disjoint S T) :
    starHomSpectralOperator Φ (S ∪ T) =
      starHomSpectralOperator Φ S + starHomSpectralOperator Φ T

entries.docstring: The operator at `S`, valued in the weak-operator-topology type.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def starHomSpectralMeasureFun (S : Set (X)) : H →WOT[ℂ] H

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasureFun_inner
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma starHomSpectralMeasureFun_inner (S : Set (X)) (x y : H) :
    ⟪y, starHomSpectralMeasureFun Φ S x⟫_ℂ = polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralVectorMeasure
entries.docstring: The operators `E(S)`, as a vector measure in the weak operator topology.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def starHomSpectralVectorMeasure :
    VectorMeasure (X) (H →WOT[ℂ] H) where

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralVectorMeasure_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma starHomSpectralVectorMeasure_apply (S : Set (X)) :
    starHomSpectralVectorMeasure Φ S = starHomSpectralMeasureFun Φ S

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperatorAux_nonneg
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperatorAux_nonneg {S : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    0 ≤ starHomSpectralOperatorAux Φ S hS

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperatorAux_le_one
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperatorAux_le_one {S : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    starHomSpectralOperatorAux Φ S hS ≤ 1

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperatorAux_mono

lemma starHomSpectralOperatorAux_mono {S T : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S)

    starHomSpectralOperatorAux Φ S hS ≤ starHomSpectralOperatorAux Φ T hT

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomRealOperator_reApplyInnerSelf
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomRealOperator_reApplyInnerSelf
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x : H) :
    (starHomRealOperator Φ f).reApplyInnerSelf x =
      ∫ z, f z ∂starHomScalarMeasure Φ x

entries.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_le_cfcRealOperator_of_compact_subset_open
entries.snippet:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_le_cfcRealOperator_of_compact_subset_open
